A patient with ROS1 fusion-positive NSCLC was treated with crizotinib. After tumor progression, a repeat biopsy revealed ROS1 G2032R mutation. The patient subsequently enrolled in the phase I repotrectinib trial. A confirmed PR (−36.6%) was achieved with a duration of response of 7.4 months. Pharmacokinetic analyses revealed that the Ctrough (425 nmol/L) was above the IC90 (100 nmol/L) needed to inhibit ROS1G2032R Ba/F3 cell proliferation.

A patient with ETV6-NTRK3 fusion-positive mammary analog secretory carcinoma was treated with entrectinib for 6 months with partial response. After tumor progression, a repeat biopsy revealed NTRK3 G623E mutation. Rapid and dramatic response to repotrectinib was achieved within the first few days of the administration, and followed by confirmed PR with 82% tumor shrinkage. The patient's cancer started to progress slowly after 6 months of treatment Plasma exposures indicated that the Ctrough (144 nmol/L) was above the IC90 (80 nmol/L) needed to inhibit TRKCG623E Ba/F3 cell growth.

A patient with ROS1 fusion-positive NSCLC was treated with crizotinib and led to durable response (-75%) over 22 months. After tumor progression, a rebiopsy sample was obtained and revealed ROS1 S1986Y/F mutation. Variant allele frequency of S1986Y and S1986F were 18% and 17%, respectively. Subsequently, the patient was treated with Lorlatinib and achieved tumor response (-89%) at least for 6 months.

A patient with ROS1 fusion-positive NSCLC was treated with crizotinib for 26 months led to response (-64%). After tumor progression, a rebiopsy sample was obtained and revealed ROS1 D2033N mutation. Subsequently, the patient was treated with cabozantinib and obtained tumor response (-92%) at least for 8 months.

Experiments with SMAD4 mutated colorectal cancer cell lines show a lack of growth inhibition induced by TGF-beta and inability to form active complexes with SMAD2 and SMAD3. The SW948 cell line with SMAD4 D537Y mutation did not have a change in cell cycle profiles when stimulated with TGF-beta, whereas wt SMAD4 human keratinocyte cell line (HaCaT) had an increase in G1 phase cells indicating cell cycle arrest. In line with this, HaCaT cells showed expression of CDK inhibitors p15 and p21 that play a role in TGF-beta induced cell cycle arrest, while SW948 cells did not express p15 or p21 in the presence of TGF-beta. SMAD4 formed complexes with activated SMAD2 in HaCaT cells in the presence of TGF-beta, whereas SW948 cells showed no SMAD4-SMAD2 complexes despite similar amounts of SMAD2 and SMAD4 protein in all cell lines. SMAD4 with D537Y mutation does not form DNA-bound complexes with activated SMAD3, as seen in a supershift assay and luciferase assay in MDA-MB468 cells. In the absence of TGF-beta, wt and D537Y mutant SMAD4 have similar distributions in the cytoplasm and nucleus, whereas upon TGF-beta induction wt SMAD4 accumulates in the nucleus and D537Y SMAD4 does not, and it was shown that interaction with SMAD2/3 is required for nuclear retention.

Missense mutations in PTEN were characterized for phosphatase activity and the ability to bind a phospholipid membrane. Phosphatase assays revealed that PTEN R130Q retains no phosphatase activity in vitro. A membrane binding assay showed that R130Q mutated PTEN has similar membrane binding properties as wild-type PTEN, suggesting that membrane binding does not play a role in this loss of function variant.

A 16 yr-old male with precursor B-ALL was found to have the t(5;9)(q23;q34) in his peripheral blasts. Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), RT-PCR, and sequencing of the product confirmed a SNX2-ABL1 fusion gene (SNX2 exon 3 fused in frame to ABL1 exon 4) was present. The patient also was found to carry an IKZF1 deletion (exons 2-8) and amplification of PAX5. The patient was treated with vindesine, idarubicin, and dexamethasone (VDP) and VDCP (plus cyclophosphamide) regimens. He received two bone marrow transplants, but eventually died of disease. The patient did not receive tyrosine-kinase inhibitors.

The rare PIK3CA mutation Q546P was shown to have strong oncogenic transforming abilities when expressed in chicken embryo fibroblasts (CEF), similar to levels seen for hotspot PIK3CA mutations. The Q546P mutant also shows constitutive activation of downstream pathways when expressed in CEF cells in the absence of growth factors, with elevated levels of phospho-AKT and phospho-S6K relative to wt PIK3CA.

This double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, phase 3 study (GOLD) recruited Asian patients with advanced gastric cancer that had progressed after first-line chemotherapy. Patients were randomly assigned to receive olaparib plus paclitaxel or placebo plus paclitaxel. The primary endpoint was overall survival in the overall patients' population and also in patients whose tumors were ATM-negative (defined as IHC stain negative) population. A significant difference was defined as p<0.025 Overall survival did not differ between treatment groups in the overall patient population (8.8 vs. 6.9 months, p=0.026) or in the ATM-negative population (12.0 vs 10.0 months, p=0.25).

In this retrospective analysis of a phase 3 trial of cabozantinib or placebo in 330 patients. Among those, 51.2% were RET mutation-positive (38.2% with RET M918T), 34.8% were RET mutation-unknown, and 13.9% were RET mutation-negative. Sixteen patients were RAS mutation-positive. Cabozantinib appeared to prolong PFS versus the placebo in the RET mutation-positive subgroup (hazard ratio [HR], 0.23; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.14-0.38; P < .0001). Patients in a RET mutation-negative population showed relatively smaller benefits from cabozantinib (HR 0.53). The RET M918T subgroup achieved the greatest observed PFS benefit from cabozantinib versus the placebo (HR 0.15).

Seven of fourteen members of a single family tested positive for the P25L (c.74C>T) germline variant of the VHL gene. The proband was sequenced using the DYEnamic ET Terminator and Cycle Sequencing kit. The gene sequencing methodology used for the remainder of the familials is unclear. The female proband presented with a retinal hemangioma and a cyst in the right kidney of diameter less than 1cm at age 42. The rest of the famililals returned positive for the P25L germline variant but none showed visceral features of VHL. Three of these familials were above the age of 60. A single instance of renal cell carcionoma was found in the family and the carrier tested negative for P25L. ACMG evidence codes: 'PP4' since the patient presents phenotypes highly specific for a disease with a single genetic etiology.

evidence_statement: The male proband, age 29, underwent surgery for cervical hemangioblastoma (C2-C3) 2 years prior. He was genetically confirmed for Type 1 VHL syndrome although the method for genetic sequencing and analysis is not specified. Non-contrast computed tomography of the abdomen showed a lesion in the left adrenal gland with central necrosis, RCC (4cm x 3cm x 2cm) and renal cysts in bilateral kidneys and fluid attenuating pancreatic cysts. The patient subsequently underwent a left-sided adrenalectomy, identifying the encapsulated gray-brown lesion (3cm x 3cm x 3cm) having areas of hemorrhage and congestion. The patient underwent genetic analysis revealing a heterozygous 5' VHL splice site variation of exon 1 (c.340+1G>A). The author does not provide family genetic data. The probands sister presented Type 1 VHL features such as cerebral hemangiomas, RCC on the left kidney, bilateral renal cysts and pancreatic serous neoplasm. All other members of the family do not present VHL features. ACMG evidence codes: 'PP4' since the patient presents phenotypes highly specific to a disease with a single genetic etiology.

The proband was diagnosed with a normetanephrine-secreting 5cm right pheochromocytoma at age 32. She was found to harbour the hetrozygous germline c.414A>G mutation in VHL through whole exome sequencing using the NimbleGen 44Mb SeqCap EZ Exome kit v2.. Of those family members that underwent whole genome sequenicing, six member were found to have this variant. Her paternal grandfather was diagnosed with an adrenal tumor and hypertension in his 40's. The proband's father presented with pheochromocytoma and a spinal hemangioblastoma at age 73. Her brother was diagnosed at age 34 with pheochromocytoma and a renal cyst. The paternal 1st male cousin once removed was diagnosed with pheochromocytoma at age 23 while her paternal 1st male cousin was diagnosed at age 12 with pheochromocytoma. The probands paternal aunt was also found to have a history of pheochromocytoma. ACMG evidence codes: 'PM2' since this variant is absent from controls (gnomAD), 'PP1' since there is cosegregation with disease in multiple family members, 'PP2' since this is a missense variant in a gene where missense variants are a known mechanism for disease, 'PP4' since the patients phenotype and family history are highly specific for a disease with a single genetic etiology.

A complete genetic characterization of VHL, RET, SDHB, SDHC and SDHD was performed on a cohort of 240 patients presenting with a pheochromocytoma or paraganglioma. A single patient, presenting a single adrenal tumor with no other tumors and no family history of pheochromocytoma was found to have the germline mutation c.74C>T in the VHL gene. Genetic testing was completed on DNA from blood samples and point mutation analysis of exons and intron-exon boudaries was implemented. ACMG evidence codes: 'PP2' since we have a missense variant in a gene where missense variants are a common mechanism of disease, 'PP4' since the patient presents phenotypes highly specific for a disease with a single genetic etiology.

A complete genetic characterization of five susceptibility genes (VHL, RET, SDHB, SDHC and SDHD) was performed on a cohort of 240 patients, 135 of which presented with an apparently sporadic pheochromocytoma or paraganglioma (no family history of disease). Out of 135 sporadic cases, 14% (19/135) aged between 12 and 67 years (mean, 33.3 years) showed a germline mutation in one of 5 susceptibility genes analyzed (RET, SDHB, SDHC, SDHD, and VHL.) A single patient (unknown sex/age/ethnicity), presenting with a single adrenal pheochromocytoma (with no other tumors and no family history of pheochromocytoma) was found to have the germline mutation p.R161Q (c.482G>A) in the VHL gene. The complete genetic characterization of the five susceptibility genes mentioned in this paper included point mutation analysis of all exons and intron-exon boundaries. In order to assess the meaning of undescribed variants, the authors used DNA from 1000 unrelated and unaffected individuals as a control population. Suggested ACMG evidence codes: None

Of 46 cases of RCC in patients younger than 25 years, one patient (case 45) was found to harbour a germline VHL splicing mutation G>C at position 553+5. Genomic DNA was extracted, using DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit, from neoplastic and non-neoplastic tissue samples and was analyzed for polymerase chain reaction-based loss of heterozygosity (LOH) where results were viewed by silver nitrate staining. This patient presented with a papillary RCC (stage/diameter: pT1N0M0) on her right kidney at age 16. She presented no evidence of disease at her 36 month follow-up after undergoing a radical nephrectomy. She had a known family history for VHL disease and her mother has cerebellar hemangioblastoma. Genetic data on the mother was not described. ACMG evidence codes: 'PP4' since the patient presents phenotypes highly specific for a disease with a single genetic etiology.

evidence_statement: A female patient, age 27, was admitted and found to harbour clear cell renal cell carcinoma and MRI and CT scans showed a pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor close to the pancreatic head (Ki67<1% with no vascular/neural invasion) which was confirmed through a histological study. The patient had been previously diagnosed with DM1 at age 21. The patient had undergone surgery for left kidney renal cell carcinoma 4 years previous. Peripheral blood was analyzed for genetic mutations in the VHL gene showing a frameshift mutation in exon 1. A subsequent brain MRI found a hemangioblastoma of the medulla oblongata. ACMG evidence codes: 'PVS1' since we have a frameshift variant, 'PP4' since the patient presents phenotypes highly specific for a disease with a single genetic etiology.

Recurrent PIK3CA mutations detected in breast cancer were evaluated by in vitro and in vivo growth and transformation assays. The PIK3CA mutation Q546R was found in 16 samples from COSMIC. Expression of PIK3CA Q546R in Ba/F3 cells resulted in increased growth and survival relative to wild-type PIK3CA expressing cells. PIK3CA Q546R expression in MCF10A breast epithelial cells resulted in increased growth in the absence of insulin and EGF, as well as increased colony formation in a soft agar colony formation assay, indicative of cell transformation. Human mammary epithelial cells with Q546R mutated PIK3CA formed tumors in athymic mice, whereas wild-type PIK3CA did not induce tumorigenesis. In addition, proteomic analysis of lysates from MCF10A cells expressing Q546R mutated PIK3CA showed a significant shift in expression or phosphorylation of many cancer associated proteins, similar to other oncogenic PIK3CA mutants.

In a case report, a 3‐year‐old girl with glioblastoma harboring a probable germline heterozygous BRCA2 Lys3326Ter (K3326*) nonsense variant. After debulking surgery, the patient received standard‐of‐care treatment with radiation and temozolomide. Nine months later the PARP inhibitor olaparib was administered in combination with temozolomide for 16 cycles. This regimen was well tolerated by the patient and serial imaging showed a reduction in tumor size.

In a retrospective study, the authors evaluated the association between IDH1/IDH2 mutation and prognosis in patients with high-grade central chondrosarcoma. Although no association was discovered between IDH mutation status and the patient's overall survival, IDH1/IDH2 mutation was found to be associated with longer relapse free and metastasis free survival in high-grade chondrosarcomas.

Although no association was discovered between IDH mutation status and the patient's overall survival, IDH1/IDH2 mutation was found to be associated with longer relapse free and metastasis free survival in high-grade chondrosarcomas.

evidence_statement: In this phase 3 trial (ADMIRAL), 371 patients with relapsed or refractory FLT3-mutated AML (required to have FLT3 ITD or TKD D835 or I836 mutations) were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive either gilteritinib (n=247, at a dose of 120 mg per day) or salvage chemotherapy (n=124). Median overall survival in the gilteritinib group was significantly longer than in the chemotherapy group (9.3 months vs. 5.6 months; hazard ratio for death, 0.64; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.49 to 0.83; P<0.001). Median event-free survival was 2.8 months in the gilteritinib group and 0.7 months in the chemotherapy group (hazard ratio for treatment failure or death, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.58 to 1.09). The complete remission rate with full or partial hematologic recovery was 34.0% in the gilteritinib group and 15.3% in the chemotherapy group (risk difference, 18.6 percentage points; 95% CI, 9.8 to 27.4); the percentages with complete remission were 21.1% and 10.5%, respectively (risk difference, 10.6 percentage points; 95% CI, 2.8 to 18.4). Notably, gilteritinib treatment resulted in similar median overall survival (9.3 months vs. 8.0 months) and percentage of complete remission (20.5% vs. 19.0%) in patients with ITD mutations and patients with TKD mutations. The authors concluded gilteritinib therapy in relapsed or refractory FLT3-mutated AML patients resulted longer survival and improved response versus salvage chemotherapy.

In a multi-cohort biomarker selected phase 2 study, patients with gastric cancer harboring MET amplification were treated with Savolitinib. Gene alterations were evaluated using tumor samples. MET amplification was detected in 3.5% (25/715) of patients. The response rate was 50% (10/20).

In a case report, a patient with pancreatic cancer harboring BRAF N486-P490del was treated with trametinib. Within 4 weeks of initiating therapy, her serum CA19-9 had fallen from 36,000 to 8,100 U/mL, and the radiographic partial response was revealed by CT at 8 weeks after initiation of trametinib. cfDNA measurements for BRAF and TP53 alleles revealed a dramatic decline in response to trametinib. After 6 months of therapy, radiographic progression was identified.

In this case report, a 66-year old woman with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma was treated with trametinib for a BRAF in-frame-deletion and TP53 mutation and achieved an initial partial response for close to 6 months. Resequencing after progression revealed the emergence of MAP2K2 H123Q, G132D and G132S mutations in cfDNA measurements.

Ten members (7 male, 3 female) of 3 generations (2 grandparents, 2 parents and 6 children) of an Arabic-Persian family from Kwuait, of which 1 was clinically diagnosed with VHL disease, were recruited for the study. The mutation in the VHL gene was found in nucleotide number one of the first intron, designated as IVS1 + 1 G→T mutation in 4 of the children. The origin of the mutation was from the Arabic side of the family. The patient with VHL mutation and clinically diagnosed VHL disease was 39 years old. The other 3 children with confirmed VHL mutations were 2 males 32 and 20 years old, and one female was 24 years. Ages were recorded at the time of genetic testing. The patient aged 39 years died only a few weeks before completion of the study. Phenotypes were not specified. Evidence may suggest PP1, although should be interpreted with caution because of lack of phenotype described in 3 other patients with the mutation.

A retrospective study of thirty-one subjects with chromaffin tumours from the St Bartholomew’s Hospital found 12 patients with VHL mutations. Patient #18 was male and diagnosed with VHL and a nonsense mutation at 30Y. He presented with abdominal paraganglioma (age of presentation unknown) and retinal angiomas at 16Y. Patient's phenotype is highly specific to VHL disease with single etiology (PP4) and disease causing missense variants are common in VHL disease (PP2).

Patient #20 was male and diagnosed with VHL and a germline missense mutation (c.499C>T) at 14Y. Another family not related to patient #20 (family ID 4) was found with the same mutation (c.499C>T). Family 4 had four affected patients described: Patient #22 was 8Y female with asynchronous multifocal pheochromocytoma; Patient #23 was 25Y male with synchronous pheochromocytoma; Patient #24 was 14Y male with multifocal pheochromocytoma; Patient #25 was 12Y female with multifocal pheochromocytoma. Evidence may suggest cosegregation with multiple affected family members (PP1) and missense mutation is occuring in a VHL hotspot (PM1).

However, the patient's phenotypes are highly specific to VHL disease (PP4) and disease-causing missense variants are common in VHL disease (PP2).

Her clinical presentation was pancreatic cysts and lesions in the CNS and kidney (unspecified). Family history was not provided. Family history not provided. A frameshit mutation may indicate PVS1. This case report describes a 7-year old boy with B-ALL who presented with high white blood count (115.4x109 /L). Karyotype analysis showed a t(5;9)(q22;q34), resulting in a SNX2-ABL1 fusion. The patient was treated based on the ALL-BFM95 regimen; although he received remission, he relapsed during maintenance, 15 months after the initial diagnosis. He could not achieve the second remission using chemotherapy, but was treated at this time with imatinib (dose of 240 mg/m2 /d once daily); this allowed to achieve disease control and proceed with an umbilical cord blood transplant. However, at 6 months from transplantation, the patient developed bone marrow relapse again. He never achieved a remission after the second relapse (despite salvage chemotherapies and therapy with both imatinib and dasatinib). The patient died of progressive disease.

evidence_statement: Patients presenting with cerebellar hemangioblastomas (HBs) were prospectively enrolled alongside family members, resulting in 84 patients in 7 families with VHL mutations, and subjected to peripheral blood draw and PCR-based mutation screening, as well as full clinical screening for symptomatic individuals. 19 individuals across two unrelated families (Families B and C) presented with a c.298dupA mutation (noted as 1012_1013insA in the source), leading to a frameshift. Among these individuals, no tumors were found in 2 members of family B (ages 7 and 2), and 5 members of family C (ages 17, 12, 13, 29, 9). The other 12 individuals across the two families (3 and 9 individuals in families B and C) who harbored tumors had a median age of 30.25 years (13-54 years). Eight had cerebellar HBs, two had medullar HBs, three had bilateral retinal angiomas, seven had renal cysts, six had pancreatic cysts, three had renal cell carcinoma, one had epididymal cystadenoma. Eight patients harbored more than one tumor type. ACMG Evidence Codes: PVS1 as loss of function in VHL is a known mechanism of disease, PM4 because protein length is expected to change due to in-frame insertion, PP1 as the gene co-segregates with multiple family members suffering from the same disease, PP4 because the patients' phenotypes or family histories are highly specific for VHL disease.

In a phase 2 clinical trial of 39 stage 3/4 chemotherapy-naive unresectable melanoma patients receiving dasatinib without prior biomarker screening, six patients achieved clinical benefit (2 PR; 4 SD). Tissue was available for IHC (but insufficient for mutational analyses) on three patients with primary ocular melanoma. All had expression by IHC, none responded.

In a phase II trial, patients with DLL3-expressing small cell lung carcinoma were treated with rovalpituzumab tesirine. Only patients with 1% or more tumor cells expressing DLL3 were enrolled. In this study, cut-off points of DLL-3 positive and DLL-3 high were defined as 25% or 75% tumor cells expressing DLL3. The response rate was 13.2% (38/287) and 14.3% (34/238) in DLL3-positive and DLL3-high patients, respectively.

Skipping of exon 2 of both the CDKN2A p14 and p16 isoform transcripts was detected by RT-PCR in a lymphoblastoid cell line derived from a patient carrying the c.151-1G>C variant. The novel CDKN2A splicing variant segregated with disease in a displastic nevous family. The authors state this finding provides further evidence that the disruption of CDKN2A can be predisposing for nervous system tumors, melanomas and displastic nevi.

evidence_statement: Bone marrow mononuclear cells isolated from a chronic myeloid leukemia patient with the BCR-ABL1 fusion and E255K and V299L secondary variants in ABL1 showed a high drug sensitivity score to ponatinib and dasatinib.

This case report describes a 15 year old patient with relapsed B-ALL positive for the RCSD1-ABL1 fusion, who was successfully treated with chemotherapy with addition of imatinib; the patient remained disease free for 36 months. This case supports sensitivity of B-ALL with RCSD1-ABL1 fusions to ABL-type tyrosine kinase inhibitors.

This study illustrates the prevalence of CTNNB1 mutations in sporadic desmoid tumors, and examines whether the presence of CTNNB1 mutations correlates with the disease outcome. CTNNB1 mutations (including specific exon 3 mutations T41A, S45F, S45P, and S45C) were found in 106 out of 145 desmoid tumor specimens, and in 86 out of 115 specimens from patients who had undergone complete surgical resection. At a median follow-up of 31 months, the 5-year recurrence free survival rate of patients with the beta-catenin mutated tumors was worse than that of the patients with wild-type tumors (58% vs 74%), however, the difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.285). Thus, the study shows that there is no statistically significant correlation between the CTNNB1 mutation and the recurrence risk of sporadic desmoid tumors, even though specific exon 3 CTNNB1 mutations are commonly identified in these tumors.

Preclinical experiments with 27 GBM patient-derived cell lines showed selective sensitivity to the PARP inhibitor talazoparib in EGFR amplified samples relative to EGFR wild-type samples (p<0.0001). Functional assays showed that EGFR signaling was required for EGFR-mediated cellular inhibition by talazoparib, and that ROS levels, DNA repair capacity, and PARP trapping are associated with response in EGFR amplified cells. Talazoparib treatment also suppressed tumour growth and induced DNA damage and apoptosis in vivo for two EGFR amplified models, but not for two non-amplified models.

molecular_profile: IKZF1 Deletion AND NOT ERG Deletion AND ( P2RY8::CRLF2 Fusion OR CDKN2A Deletion OR CDKN2B Deletion OR PAX5 Deletion )
evidence_statement: 83 of 991 cases of pediatric B-cell precursor (BCP) acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) were found to have IKZF1 deletion, previously reported as an independent factor associated with a poor prognosis. However, 63 of 991 cases of BCP ALL were found to have co-occurring deletions in CDKN2A, CDKN2B, PAX5, or PAR1 (in the absence of ERG deletion), a so-termed IKZF1 plus group; associated with the worst outcome. This data suggests IKZF1 deletions combined with other specific aberrations define a rare, highly specific very poor prognostic group--IKZF1 plus.

disease: Head And Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma
evidence_statement: A 69 year old patient diagnosed with HNSCC presented with an unresectable neck mass three months after surgery and adjuvant radiation therapy. A biopsy was taken for whole genome and transcriptome analysis and the patient was started on systemic therapy. After showing resistance to the systemic therapy treatment with 5-FU and leucovorin was initiated based on the discovery of a somatic exon 11-19 in frame deletion in DPYD, which was hypothesized to increase sensitivity to 5-FU in the tumour. A dramatic clinical and radiographic response was sustained for 17 weeks, but following a 3 week treatment break a new nodule appeared. This recurrence showed resistance to re-initiation of treatment with capecitabine (oral 5-FU), and analysis of an additional biopsy provided no evidence as to the mechanism of resistance.

Bone marrow specimens from 20/47 patients treated with bortezomib were analyzed. Researchers analyzed CCND1, CCND2, and CCND3 expression using real-time PCR. Results show all patients with CCND1 overexpression (9/20) achieved CR, PR, MR or SD with bortezomib therapy. Significantly better PFS survival was observed in patients with CCND1 overexpression (p=0.0011). There was a trend towards improved OS in patients with CCND1 overexpression, but it did not reach significance (p=0.0836).

A Phase I clinical trial of ribociclib (LEE011) was conducted in patients with advanced solid tumors and lymphomas. 3/132 patients had a partial response per RECIST. Of these three, one had BRAF/NRAS wild-type, CCND1-amplified melanoma, and another had PIK3CA mutant, CCND1-amplified ER+ breast cancer. Further genetic analysis of 53 patients found a higher proportion of those who received ribociclib for greater than 8 weeks had CCND1 alterations (8/29, 28%) versus those who received ribociclib for less than 8 weeks (4/24, 17%). Also, 3/4 patients who received ribociclib for the longest period of time had a CCND1 amplification.

Study observed the effects of ribociclib (LEE011) on anaplastic thyroid cancer (ATC) and papillary thyroid cancer (PTC) cells. qRT-PCR found Cyclin D1 mRNA to have significantly higher expression in ATC and PTC cell lines when compared to normal tissue. Treatment with ribociclib caused decreased cell proliferation, increased apoptosis and cell cycle arrest in ATC cells. ATC mouse xenografts were treated with 100mg/kg of LEE011 once daily for 21 days. Significantly decreased tumor volume and weight was observed in the LEE011 treatment group.
Small molecule inhibitors PHA-533533 and dinaciclib were used to treat CCNE1 amplified ovarian cancer cell lines. Inhibitors decreased pRb and increased apoptosis.

The effect of high CCNE1 expression on PD0332991 (palbociclib) sensitivity was observed in cell lines. One PD0332991 sensitive cell line, HEY, was engineered to constitutively express CCNE1 (HEY-CCNE1). HEY-CCNE1 was shown to have significantly increased resistance to PD0332991. CCNE1-amplified OVCAR3 cells were also resistant to PD0332991. 50-70% reduction of CCNE1 via lentiviral shRNAs sensitized OVCAR3 cells to PD0332991. These combined results suggest high CCNE1 expression is required for resistance to PD0332991.

Case Report of a a 56-year-old female (never-smoker) patient with stage IV NSCLC. NGS revealed a MET–ATXN7L1 fusion. No additional known driver gene alterations were identified. Following progression after three months of chemotherapy [paclitaxel (135 mg/m2 days 1 and 8; carboplatin AUC = 5 day 1)], the patient received crizotinib treatment (250 mg/b.i.d. orally) and exhibited a partial response that lasted for 4 months.

Patients from three (Guatemala, Singapore and Japan) separate cohorts harboring NUDT15 loss of function mutations displayed intolerance to Thiopurine treatment (p=0.021, 2.1e-5, & 0.0054). Patients with mutated alleles displayed increased thiopurine incorporation in their DNA. Stable knockdown of NUDT15 in the B-ALL NALM6 line resulted in greater sensitivity to thiopurines and increased intercellular thiopurine metabolites versus controls. In vitro isolation of recombinant mutant protein determined a decrease the protein's diphosphate activity.

An 82 year old with metastatic NSCLC had disease recurrence 39 months after complete surgical resection. Genomic profiling of the primary resection harbored a MET variant c.3028G>C, as well as a frame-shift in TP53. MET showed a 3 copy gain and IHC score of 3+. The patient was treated with the selective MET inhibitor capmatinib for over 5 months, exhibiting a partial response with 53% tumour reduction.

An 84 year old never-smoker with an upper chest mass was found to have stage 3 histiocytic sarcoma. Genomic profiling discovered a MET exon 14 variant c.2888-5_2944del62, as well as TP53 p.R175H and ZMYM3 c.3008-1G>A. After four months of crizotinib treatment tumour volume had decreased by >60%, however the patient showed progression at 11 months.

MET exon 14 skipping was modelled in vitro by expressing human MET cDNA with exon 14 deletion in HEK293 cells and mouse MET with homologous exon 15 deletion in NIH3T3 cells. NIH3T3 cells expressing MET with exon 15 deletion showed dose dependent inhibition of cell proliferation upon treatment with capmatinib, with significantly lower cell survival compared to control cells. In addition, HEK293 cells expressing MET with exon 14 deletion had increased ERK phosphorylation, while NIH3T3 cells expressing mouse MET with exon 15 deletion had increased MET phosphorylation and increased anchorage-independent colony formation compared to wt MET.

CDK4 was found to be significantly overexpressed in the bone marrow of MLL-rearranged B-ALL patients (n=70) compared to normal bone marrow (n=74, p<.001). Combination treatment with dexamethasone (glucocorticoid) and Ribociclib (a highly selective CDK4 / CDK6 inhibitor) of both glucocorticoid sensitive (Rs4;11 & NALM6) and glucocorticoid resistant (RCH-ACV & SEM) B-ALL cell lines synergistically reduced cell viability of all four lines greater than individual drug exposures. Combination therapy also synergistically reduced the cell viability of 5 primary B-ALL lines derived from diagnosis bone marrow compared to individual treatment. (Note: Expression of CDK4 was not quantitatively measured in the derived and primary B-ALL lines used). Further investigation in RCH-ACV and SEM lines revealed dexamethasone and Ribociclib combined increased apoptosis (annexin-V) and increased G1 arrest along with increased p16 (a CDK4 & CDK6 inhibitor) and decreased phosphorylation of downstream G1 to S cell cycle progression markers compared to single treatments. Combination treatment also led to the increase of NR3C1 expression. Knockdown of CDK4 and CDK6 by siRNAs in RCH-ACV sensitized these cells to dexamethasone treatment and increased NR3C1 expression.

Researchers tested the combination of dinaciclib + cisplatin in ovarian cancer cell lines and xenografts. p53 (-,-) mouse ovarian surface epithelial cells were transformed either by a CCNE1 transgene or a mutant HRAS G12V. Dinaciclib increased sensitivity of CCNE1 transformed cells, but did not change sensitivity in HRAS G12V cells. Xenografts of a human ovarian cancer cell line with CCNE1 amplification, OVCAR3, were established and treated with vehicle, dinaciclib alone, cisplatin alone, and dinaciclib + cisplatin. Combination of 40mg/kg dinaciclib and 2 mg/kg cisplatin once a week over 4 weeks was shown to significantly decrease tumor volume and increase survival time compared to single agent treatment.

In this study twelve GBM cell lines and normal human astrocytes (NHA) were treated with the CDK4/6 inhibitor palbociclib. NHA and several GBM cell lines were resistant to palbociclib with IC50 values greater than 1000 nM, while six of seven proneural subtype GBM lines were highly sensitive (IC50 9-210 nM). Palbociclib treatment induced cell accumulation in G1 phase in 3 sensitive proneural lines, but not in 3 resistant lines. Treatment with vehicle versus oral palbociclib (150 mg/kg/day) was compared in mice with intracranial implantation of proneural GBM stem cell-like G448 cells, which are shown to have higher than normal expression of CDK6. Mice receiving palbociclib had significantly longer survival time (p=0.038).

CDK6 was found to be significantly overexpressed in the bone marrow of B-ALL patients (n=299) compared to normal bone marrow (n=74, p<.001). Combination treatment with dexamethasone (glucocorticoid) and Ribociclib (a highly selective CDK4 / CDK6 inhibitor) of both glucocorticoid sensitive (Rs4;11 & NALM6) and glucocorticoid resistant (RCH-ACV & SEM) B-ALL cell lines synergistically reduced cell viability of all four lines greater than individual drug exposures. Combination therapy synergistically reduced the cell viability of 5 primary B-ALL lines derived from diagnosis bone marrow compared to individual treatment. (Note: Expression of CDK6 was not quantitatively measured in the derived and primary B-ALL lines used). Further investigation in RCH-ACV and SEM revealed dexamethasone and Ribociclib combined increased apoptosis (annexin-V) and increased G1 arrest along with increased p16 (a CDK4 & CDK6 inhibitor) expression and decreased phosphorylation of downstream G1 to S cell cycle progression markers compared to single treatments. Combination treatment also led to the increase of NR3C1 expression. Knockdown of CDK4 and CDK6 by siRNAs in RCH-ACV sensitized these cells to dexamethasone treatment and increased NR3C1 expression.

Study was a Phase 3 clinical trial of erlotinib in non-small cell lung cancer patients who has progressed after standard chemotherapy. Study found significantly increased survival time for patients with polysomy or amplification of EGFR when given erlotinib vs. placebo. (HR 0.44, p=0.008). Response to erlotinib was also higher in patients with polysomy or amplification of EGFR compared to patients without this characteristic (20% vs. 2%).

Study of malignant glioma cells with EGFR amplification, IGRG88. IGRG88 cells showed a 946 fold increase of EGFR mRNA when compared to IGRG119, a tumor known to express low levels of EGFR mRNA. IHC also found expression of EGFR in IGRG88 cells. Thus, IGRG88 cells displayed overexpression of EGFR due to EGFR amplification. IGRG88 mouse xenografts were treated with 100 mg/kg gefitinib for a total of 5 days, 1 Gy for 5 consecutive days, or a combination of both therapies. Both single agent therapies significantly increased tumor growth delay to 19 days (TGD) (p<0.05). Combination of gefitinib and irradiation increased response rate (4/9 PR, 5/9 CR, increased TGD to 33 days and one animal was tumor-free for 120 days).

Two lung cancer cell lines, 11_18 and Ma-24, were found to have significantly increased growth when treated with heregulin (HRG)‐α compared to other growth factors. Pertuzumab was found to significantly decrease the (HRG)‐α dependent growth of these cell lines (p<0.01). Overexpression of HER3 (ERBB3) was detected in both of these cell lines. Pertuzumab was found to decrease HRG‐α‐stimulated HER2/HER3 heterodimer formation in 11_18 cells.

HER2 (ERBB2) overexpressing cell lines were generated by lentiviral transduction of HER2 into three colorectal carcinoma cell lines. HER2 overexpressing cell lines were found to be resistant to cetuximab. Mouse xenografts of a HER2 overexpressing cell line (NCI-H508-HER2) were also found to be resistant to cetuximab.

HER2 (ERBB2) overexpressing cell lines were generated by lentiviral transduction of HER2 into three colorectal carcinoma cell lines. Mouse xenografts of NCI-H508-HER2 cells were treated with single agent lapatinib, trastuzumab, and combination of trastuzumab and lapatinib. Combination of lapatinib and trastuzumab was significantly more effective than either single agent therapy (p=0.0224) and caused tumor shrinkage; trastuzumab monotherapy was ineffective and lapatinib monotherapy caused delay in tumor growth. These results were seen in soft-agar assays as well.

Afatinib monotherapy was tested in patient-derived colorectal cancer (M051) mouse xenografts and gastric cancer cell-line (NCI-N87) mouse xenografts. Tumor shrinkage was observed and tumor volume was significantly decreased compared to treatment with vehicle or lapatinib monotherapy (p<0.0001 (M051 Afatinib vs. Lapatinib) and p=0.0003 (NCI-N87 Afatinib vs. Lapatinib).

Afatinib monotherapy was tested in patient-derived colorectal cancer (M051) mouse xenografts and gastric cancer cell-line (NCI-N87) mouse xenografts. Tumor shrinkage was observed and tumor volume was significantly decreased compared to treatment with vehicle or lapatinib monotherapy (p<0.0001 (M051 Afatinib vs. Lapatinib) and p=0.0003 (NCI-N87 Afatinib vs. Lapatinib).

In phase I NAVIGATOR trial (NCT02508532) took part 43 patients with GIST harboring a PDGFRA exon 18 mutation, including 38 patients with PDGFRA D842V mutation.For patients harboring a PDGFRA exon 18 mutation, the overall response rate was 84%, with 7% having a complete response and 77% having a partial response. For the subgroup of patients with PDGFRA D842V mutations, the overall response rate was 89%, with 8% having a complete response and 82% having a partial response.

In this phase II trial, patients with metastatic platinum-refractory urothelial carcinoma (UC) received afatinib (40 mg/day). Among the 21 tumors, five of six patients (83.3%) with ERBB2 (HER2) and/or ERBB3 alterations achieved 3-month progression-free survival (PFS3) versus none of 15 patients without alterations (P < .001). Three of the four patients with HER2 amplification achieved PFS3. Patients with HER2 and/or ERBB3 alterations has median time to progression/discontinuation of 6.6 months vs. 1.4 months in patients without alterations (P < .001).

Patient diagnosed with metastatic squamous cell lung cancer had high-level amplification of FGFR1 and high expression of MYC. Patient was treated with 400 mg pazopanib twice a day. CT taken four and eight weeks after start of pazopanib showed tumor regression and cavitation. Due to side effects, patient stopped taking pazopanib after 6 months. No clinical or radiologic signs of tumor progression were present at that time.

71 Childhood B-cell acute lymphocytic leukemia relapse patients had their diagnosis and relapse samples sequenced for NT5C2 mutations. Sequencing revealed an early relapse case with NT5C2 R367Q enriched to a variant allele frequency (VAF) of 25% at relapse and only a VAF of .02% at diagnosis. R367Q could drive clonal outgrowth through the promotion of drug resistance, specifically to thiopurines, which are a staple of ALL maintenance therapy that are administered daily.

Lentiviral-mediated overexpression of NT5C2 R238W in Reh cells resulted in significant resistance against thiopurines (mercaptopurine and thioguanine) versus wildtype and GFP controls, as indicated by reduced apoptosis. Compared to controls, overexpression cells also displayed reduced intercellular thioguanoside nucleotides after 24 hours of drug exposure, as measured by HPLC. Additionally, recombinant protein expression of R238W led to increased 5’ nucleotidase activity.

Lentiviral-mediated overexpression of NT5C2 S445F in Reh cells resulted in significant resistance against thiopurines (mercaptopurine and thioguanine) versus wildtype and GFP controls, as indicated by reduced apoptosis. Compared to controls, overexpression cells also displayed reduced intercellular thioguanoside nucleotides after 24 hours of drug exposure, as measured by HPLC. Additionally, recombinant protein expression of S445F led to increased 5’ nucleotidase activity.

Lentiviral mediated overexpression of NT5C2 R367Q in Reh cells resulted in no change in apoptosis after exposure to cytarabine, gemcitabine, doxorubicin, or prednisolone compared to wildtype NT5C2 overexpression and GFP control lines.
Overexpression of NT5C2 R238W in Reh cells resulted in no change in response to cytarabine, gemcitabine, doxorubicin or prednisolone versus wildtype or GFP controls as indicated by similar apoptosis.
Overexpression of NT5C2 S445F in Reh cells resulted in no change in response to cytarabine, gemcitabine, doxorubicin or prednisolone versus wildtype or GFP controls as indicated by similar apoptosis.

Within a cohort of 71 pediatric B-ALL relapse cases, all 7 patients with NT5C2 mutations detected at relapse demonstrated early relapse (<36 months from initial diagnosis) with a median time to relapse of 516 days versus a 930-day median time to relapse for the 64 patients wild type for NT5C2 (p=.03). Patients were derived from the Children's Oncology Group (COG), but Individual patient treatment regimens were not given.

Patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models derived from patients with either MLL-r acute myeloid leukemia or MLL-r acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) showed dramatic reductions of leukemia burden when treated with VTP50469, an orally available small molecule inhibitor targeting the Menin- MLL interaction. There was a significant improvement in survival in these PDX models of MLL-rearranged leukemia

One chronic myeloid leukemia patient in chronic phase had a partial best cytogenetic response to imatinib but became resistant. Bacterial clones generated using peripheral blood RNA revealed the BCR-ABL1 fusion with the D363G secondary variant in 2/10 clones.

One chronic myeloid leukemia patient in chronic phase had a complete best cytogenetic response to imatinib but became resistant. Bacterial clones generated using peripheral blood RNA later revealed the BCR-ABL1 fusion with the E98G secondary variant in 11/11 clones.

Prior to dasatinib treatment, one imatinib-resistant patient with chronic myeloid leukemia in chronic phase had the BCR-ABL1 fusion with H396R and E355G variants in 9/11 and 1/11 clones, respectively. Clones were generated using peripheral blood RNA. The patient had no best cytogenetic and complete best hematologic responses to dasatinib which were comparable to responses in patients with unmutated BCR-ABL1.

One chronic myeloid leukemia patient in chronic phase with the BCR-ABL1 fusion and the F486S secondary variant in 2/11 clones had partial best cytogenetic response to imatinib before becoming completely resistant.

One chronic myeloid leukemia patient in chronic phase had no response to imatinib. Bacterial clones generated using peripheral blood RNA later revealed the BCR-ABL1 fusion with the M244V secondary variant in 12/12 clones.

One chronic myeloid leukemia patient in chronic phase had no response to imatinib. Bacterial clones generated using peripheral blood RNA later showed the BCR-ABL1 fusion with the L364I secondary variant in 9/12 clones.

Three patients with chronic myeloid leukemia in chronic phase with the BCR-ABL1 fusion and the M351T secondary variant in 4/10, 10/10, and 11/11 clones had none, partial, and partial best cytogenetic responses, respectively, to imatinib before becoming completely resistant.

Rogaratinib (BAY 1163877) treatment was tested in vivo in a cell line-derived model of NCI‐H716 human colon cancer. This model has FGFR2 amplifications and highly elevated FGFR2 mRNA. Mice were treated with a twice daily regimen of 35, 50 or 65 mg/kg. Tumor volume was significantly decreased for all three treatment options compared to control (35mg/kg p < 0.01, 50 & 65,g/kg p < 0.001). Partial response was observed in 1/8 mice treated with 50 mg/kg dose and 5/8 mice treated with 65 mg/kg dose.

Rogaratinib (BAY 1163877) was tested in cell line- and patient-derived models of lung cancer. DMS‐114 models, which have FGFR1 amplification and overexpression, had significantly decreased tumor volume and weight when treated with single agent rogaratinib (p < 0.01) or docetaxel (p < 0.001). Combination therapy of rogaratinib and docetaxel increased partial response rate from 40% to 70% and one complete response was observed. Rogaratinib addition to carboplatin/paclitaxel therapy was also able to increase PR rate from 30% to 70%. These results were further verified in PDX models of LU299 and LXFL1121, which overexpress FGFR1 without high FGFR1 amplification. Rogaratinib or docetaxel decreased tumor volume (p < 0.001) and combination therapy was found to be significantly better than single agent docetaxel (p < 0.05). Combination therapy also improved PR rate from 30% to 70% and 3 CRs (30%) were observed. Duration of response was also significantly improved for the combination therapy when observing tumor volume 50 days post treatment (p < 0.01).

Study compares JNJ-42756493 (erdafitinib) treatment of colorectal cancer cell lines with and without FGFR2 overexpression. Overexpression determined by fold increase of FGFR2 mRNA compared to HPRT. NCI-H716 cells had 48 fold increase while Caco2 cells only had a 4 fold increase. Inhibition of NCI-H716 cells was achieved at 0.5 nM while inhibition of Caco2 cells was achieved at 5000 nM. Significantly increased apoptosis and decreased proliferation was seen in NCI-H716 cells 72 hours post treatment (p < 0.05) while no difference was observed in Caco2 cells. NCI-H716 xenografts treated with JNJ-42756493 had decreased tumor volume compared to control (p < 0.05). However, when treatment was stopped, relative tumor volume increased in the treatment group (129.4% experimental group vs. 31.1% control group, p < 0.05).

disease: Head And Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma
evidence_statement: FGFR2 p.P253R mutation detected in patient with head and neck SCC. Mutation initially detected by RNA-Seq and confirmed by Sanger sequencing. Patient is 52 y/o male with initial diagnosis of SCC of right tongue in 2008. Recurrences treated with surgery, radiotherapy and chemotherapy including carboplatin, paclitaxel, cisplatin, and cetuximab. In 2012, progression was detected in right neck and left axilla. Patient was treated with 800 mg of pazopanib daily. At 12 day follow up patient had marked reduction in tumor size. Patient continued treatment for 2 months until he presented with right carotid hemorrhage. Last follow up shows patient is alive 11 months after beginning pazopanib treatment.

Case study of a 74 year-old female with pulmonary metastases of urothelial carcinoma. Patient did not respond to carboplatin/gemcitabine or other second- and third-line therapies including MELK inhibitor OTS167. Patient was started on pazopanib and after 3 months achieved a partial response per RECIST. Patient has sustained partial response on pazopanib for 9 months and then experienced enlargement of retroperitoneal nodes followed by systemic disease progression.

Clinical trial of soft tissue sarcoma patients found no responses to pazopanib + trametinib combination in Ewing sarcoma patients. Comparison was done to previously treated Ewing sarcoma that responded to pazopanib. Amplification of FGFR3 (8.3), FGFR4 (5.2), and FLT4 (4.8) was identified in the responder and not in the non-responder (FGFR3 2.6, FGFR4 2.8, FLT4 2.6).

Clinical trial of soft tissue sarcoma patients found no responses to pazopanib + trametinib combination in Ewing sarcoma patients. Comparison was done to previously treated Ewing sarcoma that responded to pazopanib. Amplification of FGFR3 (8.3), FGFR4 (5.2), and FLT4 (4.8) was identified in the responder and not in the non-responder (FGFR3 2.6, FGFR4 2.8, FLT4 2.6).

Trop2 (TACSTD2) levels were evaluated from 234 patients who underwent radical prostatectomy. These levels were found to be significantly correlated with recurrence (P=0.01), with 58 patients displaying recurrence by 9 year follow-up. There was also a significant difference (P=0.02) in Trop2 levels between patients with (n=204) or without (n=18) metastasis, with higher levels being associated with the occurrence of lymph and bone metastases. Preclinical experiments showed that deletion of Trop2 decreased cell growth, migration, invasion, and metastatic colonization while over-expression enhanced tumour growth, plasticity, and metastasis. This evidence points to Trop2 expression being associated with worse outcome as metastatic prostate cancer is invariably lethal.

In an in vitro study, six CML cell lines expressing the BCR-ABL1 fusion protein showed sensitivity to nilotinib (IC50: 24.3-84.5 nM), dasatinib (IC50: 1.5-10.9 nM), and bafetinib (IC50: 11.8-87.7 nM). When comparing potency of these treatments against the 6 CML cell lines, dasatinib, nilotinib and bafetinib were on average 98.6, 9.85 and 16.4 times more potent than imatinib. Sensitivity was determined by assessing cell proliferation using the MTT assay.

In an in vitro study, a Ba/F3 cell line stably expressing the F317L mutation in the ABL1 portion of the BCR-ABL1 fusion protein was associated with resistance to imatinib and dasatinib treatment (IC50: > 2000.0 nM) as compared to wild-type BCR-ABL1 expressing Ba/F3 cells (IC50: 1712 nM and 87.6 nM). Sensitivity was determined by assessing cell proliferation using the MTT assay.

In a phase 2 trial, patients with NSCLC harboring MET alterations were treated with crizotinib. MET alterations were kinase domain activating mutations included V1110L, H1112L, H1112Y, H1124D, M1149T, T1191I, V1206L, L1213V, V1238I, M1268T, P1009S, T1010I, R988C, V941L but excluding Y1248C, Y1248H, Y1248D, Y1253D. Sixty-nine patients were treated and 65 patients were tumor-response evaluable. The objective response rate was 32%. The response was observed independent of the MET exon 14 alteration splice site or mutation type (base substitution or indel).

In an in vitro study, a Ba/F3 cell line stably expressing the M351T mutation in the ABL1 portion of the BCR-ABL1 fusion protein was associated with resistance to imatinib treatment (IC50: >2000.0 nM) as compared to wild-type BCR-ABL1 expressing Ba/F3 cells (IC50: 1712 nM). Sensitivity was determined by assessing cell proliferation using the MTT assay.

In an in vitro study, a Ba/F3 cell line stably expressing the dasatinib-resistance variant T315A in the ABL1 portion of the BCR-ABL1 fusion protein was associated with similar sensitivity to nilotinib and bafetinib (INNO-406) treatment (IC50: 949.2 nM, 422.5 nM) as compared to wild-type BCR-ABL1 expressing Ba/F3 cells (IC50: 642.3 nM and 152.9 nM). Sensitivity was determined by assessing cell proliferation using the MTT assay.

In an in vitro study, a Ba/F3 cell line stably expressing the dasatinib-resistance variant F317V in the ABL1 portion of the BCR-ABL1 fusion protein was associated with similar sensitivity to imatinib, nilotinib and bafetinib (INNO-406) treatment (IC50: 1053.7, 286.9 nM, 284 nM) as compared to wild-type BCR-ABL1 expressing Ba/F3 cells (IC50: 1712 nM, 642.3 nM, and 152.9 nM). Sensitivity was determined by assessing cell proliferation using the MTT assay.

In an in vitro study, a Ba/F3 cell line stably expressing T315A in the ABL1 portion of the BCR-ABL1 fusion protein was associated with resistance to imatinib and dasatinib treatment (IC50: >2000.0 nM) as compared to wild-type BCR-ABL1 expressing Ba/F3 cells (IC50: 1712 nM and 87.6 nM). Sensitivity was determined by assessing cell proliferation. The authors examined X-ray crystal structure of dasatinib/ABL to determine why dasatinib was ineffective against mutations at amino acid 315, and found that T315A causes decreased steric and hydrogen-bonding interactions with dasatinib.

Sensitivity was determined by assessing cell proliferation using the MTT assay.

Sensitivity was determined by assessing cell proliferation using the MTT assay.

Two human esophageal squamous cell carcinoma cell lines, KYSE170 and TE13, were transfected with the IL6 gene. These cell lines produced 5-6 fold (KYSE170) and 16-17 fold (TE13) IL6 compared to control transfected cells. Both cell lines had reduced sensitivity to cisplatin at 0.1 μg/ml and 1.0 μg/ml. siRNA inhibition of IL6 helped restored sensitivity of IL6 overexpressing cells to cisplatin.

Sequencing of an 8-year old patient diagnosed with a left tentorial-based CNS sarcoma discovered an EWSR1-ATF fusion and IL6 and JAK1 overexpression. Patient was treated with ruxolitinib based on overexpression of JAK1. Stable disease per RECIST and improvement of Lansky score from 60 to 90-100 was observed for 5 months. After ruxolitinib discontinuation, the patient's symptoms worsened and lung lesions progressed. Ruxolitinib was started again per family request and patient again had stable disease and improvement in body weight and Lansky score. Dose reduction was required because of myelosuppression and patient death occurred 23 months after relapse.

In an in vitro study, a Ba/F3 cell line stably expressing the G250E mutation in the ABL1 portion of the BCR-ABL1 fusion protein was associated with resistance to imatinib and bafetinib (INNO-406) treatment (IC50: > 2000.0 nM and 852 nM) as compared to wild-type BCR-ABL1 expressing Ba/F3 cells (IC50: 1712 nM and 152.9 nM). Sensitivity was determined by assessing cell proliferation using the MTT assay.

Phase 2 study of pazopanib in pretreated advanced neuroendocrine tumors. Study found that patients with immunoexpression of VEGFR2 (KDR) above the median had longer PFS (12.6 months vs 9.1 months, P=0.067). This was statistically significant when looking at patients who were not previously treated with an antiangiogenic therapy (20.1 months vs 9.1 months, P=0.028)

In a phase II basket trial (NCI-MATCH), patients with solid tumors or hematologic malignancies harboring BRAF non-V600 mutations were treated with trametinib. Among 50 patients assigned, 32 were eligible and received therapy with trametinib. Most common tumor histopathologic subtypes were GI cancers (n=8, of which 7 were colorectal adenocarcinoma), lung adenocarcinoma (n=9), prostate adenocarcinoma (n=4), gynecologic cancer (n=4), BRAF alterations included BRAF fusion (n=1), G464 (n=2), G466 (n=4), G469 (n=7), N581 (n=3), D594 (n=11), L597 (n=2) and K601 (n=1). Of the 32 patients evaluable for efficacy endpoints, the response rate was 3% (3/32). The patient with a partial response had invasive breast cancer with a BRAF G469E mutation. The median PFS was 1.8 months and the median OS was 5.7 months.

In NCI-MATCH, patients with advanced solid tumors other than breast and gastro-esophageal tumors harboring ERBB2 amplification were treated with ad-trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1). ERBB2 amplification was defined as a copy number > 7 based on targeted NGS. Among enrolled patients, 3 had salivary gland cancers. Two of 3 patients showed partial response.

In a multicenter phase II trial in Korea, patients with NSCLC harboring EGFR mutations other than the exon 19 deletion, L858R, T790M, and exon 20 insertion were treated with osimertinib. Patients who were previously treated with other EGFR inhibitors were excluded. Thirty-seven patients were enrolled. Among patients, 61% received osimertinib as first-line therapy. The mutations were G719X (n=19), L861Q (n=9), S768I (n=8) and others (n=4). The objective response rate was 50% (18/36). Median progression-free survival was 8.2 months and median overall survival was not reached. The median duration of response was 11.2 months.

Lentiviral-mediated overexpression of NT5C2 R367Q in Reh cells resulted in significant resistance against thiopurines (mercaptopurine and thioguanine) versus wildtype and GFP controls, as indicated by reduced apoptosis. Compared to controls, overexpression cells also displayed reduced intercellular thioguanoside nucleotides after 24 hours of drug exposure, as measured by HPLC. Additionally, recombinant protein expression of R367Q led to increased 5’ nucleotidase activity.

71 Childhood B-cell acute lymphocytic leukemia relapse patients had their diagnosis and relapse samples sequenced for NT5C2 mutations. Sequencing revealed 3 early relapse cases with NT5C2 R238W enriched at relapse at variant allele frequencies (VAF) of 27%, 18%, and 31% and only a VAF of .01%, 0%, and 0% at diagnosis. R238W could drive clonal outgrowth through the promotion of drug resistance, specifically to thiopurines, which are a staple of ALL maintenance therapy that are administered daily.

Treatment of crizotinib resistant patients harboring ALK L1196M by ensartinib resulted in an objective response rate of 25% and disease control rate of 91% in a multicentre phase II clinical trial.

Two patients with IDH wild-type, MGMT promoter unmethylated glioblastoma were treated with crizotinib. Patient 1 had weak expression of ALK in 25% of tumor tissue and polysomy of ALK in 53% of nuclei; weak and moderate expression of MET detected in 70 and 20% of tumor cells and low amplification detected in 36% of nuclei. Patient 2 showed no expression of ALK; moderate and strong expression of MET detected in 20 and 80% of tumor cells and high amplification detected in 70% of nuclei. Neither patient had ROS1 expression or copy gain. Patient 1 had stable disease and significant clinical improvement on crizotinib. Patient 2 had disease progression after 4 months on treatment. The main difference between the two patients was ALK expression and likely explains the different response to crizotinib.

Researchers compared biomarkers in breast cancer stem cell (BCSC) enriched and mature cancer cell populations from human breast cancer cell lines. Overexpression of PARP1 was found in BCSC enriched populations (detected by ALDH+) when compared to mature cell populations (ALDH-) in 4 BRCA1 mutant and 1 BRCA1 wild-type cell lines. Cell lines were treated with 10 µm olaparib. The cell line with the highest PARP1 expression (HCC1937) showed a significant increase cell population after treatment (p=0.01). PARP1 overexpression was found to be positively correlated with olaparib resistance (R²=0.9374).

Study of combination of trabectedin + olaparib in sarcoma cell lines and xenograft models. Initial results found combination therapy significantly reduced colony growth (p<0.001) in high-PARP1-expressing cells while no significant reduction was observed in low-PARP1-expressing cells. Xenograft model of a high PARP1 uterine leiomyosarcoma found trabectedin + olaparib significantly reduced tumor growth and halted the spread of metastasis (p<0.001 vs. single agents and control). In comparison, the xenograft model of low PARP1 osteosarcoma found the combination had a non-significant benefit compared to trabectedin alone. Finally, silencing of PARP1 reduced sensitivity to combination therapy while lentiviral overexpression of PARP1 increased sensitivity to combination therapy.

EML4-ALK fusion positive lung adenocarcinoma cell lines (H3122 and the newly established JFCR013-2) with high expression of P-gp (ABCB1 gene) were found to be resistant to crizotinib and ceritinib. P-gp knockdown via shRNA increased the sensitivity of H3122 cells to crizotinib and ceritinib. A cell line developed to overexpress P-gp had increased resistance to crizotinib and ceritinib.
A novel compound identified in a high-throughput screen is highly selective for KIT V559D in cell lines and mice models. In mice, there was a dose-dependent reduction in tumor size.

Sequencing revealed relapse specific PRPS1 mutations in 24/358 (6.7%) relapsed childhood B-ALL cases derived from multiple cohorts. In the Chinese cohort, 18/138 (13%) cases harbored relapse specific PRPS1 mutations. In the German cohort, 6/220 (6.7%) cases harbored relapse specific PRPS1 mutations. All patients with PRPS1 mutations relapsed early (< 36 months after initial diagnosis) (Chinese: 18/18 PRPS1 vs. 77/120 (64.2%) wildtype, p=.002; German: 6/6 PRPS1 vs. 79/214 (36.9%) wildtype, p<.001). All patients with PRPS1 mutations also relapsed while on therapy (Chinese: 18/18 PRPS1 vs. 77/120 (64.2%) wildtype, p<.001; German: 6/6 PRPS1 vs. 51/214 (23.8%) ( p<.001). Of the 24 cases, there were 17 unique PRPS1 mutations. Further experimental data demonstrated 12/17 mutations conferred resistance to thiopurines.

National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) guidelines recommend alectinib for advanced ALK-positive NSCLC who are previously untreated or previously treated with crizotinib, including those with brain metastases.

Cabozantinib's effect on cell proliferation was studied in a variety of cell lines. In two gastric adenocarcinoma cell lines with MET amplification (SNU-5 and Hs746T) were the most sensitive to cabozantinib (IC50 = 19 and 9.9 nmol/L, respectively). Other cell lines (SNU-1 and SNU-16) lacking MET amplification were more resistant to cabozantinib (IC50 = 5,223 and 1,149 nmol/L, respectively).

The BCR-ABL1 expressing imatinib-resistant cell line MYL-R overexpresses LYN, an SRC family kinase. Dasatinib showed the most potency against MYL-R compared to the non-resistant MYL cell line (IC50: 6.4nM vs. 6.5 nM), while bafetinib (INNO-406) showed 3.1 times more potency than nilotinib against MYL-R (IC50: 324.1 nM vs. 993.6 nM) as compared to MYL (IC50: 87.7 nM and 84.5 nM). The authors state that this is in line with experiments showing INNO-406 specifically inhibits LYN and LCK, which may provide a more favorable side effect profile than dasatinib, that was shown to strongly inhibit all 8 SRC family kinases.

Lentiviral-mediated overexpression of D183H in Reh cells resulted in significant resistance against mercaptopurine (6-MP) and thioguanine (6-TG) as indicated by IC50 increases and reduced apoptosis compared to multiple controls (empty vector and overexpression of wildtype or known reduced-function PRPS1 mutants). 6-MP cytotoxicity results were confirmed using Jurkat cells. The enhanced production of hypoxanthine likely leads to reduced conversion of thiopurines to their active form due to competitive inhibition.

A190T results in the activation of the de novo purine synthesis pathway by reducing feedback inhibition, allowing the cell to continue to create nucleotides even when concentrations are elevated. This overactivation creates increased hypoxanthine levels, which likely competitively inhibits the conversion of the thiopurines to their active form.

To find authentic targets regulated by EWSR1-WT1 fusion protein in desmoplastic small round-cell tumor (DSRT), a primitive tumor characterized by t(11;22)(p13;q12) chromosomal translocation, the authors generated cell lines with inducible expression of EWSR1-WT1 fusion protein and found in experiments that the expression of fusion protein up-regulated the expression of endogenous platelet-derived growth factor-A (PDGFA), while native PDGFA was not regulated by wild-type WT1. Primary tumor tissues of DSRT were also used to verify the association of EWSR1-WT1 fusion with PDGFA expression. It was concluded that the EWSR1-WT1 fusion in DSRT induces the expression of PDGFA, contributing to the characteristics of this tumor.

The authors analyzed 52 hepatoblastoma (HB) biopsies and three HB cell lines from sporadic HBs and found 48% of them bearing mutations on beta-catenin exon 3, which encodes the degradation targeting box of beta-catenin. The mutation leads to accumulation of intracytoplasmic and nuclear beta-catenin protein.

Phase 2 clinical trial tested crizotinib in clear-cell sarcoma (CCSA) patients. Patients were grouped by presence (MET+) or absence (MET-) of the EWSR1 rearrangement. Objective PR observed in 1/26 MET+ patients (3.8% ORR) and SD observed in 17/26 MET+ patients. No responses observed in the 2 MET- patients; one had SD followed by PD and the other had PD. Median PFS of 4.4 months observed in MET+ patients.

Transcriptome sequencing found ovarian clear cell carcinoma (CCC) tissue has 2.2-fold increased expression of MET compared to high-grade serous carcinoma (HGSC) cells. The effects of cabozantinib were studied in the CCC cell line with the highest MET expression, RMG-I. In vitro experiments found significantly reduced tumor volume at day 15 in mice treated with 3mg/kg, 10mg/kg, or 30mg/kg cabozantinib (p<0.01).

A phase 2 clinical trial studied the efficacy of Crizotinib in East Asian NSCLC patients positive for ROS1 rearrangements (detected by RT-PCR AmoyDx assay) and negative for ALK1 rearrangements. Of the 127 patients enrolled, 17 achieved complete response and 74 achieved partial response. Overall response rate by independent radiology review was 71.7% (95% CI 63-79.3%) Time to response was rapid (median 1.9 months) and durable (Duration of response median 19.7 months). Median progression free survival was 15.9 months. Crizotinib was clinically beneficial regardless of demographics and prior therapy. Based on these results, Crizotinib was approved for the treatment of ROS1 positive NSCLC in 2017 in Japan, Taiwan, China, and Korea.

Tumor cell line generated from pediatric high-grade glioma patient was found to have amplification of PDGFRA and FGF2. Gene expression of PDGFRA and FGF2 was found to be in the 99th percentile compared to all other cancers in their compendium. The most effective of cell growth was dasatinib. Dasatinib treatment in a PDGFRA non-amplified cell line was not as effective. Proliferation was reduced by addition of siPDGFRA but not siFGF2, suggesting overexpression of PDGFRA was driving tumor cell growth.

NIH3T3 cells were transfected with control or KRAS R164Q plasmid and focus formation assays were performed. R164Q cells formed 0 foci > 5mm diameter per well, which was the same as wt cells. In contrast, known gain of function mutations KRAS G12V and G12D formed over 70 foci > 5mm diameter average per well. In conclusion, these data suggest that R164Q does not promote oncogenic transformation of NIH3T3 cells by loss of contact inhibition, and gives support for ClinGen/CGC/VICC Oncogenicity Code SBS2.

NIH3T3 cells were transfected with control or KRAS Q61H plasmid and focus formation assays were performed. Q61H cells formed approximately 50 foci > 5mm diameter per well, where wt cells formed none, demonstrating Q61H promotes loss of contact inhibition suggestive of oncogenic transformation of NIH3T3 cells. This evidence provides support for the OS2 ClinGen/CGC/VICC evidence code for in vitro functional assays suggesting variant oncogenicity.

NIH-3T3 cells with the FGFR2 W290C extracellular domain mutation demonstrated an increase in colony formation in an anchorage independent growth assay, which was lost with the introduction of AP24534, BGJ398, or pazopanib. Xenograft assays showed similar results for FGFR2 W290C leading to increased tumor growth compared to wild-type. A crosslinking assay demonstrates that this mutation forms disulfide crosslinks under reducing conditions.

Xenograft assays showed similar results with all transforming FGFR2 mutations leading to increased tumor growth compared to wild-type. A crosslinking assay demonstrates that this mutation forms disulfide crosslinks under reducing conditions.

NIH-3T3 cells with the FGFR2 K660E kinase domain mutation demonstrated an increase in colony formation relative to wild-type in an anchorage-independence assay, which was lost with the introduction of AP24534 and BGJ398. Xenograft assays showed similar results with all transforming FGFR2 mutations leading to increased tumor growth compared to wild-type.

Xenograft assays showed similar results with all transforming FGFR3 mutations leading to increased tumor growth compared to wild-type.

Xenograft assays showed similar results with all transforming FGFR3 mutations leading to increased tumor growth compared to wild-type.

Prior to dasatinib treatment, one imatinib-resistant patient with chronic myeloid leukemia in chronic phase had the BCR-ABL1 fusion with E450Q/M351T and E450Q variants in 1/10 and 9/10 clones, respectively. Clones were generated using peripheral blood RNA. The patient had complete best cytogenetic and complete best hematologic responses to dasatinib which were improved compared to responses in patients with unmutated BCR-ABL1.
