Cyclin-dependent kinase 9 (CDK9) was predominantly overexpressed in esophageal carcinoma tumor samples compared to normal esophageal cell lines. This high expression was also found in 90% of invasive adenocarcinoma cells. To investigate the potential effects of downregulating CDK9, SKGTA esophageal carcinoma cell line overexpressing CDK9 was downregulated CDK9 expression by transducing a lentivirus carrying shCDK9. This induced apoptosis p (< 0.05), G1 arrest p(< 0.01), as well as reduced proliferation p(< 0.01) in comparison to the control SKGT4 cells. All three cell lines overexpressing CDK9 (FLO-1, SKGTA, and OE33) showed a decrease in proliferation in a dose-dependent manner in response to flavopiridol in comparison to the untreated controls. However, only FLO-1 showed decreased cellular proliferation in response both to 20 μm of CAN508(p <0.05), and 0.4 μm Flavopiridol. Mouse models injected with FLO-1 and independently treated with Flavoripol or CAN508 demonstrated a 50% reduction of tumor growth with CAN508 (p<0.001) and a 63.1% reduction with Flavopiridol (p<0.001) in comparison to controls. Considering all data, the potential use of CDK9 inhibitors in CDK9 overexpressing adenocarcinoma tissue may demonstrate similar inhibitory effects.

This preclinical study elucidated the potential varying efficaciousness of cyclin dependent Kinase inhibitor (CDK) dinaciclib. When forcing overexpression of differing CDKs (CDK1 and 9). Overall Hepatocellular Carcinoma (HCC) cell lines, without manipulation of siRNA or forced CDK overexpression, dinaciclib demonstrated significant potent activity as there was a decrease in proliferation and increased cell cycle arrest in the G2/M phase. Furthermore, the in vivo effects of dinaciclib presented slower tumor growth when treated with 20 or 40 mg/Kg 3 times per week; this was done in comparison to the vehicle treated mice. In determining the possible correlation of efficacy of dinaciclib and overexpression of CDKs, cell lines with transfected vectors overexpressing CDK1 or CDK9 were treated with dinaciclib. It was found that those HCC cells transfected with overexpressing CDK9 demonstrated reduced colony formation inhibition by dinaciclib in comparison to CDK1.

Within a preclinical study, the efficacy of Dinaciclib and ABT-199 in MYC-BCL2 double expressing lymphoma (DLBCL) was investigated through mouse models and DLBCL cell lines. Overexpressing DLBCL BCL2 cell lines (SU-DHL-4 and TMD8 cells) indicated resistance to the cyclin dependent inhibitor dinaciclib, with an increased IC50 (p=0.0068); increased expression of MCL1 did not exhibit the same effects. However this resistance was overcome by the synergistic effects demonstrated through the SCID mouse model with a combination of both dinaciclib and a BCL1 inhibitor ABT-199. Combination of ABT199/dinaciclib (n=80) displayed a substantial improved survival rate (p<0.0001) in comparison to the tumor-bearing mice with an IP vehicle present with either ABT-199 or dinaciclib. These results indicate the potential synergistic effects of targeting both BCL2 and MCL2 expression.

To understand the role of TCF19 expression in NRAS-mutant melanoma, an analysis of a TCGA cutaneous melanoma data set showed that patient survival was inversely correlated with levels of BRD4 and TCF19. Although this was not significant, when looking at NRAS‐mutant melanoma cells with high TCF19 and BRD4 protein levels, there was a positive correlation with an increased sensitivity to BETi (P = 0.023).With combined BETi/MEKi (OTX‐015/PD901) TCF19 was synergistically downregulated resulting in the apoptosis of therapy-resistant tumor cells. Significantly, TCF19 appears to be essential to NRAS-mutant melanoma as depletion of TCF19 through shRNA leads to an increased cell death. From analyzing TCF19 mRNA levels were upregulated in 82% of progression biopsies from non-responders and downregulated in 93% post-treatment biopsies from responders (P=0.001).

BET inhibitor JQ-1 induced a decrease in viability to NRAS mutant melanoma cells with an increase in sensitivity in those highly expressing BRD4 in comparison to BRD2 and BRD3 expression (P = 0.018); conversely low expression of BRD4 indicated a decrease in sensitivity. Further validation of BRD4 being a potential therapeutic target was found through data analysis of the TCGA skin cutaneous melanoma dataset as BRD4 mRNA correlated with poor patient survival (p=0.001) and disease-free survival (p=0.0008) in NRAS-mutant melanoma patients. Confirming BRD4 as a potential drug target, siRNA depletion of BRD4 decreased the overall viability of NRAS mutant melanoma cells and induced apoptosis adequately. This data suggests BET family member BRD4 is essential for proliferation in melanoma cell lines and can be attenuated with BET inhibitors.

Predominantly high-level expression of BRD4 was found in the majority of medulloblastoma cell lines examined (HD-MB3, ONS-76, UW-228, D-341, and D-283); the exception being the Daoy cell line exhibiting lower expression of BRD4 (Daoy cell line also possesses a TP53 mutation). Additionally, 99 of 115 pediatric primary medulloblastomas demonstrated high expression of BRD4 in comparison to normal cerebellar tissue with diminutive expression of BRD4. In assessing the potentiality of JQ1 in medulloblastoma cell lines, JQ1 concentrations between 78nM and >1μM showed a profound decrease in cell viability and proliferation except for the low BRD4 expressing Daoy cell line. To examine the functionality of BRD4, a knockdown in transfected HD-MB3 cells demonstrated similar effects to non-transfected HD-MB3 cells treated JQ1 as attenuated MYC expression and decreased cell viability was observed. Furthermore, the effects of JQ1 in vivo with cell line HD-MB3 showed a significant increase in survival in the treated group (7 mice once a day at 50 mg/kg) compared to the non-treated group (p=0.0019).

Missense mutations in the Kelch domains of LTZR1 were tested for their RAS-binding ability. A co-immunoprecipitation assay showed that G248R caused reduced binding with RAS, suggesting a loss of RAS ubiquitination by the LTZR1-CUL3 complex.
The CDKN2A E88K mutation, located in the CDK-binding interface, was found to cause near complete loss of binding to CDK4 and CDK6 as measured by an in vitro association assay.

Analysis of several CDKN2A variants was performed to discover their functional impact. An in vitro binding assay found that CDKN2A D84Y resulted in complete loss of binding to CDK4 and CDK6. Protein structure modeling showed that residue D84 is part of the predicted CDK-binding interface and the authors suggest that replacing the negatively-charged amino acid is likely to drastically alter the electrostatic character of the binding surface.

Protein structure modeling showed that residue D84 is part of the predicted CDK-binding interface and the authors suggest that replacing the negatively-charged amino acid is likely to drastically alter the electrostatic character of the binding surface.

Analysis of several CDKN2A variants was performed to discover their functional impact. An in vitro binding assay found that CDKN2A L16P resulted in decreased binding to CDK4 and CDK6. Protein structure modeling showed that residue L16 is part of the hydrophobic core and that replacing this residue with a proline would affect protein structure.

Analysis of several CDKN2A variants was performed to discover their functional impact. Both in vitro and in vivo binding assays showed that the A20P mutation resulted in complete loss of binding to CDK4 and CDK6. Transfected human fibroblasts had similar expression levels of A20P compared to wild-type CDKN2A as seen in a Northern blot, while an immunoblot showed decreased protein expression suggesting that this mutation causes instability. Protein structure modeling showed that residue A20 is part of the hydrophobic core and that replacing this residue with a proline would affect protein structure.
A functional screen of mutations found in large-scale cancer data sets identified PIK3CA E39K as an activating mutation, as measured by growth-factor independent growth in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cells.

Three recurrent CTCF mutations found in endometrial carcinoma were expressed in Ishikawa cells and compared to expression of wild-type CTCF. CTCF R377H showed similar nuclear localization and protein expression level as wild-type CTCF. The R377H mutation abolished inhibitory effects on growth and clonogenicity compared to wild-type CTCF as measured by MTT and colony-formation assays, showing loss of tumour suppressive functions.

Functional analysis of PTEN mutations was performed using an in vivo heterologous yeast reconstitution system to measure PTEN activity and rescue of growth arrest caused by hyperactive p110-alpha. The cancer-associated PTEN H93R mutation resulted in partial loss of PTEN activity as measured by PIP3 phosphatase activity, but retained the ability to rescue growth arrest.

YAP1 and EGFR were found to be highly expressed in esophageal cancer (EC) cells and play an important role in resistance to 5-FU or docetaxel. Treatment of the EC cell line JHESO with the YAP1 inhibitor verteporfin had minimal effect on cell growth while verteporfin and docetaxel caused significant growth inhibition compared to either drug alone, as measured by MTS assay. Cell growth inhibition was attributed to decreases in YAP1, EGFR, and downstream AKT phosphorylation, determined by immunoblotting.

FFPE tumor tissue from 1506 colorectal cancer patients was analyzed at codons 12, 13, 61 and 146 by PCR. 672 KRAS mutations were found in 670 patients, and from these, two were inframe insertions located near codon 12. G10_A11insG was validated by direct sequencing. G10_A11insG, G12V and wildtype KRAS were transfected into 293FT and NIH3T3 cells. Increased p-ERK and GTP-bound RAS was seen with G10_A11insG and G12V, but not wildtype. Significantly increased colony formation, and larger tumor size of NIH3T3 cells injected into nude mice was seen with G10_A11insG and G12V over wildtype cells. Enhanced signaling, clonogenicity, and growth suggest G10_A11insG promotes oncogenic transformation in these cell types.

SPOP is a ubiquitin ligase complex adapter protein capable of targeting ER-alpha (encoded by ESR1) for ubiquitination and subsequent degradation. Preclinical experiments showed that the MATH domain of SPOP is critical for binding to ER-alpha. The E47K variant within the MATH domain caused a significant decrease in binding between SPOP and ER-alpha in a co-IP assay. E47K also resulted in a lack of ER-alpha polyubiquitination and protein degradation, suggesting that this variant results in loss-of-function of SPOP.

A moderate throughput platform was used to functionally characterize 1000 somatic cancer variants. The platform found EGFR R222C to be an activating mutation based on in vitro screening in two growth-factor–dependent cell models using reverse-phase protein arrays for assessment. This was also the consensus from 5 other tools as well: HotSpot3D, HotMAPS, VEST, CanDrA, and Mutation Assessor (supplemental figure S5).

R1032Q affects the gene's universal kinase catalytic motif. The authors found that injection of mice with COLO-320 cells that harbor this mutation resulted in tumor generation, indicating that this mutation could have oncogenic potential. In vitro kinase assays showed R1032Q reduced VEGFR2 kinase activity. Using proliferation studies with the COLO-320 cell-line, the authors observed sensitivity to 4 tyrosine kinase inhibitors. Treatment of the MDST8 colorectal cancer cell line carrying the R1032Q mutation with cabozantinib resulted in significant reduction in cell growth and increased ERK phosphorylation levels.

The proband was found at 44Y with RCC and the mother died due to complications of RCC at 56Y. Both the proband and mother were found with a translocation mutation. The aunt of the proband was not found with the mutation and was surgically treated 65Y to remove a papillary RCC tumour from the right kidney. ACMG: PP4

A case report presented a 42-year-old female with hemangioblastoma in the posterior cranial fossa and endolymphatic sac tumour. Genetic analysis of the peripheral blood revealed a germline insertion mutation of 10 nucleotides in exon 1 at the 291 amino acid. Family history not described. The insertion mutation resulted in a frameshift, which may suggest a PVS1. Patient' phenotypes are highly specific to VHL disease (ACMG PP4).

Molecular screening for germline mutations of the genes NF1, RET and VHL were performed and revealed mutations in the VHL (p.Pro192Arg) and NF1 gene (c.3516_3517delTC, p.D1172DfsX21). Her 40Y son had no mutations. Another son passed away 20Y ago at 17Y old from 'undefined malignancy' and clinical characteristics consistent with NF1. ACMG: PP4

Six patients with classic VHL disease (VHL patients) and 6 healthy control participants took part in the study. The patients were free from any associated neoplasia at the time of the study and had no other medical disorders. VHL patients were recruited through their respective physicians. Control participants were recruited through advertisement and were chosen to match VHL patients for sex, age, height, weight, and body mass index. One 37Y VHL patient with unknown phenotype besides 'Type 1 VHL' was described to have this VHL mutation.

301 were enrolled in a prospective clinical protocol to evaluate the natural history of vHL-associated pancreatic lesions (NCT00062166). Of these, 69 patients with pancreatic manifestations of vHL disease and missense VHL mutations were included in the current study. Individual patient phenotype was not described, but overall of the 60 patients, 57 had RCC, 41 had CNS hemangioblastomas, 28 had retinal hemangioblastoma, 23 had pheochromocytoma. 36/69 patients were female and the mean age was 50.5 years old. 11 patients were listed with this missense mutation. In this study, 560 cases of B-ALL were analyzed by RNAseq, 22 (3.9%) of which (3.9%) demonstrated rearrangements of MEF2D at chromosome 1q21–22, encoding myocyte enhancer factor 2D, representing 15 of 367 (4.1%) childhood cases (up to age 15 years), 4 of 62 (6.5%) adolescent cases (age 16–20 years), 2 of 73 (2.7%) young adults and a single case in 56 older adults. In one instance (48-year-old woman), the amino terminus of MEF2D was fused in frame with the carboxy-terminal portion encoded by CSF1R, confirmed by reverse transcription and PCR (RT–PCR) followed by Sanger sequencing. Xenografts of leukemic cells of five cases with MEF2D-rearranged B-ALL were then engrafted in immunocompromised mice. These cells demonstrated sensitivity to the HDAC inhibitor panobinostat, suggesting HDAC inhibition as a therapeutic option.

This study describes a cohort of 24 patients with BCR-ABL1-like B-ALL and ABL-class kinase rearrangement exposed to TKI frontline or at relapse, who showed favorable MRD response and outcome. Specifically, one 34-year-old man with MEF2D-CSF1R identified by RNAseq was prescribed an unspecified dose of imatinib as adjuvant to his frontline chemotherapy (protocol GRAALL-2014). His initial MRD analysis at 94 days remained positive for blasts (1 x 10^-4), but was consistent with continuous complete remission (CCR) at day 147. Although he achieved CCR with chemotherapy and imatinib, the patient's disease eventually recurred and he died in the first relapse.

This study included 1389 cases of high-risk pediatric B-ALL, of which 284 were identified by TaqMan Low Density Array to have a BCR-ABL1-like (Ph-like) gene expression signature. RT-PCR or RNAseq performed on Ph-like, CRLF2 negative patients revealed one case of the novel TBL1XR1-CSF1R fusion. No clinical information pertaining to this individual was disclosed. Considering the previously confirmed Ph-like expression signature in the tested cases, the results suggest that the presence of the TBL1XR1-CSF1R fusion in B-ALL may indicate the BCR-ABL1-like (Ph-like) subtype of the disease.

219 newly diagnosed NCI high-risk, Ph-negative, B-ALL patients between ages 1 to 18 were enrolled on DFCI ALL Consortium protocol 05-001 (NCT00400946) between 2005 and 2011. This study sought to determine the frequency of kinase-activating fusions in this patient cohort. Testing of 105 patients by validated multiplex reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) assays identified one male patient (age>10) with the SFPQ-ABL1 fusion. This patient was also positive for the IKZF1 gene deletion. Although no other information is available for the patient with the SFPQ-ABL1 fusion, in univariate analysis, fusion-positivity and IKZF1 deletion were each associated with inferior event-free survival and IKZF1 deletion also retained statistical significance in multivariable analysis.

A phase I safety and dose-escalation study (NCT01897571) was completed for tazemetostat in relapsed or refractory B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma or advanced solid tumors. Durable objective responses, including complete responses, were observed in eight (38%) of 21 patients with B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma and two (5%) of 43 patients with solid tumours. EZH2 mutation status was assessed retrospectively. Two DLBCL patients had mutations. One of these (with a Y646H mutation) had a durable partial response before disease progression after 16 months on study. The variant in the second patient was not reported and the duration of therapy for this patient that did not respond was among the shortest in the trial.

In RG7356 xenograft models, cell lines expressing predominantly a mixture of CD44v8-v10 and CD44v3-v10 show no response to treatment with RG7356 measured as a percentage of tumor growth inhibition. In a retrospective clinical study including 11 patients treated with RG7356, all 7 colorectal carcinoma patients expressing predominantly CD44v8-v10 show an increase in tumor target lesions measured according to RECIST1.1. Predominant expression of CD44v8-v10 and CD44v3-v10 induces a resistance to RG7356 treatment in different cancers including colorectal carcinoma.

evidence_statement: In 72 nonchemioradioselected (N-CRS) patients the CD44v9-positive by immunohistochemistry staining group demonstrated worse disease-specific survival than the CD44v9-negative groupe (p = 0.008) after treatment with concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT), In 30 N-CRS patients, CD44v9 induced after CCRT group demonstrated worse DSS (p = 0.004) than the CD44v9 non-induced group. These results indicate that the expression of CD44v9 in N-CRS patients is a prognostic factor of poor DSS.

After second line treatment with cisplatin, 64 patients with positive immunohistochemical staining of CD44v9 show a significant decrease of cancer specific survival rate (p = 0.008). In multivariate analyses, CD44v9 positivity is significantly correlated with cancer-specific mortality (p = 0.024).

The patient was 32Y and female; genetic analysis confirmed a germline mutation C>A in the -1 position of the exon 3 splice acceptor sequence. The mutation was found in her father and 2 sons who had VHL symptoms (undescribed). Cosegreation with multiple affected family members may suggest PP1. The index patient's phenotypes are highly specific to VHL disease (PP4).

evidence_statement: Of 246 patients affected with von Hippel-Lindau disease, 64 patients (26%) from 38 families had pheochromocytoma, including 33 newly diagnosed during screening studies and 31 treated before screening at NIH. Germline mutations in the VHL gene was determined from peripheral blood. Five families were found with this VHL germline mutation. Family ID 4334 had 4 members and phenotypes pheochromocytoma; hemangioblastoma; retinal capillary hemangioma; unspecified cyst; and pancreatic endocrine tumour. Family ID 4477 (previously partially reported by Chen et al) had 2 members, 1 member with retinal capillary hemangioma; hemangioblastoma; pheochromocytoma and the other with pheochromocytoma; hemangioblastoma; retinal capillary hemangioma; unspecified cyst; pancreatic endocrine tumour. Family 6103 had one member with pheochromocytoma; hemangioblastoma; unspecified cyst; retinal capillary hemangioma. Family ID 6104 had 5 members and phenotypes pheochromocytoma; renal cell carcinoma; hemangioblastoma; retinal capillary hemangioma; and unspecified cyst. Finally. Family ID 6107 had 2 members, one with pheochromocytoma; hemangioblastoma; retinal capillary hemangioma and the other with pheochromocytoma; hemangioblastoma. ACMG PP1 PP4

This case reports a 16-mo-old boy with metastatic neuroblastoma (stage M). Genomic analysis of a diagnostic biopsy of the tumor and matched normal identified two germline mutations in FANCA and somatic ALK-I1171T mutation. Functional investigation of this mutation including PC12 cell neurite outgrowth, NIH3T3 transformation and phosophoproteomics showing increased ALK signaling all suggested that it was a gain function. The patient was treated with Ceritinib as a monotherapy for 7.5 months. The residual primary decreased in size (44% volume reduction at 6 months of treatment) and was surgically removed. At 21 months of followup a complete remission was observed (including all metastatic sites).

MET mutations found in papillary renal carcinomas were introduced into a chimeric construct composed of NGF and the intracellular portion of MET, and these were expressed in NIH3T3 cells. Expression of M1250T resulted in increased activation of ERK1/2 compared to wild-type MET, as seen on a Western blot.

Among 51 patients, patients expressing CD44v6 in primary melanoma were classified in the "high-risk for MBM" group with a sensitivity of 71.4% and a specificity of 60.9% (AUC = 0.68) Moreover, among 50 patients, patients expressing CD44v6 in primary melanoma show a significant decrease in melanoma brain metastasis free survival (p= 0.03). Among 23 patients, patients expressing CD44v6 in lymph node metastasis show a significant decrease in melanoma brain metastasis free survival (p = 0.05). This suggests that CD44v6 expression is prognostic of melanoma brain metastasis development.
In a meta-analysis including nine trials with a total of 942 patients, high CD44v6 expression is significantly associated with a decrease in survival outcome (HR 2.13, 95% CI: 1.58 to 2.88).

In a meta-analysis including 4 studies with a total of 629 patients, CD44v6 expression is significantly correlated with a decrease in OS (HR 1.76, 95% IC: 1.30 to 2.39). One study that affects heterogeneity had to be excluded.

Cancer-associated mutations in p16 (CDKN2A) were assessed for their ability to bind cyclin-dependent kinases, inhibit kinase activity, and induce cell-cycle arrest in G1 phase. D84G caused reduced binding to CDK4 and CDK6 as seen in a co-precipitation assay, as well as defective kinase inhibition. U2OS osteosarcoma cells were transfected with wild-type or mutant CDKN2A and cell cycle phase was analyzed by flow cytometry. The D84G mutation caused a drastic decrease in G1-phase arrest relative to wild-type, suggesting loss of p16 function.

Using a baculovirus expression system, wild-type EZH2 or Y641 (Y641F, Y641H, Y641N, Y641S) mutants were coexpressed with the PRC2 complex in Spodoptera frugiperda cells. Methyltransferase activity assays showed that while the mutants have decreased catalytic efficiency for unmethylated substrates, they are significantly more efficient than the wild-type at catalyzing both mono-to-dimethyl and dimethyl-to-trimethyl reactions. This indicates a critical dependency on "enzymatic coupling" between the normal enzyme (which performs H3K27 monomethylation) and the disease-associated mutant enzyme (which efficiently performs the subsequent methylation steps). Western blots of patient-derived lymphoma cell lines supported this: a homozygous wild-type line demonstrated increased H3K27me1 and me2 but decreased H3K27me3, whereas four heterozygous mutant lines displayed increased H3K27me3, consistently decreased H3K27me2, and variably decreased or comparable H3K27me1. Together, these results demonstrate that this enzymatic coupling of wild-type and Y641 mutant alleles results in an overall gain-of-function phenotype regarding H3K27 trimethylation.

phenotypes: Abnormal fundus morphology,Adenomatous colonic polyposis,Cerebellar hemangioblastoma,Retinal capillary hemangioma,Neoplasm of the rectum
evidence_statement: A 21-year-old man presented in 1963 with 2 retinal hemangiomas characteristic of von Hippel-Lindaudisease (VHLD). Two pigmented ocular fundus lesions were noted but their significance was not realized until after the patient's death in 1983. He died of cerebellar hemangioblastoma and rectal carcinoma, and an autopsy revealed multiple colonic polyps. Colonoscopy diagnosed familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP) in his 2 teenaged children. Funduscopy revealed bilateral pigmented ocular fundus lesions in both siblings. Neither had retinal hemangiomas or other extra ocular manifestations of VHL disease or FAP. Cytogenetic analysis revealed normal chromosomes, but molecular genetic analysis of the APC (adenomatous polyposis coli) gene revealed a R1114* (c.3340C>T) nonsense mutation in both siblings. A VHL (von Hippel-Lindau) gene deletion was identified in 1 sibling only, but the paper is not specific as to the nature/ extent of this deletion. ACMG evidence codes: none.

Functional experiments were performed for several CDKN2A variants, including transfection of U2OS cells and analysis of cell cycle phase by flow cytometry. CDKN2A D108H caused a loss of cell cycle arrest relative to wild-type.

Lymphoblastoid cell lines were derived from patients with megalencephaly syndromes, who had the PIK3R2 p.G373R mutation. PIP3 immunostaining was used to compared PI3K activity among mutant and control cell lines. The mutant cell line had increased PIP3 levels compared to the control, pointing to increased PI3K activity, since PI3K converts PIP2 to PIP3. Use of PI3K inhibitor, PI-103, led to reduction of PIP3 levels in the mutant cell line, suggesting that the impact of the PIK3R2 mutation on PIP3 levels depends on PI3K.

In PHTS-derived lymphoblasts, PTEN protein expression, PTEN mRNA levels, and proteasome activity was measured in the PTEN C136R and control cells. In PTEN-C136R cells, PTEN protein expression was significantly reduced, PTEN mRNA levels was comparable to wildtype(wt), and proteasome activity was 30% greater than wt. This increased proteasomal activity was also found in MCF-7 and HEK-293 cell lines transfected with C136R-PTEN, and in mice expressing C136R-PTEN. Further experiments found the mutant localizes to the cytosol, where its increased proteasomal activity is observed. Cycloheximide (CHX) treatment of MCF-7 cells expressing wt or C136R-PTEN revealed this mutant to be highly unstable. Using P-AKT and P-ERK as markers of PI3K and MAPK pathway activity, respectively, it was found that C136R-PTEN resulted in increased fold change of both, inferring increased pathway activation. The authors further inferred that the mutant results in impaired PTEN lipid phosphatase and protein phosphatase.

phenotypes: Retinal capillary hemangioma,Neoplasm of the pancreas,Renal cell carcinoma,Hemangioblastoma
evidence_statement: Germline mutations were found in 20 Brazilian, VHL probands and their families. Peripheral blood samples were taken and genomic DNA was sequenced using PCR and Southern Blotting. The three exons of the VHL gene were amplified by PCR, sequenced in both strands with Big Dye terminators (Applied Biosystems), and collected and analysed on an ABI Prism 377 (Applied Biosystems). Germline rearrangements involving part or the entire VHL gene were detected by quantitative Southern blotting using g7 cDNA11 and a β globin probe. This splice site mutation, c.463+1G>T (stated as IVS2+1G>A in the paper), was found in a VHL type 1 South American family of five affected individuals (family 14). Three family members had hemangioblastoma of central nervous system, one had a retinal capillary hemangioma and another had renal cell carcinoma. One or more members of the family had pancreatic cyst-adenoma. No ACMG code available.

Melanoma-associated germline CDKN2A mutations were assessed for functional effects. Amino acid conservation between human and nine other species showed that proline 81 is highly conserved and changes at this position would likely affect folding of the ankyrin repeat. A co-immunoprecipitation assay showed loss of CDK4 binding for the P81T mutant. Similarly, in silico prediction scores were in concordance with functional results, supporting loss of function effect for this variant.

Fourty-four of 389 patients with VHL (between 1988-1999) screened positive for pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours (PNETs) either by pathologic analysis of tissue specimens or by characteristic radiographic appearance on CT and MRI. VHL gene germline mutations were determined by quantitative Southern blotting to detect deletions of the gene and gene rearrangements as well as complete gene sequencing. Five patients presented with the c.500G>A VHL gene mutation (stated as 713 G to A in the paper which used the Latif sequence as reference) causing a change of Arg to Gln at protein position 167. From family 5960, patient 38 (41-year-old male) presented with a single radiologic PNET and patient 39 (39-year-old female) presented with a single pathologic PNET. From family 5069, patient 41 (48-year-old male) presented with five pathologic PNETs, and patient 42 (16-year-old male) presented with a three pathologic PNETs. Unrelated patient 40 (31-year-old female) presented with a single pathologic PNET. No ACMG code.

In a multivariate analysis from a clinical study including 123 resected primary gastric cancer, CD44s expression at invasive tumor front correlates with a decrease in survival (p< 0.0001). Moreover CD44s expression at invasive tumor front is significantly correlated with peritoneal recurrence rate, lymphatic recurrence rate and hematogenous recurrence rate (p< 0.001, p< 0.001 and p = 0.008).

In a clinical study including 59 stage III-IV ovarian cancer patients with peritoneal disseminated tumors, Kaplan-Meier analysis showed a significant association between CD44v6 high expression and worse OS (P=0.0059), but not PFS (P=0.4290). Similarly, high CD44v6 expression was found to be a predictive factor by univariate (P = 0.007; HR, 2.930; 95% CI, 1.334–6.436) and multivariate (P = 0.022; HR, 2.568; 95% CI, 1.149–5.738) analyses. In vivo experiments showed that CD44v6-positive ES-2 cells produced larger tumors and more frequent metastases than CD44v6-negative cells, when implanted in nude mice.

phenotypes: Lisch nodules,Multiple cafe-au-lait spots,Axillary freckling,Cerebellar hemangioblastoma,Capillary hemangioma
evidence_statement: A case report describes a 34-year-old man with a history of VHL and NF1. NF1 was diagnosed clinically in childhood from multiple café au lait macules, axillary freckling, and Lisch nodule. VHL was later suspected due to cerebellum hemangioblastoma. The patient also had recurring lobular capillary hemangiomas. Genetic analysis revealed a germline VHL missense mutation. Genetic testing for NF1 mutations was not described. There was no family history of NF1 or VHL, although genotypic information from the parents was not described. ACMG PP4

In an in vitro chemosensitivtiy assay, FACS-sorted CD44v6-positive cells show a significantly higher viability compared to CD44v6-negative cells when treated with 10nM of paclitaxel or 9 uM of cisplatin (p< 0.01). This result indicates that CD44v6-positive cells are associated with tumor resistance to chemotherapy.

In an in vitro study, CD44v6 expressing cell lines survive better to 10 uM of cisplatin compared to mock cells, whereas no differential response was observed in response to 5-fluorouracil (p< 0.05). Moreover, CD44v6 expressing cell lines significantly decreases their apoptotic levels in response to cisplatin in comparison to both isogenic counterparts (p< 0.001). CD44v6 depleted cells with CD44v6 siRNA have a higher cisplatin-induced apoptosis levels when compared to controls (p< 0.001). These results suggest that CD44v6 is a predictive factor of resistance to cisplatin. In a co-culture of CD44v6-positive and CD44v6-negative cells treated with cisplatin 10 uM, CD44v6-positive cells constitute more than 70-80% of the entire cell culture from day 9 onwards (p< 0.0001).

The phase II cohort of the CodeBreaK 100 study (NCT03600883) investigated the activity of the KRAS G12C inhibitor sotorasib in previously treated patients with KRAS G12C-mutated non-small cell lung cancer. A total of 124 patients had measurable disease and were evaluated for response by independent central review. Complete response was seen in four patients and partial response in 42 patients, for an objective response rate of 37.1% (95% CI, 28.6 to 46.2). The median progression-free survival and overall survival were 6.8 (95% CI, 5.1 to 8.2) months and 12.5 months (95% CI, 10.0 to could not be evaluated), respectively.

In a clinical study including 105 patients with resectable colorectal carcinomas, a Kaplan-Meier analysis showed a significant association between CD44v5 high expression and worse free time of disease (p = 0.048) but not a significantly decrease in OS (p = 0.669). Similarly, high CD44v6 expression showed a significant association with worse free time of disease and OS (p = 0.038 and p= 0.046). High CD44v6 expression was found to be a predictive factor by multivariate analysis (p = 0.03 and p = 0.02).
In a multivariate analysis from a clinical trial of 101 patients, CD44v6 expression combined with CD44s non-expression is significantly correlated with a reduced survival (p= 0.003).
In an in vitro study using docetaxel-resistant PC-3R cells, knockdown with CD44v8-10 siRNAs increased sensitivity to docetaxel (p < 0.05) compared to negative control.

In a clinical study including 82 patients, a Kaplan-Meier analysis showed a significant association between CD44v6 expression (high and low) and worse disease-free survival (p = 0.03). Another Kaplan-Meier analysis showed a significant association between CD44v10 high expression and worse disease-free survival (p= 0.04).

In an in vitro study, CD44v6 knockdown or deletion of exon 11 (v6 specific) had an decrease in cell survival compared to mock cells treated with scramble siRNA when treated with cisplatin or 5-fluorouracil. This demonstrates that exon-v6 specific removal from CD44v isoforms increase cell sensitivity to cisplatin.

A 4 year old female with macrocephaly and widespread capillary malformations was identified to have a de novo PTEN T277I (c.830C>T) variant (Patient 6). At birth she was noted to have a 46,XX karyotype, macrocephaly and required closure of a patent ductus arteriosus at age 3 months. She also had speech support for learning difficulties but normal intelligence.

Functional analysis of PTEN variants identified in primary malignant glioblastoma cells were compared. Analysis of primary cells from GBM276 (53 year old female patient) identified a T277A variant. PTEN protein and RNA was detectable by Western blot and RT-PCR, respectively. Phosphatase activity measured in HEK293T cells showed phosphate release equivalent to wildtype control. Ectopic expression in a PTEN-null GBM cell line showed reduced ability to inhibit AKT phosphorylation compared to wildtype. Measuring protein half-life in GBM U87MG cells showed a significantly shorter half-life of T277A protein than wildtype. Additionally, PTEN membrane localization was reduced by T277A in HEK293T cells. These studies indicated the variant was enzymatically active but lost critical functions due to reduced stability and aberrant localization.

evidence_statement: Sanger sequencing of cDNA from two tissues samples derived from a patient with cutaneomucosal venous malformation (VMCM) known to harbor germline R849W revealed a distinct somatic mutation in each tissue, which both result in the C-terminal truncating Y1108* (c.3324T>C in one tissue, and c.3320_3321del in the other). TOPO cloning confirmed each somatic variant was present on the same allele as the germline variant.

TIE2 double mutant (T1105N plus T1106N) and wildtype were expressed through retrovirus in Human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs). Unlike wildtype cells, the double mutant demonstrated ligand-independent phosphorylation of TIE2 as measured by Western blot. Compared to wildtype, double mutant cells demonstrated significantly (p<.05) improved invasion and colony formation as measured by GFP infiltration of a non fluorescent monolayer. Double mutant cells possessed increased viability of detached cells and were able to form colonies upon replating 26-352 colonies per million cells versus only solitary colonies formed by the wildtype cell line. Overall, the presence of T1105N plus T1106N enhanced the cellular properties of colony formation, viability, and invasion compared to the TIE2 wildtype and commonly found germline (R849W) and somatic (L914F) TIE2 variants.

Public cancer genome sequencing data sets were used to generated a catalog of mTOR pathway mutations, identified 33 MTOR mutations which confer pathway hyperactivation. A single instance of T1977K was found. mTOR with T1977K was reported to have increased level of S6K1 phosphorylation over wild type mTOR in transfections.

In a clinical trial including 21 patients, CD44v6 expression (prior to and after to NAC) is a predictive factor of response to NAC by multivariate analysis (p = 0.0099 and p = 0.0470). Moreover, CD44v6 is also a predictive factor of OS (p = 0.013).

A retrospective analysis of 164 patients waiting for surgery for hemangioblastomas at Freiburg University Medical Center, Freiburg, Germany was conducted. Bidirectional direct sequencing by use of an ABI PRISM 3130 DNA Genetic Analyzer (Applied Biosystems) was used to identify mutations in abnormal samples. One patient was found to carry the germline point mutations c.194C>G, p.Ser64Trp in the VHL gene (stated as c.407G>C in the paper which used the Latif sequence as reference). The patient (12) was a 56-year-old female with cerebellar hemangioblastoma and elevated hemoglobin levels indicative of polyglobulia. Family history was not described. ACMG: PP4

evidence_statement: In a study examining PIK3CA variants associated with PIK3CA-Related Overgrowth Syndrome (PROS), somatic PIK3CA E81K (c.241 G>A) was identified at various allele frequencies in hair follicles, saliva, and left and right leg biopsies from a 10.37 year old female clinically diagnosed with megalencephaly-capillary malformation (MCAP) syndrome. The variant was absent from the patient's blood and that of the patient's parents. The patient presented with choroid plexus cyst and echogenic intracardiac focus at gestational week 21 (detected by ultrasound). At birth, her weight, length, and head circumference were in the 90+ centile; diffuse capillary malformation of the trunk and limbs and syndactyly of the 2nd and 3rd toes were observed. In subsequent examinations, left hemihyperplasia, focal hemimegalencephaly, perisylvian polymicrogyria, antiepileptic-refractory generalized tonic-clonic seizures, mild cognitive impairment, temper tantrums, and dysmorphic features were observed. Cultured fibroblasts from the leg biopsies showed increased levels of phosphorylated AKT at threonine 308 and serine 473 compared to IMR90 primary normal human fibroblasts. Treatment with PI3K inhibitors wartmannin and LY294002 abrogated over-activation of the PI3K pathway and inhibited growth-factor-independent cellular proliferation. Authors conclude that PIK3CA E81K can be responsible for PIK3CA-related overgrowth spectrum disorders.

In a study examining PIK3CA variants associated with PIK3CA-Related Overgrowth Syndrome (PROS), somatic PIK3CA H1047R (c.3140 A>G) was identified by targeted deep sequencing analysis in cultured dermal fibroblasts with a frequency of 9.1% from an 18 year old female clinically diagnosed with fibroadipose overgrowth. The variant was absent from the patient's blood. The patient presented with macrodactyly of the right 4th finger at birth, fibrolipomatous tissue requiring surgical excision at 3 and 5 years, and unevenly distributed right hand nodular areas without bone overgrowth. Cultured fibroblasts showed increased levels of phosphorylated AKT at threonine 308 and serine 473 compared to IMR90 primary normal human fibroblasts. Treatment with PI3K inhibitors wartmannin and LY294002 abrogated over-activation of the PI3K pathway and inhibited growth-factor-independent cellular proliferation. Authors conclude that PIK3CA H1047R can be responsible for PIK3CA-related overgrowth spectrum disorders.

In a study examining PIK3CA variants associated with PIK3CA-Related Overgrowth Syndrome (PROS), somatic PIK3CA H1047L (c.3140 A>T) was identified by targeted deep sequencing analysis of a finger tissue biopsy with a frequency of 15.5% from a male clinically diagnosed with fibroadipose overgrowth. The variant was absent from the patient's blood. The patient presented with macrodactyly involving soft tissues and skeletal segments of the left 2nd and 3rd finger at birth, soft swelling of the deltoid region and slight overgrowth of the left arm and forearm at 10 months. Authors conclude that PIK3CA H1047L can be responsible for PIK3CA-related overgrowth spectrum disorders.

Three siblings had a phenotype which overlaps with known megalencephaly syndromes and RASopathies, including Costello syndrome, and were all heterozygous for mTOR c.5395G>A; p.Glu1799Lys. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) were isolated from one sibling, and PBMCs were stimulated with CD3 and CD28 in the presence of IL-2 for 3 days, then washed and restiumlated with CD3 +/- rapamycin, stained with anti phospho S6 and analyzed with flow cytometry. The patient sample had increased p-S6, in comparison to 4 healthy and unrelated control samples. The increased pS6 response was blocked by the addition of rapamycin.

The Cys1483Arg (c.4447T>C) variant of mTOR was found in brain tissue samples from 1 focal cortical dysplasia type II (FCDII) pateint at Hybrid capture % of mutated allele 6.38%. In HEK293T cells, mTOR C1483R increased S6 phosphorylation over wild type, and showed increased activity in kinase assays.

The Leu2427Gln (c.7280T>A) variant of mTOR was found in brain tissue samples from 1 focal cortical dysplasia type II (FCDII) pateint at Hybrid capture % of mutated allele 3.05%. In HEK293T cells, mTOR L2427Q increased S6 phosphorylation over wild type, and showed increased activity in kinase assays.

The L2427P (c.7280T>C) variant of mTOR was found in brain tissue samples from 2 focal cortical dysplasia type II (FCDII) patients at allelic frequencies of 9.6–12.6% and 6.9–7.3% in biological replicates from each patient. In HEK293T cells, mTOR L2427P increased S6 phosphorylation over wild type, and showed increased activity in kinase assays. In utero electroporation of wild type or L2427P mTOR was performed in mice. After weaning, more than 90% of mice with the mutant construct displayed spontaneous seizures with epileptic discharge, whereas wildtype mice were seizure free. Rapamycin administration initiated after seizure onset almost completely eliminated seizures. Rapamycin also reversed increased size of L2427P neurons.

A large Hungarian VHL type 2 family involving 32 members underwent mutational analysis of their peripheral blood and had exons 1, 2, and 3 of the VHL gene sequenced using direct sequencing of PCR-amplified DNA. Only two members of the family (II-1 and III-6) were found to carry this germline missense mutation, c.74C>T resulting in an amino acid change at protein position 25; from proline to leucine. Patient II-1 was a 70-year-old asymptomatic compound heterozygote who also carried the Ser80Ile mutation. She had one daughter (III-1), the proband, who did not carry the Pro25Leu mutation but carried the Ser80Ile mutation. Family history revealed that one sister of the patient, (II-5) died due to bilateral renal cell carcinomas. Another sister of the patient (II-4) died because of a metastatic pancreatic tumor. The patient's niece (III-6), daughter of patient II-5, was the other family member found to carry the Pro25Leu mutation. Patient III-6 was a 44-year-old asymptomatic female, but unlike her aunt, was not a compound heterozygote. She had two children but neither were found to carry either mutation.

Fifty missense mutations identified in sporadic breast cancer were assessed for qualitative and quantitative changes in their ability to transactivate from 11 human promoter response elements in a yeast reporter system. The T125R mutant showed transactivation levels that differed from those of wild-type p53 at several response elements, with almost no ability to transactivate from the Cyclin G response element. The authors considered this an altered function variant as a result of the loss of transactivation function at some response elements.

Fifty missense mutations identified in sporadic breast cancer were assessed for qualitative and quantitative changes in their ability to transactivate from 11 human promoter response elements in a yeast reporter system. The L130V mutant showed transactivation levels similar to wild-type p53 when expressed at high levels, but had a pattern that differed from wild-type when expressed at low levels. Specifically, L130V resulted in reduced transactivation of 14-3-3 sigma, but had enhanced transactivation ability for the AIP1 response element, relative to wild-type. The authors considered this an altered function variant as a result of the differences in transactivation function compared to wild-type.

However, when expressed at low levels C141W differed from wild-type in the pattern of transactivation at several REs, including reduced transactivation of p21 and MDM2 REs and enhanced transactivation ability for GADD45 and AIP1 REs, relative to wild-type. H3K27me3 (histone H3 Lys-27–specific trimethylation) level was higher in EZH2 (Y641F) bearing germinal center B-cell type DLBCL derived lymphoma cell lines and tumors than in wild-type cells. Expression of Y641F mutation in HEK293T cells with wild-type EZH2 led to an increase in H3K27me3. Primary murine B-cell lines with Y641F mutation also showed an increase of H3K27me3. Structural modeling indicated that Y641F/N helped push the equilibrium to favor trimethylated products. A 3H methyl incorporation assay was used to study the activity of the PRC2 complex containing Y641F mutation in vitro. PRC2 complexes containing Y641F showed nearly two times higher activity with H3K27me2 substrates than PRC complexes with wild-type EZH2. This study indicates that EZH2 (Y641F) increases H3K27 trimethylation.

A large scale tumor genome analysis identified p190RhoGAP-encoding gene ARHGAP35 to be frequently mutated in endometrial tumours, including the nonsense mutation R997*. Mutant and wild-type HA-tagged ARHGAP35 constructs were created and expressed in Huh7 cells for functional analysis. The R997* truncating mutation results in a complete lack of the C-terminal GAP domain, a loss of binding to active RhoA, and no effect on stress fiber formation. The authors conclude that R997* results in loss of p190RhoGAP function.

A fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) assay was used to assess the interaction between the Nrf2 (NFE2L2) ETGE motif and the Keap1 Kelch binding domain. A peptide containing the E82D mutation showed reduced affinity for the Kelch domain compared to wild-type, as measured by the FRET assay. This result suggests that E82D causes a loss of binding between Nrf2 and it's negative regulator Keap1, which would result in activation of Nrf2.

CIC repressor activities were assessed in transfected HEK293 cells using a luciferase reporter controlled by a promoter containing CIC binding sites. The R215W mutation in the HMG-box of CIC showed decreased repressor activities in the reporter assay relative to wild-type. The association of CIC mutants to endogenous ETV/PEA3 gene promoters was tested by ChIP assay and R215W showed reduced ChIP signals compared to controls, representing reduced promoter occupancy. Similarly, a DNA binding assay found that HMG-box mutations including R215W reduced binding to a probe from the ETV4 gene, while a wild-type construct efficiently bound this probe.

Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) was performed on the diffuse intrinsic pontine gliomas (DIPGs) and matched germline DNA of 7 pediatric patients. Targeted sequencing was performed on an additional 43 DIPGs and 36 non-brainstem pediatric glioblastomas (non-BS-PGs). Authors identified the G34R variant in 5/36 (14%) non-BS-PGs (age between 7 and 16 years). No histone H3 mutations were found in any other pediatric brain tumors including 7 low-grade brainstem gliomas, 15 low-grade non-brainstem gliomas, 38 medulloblastomas, and 22 ependymomas. H3F3A G34R was also not found in an additional 170 non-central nervous system pediatric tumors.

The BRAF mutation G463E resulted in elevated kinase activity relative to wild-type BRAF in vitro. B-RAF activity was determined using kinase dead MEK as a substrate. G463E activity was 28 times higher than basal WT BRAF. The authors classified G463E activity as intermediate since its kinase activity was between basal WT BRAF and G12V RAS-activated WT B-RAF cells. In comparison, some BRAF variants displayed high kinase activity above the G12V RAS-activated WT BRAF cells. NIH3T3 transformation assay yielded 24 +/- 14 foci/ng of transfected BRAF DNA, in comparison to WT, which yielded zero foci, indicating an oncogenic effect of BRAF G463E.

Functional effects of the RRAS2 (TC21) Q72L mutation was assessed in NIH3T3 and 293T cells. RRAS2 Q72L expressed in NIH3T3 cells caused strong activation of AKT by Western blot, higher even than the activating HRAS G12V mutation. Q72L also activated ERK to similar levels as HRAS G12V. Using HA-tagged wild-type and mutant RRAS2 expressed in 293T cells, an immunoprecipitation assay showed increased interaction between RRAS2 Q72L and p85 subunit of PI3K, compared to wild-type RRAS2. These results suggest that Q72L causes gain of function resulting in increased activation of PI3K/AKT and ERK pathways.

The functional significance of several PIK3CA mutations found in endometrial cancer were assessed by measuring AKT phosphorylation in transfected U2OS cells. PIK3CA R93Q showed levels of AKT activation similar to wild-type PIK3CA and much lower than other activation PIK3CA mutations such as H1047R, suggesting that this mutation alone does not cause gain of function. Interestingly, the three tumors with R93Q mutation had at least one additional PIK3CA mutation. The authors suggest that R93Q may be able to synergize with other mutations to activate PIK3CA, as has been noted in other cases where PIK3CA mutations co-occur in different domains.

The ability of FLT3-N676K mutation to induce leukemia by itself in mouse models is explored in this study. Furthermore, the leukemogenic potential of FLT3-N676K is compared to two well established, canonical FLT3 mutations, namely, ITD and D835. 32D cells and hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs), were transduced with retroviral constructs carrying FLT3-ITD or FLT3-N676K or FLT3-D835 or FLT3-ITD-N676K double mutants, and subsequently transplanted into two different mice strains (either C3H/HeJ or C57BL/6J), and followed over several days for leukemia development. N676K mutant animals showed higher BM blast percentages, similar to D835 and ITD carrying animals, suggesting that N676K mutation alone is sufficient to cause leukemia. Protein phosphorylation studies showed increased FLT3 autophosphorylation in the presence of N676K mutation alone, consistent with other well studied FLT3 mutations. Phosphorylation studies also showed that N676K mutants worked through the MAPK pathway, just like the D835 mutants, and not the STAT5 pathway used by the ITD mutants.

This study evaluated 641 cases of rhabdomyosarcoma (RMS), enrolled on Children’s Oncology Group trials (1998-2017) and UK malignant mesenchymal tumor and RMS2005 trials (1995-2016), for mutations in 39 genes previously implicated in RMS. The analysis was done using a custom-capture sequencing assay. MYOD1 L122R variant was identified in 17 cases (3%) and was not restricted to spindle-cell histology, but was also observed in association with other histologic patterns (including cases with densely packed cells that mimicked embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma (ERMS) or RMS not otherwise specified ). MYOD1 mutation showed association with older age, head and neck primary site, and a dismal survival. In both COG and UK patient cohorts, patients with the MYOD1 L122R mutation had rapid disease progression and significantly worse event free survival as compared to the patients with wild-type MYOD1.

Authors identified the HIST1H3B K27M variant in 9/50 (18%) DIPGs (age between 3 and 12 years) and 1/36 (3%) non-BS-PGs (age of 4 years). This multicenter clinical trial study (PROPHECY) enrolled 118 patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancers (CRPC) on Abiraterone or Enzalutamide treatment. The authors demonstrated that detection of this variant is independently associated with poor PFS and OS in patients treated with Abiraterone or Enzalutamide suggesting that alternative treatment options should be offered when AR-V7 is detected.

A clinical study including 37 patients with mCRPC commencing abiraterone or enzalutamide treatment shows no significant changes in PSA PFS response when AR-V7 is expressed (p = 0.4). The same result is found when AR-V9 expression is added (p = 0.9).

Functional analysis of the mTOR R2152C mutation was performed in HEK-293T cells co-transfected with HA-GST-S6K1. Immunoblots showed R2152C resulted in similar low level of S6K1 phosphorylation as wild-type mTOR, suggesting that this mutation does not alter mTOR activity.

Transcriptomic analysis was performed on 17 meningiomas, 7 with K409Q mutation and 10 wild-type for KLF4. Further experiments showed that K409Q altered the degradation of HIF-1 alpha by reducing activity of the oxygen-dependent hydroxylases required for HIF-1 alpha ubiquitination.

NIH3T3 transformation assay yielded 256 +/- 85 foci/ng of transfected BRAF DNA, in comparison to WT, which yielded zero foci, indicating an oncogenic effect of BRAF G468A.

Mutations in histone modifier genes were analyzed in exome sequence data from 113 esophageal squamous cell carcinoma tumors. KYSE-150 and KYSE-450 ESCC cell lines were depleted of EP300 using shRNA, then reconstituted with wild-type of mutant EP300. EP300 Y1414C caused increased cell proliferation relative to wild-type, supporting an oncogenic role of this mutation. The authors also show that overall survival is worse in ESCC patients with EP300 mutations compared to wild-type.

The NFE2L2:p.G31A allele was expressed in HA1E-M cells and its tumorigenic potential was tested in a pooled and individual in vivo (mice) assay. The G31A mutation did not lead to tumor formation in the pooled assay but did cause tumor formation in 6/6 mice in the individual experiment. The NFE2L2:p.G31A allele was also found to be expressed at significantly higher levels as compared to wild type. Short term gene expression correlation analysis was also completed using HA1E cells and the L1000 Luminex bead-based gene expression assay. Transcript level of 978 landmark genes were measured to formulate a gene expression signature for the allele. Overexpression of the mutant allele led to a similar signature as overexpression of the wild type, suggesting that the gain-of-function changes induced by the mutant can also be seen in NFE2L2-overexpressed cells.

A phase Ib trial assessed preliminary activity of the PIK3CA inhibitor alpelisib in combination with letrozole in ER+/PIK3CA mutant patients. One patient was found to harbor a novel deletion in the C2 domain of PIK3CA by NGS analysis. This protein domain is involved in binding to p85, a regulator of p110-alpha. This patient with PIK3CA P447_L455del achieved partial response and was on treatment for more than one year.

In a clinical study including 37 patients treated with taxanes or enzalutamide and abiraterone: - AR-V7 is associated with resistance to enzalutamide and abiraterone, but its relevance in the context of taxmen chemotherapy is unknown. - AR-V7 is not associated with primary resistance to taxmen chemotherapy: patients expressing AR-V7 may retain sensitivity to taxanes. - In males patients expressing AR-V7, taxanes may be more efficacious than AR-directed agents. - In males patients not expressing AR-V7, taxanes appear to have comparable efficacy to AR-directed agents.

In a prospective clinical study including 52 patients, expression of AR-FL or AR-V1 or AR-V3 or AR-V7 or AR-V9 are not significantly associated with PSA response change. However, in a multivariate analysis, AR-V1 expression after two cabazitaxel cycles is significantly associated with a decrease of OS (p = 0.031)

In a clinical study including 168 patients treated with abiraterone or enzalutamide, a multivariate analysis including tumor burden and TP53 status show no significant correlation between AR-V1, AR-V2, AR-V3, AR-V4, AR-V5, AR-V7 or AR-V9 and PFS but a significant correlation with TP53 .
In a clinical study including 54 patients treated with taxane, AR-V567es expression is significantly correlated with a response change in PSA (p = 0.04) and a decrease in PFS (p = 0.02).

A case study of a pediatric patient presenting with choroid plexus carcinoma and adrenocortical carcinoma identified a de novo germline TP53 E285V mutation in peripheral blood DNA. A promoter-reporter assay using transfected SaOS-2 cells showed that wild-type p53 efficiently induced promoter activity, while E285V did not. The E285V mutant resulted in a loss of growth inhibition in a colony growth assay and a loss of apoptotic activity, suggesting a lack of tumor suppressive function. Further experiments showed that E285V is capable of blocking wild-type p53 activity, and therefore the authors consider this a dominant negative mutation.

Multi-gene cancer predisposition panel testing of a 51 year old patient diagnosed with breast cancer revealed a pathogenic PALB2 c.1240C>T, p.R414X variant. This patient had a family history of cancer among their 1st, 2nd, and 3rd degree relatives in Breast, Lung, Colon, Brain Tumors and Hodgkins Lymphoma. The identification of a PALB2 pathogenic variant in this patient resulted in a change in clinical management recommendation including increased breast cancer screening and bilateral mastectomy.

Two types of UC cell lines were compared in this study. T24 and J82 which are mesenchymal subtype and overexpress FGFR1, and RT-4 and UMUC-14, epithelial subtype which do not express FGFR1. T24 and J82 are more aggressive in colony formation assays and show higher IC50 values for Paclitaxel(PTX) treatment, when compared with the epithelial subtype UC cell lines. PTX acts by arresting cells in G2/M phase, preventing progression to G0/G1 phase and promoting apoptosis. Cell cycle analysis demonstrated that T24 AND J82 cell lines have increased fraction of cells in S-phase and reduced fraction in G2/M-phase, no evidence of the pro-apoptotic markers such as cleaved caspase-3 and cleaved PARP, whereas RT-4 and UMUC-14 showed increased fraction of cells in G2/M and overexpression of pro-apoptotic cleaved caspase-3 and cleaved PARP. These findings suggest FGFR1 overexpression may be associated with resistance to PTX in mesenchymal subtype.

Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) was performed on the diffuse intrinsic pontine gliomas (DIPGs) and matched germline DNA of 7 pediatric patients. Targeted sequencing was performed on an additional 43 DIPGs and 36 non-brainstem pediatric glioblastomas (non-BS-PGs). Authors identified the H3C2 K27M variant in 9/50 (18%) DIPGs (age between 4 and 12 years) and 1/36 (3%) non-BS-PGs (age of 4 years). The authors comment that the K27M mutation appeared exclusive to pediatric high grade gliomas, but no histone H3 mutations found in any other pediatric brain tumors including 7 low-grade brainstem gliomas, 15 low-grade non-brainstem gliomas, 38 medulloblastomas, and 22 ependymomas. H3 K27M was not found in an additional 170 non-central nervous system pediatric tumors.

A functional screen of somatic mutations found in large-scale cancer data sets classified EGFR E114K as neutral, based on growth-factor independent growth in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cells, and consensus among five in silico functional annotation tools.
Ba/F3 cells transfected with EGFR E114K had levels of p-EGFR, p-STAT5, and p-AKT that were similar to known activating mutation L858R and higher than in cells expressing wild-type EGFR.

The oncogenic potential of somatic EGFR mutations found in colorectal cancer samples were tested. IL-3 independent growth of Ba/F3 cells was achieved when cells were transduced with EGFR E114K. NIH-3T3 cells expressing E114K showed a significant increase in colony formation in the presence of EGF, relative to EGFR wild-type cells.

Oncogenic somatic EGFR mutations found in colorectal cancer samples were tested for sensitivity to EGFR inhibitors cetuximab and panitumumab. Ba/F3 cells expressing EGFR E114K showed a dose-dependent reduction in cell viability in response to both inhibitors, as well as reduced p-EGFR, p-STAT5, and p-AKT. Treatment of NIH-3T3 cells expressing EGFR E114K with cetuximab or panitumumab resulted in significant decreases in colony formation as well as decreased EGF-induced p-EGFR and p-STAT5 levels, compared to untreated cells.

One patient was identified with a LMNA-NTRK1 positive tumor in this Phase I study (NCT02122913), which involved 70 heavily pretreated patients with a median age of 59.5 years, with multiple solid tumor types. A total of eight patients had NTRK fusions, and by independent radiology review, all patients with TRK fusion were considered to have had an objective response. The average time on treatment was 28.4 months for patients with NTRK fusion cancer, compared to 1.8 months for those without an NTRK fusion. Authors concluded that NTRK fusions may represent tissue and age agnostic oncogenic drivers, and that Larotrectinib was well tolerated in the patients and demonstrated activity in all tumors with NTRK fusions.

This Phase I study (NCT02122913) enrolled 70 heavily pretreated adult patients (median age 59.5 years) with various advanced solid tumors. Among them, one patient was identified with a TPR::NTRK1 fusion-positive tumor. In total, eight patients had tumors harboring NTRK gene fusions. By independent radiology review, the objective response rate in this fusion-positive group was 100% (8/8), with responses observed across different cancer types. The median time on treatment for patients with NTRK fusion cancer was 28.4 months, compared to 1.8 months for those without a fusion. The authors concluded that NTRK fusions are tissue- and age-agnostic oncogenic drivers and that larotrectinib was well-tolerated and demonstrated activity in all patients with NTRK fusion-positive tumors.

In this Phase I study (NCT02122913), which involved 70 heavily pretreated patients with a median age of 59.5 years, with multiple solid tumor types, None of the patients with NTRK point mutations had an objective response. The authors conclude this is consistent with prior analyses suggesting that point mutations in NTRK are not usually oncogenic.

A 58-year-old male with NTRK-fusion positive gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST) demonstrated initial response to Larotrectinib but progressed after developing a gatekeeper mutation (TRKC F617L).

This study evaluated 641 cases of rhabdomyosarcoma (RMS) that were enrolled in the Children’s Oncology Group (COG) trials from 1998 to 2017 and the UK malignant mesenchymal tumor and RMS2005 trails from 1995 to 2016. Molecular testing included 39 genes which had been implicated in the past with regards to RMS. The analysis was performed with a custom-capture sequencing assay. Altered TP53 was noted in 69 out of 515 FOXO1 fusion-negative RMS cases (13%), with the most frequent mutations at codons G245S (6 cases), R248Q or W (6 cases), R175H (4 cases), and P72A (4 cases). These cases displayed a worse event free survival. In FOXO1 fusion-positive RMS subtype, there was a small number of cases with altered TP53 (3 and 2 cases in the COG and UK patient cohorts, respectively), but they were universally fatal. Due to lack of a matched germline sample, it could not be determined whether the TP53 abnormalities were of somatic or germline origin. Nevertheless, both cohorts show that mutations in TP53 are associated with a poor prognosis in both fusion-negative and fusion-positive RMS, with a particularly bleak outcome in fusion-positive RMS.
Ba/F3 cells transfected with EGFR R165Q had levels of p-EGFR, p-STAT5, and p-AKT that were similar to known activating mutation L858R and higher than in cells expressing wild-type EGFR.

The oncogenic potential of somatic EGFR mutations found in colorectal cancer samples were tested. IL-3 independent growth of Ba/F3 cells was achieved when cells were transduced with EGFR R165Q. NIH-3T3 cells expressing R165Q showed a significant increase in colony formation in the presence of EGF, relative to EGFR wild-type cells.

Oncogenic somatic EGFR mutations found in colorectal cancer samples were tested for sensitivity to EGFR inhibitors cetuximab and panitumumab. Ba/F3 cells expressing EGFR R165Q showed a dose-dependent reduction in cell viability in response to both inhibitors, as well as reduced p-EGFR, p-STAT5, and p-AKT. Treatment of NIH-3T3 cells expressing EGFR R165Q with cetuximab or panitumumab resulted in significant decreases in colony formation as well as decreased EGF-induced p-EGFR and p-STAT5 levels, compared to untreated cells. Reduction in p-EGFR was also seen in WiDr colon cancer cells expressing R165Q when treated with either inhibitor. Mouse xenograft models were created using R165Q transformed Ba/F3 cells and showed that tumor size was dramatically decreased when treated with cetuximab or panitumumab.

In a clinical study including 285 patients, KRAS4A low expression is significantly correlated with reduced OS by a multivariate analysis (p = 0.0038). Such significant correlation is observed in the whole cohort and in the cohort of patients don't expressing KRAS mutations.

In a clinical study including 151 patients expressing KRAS WT, KRAS4A low expression is significantly correlated with reduced OS by a multivariate analysis (p = 0.018). Such significant correlation is not observed in patients expressing KRAS mutants.

In a clinical study including 148 patients expressing KRAS mutants, low expression of KRAS4A is significantly associated with decreased OS (p = 2.72 x 10^-3) and low proportion of KRAS4A is also significantly associated with decreased OS (p = 2.50 x 10^-3). Such significant correlation is not observed in the whole cohort (including non mutants).

An in vitro study shows that KRAS4A KO is significantly associated with reduced cell viability when cells are treated with KG5 (p < 0.0001). Moreover KRAS4A KO is significantly associated with reduced cell viability when cells are treated with Rigosertib (p < 0.001).
In an in vitro study, an increased gemcitabine IC50 significantly correlated with increased concentration of TNfnA-D (TNC-L). Resistance reached a platform at 20 ug/ml (p < 0.01).
In a clinical study including 106 patients, over expression of TNC-L is significantly associated with decreased OS by a multivariate analysis (p = 0.0005).
In a clinical study including 164 patients, CEACAM1-L dominant expression is significantly associated with decreased OS by a multivariate analysis (p = 0.02).

In a clinical study including 128 patients, CEACAM1-L dominant expression is significantly associated with decreased recurrence-free survival rate by a multivariate analysis (p = 0.04). Moreover CEACAM1-L dominant expression is significantly associated with decreased disease-specific survival rate (p = 0.013).

In a clinical study including 67 patients with liver metastases, enhanced CEACAM1-S expression in the state of CEACAM-L dominance at the primary tumor invasion front is significantly correlated with decreased recurrence-free survival by a multivariate analysis (p = 0.047). It is also significantly correlated with decreased OS (p = 0.006).

In this retrospective study, 112 adolescents and young adults (AYA; between 15 and 25 years of age; median 21 years) who had a histopathological diagnosis of high-grade gliomas were analyzed. The H3K27 variant has been found in 21 cases (26.3%): 14 non-brainstem diffuse midline gliomas (66.7%; age at diagnosis between 15 and 25 years), 5 diffuse intrinsic pontine gliomas (DIPG; 23.8%; age at diagnosis between 15 and 20 years) and 2 diffuse non-midline glioma cases (9.5%; age at diagnosis between 21 and 23 years). The H3K27 variant in the H3.1 gene was found in 1 DIPG case and the H3K27 variant in the H3.3 gene was found in 18 cases. The H3G34R variant was found in 11 cases (13.7%): 3 anaplastic astrocytoma, grade III and 8 glioblastoma, grade IV cases. The diagnosis median age of H3K27 cases was 20 years and for H3G34R cases was 18 years. In a clinical trial including 105 patients, beta-2 expression is significantly associated with an increased RFS (p = 0.006) and OS (p= 0.0008) by a multivariate analysis. This significative correlation is confirmed in the subgroup of ERalpha positive breast cancer. Moreover beta-5 expression is also significantly correlated with an increased RFS (p < 0.005).

In a clinical trial including 718 patients treated with exemestane (367) or tamoxifen (351), patients treated with tamoxifen and underexpressing beta-1 show a significant correlation with decreased DFS (p= 0.001) and OS (p = 0.005) by a multivariate analysis. Moreover, patients underexpressing beta-1 show a significant correlation with benefit of exemestane over tamoxifen (OS and DFS).
In a clinical study including 903 patients, ERalpha negative patients with no expression of beta-1 is significantly correlated with decreased DFS (p < 0.0001).

Two groups were analyzed for germline VHL mutation where Group 1 (84 individuals) presented with only one hemangioblastoma and no other clinical VHL features and those in Group 2 (4 individuals) presented with multiple hemangioblastomas and no other VHL clinical features. Peripheral blood analysis was conducted of all exons and flanking regions (90 nucleotides upstream and 45 downstream) of the VHL gene (numbered using Genbank accession number L15409). Southern blot, PCR and SSCP were performed. Patient B1 of Group 1 presented with a singular cerebellar hemangioblastoma at age 29 and was found to be harbouring a 7bp frameshift T124del (c.369_371del), referred to in the paper as del 582 GACACAC due to a difference in transcript sequence. She developed pancreatic cysts at age 34.

In a clinical study including 144 patients, nuclear beta-2 expression is significantly correlated with decreased RFS (p < 0.01), decreased MFS (p < 0.01) and PSA failure (p < 0.01). Moreover cytoplasmic beta-5 expression is significantly correlated with decreased MFS (p = 0.03). In a clinical study including 571 patients TN, nuclear (mainly) underexpression of beta-1 is significantly associated with decreased OS (p = 0.007), decreased DFS (p = 0.009) and decreased distant MFS (p = 0.005) by a multivariate analysis.

The efficacy of novel AURKA inhibitor alisertib (MLN8327) was tested alone or in combination with cisplatin in three esophageal adenocarcinoma cell lines (FLO-1, OE19 and OE33) that overexpress AURKA. Flow cytometry analysis of cell cycle progression showed that treatment with alisertib or alisertib plus cisplatin caused increased cell death and cell cycle transition delay, with combination treatment having a significantly stronger effect. Similar results were seen in cell viability and colony formation assays, with combination treatment having significantly stronger inhibitory effects than monotherapy. FLO-1 and OE33 xenograft tumors showed significantly more growth inhibition when treated with alisertib and cisplatin than either therapy alone.

The DNMT3A mutation R736H within the tetramer interface has been identified in adult AML patients. Functional analysis showed that this mutation disrupts tetramerization as seen in a gel shift assay. R736H caused an 8-fold reduction in enzyme activity, as well as decreased substrate affinity and increased dissociation rate. DNMT3A R736H also showed minimal activation in the presence of DNMT3L, compared to wild-type.

12 patients with supratentorial hemangioblastoma were studied at Le Kremlin-Bicêtre University. Other phenotypes included: 6 patients with pancreatic cysts, 1 patient with an endocrine pancreatic tumor, 5 patients with renal cell carcinoma, 3 patients with phaeochromocytoma, and 6 patients with retina hemangioblastomas, although specific phenotypes for each patient was not described. Blood samples were isolated from patients and the coding sequence and flanking intronic sequences were directly sequenced. Quantitative Southern blotting and multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification studies were performed to detect large genomic rearrangements. Two related patients were found with the germline p.Arg167Gln mutation. Patient 11, was a female patient diagnosed with hemangioblastoma of the optic nerve at age 35. She underwent surgery and was classified as "alive without disease". Patient 12, was a male diagnosed with suprasellar hemangioblastoma at age 30. His tumor could not be resected due to its high vascularization. He was followed up 10 years later and died due to the hemangioblastoma.

Oncogenic somatic EGFR mutations found in colorectal cancer samples were tested for sensitivity to EGFR inhibitors cetuximab and panitumumab. Ba/F3 cells expressing EGFR R222C showed a dose-dependent reduction in cell viability in response to both inhibitors, as well as reduced p-EGFR, p-STAT5, and p-AKT. Treatment of NIH-3T3 cells expressing EGFR R222C with cetuximab or panitumumab resulted in significant decreases in colony formation as well as decreased EGF-induced p-EGFR and p-STAT5 levels, compared to untreated cells. Reduction in p-EGFR was also seen in WiDr colon cancer cells expressing R222C when treated with either inhibitor. Mouse xenograft models were created using R222C transformed Ba/F3 cells and showed that tumor size was dramatically decreased when treated with cetuximab or panitumumab.

Ba/F3 cells expressing EGFR S492R showed a dose-dependent reduction in cell viability as well as reduced p-EGFR, p-STAT5, and p-AKT in response to panitumumab but not cetuximab. Mouse xenograft models were created using S492R transformed Ba/F3 cells and showed that tumor size was dramatically decreased when treated with panitumumab, but tumor size did not decrease with cetuximab treatment.

41 non-related patients with retinal angiomatosis presenting in the Benjamin Franklin University Eye Clinic between 1988 to 1999 Germany were evaluated for the presence of other VHL lesions. VHL disease was diagnosed clinically in 33 patients based on the presence of other severe VHL lesions (spinal hemangioblastoma 45% prevalence, cerebellar hemangioblastoma 42% prevalence, renal cysts 39% prevalence, pancreatic cyst 39% prevalence, renal carcinoma 18% prevalence, PCC 18% prevalence). Blood samples were taken and analyzed by PCR and single-strand conformational polymorphism (SSCP).VHL germline mutations were identified in 27 out of 29 VHL families who underwent genetic testing. This patient (group 9) with VHL-related retinal angiomatosis, was found to have germline missense c.264G>C mutation in the VHL gene (stated as 477G>C in the paper which used the Latif sequence as reference). No other affected family members were described for this patient. Other VHL lesions harbored by the patients were not specified.

Characterization of hepatoblastoma (HB) with whole-exome sequencing identified recurrent CTNNB1 mutations in 12 of 15 tumors. All 12 impacted exon 3, including 4 missense mutations at position G34 (G34V [n=3], G34E [n=1]) and 8 deletions encompassing all or part of exon 3. In 3 cases, the CTNNB1 mutation was the only alteration identified. Targeted genotyping of an additional 33 primary tumors and cell lines revealed an overall CTNNB1 mutation frequency in hepatoblastoma of 72.5%.

disease: Head And Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma
evidence_statement: This retrospective preclinical study assessed the efficacies of cetuximab, afatinib, and erlotinib towards head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) & esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) cell lines expressing the EGFR amplification mutation. According to the results of a copy number assay, OSC-20 and KYSE-30 cell lines expressing EGFR amplification mutation exhibited high levels of EGFR copy number gains greater than or equal to 5 copies. Both cell lines with high levels of EGFR copy number gains were shown to be insensitive towards cetuximab, afatinib and erlotinib treatments respectively (OSC-20 & KYSE-30 IC50s = >200 mg/L & >200 mg/L (cetuximab), 1.33 uM & 0.54 uM (afatinib), 13.07 uM & 3.84 uM (erlotinib)).

In an in vitro study, an esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) cell line KYSE150 expressing ERBB3 (HER3) D297Y mutation was associated with insensitivity to cetuximab, afatinib, and erlotinib treatments respectively (IC50 = >200 mg/L, 15.70 uM, and 0.78 uM). Sensitivity was determined by assessing cell proliferation.
