evidence_statement: This retrospective preclinical study assessed the efficacy of afatinib towards head-and-neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) human cell lines expressing ERBB4 (HER4) G1109C mutation. According to the various datasets in cBioPortal, genomic alterations in HNSCC cell lines were shown to be relatively frequent in the HER4 domain (~5%). In an in vitro experiment, a HNSCC SAS HER4 G1109C expressing cell line was shown to be hypersensitive towards the afatinib treatment (IC50 = 0.020 uM). To further support this claim, mice xenografts were injected with the SAS HER4 G1109C expressing cell line and then they were treated with afatinib at 5 mg/kg and 15 mg/kg concentrations. After a period of 15 days, both concentrations significantly reduced tumor growth of mice xenografts compared to the vehicle (i.e. control). In another in vitro experiment, HEK293 and NIH3T3 cell lines expressing either HER4 G1109C or E317K mutations showed that there was enhanced cellular growth in both cell lines compared to the controls. However, cellular growth stopped for both cell lines after being treated with low concentrations of afatinib (0.01 uM). To further understand the molecular mechanisms surrounding this HER4 mutation, SAS HER4 G1109C and OSC-19 HER4 wild-type expressing cell lines were treated with varying concentrations of afatinib. Cleaved PARP and cleaved capase-3 signaling increased in the SAS cell line compared to the OSC-19 cell line. From the previous results, the authors suggest that apoptosis was induced through the inhibition of HER4 signaling when the SAS HER4 G1109C cell line is treated with low concentrations of afatinib.

Multiple retrospective preclinical experiments were investigating the functional role of ERBB4 (HER4) G1109C mutation in various cell lines. HEK293 and NIH3T3 cell lines expressing either ERBB4 (HER4) G1109C or E317K mutations showed an increase of HER4 phosphorylation activity compared to the aforementioned cell lines expressing the HER4 wild-type. Similar results are shown when HEK293 G1109C expressing cell line is incubated in serum-free medium where the NRG-1 ligand increased cellular growth and HER4 phosphorylation. However, based on the results from the experiments, the authors interpret that the HER4 G1109C mutation is not correlated to the response of the NRG-1 ligand. Additionally, the NIH3T3 HER4 G1109C cell line exhibited both transformational and tumorigenic abilities (5/5) similar to the NIH3T3 HER4 E317K expressing cell line (5/5). Furthermore, the controls of this study did not exhibit any transformational and tumorigenic abilities (0/0) compared to the aforementioned cell lines. Lastly, both HEK293 HER4 G1109C and HEK293 HER4 E317K expressing cell lines showed increased phosphorylation levels in EGFR, HER2, and HER3 domains compared to the HEK293 wild-type expressing cell line. From these results, the authors interpret that the HER4 G1109C mutation is an activating oncogenic mutation that has transforming and tumorigenic capabilities and could trigger other HER family members while functioning as a heterodimer.

Multiple retrospective preclinical experiments were investigating the functional role of ERBB4 (HER4) E317K mutation in various cell lines. HEK293 and NIH3T3 cell lines expressing either ERBB4 (HER4) G1109C or E317K mutations showed an significant increase of HER4 phosphorylation activity compared to the aforementioned cell lines expressing the HER4 wild-type. Additionally, the HEK293 HER4 G1109C and HEK293 HER4 E317K expressing cell lines showed increased phosphorylation levels in EGFR, HER2, and HER3 domains compared to the HEK293 wild-type expressing cell line. Lastly, the NIH3T3 HER4 E317K cell line exhibited both transformational and tumorigenic abilities (5/5) similar to the NIH3T3 HER4 G1109C expressing cell line (5/5). Furthermore, the controls of this study did not exhibit any transformational and tumorigenic abilities (0/0) compared to the aforementioned cell lines.

This retrospective preclinical study assessed the efficacy of afatinib towards esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) cell lines expressing EGFR L861Q mutation. In one experiment, a ESCC KYSE270 EGFR L861Q expressing cell line was shown to be hypersensitive towards the afatinib treatment (IC50 = 0.0072 uM). In another experiment, mice xenografts were injected with the KYSE270 cell line and then they were treated with afatinib at concentrations of 5 mg/kg and 15 mg/kg. After a period of 15 days, both concentrations significantly decreased tumor growth of mice xenografts compared to the vehicle (i.e. control). Lastly, KYSE270 EGFR L861Q and KYSE50 EGFR wild-type cell lines were treated with differing concentrations of afatinib. At 0.01 uM of afatinib, EGFR, AKT, and ERK1/2 phosphorylation signaling was significantly inhibited in the KYSE270 cell line compared to the KYSE50 cell line. Conversely, cleaved PARP and cleaved capase-3 signaling increased in the KYSE270 cell line compared to the KYSE50 cell line. From the previous results, the authors suggest that apoptosis was induced through the inhibition of EGFR signaling when the KYSE270 expressing L861Q mutation cell line is treated with low concentrations of afatinib, thereby indicating that this mutation is an activating oncogenic mutation.

Somatic mutations in ERBB3 were identified in ~11% of gastric and colon cancers. Relative to wild-type ERBB3, the G284R mutation in the presence of ERBB2 resulted in increased anchorage independent growth in immortalized mouse epithelial cells (IMCE), MCF10A cells, and Ba/F3 cells. In line with these results, G284R in the presence of ERBB2 caused increases in levels of pERBB3, pAKT, and pERK1/2, relative to wild-type ERBB3. G284R mutated cells implanted into mice were tumorigenic and resulted in reduced survival relative to wild-type ERBB3. In addition, several inhibitors of ERBB2 or ERBB3 were able to reduce survival of BaF3 cells expressing G284R in the presence of ERBB2.

A novel rearrangement event between KIAA-1549 and BRAF was found in 66% (29 of 44) of pilocytic astrocytomas. The fusion gene was shown to delete the N-terminal BRAF auto-regulatory domain which leads to constitutive activation of BRAF in vitro. Cos7 cells were transfected with two isoforms of KIAA1549-BRAF (both exon 16:exon 9), BRAF V600E, or wildtype BRAF and evaluated activity via BRAF kinase assay. Both fusion isoforms showed similar or higher kinase activity than V600E transfected cells. NIH3T3 cells transfected with V600E or the short fusion isoform also demonstrated anchorage-independent growth in soft agarose.

In an in vivo study, mice injected with v242 show significantly reduced survival compared to mice expressing WT (p < 0.001) when treated with anti-PD-L1 antibody. Moreover mixing only 1% MC38 cells with v242 variants and 99% of cells that exposed WT PD-L1 induced resistance to PD-L1 blockade in the MC38 xenograft model. Anti-PD-1 antibody treatment overcame the resistance mediated by the secreted PD-L1 variants.

Study evaluated 42 cases with aggressive fibromatosis were genotyped for the M541L (c.1621 A>C; rs3822214) was evaluated and compared to gender- and age-matched 126 healthy controls. In 4/7 cases with the M541L variant, non-neoplastic tissue available and the M541L variant was found in both the neoplastic and non-neoplastic components. In the 126 matched normal controls, 21 individuals were heterozygous and 1 was homozygous for the M541L variant. An additional historical set of 166 controls showed 25 heterozygous and 1 homozygous individual. No statistically significant difference between cases and either control cohort was shown.

Primary imatinib resistance is caused by a deletion polymorphism in intron 2 (see EID 1280 and 1281). An in vitro study shows that the deletion biases BIM splicing from exon 4 to exon 3. Adding ASOs that increased exon 4 levels in BIM deletion-containing cells restore imatinib sensitivity (p < 0.05).
In an in vitro study, cells transduced with CD19 delta5-6 and CD19 delta2 show significantly no response to CART-19 therapy compared to CD19-FL transduced cells.
In a clinical study including 200 patients, deletion polymorphism is not significantly associated with resistance to imatinib (p = 0.116).

In an in vitro study, SKMEL-239 cells were exposed to 2uM vemurafenib for 2 months. Five independent cell lines were recovered and assessed for resistance alterations. Three cell lines expressing p61BRAF(V600E) isoform, lacking exons 4-8 which includes the RAS-binding domain (RBD), have elevated pERK and pMEK and are resistant to vemurafenib. The cell lines did not have other known resistance alterations such as BRAF or RAS mutation, upregulated receptor tyrosine kinase activity, or COT overexpression. Analysis of BRAF locus by array CGH showed no evidence of structural deletion in the BRAF gene. Expression of p61BRAF(V600E) isoform in 293H cells, parental SKMEL-239, or HT-29 cells caused a lack of ERK signaling inhibition by vemurafenib. Moreover, several isoforms lacking the RBD were observed in 6/19 patients with acquired vemurafenib resistance, including one patient with the exact variant identified in the resistant cell line

A 62 year old male with melanoma was treated with vemurafenib and achieved PFS of 148 days and 47% tumor reduction. Upon progression tumor samples were assessed for mutations in BRAF and NRAS by PCR. This patient was found to have a BRAF splice variant lacking exons 4-8 and retaining the V600E mutation, known as isoform p61BRAF(V600E). In vitro experiments showed that this isoform can arise as a result of continuous vemurafenib treatment and results in acquired resistance characterized by the inability of vemurafenib to inhibit elevated levels of pMEK and pERK.

Novel variant found through WES on all affected individuals of a family with short stature. The segregation of the variant was confirmed by sanger sequencing (ACMG: PP1). The affected members presented milder phenotypes of hypochondroplasia than the ones described in the literature. The variant was predicted to be possibly damaging in several in-silico predictors (align GVGD, SIFT, MutationTaster, PolyPhen and HumVar). Functional studies determined that the variant was activating (activating FGFR3, STAT and ERK/MAP kinase), showing similar results in the transfection studies into cultured cells. Functional modelling of the protein showed that the variant, located in the conserved αC helix, has a critical role in the TKD activation.

A rare variant was found through Sanger sequencing on affected members of a family with short stature. The segregation of the variant was not entirely related to the phenotype since it was present in affected individuals but absent in other affected individuals. The variant is predicted to be benign by in-silico predictors (align GVGD, SIFT, MutationTaster, PolyPhen and HumVar). Functional studies demonstrated the variant was not activating but the data was not shown.

A case report of a 74 year old female who was diagnosed with MPAL, B/myeloid with bone marrow blasts were positive for myeloperoxidase, CD19, and CD22. Chromosome analysis showed 46,XX,+1,der(1;18)(q10;q10),t(2;16)(q13;q13),t(12;17)(p13;q21). Expression of the TAF15-ZNF384 fusion transcript was confirmed via reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR). Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) on metaphase spreads revealed that the ETV6 signals at 12p13 remained on the der(12)t(12; 17) as well as on a normal chromosome 12 (data not shown).

Treatment shows good tolerability and durability of response in both groups of patients.

Overall response rate was 21% in this clinical trial with Pexidartinib on relapsed or refractory AML patients with FLT3-ITD. Forty two out of the total 90 patients were tested for FLT3 KD mutations before treatment. Four patients were F691L positive, and three of them had no response to Pexidartinib, one of them achieved a incomplete hematologic recovery, the F691L was detected in 2.58% of non-ITD containing FLT3 alleles. This patient acquired new D835Y mutation and the F691L was not detectable at the time of Pexidartinib relapse. Of note, all 4 patients were treated below the recommended phase 2 dosage of 3000 mg per day. The response rate and any other FLT3 KD mutations were not particularly described for those 38 F691L negative patients.

Using AC220 (Quizartinib) treatment in Ba/F3 cell lines in a in vitro saturation mutagenesis assay, variants in four residues in FLT3 kinase domain were found, including E608, F691, D835 and Y842. Except for E608K, cell lines bearing these variants were verified to be AC220 resistant in separate cell viability assays. Molecular modeling revealed that substitutions at the gate residue F691 with non-aromatic residues such as leucine may affect interaction with AC220. This study also reported data from 8 FLT3-IDT positive AML patients treated with AC220 monotherapy, all of them were found to bear FLT3 kinase domain variants at relapse either at F691 or D835 on the FLT3-IDT alleles. F691L were seen in 3 patients.

t(3;21)(q26.2;q22) is a rare variant of AML, occurring in approximately 1% of cases. It carries a very poor prognosis with none of the reported patients surviving longer than 28 months and with an average survival time of 12 months from time of diagnosis.

In this study >1000 well-characterized pediatric and adult AML cases were screened using a NUP98/NSD1-specific RT-PCR. In the pediatric cohort (n = 293; age, 0-18 years), NUP98/NSD1 was present in 16.1% of the cases. The authors identified the cytogenetically cryptic NUP98/NSD1 translocation as an independent factor for dismal clinical outcome for both pediatric and adult patients. The remission rate (CR) of NUP98/NSD1-positive cases in the pediatric cohort was 100%, but 10 of the 12 cases relapsed early. The cumulative incidence of nonresponse/relapse (pCIR) at 4 years was 83 ± 13% for NUP98/NSD1-positive versus 45 ± 3% for negative cases (P < .001). NUP98/NSD1 cases had a poor event-free survival (pEFS) and overall survival (pOS) (4-years pEFS, 8 ± 8% vs 46 ± 3%, P < .001; and 4-years pOS, 31 ± 16% vs 64 ± 3%, P = .011 for NUP98/NSD1-positive vs negative cases, respectively).

In the study involving 1725 B-ALL patients, 264 were identified by microarray-based algorithm to have a Ph-like expression signature. Next generation sequencing (RNAseq, WGS, and/or WES) performed on 154 Ph-like patients revealed 91% possessed genomic alterations activating kinase signaling with 96 (62%) involving rearrangements. In one young adult male, an in-frame PAG1-ABL2 fusion (exon 8 and exon 6) with the ABL2 tyrosine kinase domain intact was identified and confirmed by RT-PCR. This patient, evaluated by WES and RNA-seq, also harbored IKZF1, PAX5, EBF1, and VPREB deletions, and was designated Ph-like non CRLF2.

This study assessed the potential for mutated genes associated with urothelial bladder cancers as candidates for platinum-based neoadjuvant therapy. Nineteen patients (18 male, 3 female) diagnosed with urothelial bladder cancer were assessed, and experiments were performed in silico. The E86Q mutation was identified in one case, and was predicted to be deleterious (0) by Sorting Intolerant From Tolerant (SIFT), damaging (0.998) by Polymorphism Phenotyping 2 (PolyPhen2), and with mutational impact in the top 1% of variants (25.4) by Combined Annotation Dependent Deletion (CADD). The authors concluded that the E86Q mutation was “likely” to be pathogenic (p. 7) and as such, patients harboring the mutation would be receptive to platinum-based neoadjuvant therapy in combination with the results of two cases with another ERRC2 mutation (E606Q) treated by platinum-based chemotherapies.

In this study of pediatric cases of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) comparing the prognosis of several recurrent translocation partners for the KMT2A/MLL gene at 11q23, the specific MLL-AF6 fusion gene (seen cytogenetically as t(6;11)(q27;q23)) conveys a worse prognosis independent of other prognostic factors. This finding has been previously reported in adult populations, but is first described here in pediatric populations. These cases are also associated with higher WBC and age at presentation compared to other KMT2A-rearranged AML cases.

These translocations must be identified by specific FISH studies due to heterogeneity in the breakpoints.

Ultimately, age and sex SIRs proved the greater indicator of cancer risks. This study found, PHTS (p<0.05), that women were twice as likely as men to develop PHTS cancers.

phenotypes: Diabetes mellitus,Renal cyst,Renal cell carcinoma,Hemangioblastoma,Spinal cord lesion
evidence_statement: A 38-year-old male patient presented with a hemangioblastoma, renal cyst, renal cell carcinoma, spinal cord lesion, and diabetes mellitus. Sanger sequencing revealed a missense mutation in the VHL gene c.227_229delTCT. No other family members underwent genetic testing. The patient's mother (I-2) was deceased, and the cause may have been associated with VHL. The patient's father (I-1) suffered from hypertension and diabetes. One of the patient's sisters (II-3) suffered from diabetes, and the remaining siblings had no history of hypertension, diabetes, or tumor.

Patients originated from 4 international (UK, Netherlands, Germany, and US) studies, and included 16 B-cell precursor ALL (B-ALL) patients (aged 2-29 years) with SSBP2-CSF1R fusions arising from different abnormalities involving chromosome 5. Examples include balanced translocations [t(5;5)(q14;q33)], duplications [dup(5)(q14q33)], a paracentric inversion [inv(5)(q15q33)], and other complex rearrangements. Of the 16 patients, 14 patients were noted to be Ph-like (2 were noted not applicable). Treatment protocols ranged from Standard to High and all patients achieved complete remission. Among 14 patients with available MRD data, 7 patients remained positive at the end of induction therapy. Among 9 patients classified as high risk by NCI and treated on high-risk arms of NCI respective protocol, 5 patients remained positive at end of induction therapy.

In a cohort Dutch/German patients (age <15 years) with B cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia, 14 tyrosine kinase fusions were identified among 77 BCR-ABL1-like cases, and zero were identified among 76 non-BCR-ABL1-like B-other cases. RCSD1-ABL2 was identified in a male BCR-ABL1-like patient which is confirmed by RT-PCR and TLA. Karyotype of this patient was 46,XY/42~ 46,XY,inc. FISH and microarray data were not available. The exons involved in the RCSD1-ABL2 fusion in this patient was novel, involving fusion of RCSD1 exon 3 to ABL2 exon 5. Using Affymetrix U133 Plus 2 arrays, the percentile in rank of the tyrosine kinase gene expression among 153 B-other BCP-ALL cases has determined to be 1%. In addition to the fusion, he was also found to have EBF1 exon 16 deletion determined by MLPA, and, IKZF1 deletion of exons 2-3. This patient was followed up for ~4 years. He undergone bone marrow transplant, and was treated for Dutch Childhood Oncology Group trial ALL10-hR, He had good prednison window response, the morphological response after induction therapy was unknown, and the minimal residual disease after the first induction course of chemotherapy (day 33) and before consolidation (day 79) were both high. In conclusion, the authors suggested that, in the fusion-positive BCR-ABL1-like group, IKZF1 deletions were commoly seen, the non/late response rate and levels of minimal residual disease were higher, the 8-year cumulative incidence of relapse were comparable. Therefore the tyrosine kinase fusion positive cases are high risk.

In a study of Transcriptome sequencing to identify fusions and mutations on 560 ALL Patients enrolled on a multi-center Alliance, two patients were identified to carry the RCSD1-ABL2 fusion. One was a 22.3 year old male patient diagnosed with Ph-like B-ALL ABL1/ABL2 subgroup, He was under protocol S9400 by Southwestern Oncology Group (SWOG). He did not carry any mutations in 4 RAS pathway genes: NRAS, KRAS, NF1 and PTPN11. Gene expression profile from RNAseq was available for this patient but not described. Another patient was a 18.5 year old male patient diagnosed with Ph-like B-ALL ABL1/ABL2 subgroup. He was treated under COG protocol AALL0232, and no mutation in 4 RAS pathway genes: NRAS, KRAS, NF1 and PTPN11. Gene expression profile from RNAseq was not available for this patient.

A 20-year-old male patient was diagnosed with precursor B-ALL (immunophenotype: CD34+, DR+, TdT+, CD19+, CD20 partial+, CD10+, cyCD79a+, CD24+, surface/cyCD22+, cyIgM+, sIg−, MPO−, CD13+, CD33+). Chromosome analysis identified a normal male karyotype, 46,XY[20]. RT-PCR based low-density array of 15 selected genes of the leukemia cells have identified an expression pattern consistent with Ph-like B-ALL. CMA identified a 127 kb deletion affecting the IKZF1 gene, as well as a complex rearrangement involving 1q24.2, with two proximal deletion and a distal deletion separated by a 620 kb undeleted fragment. Analysis of the breakpoints showed that this is consistent with the formation of RCSD1–ABL2 fusion, which is confirmed by RT-PCR. Sanger sequencing confirmed the breakpoints to be exon 3 of RCSD1 and exon 5 of ABL2. The patient received a pediatric intensive four-drug regimen including vincristine/peg-asparaginase/daunorubicin/ prednisone with intrathecal cytarabine and methotrexate. MDR was present in the marrow at day 15 (95% cellularity, 60 – 70% blasts) and day 29 (50% cellularity, 15% residual disease by flow) of induction. Later the patient was treated by additional therapy with cytoxan, cytarabine, 6-mercaptopurine (6MP), decadron, vincristine, peg-asparaginase and intrathecal therapy with methotrexate. After 8 weeks of treatment, patient presented with hypocellular bone marrow, consistent with morphologic remission but high-level MRD by flow cytometry. After additional consolidation therapy resulting in low level MRD, the patient proceeded to hematopoietic stem cell transplant from an unrelated donor and received a total body irradiation and etoposide based preparative regimen. He remains in complete remission 8 months post-transplant, with no evidence of MRD.

In a study of 1389 consecutively enrolled, newly diagnosed patients with B-ALL, two male patients with high risk Ph-like disease were identified to carry RCSD1-ABL2 fusion by RT-PCR and are eligible to have dasatinib added to their backbone chemotherapy regimen.

A 5 year-old male patient with B-ALL was described with an initial WBC of 57,700 (Supplementary Appendix 2). Chromosome analysis showed 47,XXYc with a confirmed diagnosis of Klinefelter syndrome. FISH showed disruption of ABL2, and no sign for BCR-ABL1. RT-PCR showed RCSD1-ABL2 fusion. MRD levels were 1.2% after a 4- drug induction. The patient remained MRD positive 6 months into therapy (0.029%). He was treated using imatinib based on the poor MRD response and ABL2 rearrangement. Two months later no MRD was identified in marrow and he remained in complete remission approximately one year post-diagnosis, receiving chemotherapy plus imatinib. The LDA analysis was consistent with Ph-like expression pattern.

To investigate the functional role and targetability of the tyrosine kinase fusions identified in Ph-like ALL, murine Arf−/− pre-B ALL expressing tyrosine kinase fusions were developed. It showed that IL-7–dependent Arf−/− Mice transplanted with cells expressing RCSD1-ABL2 in the presence of a dominant negative isoform of Ikaros, IK6, have developed leukemia with a median latency of 36 days, compared to mice with empty vector which were still alive up to day 300. At end-stage disease, for tumors harboring RCSD1-ABL2 a significant increase in spleen weight was observed(450 ± 42 mg, n = 5; P = .0002). Additionally, a >70% replacement of GFP/RFP+ cells in the bone marrow with infiltration of B220+ leukemic blasts were observed in the spleen, bone marrow, liver, and brain, and a pre-B immunophenotype (CD43+, B220+, CD19+, BP-1+, and IgM−), confirming that the fusion can induce the development of ALL. Bosutinib was shown to be effective against Ba/F3 cells expressing RCSD1-ABL2 fusion, with IC50 values of 2 nM. Dasatinib-treated mice using PDX models in a preclinical studies showed reduction of leukemic burden, compared with vehicle-treated mice, in lower peripheral blasts, spleen weight, and infiltration into the central nervous system at the end of treatment. Phosphorylation of STAT5 and CRKL was also attenuated in cells harvested from dasatinib-treated mice compared with vehicle-treated mice.

Using molecular docking simulations, the authors computationally screened a library of clinical compounds and identified KX2-391(Tirbanibulin, an SRC/tubulin dual inhibitor) to be a candidate FLT3 inhibitor. The effect was verified in cellular thermal shift assay and proliferation assay with Ba/F3 cells. Ba/F3 cells bearing FLT3-ITD-F691 were 10-fold more sensitive to KX2-391 than Ba/F3 cells without the mutations, 0.032 uM vs 0.372 uM. The effect was tested with in vivo leukemia model of Ba/F3-ITD-F691 as well, KX2-391 prolonged the survival period from 12 days in the control to 23.5 days in the treated (P<0.0001), without significant weight loss or other toxicity signs.

301 were enrolled in a prospective clinical protocol to evaluate the natural history of vHL-associated pancreatic lesions (NCT00062166). Of these, 69 patients with pancreatic manifestations of vHL disease and missense VHL mutations were included in the current study. Individual patient phenotype was not described, but overall of the 60 patients, 57 had RCC, 41 had CNS hemangioblastomas, 28 had retinal hemangioblastoma, 23 had pheochromocytoma. 36/69 patients were female and the mean age was 50.5 years old. All patients underwent genetic testing using Sanger sequencing and Southern Blotting. One patient was listed with this missense mutation, c.361G>T. ACMG: PP4

In a phase II study of JAK2 inhibitor ruxolitinib, patients with advanced relapsed or refractory Hodgkin lymphoma examined potential JAK2 amplification in 12 patients which found JAK1 amplification to be in one sample, and polysomy affirming potential hyperdiploidy in the remaining samples (n=12). In response to ruxolitinib, the patient exhibiting JAK2 amplification obtained a partial response. Although this clinical trial did not meet its primary efficacy goal (with an overall response rate of 9.4%), biological indicators such as JAK2 amplification/JAK2 polysomy and partial patient response may suggest possible combinational therapies to improve outcomes.

therapies: Multi-subtype Natural Human Leukocyte Interferon Alpha
evidence_statement: The examination of interferon-resistant melanoma cell lines in relation to STAT5 expression, indicated a correlation between overexpression and resistance to interferon α (IFNα) immunotherapy. From an analysis of various melanoma cell lines such as D10, MM96, Mel19, and WM164, a consistent presentation of enhanced protein expression of STAT5 was demonstrated. Importantly, overexpression of STAT5 in cell lines D10 and MM96 was substantially associated with resistance to IFNα. To validate overexpression of STAT5 to be the main contributing factor of IFNα resistance, silencing of STAT5 was performed in an overexpressing STAT5 cell line MM96. In comparison to the control of MM96 cells left untreated, successfully transfected MM96 cells STAT5-specific siRNA efficaciously demonstrated antiproliferative effects of IFNα immunotherapy. These results are indicative of the resistance of IFNα immunotherapy in advanced cell lines of melanoma to be dependent upon overexpression of STAT5.

From a phase one clinical trial, pediatric patients with refractory CNS malignancies were administered 300-1150 mg/m2 twice daily of ERBB2 and EGFR inhibitor lapatinib. The maximum-tolerated dose was established at 900 mg/m2 twice daily, regardless of steroid use. From the 59 patients, 12 patients, including 5 diagnosed with ependymoma, demonstrated a prolonged stable disease in response to lapatinib. In comparison to other CNS tumors, pretrial samples from patients with ependymoma tumors displayed high expression of ERBB2 and activation of ERBB2 signaling. Due to the high expression of ERBB2 receptors, targeting ERBB2 may be a viable treatment for patients with ependymoma tumors and other high expressing ERBB2 brain tumors.

The F691L/I mutation in FLT3 kinase domain conferred resistence to AC220 (Quizartinib). These mutations were identified by in vitro screening assays and from AML patients who developed resistance to Quizartinib. Ba/F3 cells with FLT3-ITD or FLT3-ITD with F691L or F691I mutation were treated with increasing concentrations of Quizartinib. Cell proliferation studies for 24 h and FLT3 autophosphorylation as a measurement of its activity after 90 min of inhibitor treatment showed the most resistance in these assays compared to other FLT3 kinase domain mutations (N676D and D835Y). These mutations demonstrated a clear shift in the IC50 values by in vitro screening compared to FLT3-ITD alone.

A series of 60 endometrioid endometrial carcinomas were tested for CCND1 expression and amplification. Two samples with CCND1 expression measured via IHC were shown to have somatic mutations but no amplification. The authors propose that alterations at amino acid 287 of CCND1 would affect the ability of GSK-3B to phosphorylate it, inhibiting turnover of CCND1.

The authors propose that alterations at amino acid 287 of CCND1 would affect the ability of GSK-3B to phosphorylate it, inhibiting turnover of CCND1.

In this study, activating FLT3 mutations identified in patients with Acute Myeloid Leukemia were modeled using Ba/F3 cell lines generated by site-directed mutagenesis and transfection. These cells were assessed using proliferation (MTT) assays and signaling analyses, including Western blotting of FLT3 autophosphorylation and downstream pathways. Ba/F3 cells expressing the FLT3 I836S activation loop mutation demonstrated IL-3–independent growth and FLT3 autophosphorylation indicating constitutive activation of FLT3. Autophosphorylation was inhibited in a dose-dependent manner by several FLT3 inhibitors. Drug sensitivity testing across a panel of 13 tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) showed that the I836S mutation exhibited reduced sensitivity to several inhibitors. The authors concluded that FLT3 activating mutations confer differential sensitivity to TKIs and that identification of the specific mutation is important for selecting appropriate targeted therapy in AML.

In this study, FLT3 activating mutations identified in patients with acute myeloid leukemia were modeled using murine Ba/F3 cells generated by site-directed mutagenesis and transfection. These cells were assessed using proliferation (MTT) assays and signaling analyses, including Western blotting of FLT3 autophosphorylation and downstream pathways. Ba/F3 cells expressing the FLT3 I836T mutation demonstrated IL-3–independent growth and FLT3 autophosphorylation, indicating constitutive activation of FLT3. Drug sensitivity testing across a panel of 13 tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) showed that the I836T mutation exhibited reduced sensitivity to several inhibitors. The authors concluded that FLT3 activating mutations, including I836T, promote cytokine-independent proliferation and exhibit differential sensitivity to TKIs and that identification of the specific mutation is important for selecting appropriate targeted therapy in AML.

A lung cancer patient was found to have TP53 V157D and PMS2 R20Q mutations in tumor tissue and distant normal lung tissue. These germline mutations were expressed alone or in combination in A549 lung cancer cell lines and showed increased cell proliferation and colony formation compared to wild-type. Similar results were seen when the mutants were expressed in mouse embryonic fibroblasts and had increased foci formation. An in vivo transgenic drosophila assay showed that these mutations could induce tumorigenesis following exposure to UV irradiation. The mutations were also shown to reduce apoptosis, with a stronger effect when both mutations were present, relative to controls.

This study analyzed 27 formalin-fixed-paraffin-embedded samples of patients with known dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans (DFSP) using a newly designed multiplex RT-PCR assay. The assay identified COL1A1-PDGFB fusion transcripts in all but one DFSP case, which was consistent with concurrent FISH testing on the same samples. The study concluded that COL1A1-PDGFB rearrangements appear more prevalent in DFSP (96%) than previously reported. The use of sensitive molecular assays for detection of COL1A1-PDGFB fusion may improve diagnosis in cases of atypical, variant, or metastatic DFSP.

This was a multi-institutional retrospective cohort study which looked at the prognostic value of CTNNB1 gene mutations in aggressive fibromatosis (also known as desmoid tumor). The study analyzed 101 patients who had undergone surgical resection of confirmed primary extra-abdominal or abdominal wall aggressive fibromatosis. Specimens were reviewed for the presence of T41A, S45F, and 45P mutations on the CTNNB1 gene. Mutations were found in 76 patients, with T41A being most common (n = 49), followed by S45F (n = 18), and 45P (n = 3). The 5-year cumulative risk of recurrence was 22.8%. Further analysis revealed that patients with an S45F mutation had a 5-year recurrence risk of 63.8% and an 8.5-fold higher risk of recurrence compared to patients with wild type tumors (P=0.006).

A pediatric case of ganglioglioma was previously reported (PMID: 29434027) to harbor a BRAF p.T599dup variant (observed at VAF of 5.2%). The patient had a partial resection and was then treated with Vinblastine for 9 months. Regular tumor monitoring was performed by MRI. At 9 months post surgery, progression was observed and a second resection performed. The BRAF p.T599dup variant was again detected in this second tumor sample (observed at VAF of 5.9%). Followup imaging 3 months after the second surgery revealed further progression. Treatment with dabrafenib and trametinib was initiated. Followup scans showed reduced tumor size followed by stable disease on therapy for 15 months at the time of this report.

Functional analysis was performed for ERBB2 transmembrane domain (TMD) and juxtamembrane domain (JMD) mutations. The JMD mutation Q709L was expressed in BaF3 cells and showed a significant increase in IL-3 independent cell survival as well as increased pERBB2, most notably in the presence of wt ERBB2. Expression of Q709L in MCF10A cells resulted in spheroid growth in a matrigel assay in the absence of exogenous EGF, confirming the oncogenic potential of this mutation. Structural modeling suggested that a hydrophobic residue at position 709, such as leucine, would stabilize the dimerization interface of the C-lobe and juxtamembrane latch required for allosteric activation of kinase activity.

Zhang et al. (2013) studied 151 tumors from 149 patients. The H3F3A p.K27M variant has been reported in 3 tumors (1.9%). The first sample (SJLGG037_D) was of a less than 3-year-old male patient screened by whole genome sequencing and RNA-seq methods, who had diffuse glioma located in the cerebral cortex (Figure 1). The second sample (SJLGG001284_D1) was of a female who had surgery at 10 years of age, affected with diffuse glioma located in the diencephalon, and also carried BRAF p.V600E variant (Supplementary Table 4, Figure 2). The third sample (SJLGG010126_D1) was of a female who had surgery at 8 years of age, affected with diffuse glioma located in the diencephalon, and also carried KRAS p.Q61H variant (Supplementary Table 4, Figure 2).

150 index patients with pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma were evaluated. Phenotypic data were collected and germline mutations in five susceptibility genes (RET, VHL, SDHB, SDHD and SDHC) were tested. Out of 30 patients with familial presentation, 13 were clinically diagnosed as VHL syndrome. A 20 year old Asian Indian female presented with bilateral pheochromocytoma with pancreatic cysts. Using PCR and Sanger sequencing through peripheral blood, genetic testing confirmed a mutation at c.588_588dupA of the VHL gene. Family history is positive.

Gessi, et al. (2015) studied 30 primary spinal diffuse high-grade gliomas (HGG) and 6 diffuse astrocytomas. The H3F3A p.K27M variant has been reported in 16 HGG (including 2 anaplastic gangliogliomas, 3 anaplastic astrocytomas, and 11 glioblastomas) and in 1 diffuse astrocytoma. Out of 16 HGG H3F3A p.K27M cases, 10 were between 4 and 17 years of age, 3 were between 18 and 40 years of age, and 3 were more than 40 years of age (Fig. 1f). The authors also noted that the mean age of adult patients with variant (34 years) was lower than the mean age of patients without variant (53 years; Fig. 1f).

The H3F3A p.K27M variant has been reported in 2 GG: first was from 6 years old female metastatic patient (deceased with an overall length of survival of 1.61 years; Table 1); the second was from 13 years old male patient (deceased with an overall length of survival of 0.79 years; Table 1).

A retrospective study reviewed cases of 23 patients with advanced and complicated VHL eye disease who underwent pars plana vitrectomy in the years 1999 to 2012 that were a part of 223 VHL patients consulted at the International Hereditary Cancer Center and Polish VHL Registry. Genetic molecular analysis was performed in 22/23 patients through PCR and MLPA, and 24 eyes from 23 patients were studied. A germline mutation was found in 3 individuals: A 30 year old (patient 8), a 32 year old (patient 10), and a 31 year old (patient 11). All were documented with a c.226delTTC mutation resulting in an inframe deletion with previous history of HbCNS. Patients were all examined in a study of advanced VHL eye disease and had multiple retinal capillary hemangioblastomas requiring surgery. Since patients were listed 'by eye' it is impossible to determine how many patients listed above actually represent unique patients.

A multicenter, retrospective study that included 1389 consecutively enrolled, newly diagnosed patients with B-lineage acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL). There were 3 patients that harbored SSPB2-CSF1R fusions that were classified as high risk, Ph-like, ABL1-class kinase group.

An 18-year-old male with B-ALL presented with hyperleukocytosis (WBC 171×10⁹/L, 90% blasts). Conventional cytogenetics showed a normal male karyotype (46,XY), and FISH/PCR were negative for ETV6-RUNX1, BCR-ABL1, TCF3-PBX1, and KMT2A. MLPA identified an IKZF1 deletion (exons 4–8) along with deletions in PAX5 and EBF1. Following high-risk CAALL-F01 therapy, bone marrow evaluation at day 35 demonstrated induction failure with persistent disease (~3% blasts). Subsequent RT-MLPA detected a ZC3HAV1(exon 12)::ABL2(exon 3) fusion. The open-label phase 3 BEACON CRC trial included 665 patients with BRAF V600E-mutated metastatic CRC. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive encorafenib, binimetinib, and cetuximab (triplet-therapy group); encorafenib and cetuximab (doublet-therapy group); or the investigators’ choice of either cetuximab and irinotecan or cetuximab and FOLFIRI. The median overall survival was 8.4 months (95% CI, 7.5 to 11.0) in the doublet-therapy group and 5.4 months (95% CI, 4.8 to 6.6) in the control group, with a significantly lower risk of death compared to the control group (hazard ratio for death doublet-group vs. control, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.45 to 0.79; P<0.001). The confirmed response rate was 26% (95% CI, 18 to 35) in the triplet-therapy group, 20% in the doublet-therapy group (95% CI 13 to 29) and 2% (95% CI, 0 to 7) in the control group (doublet group vs. control P<0.001). Median PFS was 4.2 months (95% CI, 3.7 to 5.4) in the doublet-therapy group, and 1.5 months (95% CI, 1.5 to 1.7) in the control group (hazard ratio for disease progression doublet-group vs control, 0.40; 95% CI, 0.31 to 0.52, P<0.001).

Expression analysis of multiple cohorts of gastric cancer patients in addition to in vivo selected metastatic cell lines, identified DDR2 as the driver of peritoneal dissemination. Within the Singaporean and Japan cohorts, samples exhibiting high expression of DDR2 correlated with poor prognosis and peritoneal dissemination. Elevated expression of DDR2 was also found in 58As9 cells in comparison to the parent cell line (HSC-58). To analyze the role of DDR2, a knockout was performed with two shRNAs in presence or absence of collagen. In the presence of collagen 1, cellular proliferation was significantly suppressed. Additionally overall DDR2 knock down also debilitated the capacity of 58As9 cells for invasion and migration. In vivo DDR2 knockdown and transplant of 58As9 cells into mouse models greatly reduced the amount of disseminated metastases and tumor weights within the gastric walls. In analyzing the potential use of dasatinib intraperitoneally and orally, mice treated with dasatinib (50 mg/kg·day) acquired a significant increase in survival times (p < 0.05) in addition to suppressed peritoneal metastasis (p < 0.01) in comparison to the vehicle control. Considering this data DDR2 overexpression may be indicative of a potential therapeutic target.

Validating predominant overexpression of DDR2 in 554 head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) patients indicated the potentiality of utilizing dasatinib as a DDR2 inhibitor. From these patients, 781 tissue samples were acquired and analyzed for protein expression and DDR2 expression was found to be higher within the tumor tissue than in the normal mucosa (p= 0.007). In-vivo analysis of overexpression of DDR2 in the HNSCC cell line FaDu, displayed a 2.5 times higher invasion rate (p<0.01) in comparison to the control GFP cells. Also the HSC-3 cells overexpressing DDR2 showed a 1.4 times higher invasion rate (p < 0.05). Dasatinib pretreatment nearly eradicated all migration and invasion of overexpressing DDR2 cell line FaDu cells (p < 0.001, p < 0.01) while not affecting the control GFP cells. In viewing the other overexpressing cell line, HSC-3, in response to dasatinib pretreatment it was found that the migration and invasion rate was reduced by 60% (p < 0.05 and p < 0.01). Xenograft models demonstrated that DDR2 expression can not only enhance the migratory capacity of FaDu cells when overexpressed (p < 0.0001), but also decrease the migratory effects through regulation of DDR2 expression with the treatment of dasatinib (p < 0.05).

Goodwin, et al. (2014) presented in vivo study on mice carrying the ASPSCR1-TFE3 fusion gene. The results showed that Rosa26-LSL-AT3/CreER mice expressed tumors histological equal to the human’s alveolar soft part sarcoma (ASPS) and recapitulate human’s transcriptome profile. The study also showed that tumors were formed in location high in lactate ), had a high degree of lactate importers, expressed up-regulation of mitochondrial genes, and responded to the addition of lactate with a proliferation of tumor as well as with angiogenesis.

Ishiguro, et al. (2016) presented in vitro functional study on different cell lines. The ASPSCR1-TFE3 (here referred to as ASPL-TFE3) fusion gene induction of expression resulted in cell cycle arrest (Fig.1B) as well as an increased expression of p21 protein on 293 cell line (Suppl. Fig.1). The results on HeLa, p53-/- KATO II I, and 293 cell lines showed that p21 protein expression was increased through ASPSCR1-TFE3 interaction with p21 promotor independently of p53 (Fig.3). Analysis on human mesenchymal stem cells showed that ASPSCR1-TFE3 induced senescence-related β-galactosidase activity (Suppl. Fig2, Fig.4E) and increased levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines (Fig.6).

AURELIA trial indicated substantial improvement in progression-free survival and overall survival in ovarian cancer patients with PD-L1 positive expression in response to bevacizumab plus single regime chemotherapy (BC) treatment (p<0.05). In identifying the clinicopathologic characteristics, over-expression of PD-L1 indicated close association with low histological grade, advanced FIGO stage and ascites volume >2,000 mL (p>0.05). These results are suggestive of over-expression of PD-L1 being associative with more malignant epithelial ovarian cancer phenotypes and expression of PD-L1 potentially corresponding to BC treatment. Additionally combinational therapies of bevacizumab with PD-L1 inhibitor atezolizumab in vivo elicited synergistic effects greater than the control and each single treatment (p<0.05).

Within a multicentre, open-label, phase 3 randomised control trial, investigation of the potential biomarker PD-L1 was found not to potentiate anti-tumor effects in response to atezolizumab in metastatic urothelial carcinoma in comparison to chemotherapy. 931 patients were randomly assigned, 467 were treated with atezolizumab 1200 mg and 464 with chemotherapies (vinflunine 320 mg/m2, paclitaxel 175 mg/m2, or 75 mg/m2 docetaxel). In the patient population with at least 5% PD-L1 expression (n=234), median overall survival was 11.1 for patients receiving atezolizumab and 10.6 for patients receiving chemotherapy (p=0.41). Thus this trial did not meet its primary endpoint of improved overall survival on atezolizumab in urothelial carcinoma patients with at least 5% PD-L1 expression on tumor infiltrating immune cells.

A homology directed DNA break repair (HDR) assay was used to infer the clinical relevance of missense mutations in the DNA-binding domain (DBD) of BRCA2. Mutant BRCA2 was expressed in a V-C8 hamster lung fibroblast cell line along with a reporter plasmid and GFP fluorescence was quantified as an estimate of HDR activity. evidence_statement: Foundation panel results of baseline tumour samples from 48 patients with diffuse large B cell lymphoma identified PIM1 mutations in 6 patient samples, 5 of which were the DLBCL-ABC subtype. Four out of the 5 DLBCL-ABC patients with PIM1 mutations had stable disease or progressive disease when treated with ibrutinib, suggesting innate resistance to ibrutinib therapy. Three PIM1 mutations L2V, P81S, and S97N were investigated in cell lines studies. Cells transduced with L2V, P81S, and S97N were resistant to ibrutinib compared to cells transduced with wild type PIM1. Combined treatment of PIM1 mutant lines with ibrutinib and a pan-PIM inhibitor, AZD-1208, partially rescued sensitivity to ibrutinib.

Novel variant found through WES on all affected individuals of a family with short stature (ACMG: PP1). The variant was predicted to be possibly damaging in several in-silico predictors (align GVGD, SIFT, MutationTaster, PolyPhen and HumVar). Transfection studies in 293T cells determined that the variant was activating (FGFR3, STAT and ERK/MAP), comparing the results with G380R in two independent transfections for FGFR3 and STAT and three for ERK. In determining the mechanisms of angiogenesis in gliomas, an in-depth preclinical analysis of HOXC10 overexpression in response to a vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGFA) inhibitor bevacizumab was evaluated in vivo and in vitro. Immunohistochemical and western blot analysis of 10 glioma samples exemplified the plausible clinical relevance of VEGFA as its mRNA and protein expression levels were correlated with HOXC10 levels (P<0.01). Integrating VEGFA-silenced U251MG/HOXC10 cells in mice models allowed for a longer survival and a reduction in microvascular density than the control-shRNA-transduced cells (P<0.05). With bevacizumab the HOXC10 overexpressed tumors showed significant inhibition of growth as well as impaired angiogenesis (P<0.05). These findings indicate bevacizumab having inhibitory effects on overexpressing HOXC10 tumors as these tumors upregulate VEGFA expression.

In preclinical analyses, treatment with AMG 510 led to the regression of KRAS G12C tumors and improved the anti-tumor efficacy of chemotherapy and targeted agents. AMG 510 was shown to inhibit p-ERK and cell viability in a dose-dependent manner in MIA PaCa-2 and NCI-H358 cells. Xenograft tumors made by injection of NCI-H358 lung adenocarcinoma cells into nude mice showed growth inhibition when treated with AMG 510 (3 and 10 mg/kg), while tumor regression was seen at higher doses (30 and 100 mg/kg). AMG 510 was also effective in a syngeneic KRAS G12C mouse model (CT-26), with a higher dose (200 mg/kg) required for tumor regression. In the same tumor model mice lacking T cells showed tumor regression but not cures, suggesting that the immune system is required for cures in immune competent mice.

In a dose escalation study (NCT03600883) of AMG 510 (sotorasib) treatment, four KRAS G12C mutant lung cancer patients were treated with 180 mg (n=3) or 360 mg (n=1) doses. Objective responses were seen in two patients and stable disease in the other two. After six weeks of treatment average tumor reduction in the two responders was 34% and 67%, while the second patient (360 mg dose) showed complete tumor regression at 18 weeks. These patients remain on treatment at 42 and 29 weeks. This is the first evidence of patient response to a mutant-specific KRAS inhibitor.

Alveolar soft part sarcoma (ASPS) is characterized by the presence of an unbalanced translocation der(17)t(X;17)(p11;q25). In this 2001 paper, FISH with YAC and cosmid probes was used to localize the breakpoint to a 160 kb region with additional analyses (including Southern blotting, RACE PCR, and RT-PCR) identifying a fusion between ASPSCR1 (referred to as ASPL in this paper) and the TFE3 transcription factor. RT-PCR performed on 12 ASPS patient samples showed the presence of a fusion transcript containing 5' sequences of the novel gene ASPSCR1 fused with a 3' sequences of TFE3 in all cases. Of note, the reciprocal fusion was not detected in 11 of 12 cases consistent with cytogenetic analysis. The ASPSCR1::TFE3 fusion was absent in control cell lines (K562 leukemia cell line). Like other TFE3 gene fusions reported in cancer, this transcript retains the bHLH-LZ DNA motif, encoded by exons 5 to 7 of TFE3. The ASPSCR1::TFE3 is of potential clinical utility in ASPS diagnosis.

In this phase II, multicenter study of tazemetostat (EZH2 inhibitor) in adults with INI1-negative tumors or relapsed/refractory synovial sarcoma, subjects were enrolled into one of 7 cohorts. Cohort # 5 of this protocol consisted of 62 patients age 25 to 46 years old, with locally advanced or metastatic epithelioid sarcomas. Subjects received oral tazemetostat at a dose of 800 mg twice daily in continuous 28-day cycles until disease progression. Reported outcome: In this cohort #5, tazemetostat was associated with a durable objective response in nine (15%) of 62 patients, as determined by both investigator and independent radiology review committee assessments. WES of tumor samples in 14 (37%) of 38 patients did not harbor any genomic alterations in SMARCB1, despite showing loss of INI1 expression. Epigenetic silencing (eg, methylation or microRNA overexpression), the effects of enhancers or super-enhancers, or post-translational modifications cannot be ruled out. Limitations of this study include 1) variability in patient characteristics in terms of pre-enrollement treatments received, 2) lack of objective documented progression at baseline and 3) single arm design meaning that no cohort was available for direct comparison

Analysis of genomic data from 136 uveal melanoma samples identified a hotspot mutation in CYSLTR2 that is mutually exclusive with the more common GNAQ and GNA11 mutations. CYSLTR2 L129Q expression in Melan-a cells confers TPA-independent growth, while wild-type CYSLTR2 expression did not. Similarly, L129Q expression caused Melan-a cells and NIH3T3 cells to form tumors in SCID mice significantly faster than wild-type CYSLTR2.

It has been reported that recurrent activating somatic mutations (R206H, R258G, G328E/V/W, G356D) in the ACVR1 gene, which encodes a type I activin receptor serine/threonine kinase, are in 21% (11/52) of DIPG samples. The mutations were highly specific to DIPG, with an overall frequency of 0.3% in other tumors present in the Catalogue of Somatic Mutations in Cancer database. Data was collected from whole genome sequencing on 20 pre-treated biopsy samples of DIPG as well as whole exome sequencing from 1 biopsy sample and five samples obtained at autopsy. An additional 26 DIPG biopsy samples were screened via Sanger sequencing and identified the variant (G328W). DIPG cases with somatic mutations of ACVR1 (R206H, R258G, G328E/V/W, G356D) had longer overall survival (n=11 versus 41; median of 14.9 versus 10.9 months; p=0.05, log-rank test).

A series of HER2 (ERBB2) mutations (G309A, D769H, D769Y, V777L, P780ins, V824I, R678Q, R896C, del755-759, and L755S) were functionally characterized and tested for sensitivity to lapatinib or neratinib. Increased tyrosine kinase activity and phosphorylation of signalling proteins was observed for V777L, D769H, and V842I. R678Q and G309A did not show an increase in activity. del755-759 was characterized as neomorphic. All of the mutations tested were sensitive to neratinib. All mutations but 2 (L755S, del755-759) were sensitive to lapatinib. L755S was also shown to be sensitive to canertinib.

All of these cell lines had FBXW7 mutations. FBXW7 missense (or HOMD) mutations were observed in 8.6% (7/81) of T-ALL samples. Additionally, the authors transfected 293/K562 cells with either mutant NOTCH1 or FBXW7 to determine the effect of these mutations on the the ability of FBXW7 to bind NICD. FBXW7 mutations (R465C, R479Q, R505L) were defective in binding WT NOTCH.

KMT2A is not a frequent finding. This study evaluate patients with this condition (n= 37 patients) detected by cytogenetics studies in the setting of AML/MDS. All patients showed a complex karyotype. Compared to patients with AML and no KMT2A amplification (n = 11 patients), hsr(11)(q23) was associated more often with TP53 mutations and shorter survival than patients with AML without KMT2A amplification, although the difference was not statistically significant. However indirectly it is associated with poor prognosis.

From October 2015 to April 2019, 103 HCC patients scheduled to receive chemoembolization were screened. Of them, 84 met inclusion criteria and were assigned to TT (TACE) (n = 25), Non-TT (TACE) (n = 30) and Non-TT (TACE + Sora) (n = 29) groups according to their GALNT14 genotypes. Repeated TACE sessions were performed on-demand and patients were followed until November 2020. It was found that TT (TACE) and Non-TT (TACE + Sora) patients had shorter time-to-complete response compared with that in Non-TT (TACE) patients (p < 0.001 and 0.009, respectively). These two groups also had longer time-to-TACE progression (p < 0.001 and 0.006, respectively) and longer progression-free survival (p = 0.001 and 0.021, respectively). However, TT (TACE) patients harbored longer overall survival compared with those in non-TT (TACE + Sora) and non-TT (TACE) patients (p = 0.028, < 0.001, respectively).

In a study of 138 unrelated VHL families, 109 germline mutations were found. Missense mutations were more frequently found in families with pheochromocytoma (PC). Deletions, nonsense, and frameshift mutations were more frequently found in families without PC. Large deletions and mutations predicted to cause truncated protein were associated with lower risk of PC. The mutation of c.214_215insGCCC was referred to in the paper by c.427insGCCC due to a difference in transcript sequence. This frameshift mutation was found in 1 VHL family without PC (family ID:46).

The five families (A–E) described were referred to the Department of Medical Genetics, UMC Utrecht, for germline mutation analysis in the VHL gene. Direct sequencing of the coding region of the VHL gene had failed to identify the family-specific mutation. Further molecular analysis by Southern blot and FISH of peripheral blood revealed deletions involving the VHL gene in each of these families. VHL was clinically diagnosed in, at minimum, the proband of each family. 5 family members are grouped with this deletion belonging to family A (ages 16-37Y; mean 31Y). Member 1, a female, had retinal and CNS hemangioblastomas, and RCC. Her 1 brother had retinal and CNS hemangioblastomas; Her other brother had RCC; and her last presenting brother (deceased) had CNS hemangioblastoma. This brother’s daughter also presented with CNS hemangioblastoma. The last two brothers were not tested for the DNA deletion however it is assumed by the authors due to the segregation observed.

evidence_statement: Based on a phase 1 trial of sotorasib in patients with advanced solid tumors harboring the KRAS p.G12C mutation, sotorasib (a small molecule that selectively and irreversibly targets KRAS p.G12C) showed encouraging anticancer activity. The treatment cohort consists of 129 patients (59 with NSCLC, 42 with colorectal cancer, and 28 with other tumors). Age range: 33-83 yo. In NSCLC group, 32.2% (19 patients) had a confirmed objective response and 88.1% (52 patients) had disease control ; the median progression-free survival was 6.3 months. Kao, et al. (2018) presented 36 BCOR::CCNB3 sarcoma cases (86% were males; mean and median age at presentation was 15 years (range from 2 to 44 years); 78% showed mainly primitive round cells morphology). FISH (and RNA sequencing in 4 cases) confirmed BCOR::CCNB3 fusion (RT-PCR in one case showed fusion between BCOR exon 15 and CCNB3 exon 5). A follow-up study available for 22 cases showed that 3 years survival rate was 93% and the 5-year survival rate was 72%. This study underscores the common clinical, morphologic, and molecular features of tumors with BCOR::CCNB3 fusions, reinforcing their classification as a distinct sarcoma entity.

Kawamura-Saito, et al. (2006) presented 2 soft tissue Ewing-like sarcoma cases (62 years of age female who deceased 10 months after biopsy; 31 years of age male who was without recurrence 30 months after operation) with CIC–DUX4 t(4;19)(q35;q13) fusion. The authors used chromosome analysis (FISH) as well as RT-PCR to analyze the fusion. The authors also carried out multiple in vitro studies. The CIC-DUX4 region inserted in NIH 3T3 cells resulted in an increase of anchorage-independent colonies in comparison to the wild-type (indicating potential oncogenic transcription effect). The CIC-DUX4 construct transfected into HeLa cells showed 130 times higher transcriptional activities in comparison to the wild-type. The authors isolated RNA from U2OS cells with CIC-DUX4 fusion, and showed increased expression of 22 genes. Increased expression of ETV1 and ERM was seen in tumor tissue of case 1. The segment including potential ERM gene promoter region (TATA box) was transfected into HeLa and cell line from case 2 tumor tissue (ECD1). The result showed 235 times stronger promoter activity in ECD1 in comparison to the HeLa cell line. Also, the authors co-transfected the promoter region of the ETV1 gene and CIC-DUX4 into HeLa cell lines, which resulted in recognition of the region by the CIC-DUX4.

20 patients from 6 families in the Netherlands were analyzed for opthalmological manifestations of VHL disease. Different mutations were found in all 6 families (missense mutations in A-E and a deletion in family F), confirming the diagnosis of VHL disease in these families. Genotyping information for only 2 families was reported in this paper. In family F, eight individuals are affected with clinical type 1 VHL disease. A deletion in the VHL gene was found in this family. However, the specific deletion is not reported, and no information regarding genotyping methodology is given. Phenotypic information is only reported for 2/8 patients, who presented with cerebellar hemangioblastomas and retinal angiomas. In one of these patients (unspecified whom) the retinal angiomas caused an exudative retinal detachment.

Out of 48 Danish families presenting with renal cell carcinoma, one patient was found to harbor the germline mutations c.3G>A (p.Met1Ile) and c.631A>C (p.Met211Leu) in the VHL gene. This patient was diagnosed with clear cell renal cell carcinoma (age of onset: 28). He had a family history of testicular cancer in his maternal uncle. The patient has been through the national screening program for putative VHL, which includes MRI of the cerebrum, spinal medulla and abdomen, neurological examination, auditory tests, ocular examination and blood work for chromogranin A and metanephrines, with normal results. The proband also presented with the germline variant c.1729+8T>C in BAP1. Other members of the family did not undergo genetic testing.

A case study showed that the mTOR inhibitor everolimus exhibited a relatively long-term effect in a patient with renal cell carcinoma and a FLCN germline mutation (c. 1285dupC, likely loss of function).

A randomized phase III trial of hormone sensitive (ER or PR positive) early stage breast cancer (Dutch TEAM cohort, n=2,446) examined the addition of metformin to exemestane for 155 patients. IGF1R IHC was performed and patients classified as IGF1R high (n=105) or low (n=50). In IGF1R-high patients, combining metformin with exemestane was associated with significant RFS (HR 1.12, 95% CI 0.57–2.23 for sequential treatment with metformin, HR 0.73 95% CI 0.56–0.94 for exemestane only, and HR 0.32, 95% CI 0.10–1.00 for exemestane with metformin, p = 0.02, compared to the sequential treatment arm). There was also significant association with OS (HR for OS 1.72, 95% CI 0.96–3.08 for sequential treatment with metformin, HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.62–1.03 for exemestane only, and HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.31–1.45 for exemestane with metformin, p = 0.03, compared to the sequential treatment arm). The authors conclude that adding metformin to exemestane for patients with IGF1R-high expression may have clinical benefit.

The cancer-associated SF3B1-K700E mutation compromises homologous recombination repair and increases the sensitivity to ionising radiation and DNA damaging agents, such as etoposide or small molecule inhibitors including olaparib in isogenic K562 cell line. The SF3B1-WT and SF3B1-K700E cell lines were also engrafted subcutaneously into immunocompromised mice, and the mice were treated with etoposide, olaparib or a vehicle control and monitored tumour growth for 28 days. Treatment with either etoposide or olaparib significantly reduced the volume of the SF3B1-K700E mutant tumours, but had little effect on the volume of SF3B1-WT tumours.

In a phase 2 trial, 91 patients with ERBB2-mutant metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer, refractory to standard treatment, were treated with trastuzumab deruxtecan. The objective response was 55% (95% CI, 44 to 65), the median duration of response was 9.3 months (95% CI 5.7 to 14.7), the median PFS was 8.2 months (95% CI 6.0 to 11.9), and the median OS was 17.8 months (95% CI 13.8 to 22.1). 81 of 91 patients had an Exon 20 Insertion mutation and 46 of 78 evaluable patients with this mutation type had a partial response (PR).

Eight ALK2 inhibitors were tested against 3 ACVR1 mutant cell cultures and two wild type cultures. LDN-193189 was the most potent compound with minimal selectivity for the mutant cells. LDN-214117 was the most selective compound. Inhibition of SMAD1/5/8 and ID1 signaling was observed with the use of both drugs via western blot experiments. In the ACVR1 mutant cells, induction of apoptosis as determined by an increase in cleaved PARP was noted. Both drugs were administered to mice intravenously and orally. Plasma drug exposure and bioavailability analysis revealed both drugs to be well-tolerated and drug concentration in the blood and brain persisted over 8 hrs post administration. As a next step, ACVR1-mutant and wildtype orthotopic patient-derived xenografts were treated with both drugs for 28 days. Prolonged survival and decreased cellularity was noted in the mutant, but not wild-type, animals treated with either LDN-193189 or LDN-214117.

As part of a randomized phase III trial (USO-03012) in advanced NSCLC of gemcitabine vs. combination gemcitabine and carboplatin, protein expression levels for RRM1 (n=69) and ERCC1 (n=65) were evaluated using fluorescence-based IHC. RRM1 levels were significantly inversely correlated with response (r = −0.41; P = .001, n=58), as were ERCC1 levels (r = −0.39; P = .003, n=55). RRM1 and ERCC1 levels were correlated with each other (r = 0.36; P = .003, n=65). There was no significant interaction with treatment arm (P = .64 for RRM1; P = .79 for ERCC1). The authors conclude that RRM1 and ERCC1 expression levels are predictive of response to gemcitabine, and gemcitabine and carboplatin.

IDH1 R132C mutation confers a switch of function mutation where the mutated protein produces 2-hydroxyglutarate (2HG), rather than α-ketoglutarate (αKG). The novel metabolite induces a homologous recombination (HR) defect that sensitizes the tumor cells to poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitors. PARP inhibitor sensititivity was tested in vivo in HeLa cells where the R132C mutation was create with CRISPR, the HCT116 colon cancer cell line where R132C mutation was created with recombinant adeno-associated virus (rAAV), and the HT1080 human sarcoma cell line which already has R132C. The results were then duplicated in non-commercial glioma cell lines: 6 IDH1 R132 mutant; 4 IDH1 wt.

Surgically resected PDACs were used to create tissue microarrays, which were scored for antibody staining of hENT1 (SLC29A1). For patients treated with gemcitabine (n=243), high levels of hENT1 were associated with longer survival time in Kaplan-Meier survival analysis (HR 0.43, 95% CI 0.29-0.63, P < .0001) and by multivariate proportional hazards model (HR 0.34, 95% CI 0.22-0.53, P < .0001). For patients treated with surgery alone (n=142), there was no association with survival.

Ovarian epithelial tumours (n=235) were used to create TMAs and IHC results were scored for ERCC1 (n=114 low, n=121 high). For platinum sensitive patients (n=250 in supplementary table, but not all have ERCC1 levels available), low ERCC1 was associated with better PFS (p = 0.034, HR 1.9, 95% CI 1.1-3.6). For platinum resistant patients (n=26 in supplementary table, but not all have ERCC1 levels available), there was no significant association (p = 0.550, HR 0.5, 95% CI 0.1-4.3).

Public glioma datasets were analyzed from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and the Gene Expression Omnibus. HOXC10 was seen to be significantly elevated in gliomas compared to non-tumor brain tissues, and in higher grade glioma type glioblastoma (GBM) compared to normal brain tissues. U251MG cells with transduced with vector, HOXC10-overexpressing or shRNA against HOXC10 were implanted into mouse brains. Resulting HOXC10 overexpressing tumors were significantly larger than control (p<0.05), whereas silencing HOXC10 resulted in smaller tumors (p<0.05). In Kaplan-Meier analysis of data from the TCGA and HG-UG133A datasets it was found that GBM or low-grade glioma patients with higher HOXC10 expression had shorter overall survival in comparison to patients with lower HOXC10 expression (p<=0.012). HOXC10 expression was also correlated with poorer survival in astrocytomas and oligodendrogliomas.

disease: Renal Cell Carcinoma With MiT Translocations
evidence_statement: This study evaluates 200 nephrectomy cases. Within the 200 cases, there are four cases that are Xp11.2 translocation renal cell carcinomas (RCC). Previous studies identified two stages (pediatric and adult) that were used in prognosis. The pediatric cases were associated with more indolent clinical courses, while the adult cases were associated with more aggressive clinical courses. The four Xp11.2 translocation RCC cases in this study consist of three pediatric cases and one adult case. Although two of the pediatric cases in this study had favorable clinical outcomes, one of the pediatric patients became deceased three months after diagnosis. This patient was noted to have a VCP-TFE3 gene fusion. Although there are a plethora of gene fusions that are involved with the Xp11.2 translocation RCC, including ASPL-TFE3 and PRCC-TFE3 gene fusions, the VCP-TFE3 gene fusion has not been identified. VCP was described in the literature as being a recurrent DNA amplicon that is associated with tumor metastasis in tumors involving various organs of the gastrointestinal tract, the genitourinary tract, and the respiratory system. Although the patient with the VCP-TFE3 gene fusion was in the pediatric category, she had a worse prognosis than the adult patient in this study with the PRCC-TFE3 gene fusion, who was free of disease 36 months after diagnosis. Therefore, this study illustrates that prognosis of the Xp11.2 translocation RCCs depends not only on the age range of the patients, but also on the gene fusion involved.

evidence_statement: This study screened 983 Renal Cell Carcinoma (RCC) cases and identified 65 tumors with morphologic features suspicious of RCC with Xp11.2 translocation/TFE3 gene fusion (Xp11.2 RCC). TFE3 immunohistochemical staining and fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) testing confirmed 22 of these (34%) were Xp11.2 RCC. TFE3 rearrangements define RCCs with Xp11.2 translocation/TFE3 gene fusion, which, in the 2016 World Health Organization (WHO) classification, further belongs to the category of "MiT family translocation renal cell carcinoma." The MiT family (microphthalmia-associated transcription factor family) translocation RCC comprises of the Xp11 translocation RCC harboring TFE3 gene fusions and the t(6;11) renal cell carcinoma harboring TFEB gene fusion. This study showed that the Xp11.2 translocation/TFE3 gene fusion RCC can be difficult to diagnose by pathology, and that evaluation by FISH is a useful diagnostic tool for this tumor type.

Collectively data from expression analysis of 102 esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) sample tissues established MYC and HSP90 as potential targets with overexpression of MYC observed in over half the patient samples and strong levels of HSP90 in nearly ≥47% cases of all tumors. In vitro, the relative protein expression analysis of 5 ESCC cell lines displayed concurrent overexpression of HSP90 and MYC in both KYSE-150 and Eca-109 cell lines, while overexpression of HSP90 was solely found in EC-1, TE-13 and HESS. Treatment of STA-9090 an HSP90 inhibitor, inhibited ESCC proliferation with significant sensitivity shown in cell lines overexpressing HSP90 and MYC proteins (KYSE-150 with a IC50 value of 29.32 nM and Eca-109 with a value of 69.44nM). In vivo experiments also showed benefit of STA-9090 in MYC expressing PDX models, and no beneficial effect of STA-9090 in MYC-low ESCC PDX models. These findings are indicative of potential use in ESCC tissues with the patient populations possessing overexpression of HSP90 and MYC proteins.

Imatinib-resistant GIST882IR cells were derived by treating mice inoculated with GIST882 with imatinib over 6 passages. Western blots showed increased KIT protein expression in GIST882IR cells compared to GIST882 cells. Derived imatinib-resistant cell line GIST822IR demonstrated overexpression in p55PIK in comparison to the parental cell line GIST822. To evaluate p55PIK expression relevancy GIST882 cell lines were infected with lentivirus construct expressing the p55PIK (Lenti-p55PIK) and control lentivirus (Lenti-con). Overexpressing p55PIK GIST882 cells showed greater imatinib resistance than that of the (Lenti-con) infected GIST882 cells. It was found the p55PIK increases KIT expression via the NF-κB signaling pathway. Down-regulation of p55PIK or blocking NF-κB signaling led to decreased KIT and re-sensitized GIST882IR cells to imatinib.

In vivo overexpression of HSP90 was observed in segments of the glioma-containing tissue versus the non-tumor-bearing areas in the forebrain of nude mice implanted with bioluminescent intracranial glioma xenograft cells (U251HF-Luc cells). The in vivo effects of temozolomide (TMZ) and onalespib in zebrafish implanted with U251HF-GFP demonstrated the largest reduction in tumor growth and extended survival in groups treated with TMZ and onalespib versus the control of DMSO and single-agent groups (onalespib + TMZ vs single agents p<0.01). This trend was also substantiated in vitro with HSP90 overexpressing cell lines (LN229, U251HF, and A172) responding synergistically in U251 and LN229 cells (CI of 0.11± 0.06 and 0.7± 0.1 respectively) and additively in A172 cell lines (CI=1.0 ± 0.16).

Three gastrointestinal cancer wt-KRAS cell lines (MKN45, STKM2, and RKO) had lentiviral-based expression of KRAS G12D. When these cell lines were expressing KRAS G12D, they also had increased protein expression of AURKA and p-RPS6KB1. shRNA knockdown of KRAS mutant or amplified cell lines led to decreased expression of AURKA and p-RPS6KB1. Four xenograft mouse models were generated using luminal gastrointestinal cancers with mutant KRAS. Treatment of tumors began once they reached 150-200 mm3 with alisertib (40 mg/kg, 5 times per week) for 28 days. All xenografts showed reduced tumor volume compared to control (p<0.001).

Analysis of 156 breast cancer samples from the REMAGUS-02 randomized phase II trial indicated potential clinical significance of COX2 expression with celecoxib treatment. Patient population characterization of 152 patients confirmed the highest expression of COX2 to be present in grade three tumors when compared to the lower tertiles (41.6% versus 69.6%,p=0.01). In evaluating the pathological complete response (pCR) of patients in response to celecoxib, patients with the highest tertile of COX2 also exhibited a higher pCR rate than the overall population (p=0.002).

Association between BRAF-V600E allele amplification and resistance to MEK and BRAF inhibitors was demonstrated in melanoma cell lines and PDX models. Trametinib resistant cells lines distinctly displayed the BRAF-V600E allele as an amplification variant in comparison to the wildtype allele with a mutation in a 10:1 ratio. When ectopic expression of BRAF-V600E was induced in the Mel1617 cell line, enhancement in the level of resistance to PLX4720 decreased sensitivity by 75.4%; trametinib exhibited similar results in comparison to the untreated control. In vivo treatment of trametinib and dabrafenib on xenografts derived from trametinib resistant tumors showed no ability to decrease tumor growth. Furthermore, a verified BRAF-V600E amplified tumor sample with MEK2-Q60P mutation was obtained from a biopsy of a melanoma patient who progressed on trametinib and dabrafenib. Treatment with trametinib and dabrafenib of a cell line from this tumor unsuccessfully inhibited proliferation, indicating failure to induce downregulation of MAPK signaling, and phosphorylation of S6K downstream effectors. This data indicates resistance to BRAF and MEK inhibitors to be potentially acquired through concomitant MEK2-Q60P mutation and BRAF V600E amplification.

evidence_statement: Of 65 VHL families from central Europe, 53 were identified with germline mutations using SSCP analysis of PCR products by peripheral blood. Germline rearrangements were identified in 7 families. A 2kb deletion in VHL families 19 and 24, a 2–3 kb deletion in VHL 15, a 10 kb deletion in VHL 20, VHL 35 and VHL 36, and an 11 kb deletion in VHL 14. Family 14 was a German individual with retinal capillary hemangioma, CNS hemangioblastoma, renal cysts and RCC, pancreatic cysts, as well as epididymal cysts. Family 15, also German, contained 2 individuals with: 2 retinal capillary hemangioma, 1 CNS hemangioblastoma, 1 renal cyst and 1 pancreatic cyst, as well as 1 cystadenocarcinoma of the ovary. Family 19 was another German family with 2 individuals. 1 had an CNS hemangioblastoma, 1 had renal cyst and RCC, and 1 carcinoid. Family 20, had 4 German members. Each with retinal capillary hemangiomas, 2 with CNS hemangioblastoma, renal cysts and RCC, and 1 with pancreatic cysts. Family 24 contained 1 German member with retinal capillary hemangioma, CNS hemangioblastoma, renal cyst, pancreatic cyst, and RCC. Family 35 was a Slovakian family with 8 members. 3 had retinal capillary hemangiomas, 7 had CNS hemangioblastomas, all 8 had renal cysts, with 5 with RCC, 6 had pancreatic cysts, 1 was epididymal cysts, and 1 had Liver adenoma, and Retinoblastoma. Family 36 was a Slovakian family with 5 members. 2 had retinal capillary hemangiomas, 3 had CNS hemangioblastomas, all 5 had renal cysts, with 3 with RCC, 2 had pancreatic cysts, and 1 with Wilms’ Tumor and developmental anomalies.

evidence_statement: This study screened 983 Renal Cell Carcinoma (RCC) cases and identified 65 tumors with morphologic features suspicious of RCC with Xp11.2 translocation/TFE3 gene fusion (Xp11.2 RCC). TFE3 immunohistochemical staining and fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) testing confirmed TFE3 positivity in 22/65 cases. From the 22 cases of RCC with Xp11.2 translocation/TFE3 fusion, 15 of these patients were classified in stage I/II and seven patients were classified in stage III/IV. All 15 patients in stage I/II were noted to be alive and recurrence free 34 months after surgical treatment. However, three patients in stage III/IV passed away from distant metastases after 33 months despite undergoing surgical treatment and adjuvant molecular targeted therapy. Within the stage III/IV category, two of the patients are in the pediatric population. Although the two pediatric patients did not receive adjuvant molecular targeted therapy, they displayed a favorable clinical picture in their 45 and 51 month follow-ups after surgery. Therefore, this study illustrated that the prognosis of RCC with Xp11.2 translocation/TFE3 gene fusion is more favorable in patients who are in stage I/II of the disease relative to the patients in stage III/IV of the disease; two case reports also suggest that the disease may have a more favorable course in pediatric patients.

Eleven patients with sporadic hemangioblastomas were enrolled and diagnosed with a neurological examination. Four of these were found to have a germline mutation of the VHL gene. None of these patients had a definite family history of VHL disease or hemangioblastoma brain tumors. They had negative ophthalmoscopic examinations for hemangioblastoma, and unremarkable abdominal ultrasounds and computed tomographic imaging. Patient H13 (male, 58Y) presented with a spinal hemangioblastoma at C2. This patient underwent total excision of the tumor resulting in complete recovery. He was found to have the codon 133 (ACT to AACT) germline mutation of the VHL gene found through MLPA and PCR testing.

In a phase I study of larotrectinib in 67 patients with solid tumours, 8 patients were recorded as having objective response. 7 of these harboured NTRK fusions, and one had a NTRK1 amplification. It is not stated in the publication whether a survey of amplification status in other patients in the study was done.
