After genomic sequencing, it was shown that his tumor showed strong MET overexpression (Immunohistochemistry: 3+) with MET exon 14 skipping mutation. However, it was shown via FISH that MET amplification was not present.

molecular_profile: MET Exon 14 Skipping Mutation AND MET Overexpression
evidence_statement: A 61-year old male (non-smoker) was diagnosed with sarcomatoid non-small-cell lung cancer (CK+, TTF1+, and vimentin+). Genomic profiling showed two MET alterations that showed exon 14 skipping mutation (c.2888-5_2890TTAAGATC>A and c.3028+2T>G) and an activating point mutation in MET (p.H1094, c.3280C>T). Patient was first treated with carboplatin, paclitaxel, and bevacizumab, which showed evidence of response after two cycles, but progressive disease continued after four cycles. The patient was then given crizotinib which showed partial response. The dominant right-sided chest mass decreased from 8.20 x 7.91 cm to 6.14 x 5.05 cm. This lasted for 5 months until progression of lung and in bony lesions continued and the patient was put on hospice care.

A 72-year old woman (former smoker: 12 pack-years) with advanced lung adenocarcinoma received 250 mg of crizotinib twice daily after first line chemotherapy with carboplatin, pemetrexed, and maintenance pemetrexed. Genomic sequencing showed presence of MET amplification as the main oncogenic driver mutation. Radiography assessments taken 1, 2, and 5 months after therapy show a calculated decrease of lesion size by 38.7%. At the time of the study, the clinical response was ongoing into the 11th month of therapy.

A 68-year old woman (former smoker: 24 pack-years) was diagnosed with advanced lung adenocarcinoma. Genomic profiling yielded MET exon 14 skipping mutation (c.e14 1 G>A), PIK3CA mutation (c.1624 G>A), and TP53 mutation (c.1010 G>T). 250 mg crizotinib was administered twice daily. After 1 month of treatment, the calculated decrease of target lesions was 45.1%. Brain metastatic lesions also decreased in size after crizotinib use. Clinical responses lasted for 7 months.

molecular_profile: MET Amplification OR MET Exon 14 Skipping Mutation OR v::ALK Fusion OR v::ROS1 Fusion
evidence_statement: 69 patients with lung adenocarcinoma from Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center had their cancers submitted for genomic profiling to identify crizotinib-sensitive genomic events. There were 7 cases that had putative crizotinib-response aberrations with ALK rearrangement, ROS1 rearrangement, MET amplification, and MET exon 14 skipping mutations (3, 1, 1, and 2 cases respectively). The authors state that such genomic changes predict response to crizotinib.

molecular_profile: MET Amplification OR ALK Amplification OR ROS1 Amplification
evidence_statement: Lung adenocarcinoma cell lines (H3122: EML4-ALK E13:A20, HCC78: SLC34A2-ROS1, H1993: MET amplification, and H596: MET exon 14 skipping) with putative crizotinib-sensitive genotypes were analyzed with increasing concentrations of crizotinib. H3122, HC78, and H1993 cell lines were shown to have a dose-dependent reduction in proliferation. In H1993 cell lines, they also saw a reduction in phosphorylated MET, showing the crizotinib can inhibit MET phosphorylation.

molecular_profile: MET Amplification OR MET Exon 14 Skipping Mutation
evidence_statement: A study of 687 patients with non-small-cell lung cancer were tested for MET exon splicing mutation or MET amplification. Univariable analysis showed that shorter overall disease-specific survival was associated with MET exon 14 skipping mutation (p = 0.043) and high-level MET amplification (p<0.001) individually. The authors also showed that multivariable analysis yielded that both MET amplification and MET exon 14 skipping mutation were independent poor prognostic factors.

molecular_profile: MET Amplification OR MET Exon 14 Skipping Mutation
evidence_statement: A study of 687 patients with non-small-cell lung cancer were tested for MET exon splicing mutation. In 18 cases with MET exon 14 skipping mutations, 2.6% had adenocarcinoma, 4.8% had adenosquamous cell carcinoma (ADSQ), and 31.8% had pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinoma (PSC). The significantly high MET exon14 skipping mutations in PSC were shown with statistical analysis (p = 0.001). High-level MET amplification was also more common in PSC at 13.6% (p<0.001).

molecular_profile: MET Exon 14 Skipping Mutation AND MET Y1230C
evidence_statement: A 67-year old Asian female (non-smoker) diagnosed with stage IV metastatic lung adenocarcinoma and also presented with superior vena cava syndrome and weight loss. Ultrasound-guided biopsy of lymph nodes revealed poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma (CK7+, TTF-1+, CK20-). The patient received stereotactic radiosurgery for the brain metastases and one cycle of carboplatin/paclitaxel. Genomic profiling yielded a METex14 mutation (MET D1010H) with 44% MAF. Patient was enrolled in a phase 2 trial of crizotinib which had a partial response that was maintained for 13 months. Then, metastasis to right cervical lymph nodes developed and were sequenced that showed an increase of MET Y1230C resistance mutation with MAF of 3.5%. The patient declined further chemotherapy or other treatment and returned to native country. The authors suggest that the progression of the mutation Y1230C may have led to the resistance as the specific amino acid lies within a pi binding site for crizotinib, abolishing the interaction between the drug and target.

molecular_profile: NOT MET Amplification AND MET Exon 14 Skipping Mutation
evidence_statement: A 65-year old white male (non-smoker) developed recurrent metastatic NSCLC 17 months after lobectomy for stage IA disease. Genomic profiling showed MET exon 14 skipping mutation without MET amplification. Patient was enrolled in a phase I clinical trial of crizotinib but grade 4 transaminitis developed after 4 weeks. The patient stopped the clinical trial and let his liver enzymes (AST, ALT) recover. Cabozantinib 60 mg was given orally daily and imaging 4 weeks after patient started treatment, cabozantinib showed intracranial response for brain metastases and ongoing systemic response. The authors also mention that cabozantinib did not change transaminase level and continues to receive the drug to the time of the paper.

A 60-year old woman (non-smoker) was diagnosed with stage IV lung adenocarcinoma after finding a 5.7 x 5.1 cm left pleural-based mass with multiple invasions. The patient was put on carboplatin and pemetrexed showing partial response under intravenous treatment. After two cycles of carboplatin and pemetrexed every three weeks, the patient had disease progression. Next-generation sequencing (NGS) revealed MET exon 14 skipping mutation and was treated with crizotinib, showing decrease in the size of the lung lesion. The patient had continued response meeting RECIST partial response criteria. The patient ultimately developed progressive disease and NGS revealed D1228N/H and Y1230H mutation in exon 19 of MET. The authors believe that such mutations cause changes in the MET kinase domain, leading to resistance to crizotinib.

molecular_profile: MET Exon 14 Skipping Mutation AND MET Y1230H
evidence_statement: A 71-year old male (non-smoker) was diagnosed with stage IV lung adenocarcinoma. Genomic profiling of a lung cavity showed MET exon 14 skipping mutation and the patient began crizotinib therapy. Treatment continued with stable disease for 6 months until large pleural effusion was seen. The patient’s treatment plan was switched to carboplatin and pemetrexed. Genomic profiling of the new specimen yielded a MET Y1230H mutation as well as the original MET exon 14 skipping mutation. The authors report the patient is continuing the later treatment and potentially that a type II MET inhibitor would be considered upon progressive disease.

A 69-year old male (50 year history of smoking) was diagnosed with stage IIIC lung adenocarcinoma after a 13.2 x 8.8 x 9 cm mass with multiple lymph node metastases were found in a CT scan. Next-generation sequencing yielding in a MET exon 14 skipping mutation. Patient was given 250 mg of crizotinib twice daily and showed significant reduction with mass reducing to 7.3 x 5.3 x 7.6 cm in size (-42.4% based on RECIST criteria) after 4 weeks of treatment. Patient was tested for circulating tumor cells (CTCs) as well during this time and was revealed to have increased mesenchymal CTCs. MRI scans yielded multiple lesions indicating brain metastases and died 2 months later because of brain lesions. The authors conclude that mesenchymal CTCs can be used as biomarkers for metastasis.

molecular_profile: EGFR Exon 19 Deletion AND MET Exon 14 Skipping Mutation
evidence_statement: A 53-year old woman (former smoker: 15 pack-years) was diagnosed with non-small-cell lung cancer that revealed an adenocarcinoma. Initial tumor was sequenced to find an EGFR exon 19 deletion mutation and was subsequently treated with 3 cycles of cisplatin and pemetrexed. After partial remission, ablative radio-chemotherapy was performed at 50.4 Gy on tumor site and 61.6 Gy on metastases. After 12-month progression-free survival, the patient developed new metastases and was revealed to have a MET exon 14 skipping mutation via next-generation sequencing. Afatinib was given at 40 mg daily, but progression was seen after 6 weeks. 250 mg of crizotinib twice daily was added to afatinib treatment (reduced to 30 mg) and was well-tolerated. There was a tremendous response with complete remission of liver metastases and partial remission of pulmonary tumor manifestations after 6 weeks.

A 59-year old woman was diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma after a 15 cm right upper lobe lung mass was found with multiple lymph nodes and pleural nodules. Next-generation sequencing revealed a MET exon 14 skipping mutation and the patient was treated with 250 mg of crizotinib twice daily. The patient resulted in a 60% reduction in the right upper lobe lesions and resolution of the pleural nodules on a CT scan 2 months after treatment. After 8 months of treatment, the patient still had radiologic sustained response and underwent resection of right lung mass, continuing crizotinib 1 week postoperatively. At 6-month follow up after surgery, there was no evidence of recurrent disease.

molecular_profile: MET Exon 14 Skipping Mutation AND CD274 Overexpression
evidence_statement: A 71-year old woman (non-smoker) was diagnosed with poorly differentiated lung adenocarcinoma following immunohistochemistry of tumor cells and biopsy staining. High PD-L1 expression was also confirmed by immunohistochemistry and pembrolizumab (200 mg) was given. After the first cycle, progressive disease was shown. Carboplatin and pemetrexed were given following this, which showed partial response with apparent tumor shrinkage. Next-generation sequencing panel analysis revealed MET exon 14 skipping mutation. The authors suggest that because pembrolizumab is usually effective in cells with high PD-L1, that pembrolizumab may not be effective for high PD-L1 expression and MET exon 14 skipping mutations in non-small-cell lung cancer patients.

molecular_profile: MET Exon 14 Skipping Mutation AND CD274 Overexpression
evidence_statement: A 71-year old woman (non-smoker) was diagnosed with poorly differentiated lung adenocarcinoma following immunohistochemistry of tumor cells and biopsy staining. High PD-L1 expression was also confirmed by immunohistochemistry and pembrolizumab (200 mg) was given. After the first cycle, progressive disease was shown. Carboplatin and pemetrexed were given following this, which showed partial response with apparent tumor shrinkage. Next-generation sequencing panel analysis revealed MET exon 14 skipping mutation. The authors suggest that pemetrexed-based chemotherapy strategies for non-small-cell lung cancers with MET exon 14 skipping mutation AND elevated PD-L1.

A 67-year old Asian woman (non-smoker) was diagnosed with stage IV adenocarcinoma with pleural and rib disease. The patient underwent a lobectomy and then received carboplatin/paclitaxel/bevacizumab. She then received carboplatin/pemetrexed and then docetaxel with disease control. STAMP testing revealed MET exon 14 mutation and was put on crizotinib. Complete resolution of first rib and pleural nodules compared to baseline was observed in a five-month follow up PET/CT. At the time of the article, the patient remains on crizotinib going into the 12th month of treatment showing side-effects of dizziness and bradycardia.

A 77-year-old Caucasian woman (previous smoker) was diagnosed with stage IV adenocarcinoma with pleural disease. She received six cycles of carboplatin/pemetrexed which was followed by pemetrexed maintenance. STAMP testing showed MET exon 14 skipping mutation and was started on crizotinib. Ten days into therapy, the patient developed morbilliform rash, facial edema, and severe pruritus that required hospitalization. Crizotinib was stopped and treatment was continued with cabozantinib which showed response in CT scans following 2 months of treatment, which indicated response of pleural metastasis with cavitation and reduction in tumor bulk.

A 77-year-old Caucasian woman (previous smoker) was diagnosed with stage IV adenocarcinoma with pleural disease. Initial genetic testing showed wild-type EGFR and ALK. She received six cycles of carboplatin/pemetrexed which was followed by pemetrexed maintenance. STAMP testing showed MET exon 14 skipping mutation and was started on crizotinib. Ten days into therapy, the patient developed morbilliform rash, facial edema, and severe pruritus that required hospitalization. Crizotinib was stopped and treatment was continued with cabozantinib which showed response in CT scans following 2 months of treatment, which indicated response of pleural metastasis with cavitation and reduction in tumor bulk.

A 62-year old Asian man (non-smoker) was diagnosed with stage IV adenocarcinoma with pleural metastases. He received pemetrexed, docetaxel, nivolumab, and gemcitabine. Genetic testing revealed MET exon 14 skipping mutation and was started on crizotinib with concurrent radiosurgery for three small brain metastases. He experienced lightheadedness, nausea, and vomiting after five doses of crizotinib, but a dose reduction to 200 mg twice daily was better tolerated. Three month follow up CT scan showed 33% decrease to lung mass. In addition, new sclerotic foci in L4 vertebral body and left iliac bone were found that align with treatment response. After 4 months of treatment, unfortunately he developed new brain metastases and was moved to hospice.

A 61-year old female (non-smoker) was diagnosed with stage IIIb adenocarcinoma of the left lung. Next-generation sequencing of the peripheral blood revealed MET Y1003S mutation. The patient was treated with crizotinib, with a dramatic response with observed effects that lasted more than 10 months. Lymph node lesions showed a decrease of size by ~30%. The authors report that she is in stable condition and her survival time is much greater than the average for treatment with crizotinib.

molecular_profile: MET Exon 14 Skipping Mutation AND MET D1228N
evidence_statement: An 83-year old male (smoker) was diagnosed with adenocarcinoma of right upper lung. Next-generation sequencing (NGS) analysis found MET exon 14 skipping mutation and MET C526F mutation and the patient was administered with crizotinib. After 6 months, lesions began to increase in size and NGS analysis showed an extra D1246N mutation and the loss of C526F mutation, suggesting the D1246 mutation led to resistance. Cabozantinib was then administered cabozantinib with a large cavity forming 1 month after treatment, indicating sensitivity.

17 patients with ALK-positive advanced anaplastic large‐cell lymphoma (ALCL) enrolled in the PROFILE 1013 (NCT01121588) phase 1b single-arm, open-label, multi-centre study received crizotinib. ORR was 53% for ALCL (95% CI, 28–77), with 8 CRs, 1 PR, and 3 SDs. PFS at 2 years was 63.0% (95% CI, 35.3–81.4). Note that ALK positive included ALK mutations, but the mutation vs. fusion status for the patients in the ALCL group was not specified.

phenotypes: Middle age onset,Pediatric onset,Young adult onset
evidence_statement: In an analysis of a cohort of desmoplastic small round cell tumor, evidence of a functional EWSR1::WT1 fusion was detected in 25 of 26 cases. In these cases, the genomic breakpoints in WT1 was in intron 7 and for EWSR1 the breakpoints occurred in introns 7, 8, and 9.

In an analysis of 6 desmoplastic small round cell tumors, chimeric EWSR1::WT1 transcripts were detected in 4. The translocation resulted in an in-frame fusion of the N terminus (first 7 exons) of EWSR1 to the last three zinc fingers of the DNA-binding domain of WT1.

Molecular analysis of desmoplastic small round cell tumors with recurrent translocation, t(11;22) (p13;q12) identified EWSR1 on 22q12 and WT1 on 11p13 as the genes involved in the rearrangement. Further analysis confirmed a EWSR1::WT1 fusion joining exon 7 of EWSR1 to exon 8 of WT1. This is one of the first studies identifying the underlying molecular fusion driving desmoplastic small round cell tumor.

A 73-year old male (non-smoker) with advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) was found to have EGFR L858R mutation and MET amplification. The patient had a dramatic response to erlotinib and crizotinib but after 10 months, the disease progressed. Next-generation sequencing showed EGFR L858R mutation again, but increased MET amplification (MET-to-centromere of chromosome 7 ratio > 25). The patient received preliminary systemic chemotherapy but after 7 months, disease progressed with CNS symptoms in line with enhancing brain lesions. 250 mg gefitinib was administered daily in combination with 400 mg of capmatinib twice daily. Scans after 6 weeks of treatment showed intracranial response with well tolerated treatment. Capmatinib needed to be reduced to 300 mg twice daily due to grade 3 transaminase elevations. The authors report the patient has received treatment for 19 months ongoing with no evidence of systemic disease.

A 68-year old male (former smoker: 50 pack-years) was diagnosed with stage IV lung adenocarcinoma with pleural disseminations and positive intra-abdominal lymph node. Analysis of tumor tissue showed a MET exon 14 skipping mutation. 400 mg capmatinib was administered twice daily. After ~1 month of treatment, CT scans revealed multiple ground-glass opacities, even though lung lesion had decreased. Capmatinib was discontinued and piperacillin and tazobactam were administered. Following testing, the authors diagnosed the patient with capmatinib-induced ILD (Interstitial Lung Disease) and prednisolone was started at 60 mg daily. Gradual clinical progression was noted.

A 77-year old woman was diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma harboring a MET exon 14 skipping mutation after PET-CT scans showed a right upper lobe mass, right hilar enlarged lymph nodes, and multiple bone and adrenal metastases. 250 mg of crizotinib was administered twice daily which yielded partial regression after 2 courses of treatment. Progression-free survival of crizotinib was observed for 8 months until chest CT showed the right upper lobe mass was larger than before and multiple metastases were seen in kidneys. Treatment was switched to 60 mg of cabozantinib once daily, adjusted to 40 mg after grade II hand-foot syndrome was identified. Overall evaluation of metastases and target lesions indicate partial regression. The author reports the patient is still under follow-up with overall survival > 12 months.

A 33-year old male patient (non-smoker) was diagnosed with Stage IVB adenosquamous lung carcinoma. Various treatment strategies were tried but all had progressive disease quickly after treatment. Next-generation sequencing of tumor yielded MET exon 14 skipping mutation and EGFR duplication among other loss of function mutations. MET exon 14 skipping mutation was shown to be a germline variant with allele frequency of 49.55% by Ugene panel. Patient died with an overall survival of nine months.

A 72-year old man (non-smoker) was diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma and developed multiple recurring brain and lung metastases. Systemic chemotherapy was administered, and genomic analysis of the surgical specimen revealed MET splicing site mutation (c.3028 +2 T>C). Initially, tepotinib was started at 500 mg, but grade 3 peripheral edema developed. Dosage was reduced to 250 mg and then 250 mg every other day but edema continued to worsen. Tepotinib was replaced by capmatinib at 400 mg and the authors report no exacerbation of edema and tumor was well controlled for 100 days after capmatinib administration.

molecular_profile: MET Exon 14 Skipping Mutation AND MET D1228N
evidence_statement: A 70-year old male (former smoker: 50 pack-years) was diagnosed with stage Ib lung adenocarcinoma. Next-generation sequencing showed a MET exon 14 skipping mutation, confirmed later with RNA analysis. Patient was initially treated with crizotinib, which showed 61% decrease in target lesions. After 6 months, the disease progressed and genomic profiling of the new tumor showed MET D1228N mutation. The patient was put on cabozantinib (60 mg daily) which showed 30% decrease in target lesions. After 4 months, the disease showed progression and shortly after discontinuation of treatment, the patient passed away.

molecular_profile: MET Exon 14 Skipping Mutation AND CD274 Overexpression
evidence_statement: A 58-year old male (non-smoker/non-drinker) was diagnosed with metastatic adenocarcinoma with sarcomatoid components. A tissue sample revealed a MET exon 14 skipping mutation and the patient was treated with crizotinib with partial response for one follow-up. After disease progression, the patient received chemotherapy (paclitaxel and carboplatin) with nivolumab, an immunotherapy drug when high PD-L1 expression was observed in the intestine tissue. Tumor lesions in the right clavicle, thigh, and ulna almost disappeared. Tumor lesions in left ilium were decreased significantly. The patient ultimately used nivolumab as a maintenance treatment and the authors report the patient has had continued partial response for 15 months post-immunotherapy.

An 84-year old man (smoker: 62-pack-years) was diagnosed with stage IVB non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and was started on carboplatin and nab-paclitaxel. After the tumor progressed, the patient was found to have MET exon 14 skipping mutation. The patient was given tepotinib (500 mg/day) and maintained partial response for more than 12 months. The authors report that tepotinib may improve prognosis of MET exon 14 skipping mutation NSCLC patients who are considered difficult to treat with normal cytotoxic agents.

780 patients with lung cancer were included in this retrospective study. 16 patients with MET mutations were identified, consisting of 7 with MET exon 14 skipping mutations. Analysis of survival of the patients when treated with crizotinib showed that median overall survival of these patients was 22.8 months with the median progression-free survival being 12.4 months. The authors conclude that crizotinib to be an optimal treatment for non-small-cell lung cancer patients with MET exon 14 skipping mutation.

A 65-year old female (non-smoker) presented with right leg pain and edema. Percutaneous needle biopsy was performed on a mass-like lesion that appeared in a chest x-ray and revealed moderately differentiated lung adenocarcinoma (TTF-1+). Patient was put on four cycles of pemetrexed and cisplatin while maintaining rivaroxaban for deep vein thrombosis until the primary lung mass was enlarged. The patient then received two cycles of paclitaxel until progressive disease. The patient's condition got worse including decreased mental status caused by brain metastases and the patient was hospitalized. On hospital day 4, capmatinib arrived and was administered at 400 mg twice daily through nasogastric tube. By hospital day 10, she could open her eyes without stimulation and her mentality was fully recovered by hospital day 14. Brain MRI showed CNA metastases have nearly completely disappeared and authors report the patient has maintained response without significant drug related adverse events.

molecular_profile: EGFR Exon 19 Deletion AND MET Y1003N
evidence_statement: A 65-year old female diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma revealed several brain lesions, the largest measuring 1.8 x 1.5 x 1.9 cm. COBAS EGFR mutation test was run and revealed EGFR exon 19 deletion mutation. Patient was started on osimertinib 80 mg once daily and achieved partial response, showing a shrinkage of smaller brain lesions and left lower lung mass. 19 months into treatment, brain MRI scans showed an increase in size of lesions, consistent with an increase in symptoms. Following 3 cycles of increased osimertinib dosage in combination with carboplatin and pemetrexed, the patient's condition worsened and showed increased size and density of lung cancer. Next-generation sequencing revealed MET Y1003N mutation. 300 mg capmatinib twice a day was given in combination with osimertinib 80 mg daily, which both were slowly moved up to 400 mg and 160 mg respectively. Response was observed in the chest with shrinkage of right-sided lung lesions. The authors suggest osimertinib and capmatinib has a potential role in progressive EGFR-mutated NSCLC with resistant MET mutations.

molecular_profile: MET Exon 14 Skipping Mutation AND CD274 Overexpression
evidence_statement: Twenty-four patients with MET exon 14 skipping mutation and PD-L1 expression >50% were included in this retrospective study. Median overall survival of these patients was 12.1 months (CI: 9.1 - NR) and progression-free survival was 3.5 months (CI: 2.0 - NR). Treatment was ultimately stopped in twenty one patients and nine received MET inhibitors as second-line therapy. The authors report that these results are worse than other studies done on pembrolizumab.

An 82-year old male (smoker: 60 pack-years) was diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma. Initial tumor tissue testing revealed MET amplification (GCN = 13.5). The patient was enrolled in a phase 2 trial and given capmatinib (400 mg, twice daily). However, disease continued to progress through treatment. Next-generation sequencing showed MYC amplification (estimated copy number = 5). After further treatment, multiple brain metastases developed and the patient passed away. The authors suggest a MYC inhibitor such as ICX-101 to be used after capmatinib administration to inhibit resistance of cells to capmatinib.

A patient diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma had cells cultured to create patient-derived cell lines. Such cells exhibited MET amplification and showed overexpression of MYC. Capmatinib was administered with doses ranging from 0 - 10 uM with drug resistance, consistent with drug resistance in vivo. However, ICX-101, a MYC inhibitor, showed sensitivity and was tested in combination and sequentially with capmatinib. The authors report that when cell lines were treated with capmatinib and subsequently with ICX-101, there was a synergistic anti-tumor effect. The authors suggest a MYC inhibitor could be utilized to inhibit resistance to capmatinib.

molecular_profile: MET Exon 14 Skipping Mutation OR MET Overexpression
therapies: AXL Receptor Tyrosine Kinase/cMET Inhibitor BPI-9016M
evidence_statement: 38 patients with locally advanced or metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer were divided into two groups, Part A had c-MET overexpression and Part B had MET exon 14 skipping mutation. Part A was given either 300 mg, 450 mg, or 600 mg of BPI-9016M daily and Part B was given 400 mg of BPI-9016M twice daily, both treatments going until disease progression or intolerable toxicity. Treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) were assessed along with disease full analysis set (FAS) for efficacy. The authors report that BPI-9016M was well-tolerated with potential antitumor activity in MET overexpression or MET exon 14 skipping mutations. Despite the manageable safety profile, there was limited efficacy in BPI-9016M.

High BCOR expression which was associated with an internal tandem duplication (ITD) of 89 to 144 bp in exon 16 of the BCOR gene was identified in 20 of 20 (100%) of cases of clear cell sarcoma of the kidney, but not in any of the other 193 pediatric renal tumors tested. This suggested that BCOR ITD may be useful in the diagnosis of clear cell sarcoma of the kidney.

Whole transcriptome sequencing on tumors from 8 patients with clear cell sarcoma of the kidney identified BCOR ITD and overexpression of BCOR in all samples. The BCOR ITD was confirmed on tumor DNA. All samples showed numerous deleterious SNVs and InDels, but none were common among all samples. BCOR ITD was the only common, recurrent alteration.

The article detailed a phase III trial (SOLO3) of olaparib tablets versus nonplatinum chemotherapy in patients with germline BRCA-mutated platinum-sensitive relapsed ovarian cancer who had received at least 2 prior lines of platinum-based chemotherapy. Ultimately, the cohort receiving Olaparib resulted in statistically significant and clinically relevant improvements in ORR and PFS compared with the nonplatinum chemotherapy in patients with germline BRCA-mutated platinum-sensitive relapsed ovarian cancer who had received at least 2 prior lines of platinum-based chemotherapy.

Thirty-two patients with BRAF V600E positive metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) and 7 patients with other cancers were treated with a combination of BRAF-inhibitor vemurafenib (960 mg twice daily) and EGFR-inhibitor erlotinib (150 mg daily) in a phase Ib/II trial. No dose-limiting toxicities were observed. Overall response rates were 32% [10/31, 16% (5/31) confirmed] in patients with mCRC and 43% (3/7) in patients with other cancers, with clinical benefit rates of 65% and 100%, respectively. Early ctDNA dynamics were predictive of treatment efficacy. Serial ctDNA monitoring revealed distinct patterns of acquired treatment resistance. Convergent genomic evolution was observed with frequent emergence of MAPK pathway alterations, including polyclonal KRAS, NRAS, and MAP2K1 mutations, and MET amplification.

In an analysis of 13 cases of supratentorial glial tumors with ZFTA rearrangements without RELA involvement, all were found to have DNA methylation profiles similar to ZFTA::RELA supratentorial ependymoma. The underlying ZFTA rearrangements included 3 ZFTA::NCOA1 fusions, 4 ZFTA::NCOA2 fusions, 3 ZFTA::MALM2 fusions, 1 novel MN1::ZFTA fusion, and a truncated ZFTA product. Of the 3 ZFTA::NCOA1 in-frame fusions identified, 2 contained 4 zinc finger C2H2 domains of ZFTA at the N-terminus fused to 2 transactivation domains and the histone acetyl transferase domains of NCOA1 at the C terminus. The third only contained 1 zinc finger C2H2 domain of ZFTA fused to 2 transactivation domains and the histone acetyl transferase domains of NCOA1. Of note, the 1 case with only 1 zinc finger domain had a sarcoma-like histology rather than the more classic EPN-like histology.

In an analysis of 13 cases of supratentorial glial tumors with ZFTA rearrangements without RELA involvement, all were found to have DNA methylation profiles similar to ZFTA::RELA supratentorial ependymoma. The underlying ZFTA rearrangements included 3 ZFTA::NCOA1 fusions, 4 ZFTA::NCOA2 fusions, 3 ZFTA::MALM2 fusions, 1 novel MN1::ZFTA fusion, and a truncated ZFTA product. Of the 4 ZFTA::NCOA2 in-frame fusions identified, 2 contained 4 zinc finger C2H2 domains of ZFTA at the N-terminus fused to 2 transactivation domains of NCOA2 at the C terminus and 2 contained 1 zinc finger C2H2 domain of ZFTA fused to 2 transactivation domains of NCOA2 at the C terminus. Of note, the 2 cases with only 1 zinc finger domain had a sarcoma-like histology.

In an analysis of 13 cases of supratentorial tumors with ZFTA rearrangements without RELA involvement, all were found to have DNA methylation profiles similar to ZFTA::RELA supratentorial ependymoma. The underlying ZFTA rearrangements included 3 ZFTA::NCOA1 fusions, 4 ZFTA::NCOA2 fusions, 3 ZFTA::MALM2 fusions, 1 novel MN1::ZFTA fusion, and a truncated ZFTA product. The 3 ZFTA::MAML2 in-frame fusions contained 4 of the zinc finger C2H2 domains of ZFTA at the N-terminus fused to variable proportions of MAML2, all of which included the transactivation domain of MAML2. Two of these had astroblastoma-like histology and the third had more classic EPN-like histology.

In an analysis of 13 cases of supratentorial tumors with ZFTA rearrangements without RELA involvement, all were found to have DNA methylation profiles similar to ZFTA::RELA supratentorial ependymoma. The underlying ZFTA rearrangements included 3 ZFTA::NCOA1 fusions, 4 ZFTA::NCOA2 fusions, 3 ZFTA::MALM2 fusions, 1 novel MN1::ZFTA fusion, and a truncated ZFTA product. The MN1::ZFTA was found in a 41 year old male and consisted of MN1 with 3 transactivation domains at the N terminus and the 4 zinc finger C2H2 domains of ZFTA at the C terminus. Interestingly, this had astroblastoma-like histology and epigenetically clustered with ZFTA::RELA supratentorial ependymoma rather than high-grade neuroepithelial tumor with MN1 alteration (HGNET-MN1).

In 16 of 21 supratentorial ependymomas, oncogenic fusions between ZFTA (C11orf95) and RELA were identified by a variety of methods including WGS, RT-PCR, FISH, and RNAseq. ZFTA::RELA fusions were associated with chromothripsis involving 11q13.1 that brought the 2 genes, which are normally separated by 1.9 Mb, adjacent to each other. No ZFTA::RELA fusions or 11q13.1 chromothripsis were detected in any posterior fossa tumors analyzed. The authors note this is the most common genomic alteration in supratentorial ependymoma occuring in 70% of cases and more prevalent in older children (mean age 8.3 years old).

The G530D variant (assumed somatic based on VAFs between 9-22%) was identified in 5 AML patients from the Clinical Trial cohort and presumed germline variants included 2 with p.D140fs, p.E268fs, c.1098+1G>A, and p.L283fs (Table S2). It (assumed somatic based on VAFs between 3-21%) was also identified in 7 AML patients from the Real-Life cohort and presumed germline variants included 2 with p.D140fs, p.M1?, p.S405fs, c.1732+1del, c.799-2A>T, and p.H315fs (Table S4).

The G530D variant was identified in 7 patients with AML (one also had DLBCL), 2 patients with MDS, and 1 patient with pancytopenia (VAFs between 2.0-35.3%); presumed germline variants included none in 2 patients with AML (one also had DLBCL), S217P, L327W, p.D467Y, p.G218D, p.R311*, D140fs, and 2 with R159*.

The G530D variant was identified in 8 patients with myeloid neoplasm who had somatic status confirmed by buccal swab or sorted T-cells; germline variants included none in 3 patients (one of whom had another somatic alteration), 2 with p.A500fs, and 1 each with p.E7*, p.S363del, p.G173R.

In this trial, 665 patients having metastatic colorectal cancer were randomly assigned in 1:1:1 ratio to receive encorafenib plus cetuximab plus binimetinib, encorafenib plus cetuximab, investigators' choice of irinotecan plus cetuximab or FOLFIRI, this evidence item further shares analysis of safety and efficacy data and concludes that encorafenib plus cetuximab with or without binimetinib improved OS, PFS and ORR in patients with BRAF-V600E mutated metastatic colorectal cancer. It also concluded that encorafenib plus cetuximab doublet therapy could be used as a standard care for previously treated patients with BRAF-V600E-mCRC as OS efficacy was similar with or without binimetinib.

From a retrospective review of 38,095 tumor samples from 33,997 patients that underwent fusion screening at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, 87 tumors were found to be positive for an NTRK1, NTRK2, or NTRK3 fusion. One glioma patient (cBioPortal patient ID: P‐0032222) contained a QKI::NTRK2 (e6::e15) fusion that was detected by an RNA Archer assay and was positive by a NTRK IHC assay.

disease: Polymorphous Low Grade Neuroepithelial Tumour Of The Young
evidence_statement: Molecular profiling of 13 patients with polymorphous low-grade neuroepithelial tumor of the young (PLNTY) at Mayo Clinic, identified 1 patient (15 yo female) with a QKI::NTRK2 (e6::e15) fusion.

Pajtler et al. generated genome-wide DNA methylation profiles for 500 ependymal tumors using the Illumina 450k methylation array. Tumors were classified into nine molecular subgroups of which 88 supratentorial ependymomas (SP-EPN) had a similar methylation profile with the majority of these (88%) containing one of the two most common fusions between C11orf95 (now known as ZFTA) and RELA (type 1 or 2). The negative cases were suspected to contain the less common ZFTA::RELA fusion types 3-7, which were not assayed. This molecular subgroup with a distinctive methylation profile and a high percentage positive for ZFTA::RELA was designated as ST-EPN-RELA. No ZFTA::RELA fusions were identified in the other 8 subgroups strongly suggesting it is the primary driver of this subtype. Median age at presentation is 8 years old with a range of 0-69 years.

Fusions between ZFTA (C11orf95) and RELA are identified in 70% of supratentorial ependymomas. RELA is the principal effector of NF-KB signaling. The introduction of the fusion into neural stem cells (NSC) resulted in preferential accumulation of the fusion protein in the nucleus in the absence of TNF stimulation and activation of NF-KB target genes. Introduction of these ZFTA::RELA fusion containing NSC into cerebrum of mice resulted in aggressive tumors with a histology that recapitulated human supratentorial ependymoma, whereas introduction of ZFTA or RELA alone resulted in no or very few tumors.

Viral introduction of the ZFTA::RELA fusion into periventricular neural stem cells in mice was shown to induce tumors that recapitulate human supratentorial ependymoma. Introduction of wild type ZFTA or wild type RELA had no such effect. Transcriptional profiling of ZFTA::RELA tumors demonstrated NF-KB signaling as well as activation of other signaling pathways in a profile similar to that seen in human tumors.

In a phase 3 trial (NCT03778931), the selective ER-degrader elacestrant was shown to increase progression free survival (PFS) in both ESR1 mutant and ESR1 wild type, ER-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer patients, previously treated with endocrine and CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy. Of 477 patients, 239 received elacestrant and 238 received SOC (fulvestrant or aromatase inhibitors) with almost half of all patients (228 of 477) having ESR1 mutations. Elacestrant significantly reduced the risk of progression or death compared with SOC by 30% in the overall cohort and by 45% in patients with ESR1 mutation. This led to the FDA-approval of elacestrant in 2023.

In a phase 2 trial (NCT03043313), the selective ERBB2 (HER2) small molecule inhibitor tucatinib in combination with the HER2 antibody trastuzumab yielded an overall response rate of 38% in HER2-positive, RAS wild type colorectal cancer that was chemotherapy-refractory. Of 84 patients receiving both tucatinib and trastuzumab, 3 (3.6%) had a complete response and 29 (35%) had a partial response. The median duration of response of 12.4 months.

An international multi-institutional study identified108 patients with a methylation profile of supratentorial ependymoma, ZFTA fusion-positive, by whole genome DNA methylation profiling. The study found a 5-year and 10-year PFS of 65% and 63%, with a 5-year and 10-year OS of 87% and 37% respectively. This was is in contrast to a seminal publication in ependymoma prognosis (PMID: 25965575, EID8628), which suggested that supratentorial ependymoma, RELA fusion-positive, (now classified as 'supratentorial ependyoma, ZFTA fusion-positive'), had a poorer prognosis as compared with other ependymoma subtypes. The current study findings were comparable to more recent studies showing similar improved survival outcomes in this ependymoma subtype. Additionally, the study demonstrated a trend towards improved PFS with gross total resection vs subtotal resection (68.1% vs. 53% (P = .06)), with no surival benefit conferred by chemotherapy.

In a series of 54 supratentorial ependymomas with ZFTA::RELA fusions (termed fusions between C11orf95 and RELA at time of publication), homozygous deletion of CDKN2A was found in 9 cases and hemizygous deletion of CDKN2A in 8 cases, following genome-wide copy number profiling via molecular inversion probe assay. A statistically significant correlation was found between CDKN2A copy number status and overall survival on Kaplan-Meier analysis. When OS was stratified according to no loss, monoallelic loss or biallelic loss of CDKN2A, OS significantly worsened with allelic loss in a stepwise fashion (p=0.017) Both hemi- or homozygous deletions were found to have significantly worse OS as compared to those tumours with two retained alleles (p=0.034). Homozygous deletion of CDKN2A was found to have a poorer OS compared to tumours with hemizygous deletion of CDKN2A or two retained alleles (p=0.009).

In a series of 54 cases of ependymoma diagnosed in children </= 3 years, methylation profiling of all tumours was undertaken as part of a prospective clinical trial (SJYC07 - maximal safe surgical resection with adjuvant chemoradiotherapy). Of these 54 cases, a minority of cases (8 cases) were diagnosed as supratentorial ependymoma, RELA-fusion-positive by methylation profiling (now classified as 'supratentorial ependymoma, ZFTA fusion-positive'). The current prospective study found no statistically significant difference in outcome by molecular subgroup. The authors acknowledge the limitations of the study, including small sample size and limited duration of follow-up. The findings of this study are in contrast to a publication in ependymoma prognosis civic.eid:11440 which found supratentorial ependymomas, RELA fusion-positive, to be associated with a poorer prognosis on analysis of retrospective data.

Paired-end RNA sequencing identified a fusion between C11orf95 (now known as ZFTA) and RELA in 14 of 19 supratentorial ependymomas. This fusion was not detectable in a series of other CNS tumors including 39 infratentorial ependymomas, 5 spinal ependymomas, 5 myxopapillary ependymomas , 8 ependymoblastomas, 129 medulloblastomas and 2 pineoblastomas suggesting it is specific to this cancer diagnosis. The C11orf95::RELA fusion results in an N-terminal 212aa of the hypothetical 678aa protein fused in-frame to nearly full-length RelA that is thereby uncoupled from its normal upstream regulators.

Whole genome sequencing of 96 pilocytic astrocytomas by the International Cancer Genome Consortium (ICGC) PedBrain Tumor Project identified QKI::NTRK2 (e6::e16) fusions in 2 cases (5 yo & 12 yo males). Both contained a fusion between exons 1-6 of QKI including a Qua1 dimerization domain and exons 16-21 of NTRK2 which encompasses the kinase domain. The QKI dimerization domain is predicted to induce ligand-independent dimerization and activation of the NTRK2 kinase.

Authors demonstrated that a flag-tagged QKI::NTRK2 (e6::e16) fusion was able to transform Ink4a−/−/Arf−/− astrocytes, and these cells induced astrocytomas when injected intracranially into mice. QKI::NTRK2 resulted in an increase in phospho-STAT3 and the downstream target Ccl2 suggesting oncogenicity is mediated through STAT3 signaling.

Authors demonstrated that a flag-tagged QKI::NTRK2 (e6::e16) fusion was able to transform Ink4a−/−/Arf−/− astrocytes, and these cells induced astrocytomas when injected intracranially into mice. This study included an number of other kinase fusions that did not have this effect arguing that it is a gain of function for the NTRK2 fusion.

A total of 185 patients with stage III or IV esophageal + junctional cancers were tested for amplified genes in this retrospective study. There were 5 MET amplifications, 14 EGFR amplifications, and 16 HER2 amplifications. The authors report that there was a significant difference in median survival times of MET amplified patients vs other groups (p = 0.0006). MET amplified patients had median survival times of 7.16 months, with EGFR and HER2 being 11.8 and 16.9 months respectively. The authors report that MET amplifications indicate a rare but highly aggressive subset of cancer.

A total of 114 patients with gastric cancer were subject to genomic testing for amplified genes in this retrospective study. There were 4 MET amplifications, 3 EGFR amplifications, and 4 HER2 amplifications. The authors report that there was a significant difference in median survival times of MET amplified (p = 0.01) and EGFR amplified patients (p = 0.0003) vs other groups. MET amplified and EGFR amplified patients had median survival times of 6.1 months and 2.3 months respectively, with HER2 being 14.1 months. The authors report that MET or EGFR amplifications indicate aggressive disease phenotype of gastric cancer. The authors also report preliminary responses of crizotinib in two out of four patients.

Four patients with MET amplified gastroesophageal cancer (GEC) were treated with crizotinib (250 mg, twice daily). Two patients showed rapid progression, showing growth only 43 and 27 days respectively until progression. The other two patients however, showed rapid response. The tumor reduction was calculated to be 39% and 16%, respectively, with drastic improvements to patient symptoms. Time to progression in these patients were 112 and 105 days respectively. The authors conclude that crizotinib, despite the resistances in the first two patients, may be a potential target, especially in rare and aggressive subsets of cancers such as MET amplification.

28 patients were selected from a cohort of 43 patients with clear-cell sarcoma (CCSA) for this phase II trial. 26 of such patients presented with EWSR1 rearrangement and MET overexpression (MET+ cohort), with the other two being negative for MET overexpression (MET- cohort). Both groups were given crizotinib (250 mg, twice daily). MET+ patients had a disease-control rate of 69.2% (48.2 to 85.7%), an overall survival of 277 days (232-442), and median progression-free survival of 131 days (49 - 235). The authors also report no new adverse responses to crizotinib happened. The authors conclude that they were able to demonstrate clinical benefit of crizotinib to patients with advanced or metastatic MET+ CCSA.

molecular_profile: EGFR Mutation AND ( MET Amplification OR MET Overexpression )
evidence_statement: This phase 1b/2, multicentre, randomized clinical trial was conducted on the combination of tepotinib and gefitinib on patients with MET overexpression or MET amplification that showed resistance to EGFR TKI therapies. For phase 1b, the median duration of tepotinib and gefitinib therapy was 18.5 weeks at 300 mg and 16.9 mg at 500 mg, with no dose-limiting toxic effects at either dosage. Thus, it was established that tepotinib in combination with gefitinib should be 500 mg once daily. In the phase 2 study, the authors report that progression-free survival and overall survival was improved by tepotinib with gefitinib in patients with MET overexpression and MET amplification. Patients with MET IHC3+ (overexpression) had a median overall survival of 37.3 months (24.2 - 37.3) with the treatment vs with traditional chemotherapy of 17.9 months (12.0 - 20.7). In MET amplification, with tepotinib and gefitinib, overall survival was 37.3 months (NE - NE) vs chemotherapy 13.1 months (3.25 - NE).

molecular_profile: MET Exon 14 Skipping Mutation AND CD274 Overexpression
evidence_statement: A 65-year old male (non-smoker) presented with advanced sarcomatoid non-small-cell lung cancer harboring a MET exon 14 skipping mutation with elevated PDL1 levels (tumor proportion score of 80%). After progression on a MET inhibitor, the patient was put on two cycles of carboplatin-pemetrexed plus pembrolizumab. The treatment was well tolerated with no high-grade toxicities, but imaging showed disease progression and it was decided to switch treatments. On the day of the new treatment initiation, repeat testing showed improvement compared to prior scans and the patient was put back on two cycles of the initial therapy with further response.

molecular_profile: MET Amplification OR MET Exon 14 Skipping Mutation
evidence_statement: Twenty patients with advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with MET amplification or MET exon 14 skipping mutations were enrolled in this phase II clinical trial. All patients first received crizotinib or were screened to have prior treatment with a MET TKI. Capmatinib was administered at an initial dose of 400 mg twice daily and adjusted with subsequent safety assessments. The authors report that patients who were resistant to crizotinib showed a disease control rate of 80% on capmatinib, with several patient showing stable disease lasting over 6 months. Furthermore, with patients (n=4) with brain CNS progression on crizotinib, all had stable diseases with two patients having -29% and -22% decrease in growth. However, due to low overall response rate (ORR) of 10% and median progression-free survival of 5.5 months, the authors report modest anti-tumor activity in capmatinib in crizotinib resistant MET-altered NSCLC patients.

An 84-year old man (smoker) presented with non-small-cell and small-cell lung cancer harboring MET exon 14 skipping mutations and brain metastases. Patient developed progression after eight months of carboplatin-etoposide chemotherapy and was put on capmatinib (400 mg, twice daily). However, serum creatinine levels (Scr) became elevated after 1 week, corresponding with a drop to eGFR. Capmatinib was withheld and levels returned to normal, with no evidence of other causes for acute kidney injury (AKI). Capmatinib was restarted at reduced dose but Scr and eGFR levels were abnormal, indicating that this may be a capmatinib-induced pseudo-AKI. Prior history is highlighted in the comment.

molecular_profile: MET Exon 14 Skipping Mutation AND CD274 Overexpression
evidence_statement: A 75-year old female (non-smoker) was diagnosed with stage IVA lung adenocarcinoma harboring PD-L1 overexpression (tumor proportion score = 90%). After preliminary treatments became resistant and were discontinued after 4 years, MET exon 14 skipping mutation was found on next-generation sequencing. Capmatinib was initially started, but was stopped after 6 days due to grade 2 capmatinib-induced interstitial lung disease. Tepotinib was administered at 250 mg/day which yielded in response for over 6 months with reduction to brain lesions after 3 months.

molecular_profile: KRAS G12D AND MET Splice Site (c.2888_3028del)
evidence_statement: A 45-year old male (heavy smoker) presented with stage IV NSCLC (moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma. Sanger sequencing revealed a MET exon 14 splice site mutation (c.2888_3028del) and KRAS G12D mutation. This was also associated with MET overexpression with no MET amplification. Crizotinib was given (250 mg, twice daily) but after 1 month, progressive disease developed.

molecular_profile: MET Amplification AND MET Splice Site (c.2888_2919del)
evidence_statement: A 76-year old male (non-smoker) presented with stage IV lung adenocarcinoma with metastatic disease in the lung and thoracic vertebra (T2). Next-generation sequencing revealed a MET exon 14 skipping mutation (c.2888_2919del) with MET amplification. The patient was administered 250 mg of crizotinib twice daily. After 4 weeks, the patient showed dramatic improvements in lesions throughout the body and response persisted for 9 months.

molecular_profile: MET Exon 14 Skipping Mutation AND CD274 Overexpression
evidence_statement: A 77-year old woman presented with metastatic lung adenocarcinoma with MET exon 14 skipping mutation and PD-L1 tumor proportion score of 90%. Pembrolizumab was given but progressed after 1 year. Leptomeningeal metastases were observed on MRI following resistance from second-line docetaxel and ramucirumab for 6 months. Tepotinib (500 mg) was given as a third-line treatment and after 1 month, the authors report a dramatic response. The authors also report CSF and plasma concentrations of tepotinib and report CSF penetration rate to be around 1.2-1.7%.

A 75-year old woman presented with lung adenocarcinoma (stage IVA) to which next-generation sequencing revealed METex14del. The patient was put on crizotinib (500 mg/day) and showed partial response for 2 months, unfortunately developing resistance after 4 months. After brain metastases were found on MRI, the patient was put on tepotinib (500 mg/day). In 10 days, patients' symptoms significantly improved and after 23 days, despite nausea, lesions were too small to measure on MRI examination. The authors report that symptoms experienced were adverse effects from tepotinib administration.

A 56-year old male (smoker: 50 pack-years) was diagnosed with stage IIIA lung adenocarcinoma. Patient underwent four cycles of cisplatin and pemetrexed and maintenance therapy with pemetrexed but was ultimately re-hospitalized due to leptomeningeal metastasis and hydrocephalus on MRI. The driver mutation was assessed to be MET exon 14 skipping mutation to which the patient was administered tepotinib 500 mg once daily. After 14 days of treatment, leptomeningeal metastasis improved. After 5 months however, new liver metastases developed and third-line treatment was started. The authors also report that analysis of blood and CSF tepotinib concentration indicate that tepotinib was able to maintain effective blood concentration with greater than half of IC50 concentrations.

molecular_profile: EGFR G719A AND MET Splice Site (c.2888-21_2888-20delinsGC)
evidence_statement: A 60-year old man (smoker: 300 pack-years) presented with lung adenocarcinoma measuring 3.0 x 2.3 cm and multiple lymph node metastases. Next-generation sequencing revealed a EGFR G719A (abundance 5.08%) and MET exon 14 skipping mutation (c.2888-21_2888-20delinsGC) (abundance 8.61%). The patient was given 30 mg of afatinib daily and 250 mg of crizotinib twice daily and partial response was seen after 6 weeks. The authors report that the patient has obtained the continued response for 3 months.

Variant found by RNA screening analysis in a UBC (urothelial bladder cancer) cell line (VM-CUBI). The variant is located in the transmembrane domain. RT112 cells infected with lentiviral vectors containing the variant did show significant phosphorylation and downstream target effects compared to WT and evidence of “mini-foci” formation (Figure 2; A-B). Hierarchical clustering concluded that S653C belongs to a different cluster from the one in which the WT is located. The author suggests that the mechanism of action for the variant is through disulfide bonds between cysteines, similar to the ones in the transmembrane in FGFR3.

Variant found by RNA screening analysis in a UBC (urothelial bladder cancer) cell line (VM-CUBI). The variant is located in the transmembrane domain. Regarding the response to lapatinib, after three days of treatment in RT112 cell lines, S653C did show significant sensitivity to lapatinib according to the IC50 compared with other variants tested (Figure 5). The variant was in the IIa (sensitive) Cluster according to Figure 5C. The author concluded that VM-CUBI was found to be among the sensitive cell lines (Figure 5B-C).

Variant found by RNA screening analysis in a UBC (urothelial bladder cancer) cell line (J82). The variant is located in the transmembrane domain. RT112 cells infected with lentiviral vectors containing the variant did show some phosphorylation and downstream target effects compared to WT but no evidence of “mini-foci” formation (Figure 2; A-B). Authors commented that they did not achieve a conclusion leading to a possible gain-of-function for this variant, which is comparable to the literature.

Variant found by RNA screening analysis in a UBC (urothelial bladder cancer) cell line (J82). The variant is located in the transmembrane domain. Regarding the response to lapatinib, after three days of treatment in RT112 cell lines, R678Q did show significant sensitivity to lapatinib according to the IC50 compared with other variants tested (Figure 5). The variant was in the IIa (sensitive) Cluster according to Figure 5C. The author concluded that J82 was found to be among the sensitive cell lines (Figure 5B-C).

molecular_profile: DICER1 RNase IIIb Mutation AND DICER1 Loss-of-function
evidence_statement: Analysis of DICER1 mutations in tumor/normal pairs from pediatric patients (7 months to 13 yo) with anaplastic sarcoma of the kidney identified at least 1 RNase IIIb DICER1 mutation in 8 of 9 cases (89%). A single RNAse IIIB mutation was found in 7 cases, including 1 tumor with E1705K, 1 with D1709N, 2 with G1809R, and 2 with E1813G, and 1 with E1813K. In 6 of these 7 cases, a truncating mutation (Y1675RfsX30, C1562SfsX34, R544X, R676X, R688X, or P817LfsX15) was found in the second DICER1 allele. The eighth case was unusual in having 2 point mutations in the RNAse IIIb domain, D1709N and D1713V. One case did not contain any detectable DICER1 alterations, however its diagnosis as anaplastic sarcoma of the kidney was more equivocal than the others and may represent an anaplastic Wilms tumor. In 4 of the 6 cases with a truncating DICER1 mutation, the mutation was also found in adjacent normal tissue suggesting it was either germline or mosaic in nature. This study supports anaplastic sarcoma of the kidney being a component of the pleiotropic tumor predisposition DICER1 syndrome with altered miRNA processing as a major driver of the tumor. However, it is important to note that both DICER1 mutations were somatic in 3 cases suggesting it can arise spontaneously as well.

An analysis of DICER1 mutations in anaplastic sarcoma of the kidney identified RNase IIIb DICER1 mutations in 8 of 9 cases (89%). An in vitro cleavage assay of miR122 demonstrated that three of the DICER1 mutant proteins tested (E170K, D1713V, and E1813K) exhibit impaired production of mature 5p miRNAs, instead producing 3p miRNA and an incompletely processed RNA molecule. This supports aberrant miRNA processing as a driver of this tumor type.

Analysis of DICER1 mutations in tumor/normal pairs from pediatric patients (7 months to 13 yo) with anaplastic sarcoma of the kidney identified a somatic RNase IIIb DICER1 mutation in 8 of 9 cases (89%). In 6 of these 8 cases, a truncating mutation (Y1675RfsX30, C1562SfsX34, R544X, R676X, R688X, or P817LfsX15) was found in the second DICER1 allele. In 4 of the 6 cases with a truncating DICER1 mutation, the mutation was also found in adjacent normal tissue suggesting it was either germline or mosaic in nature. This study supports anaplastic sarcoma of the kidney being a component of the pleiotropic tumor predisposition DICER1 syndrome. However, it is important to note that both DICER1 mutations were somatic in 3 cases suggesting it can arise spontaneously as well.

A 49-year old female (non-smoker) presented with a 3.8 x 2.9 cm mass that was diagnosed as Stage IIIA lung adenocarcinoma. Genetic testing revealed a MET exon 14 skipping mutation, to which the patient preferred neoadjuvant target therapy (savolitinib, 600 mg/day). The patient exhibited partial response, with the tumor lesion shrinking to 2.6 x 2.2 cm. The pathological response was 50% and after surgical resection, the patient has had 38 weeks with no sign of recurrence.

A 83-year old woman presented with sarcomatoid squamous cell carcinoma. Next-generation sequencing revealed a MET exon 14 skipping mutation (c.3028+3A>G) and the patient was treated with crizotinib (250 mg daily). Tumor size decreased significantly after 1 week with concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CRT). The authors report positive response to crizotinib-target therapy, with complete remission in CT scans after two months. The patient took crizotinib for 8 months until treatment was interrupted for financial reasons and later died of pneumonia predicted to be unrelated to treatment.

A 57-year female (non-smoker) was diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma via pleural fluid cytology. After multigene testing revealed MET exon 14 skipping mutation, the patient was switched from cisplatin and pemetrexed to tepotinib at 500 mg once daily. After 43 days, CT showed partial response of the lung cancer, but ultimately showed ground-glass opacities (GGOs). Thus, tepotinib was stopped for three weeks, to which chest CT revealed the disappearance of shadows. Tepotinib was then restarted at a reduced dose (250 mg/day) and the patient reported no recurrence of GGOs.

A 60-year old male (smoker: 38 pack-years presented with stage IIB lung adenocarcinoma. After receiving an upper lobectomy, the left lobar lymph node was pathologically positive and received cisplatin and vinorelbine for two cycles. Oncomine DxTT revealed a MET exon 14 skipping mutation, although ArcherMET revealed negative results for MET alterations. The patient received four lines of treatments, but after progression, was put on tepotinib at 500 mg daily. Partial response was seen in shrinking lymph nodes after 4 weeks. Dosage was reduced to 250 mg after grade 2 peripheral edema, but response continued for 7 months.

molecular_profile: DICER1 RNase IIIb Mutation AND DICER1 Loss-of-function
evidence_statement: In an analysis of 107 patients enrolled in the International Ovarian and Testicular Stromal Tumor Registry, 5 had gynandroblastoma (14-32 yo). 4 of the 4 gynandroblastoms with material available for testing had DICER1 hotspot mutations in the RNase IIIb domain (E1705Q, D1709G, D1810H, E1813K) and 3 had germline loss-of-function mutations. This supports gynandroblastoma being a component of the pleiotropic tumor predisposition DICER1 syndrome. Of note, DICER1 RNase IIIb domain mutations were also found in 36 of 37 Sertoli-Leydig cell tumors but no other tumor types in the registry (i.e. juvenile granulosa cell tumors), indicating DICER1 alterations may aid in the diagnosis of these tumor types.

In an analysis of 107 patients enrolled in the International Ovarian and Testicular Stromal Tumor Registry, 5 had gynandroblastoma (14-32 yo). 4 of the 4 gynandroblastoms with material available for testing had somatic DICER1 hotspot mutations in the RNase IIIb domain (E1705Q, D1709G, D1810H, E1813K) and 3 had germline loss-of-function DICER1 mutations. This supports gynandroblastoma being a component of the pleiotropic tumor predisposition DICER1 syndrome.

In an analysis of a range of different ovarian sex cord-stromal tumors, 2 of 5 gynandroblastomas were found to have the DICER1 E1705K hotspot mutation supporting a role for DICER1 in a subset of these tumors.

Genomic analysis identified DICER1 RNase IIIb domain hotspot mutations in 3 of 16 cases of gynandroblastoma, leading the authors to suggest that DICER1 hotspot mutations are a key driver in a subset of gynandroblastomas.

molecular_profile: DICER1 RNase IIIb Mutation AND DICER1 Loss-of-function
evidence_statement: An analysis of 13 infants with pituitary blastoma (age 7-24 months) demonstrated recurrent DICER1 mutations. Of those with samples available for sequencing, 9 of 9 (100%) had germline DICER1 mutations with 8 of 9 (89%) being truncating mutations. 7 of 10 patients had somatic DICER1 mutations in the RNase IIIb domain with an additional 2 patients having LOH at the DICER1 locus in the tumor. One patient with LOH in the tumor had a germline point mutation D1709H rather than a truncating mutation. The other LOH case did not have a germline DICER1 alteration identified. This supports DICER1 as a driver of this tumor type and pituitary blastoma as a component of the DICER1 tumor predisposition syndrome.

molecular_profile: DICER1 RNase IIIb Mutation AND DICER1 Loss-of-function
evidence_statement: This 2021 paper analyzed the outcomes and complications of 17 patients with pituitary blastoma. The median age of diagnosis was 11 months with a range of 2-24 months. Germline DICER1 variants were identified in 12 of 13 patients tested and 13 of 14 tumor samples had DICER1 alterations (11 hotspot mutations and 2 LOH). Due to the rarity of this disease, this was a multi-institutional study with many of the patients previously reported. Nevertheless, it further supports the importance of DICER1 alterations in the diagnosis and the association of pituitary blastoma with the hereditary DICER1 tumor predisposition syndrome.

The results and published literature suggest that in addition to guiding targeted therapy selection, comprehensive genomic profiling shows the potential to identify genomic alterations linked to response and resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICPI) therapy in metastatic breast cancer (MBC). The demonstration of the clinical benefit of immune checkpoint blockade in MBC supports the need for the development of biomarkers used to guide the use of ICPI drugs for these patients.

Altered human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) signaling caused by genomic amplification of ERBB2 or mutations is oncogenic and has been observed in multiple cancer types. Based on the study, 32% of ERBB2‐positive colorectal cancers (CRCs) harbor short variant alterations that are undetectable by routine immunohistochemistry or fluorescence in situ hybridization testing. The use of comprehensive genomic profiling in CRC cases identified several striking differences in mutation frequencies between colonic and rectal adenocarcinomas, predominantly in the PI3K/MTOR and WNT/β‐catenin pathways. Differences were observed in the mutation frequencies of genes coaltered with ERBB2 amplification versus short variant (SV) alterations. CRCs harboring ERBB2 SV had higher mutation frequencies in the PI3K, mismatch repair, and Wnt pathways, among others. In addition, HER2‐targeted therapies may one day become approved precision treatments for patients with mCRC.

molecular_profile: EGFR L858R AND EGFR T790M AND MET Exon 14 Skipping Mutation
evidence_statement: A 76-year old woman (non-smoker) presented with stage IVB ling adenocarcinoma. Genetic testing was positive for EGFR L858R and T790M and osimertinib was given. Partial response was noted until progression after 14 months. After second-line pemetrexed was given for 6.7 months, Archer MET detected a MET exon 14 deletion mutation and tepotinib was given at 500 mg/day. This resulted in partial response, with 34.5% reduction in tumor size after 2 months. After 8 months of response, the patient had disease progression and shortly died afterwards.

An 81-year old man (smoker: 40 cigarettes/day) presented with metastatic lung adenocarcinoma. No genetic variants appeared on first round genetic testing on the Oncomine Dx Target TEst Multi-CDx system. Thus, the patient was put on first-line chemoimmunotherapy consisting of carboplatin/pemetrexed and pembrolizumab every three weeks. Tumor lesions and multiple enlarged lymph nodes almost disappeared and lesion in the right adrenal glad was significantly reduced. Oncomine testing revealed an exon 14 skipping mutation on second testing. However, the treatment was discontinued and no recurrence was observed for 6 months and disease control was achieved for 11 months.

Cell proliferation analysis of NIH 3T3 cells harboring the S310Y variation exhibit an increase of colony formation in soft agar compared with a wild-type ERBB2 and cells with ERBB2 D845A kinase-inactive.

evidence_statement: This phase 3 clinical trial was conducted to assess the progression free survival in patients with IDH-mutant gliomas treated with Vorasidenib, an oral brain-penetrant inhibitor, which showed preliminary activity in mutant gliomas. In this double-blind study, participants having residual or recurrent IDH-mutated grade 2 gliomas were randomly selected to either receive vorasidenib or placebo in 28-day cycles. The results showed significant improvement in progression-free survival for patients treated with vorasidenib compared to placebo (median progression-free survival, 27.7 months vs. 11.1 months; hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.39; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.27 to 0.56; P<0.001). The ESR1::CCDC170 fusion, E2-E7 and E2-E10 variants, were expressed in T47D luminal breast cancer cells and these cells were implanted in athymic nude mice to produce xenografts. Tamoxifen treatment resulted in tumour regression in the vector control xenograft but steady growth in the fusion expressing tumours, while Kaplan-Meier analysis showed significantly worse survival in animals with fusion expressing tumours (P < 0.01). Similarly, HCC1428 cells that endogenously express E2-E10 ESR1::CCDC170 showed higher sensitivity to tamoxifen or fulvestrant when the fusion was knocked-down using siRNA.

Protein-based assays showed that ESR1::CCDC170 fusion expressing cells had increased protein expression of HER2 and SRC, as well as increased HER2 phosphorylation. The ESR1::CCDC170 fusion, E2-E7 and E2-E10 variants, were expressed in T47D luminal breast cancer cells and these cells were tested for sensitivity to tamoxifen in combination with HER2 inhibitor lapatinib or SRC inhibitor dasatinib in colony formation assays. Both therapy combinations resulted in significantly reduced colony formation compared to either therapy alone or vector control in fusion expressing cells, with the dasatinib-containing combination being the most potent. Similarly, HCC1428 cells endogenously expressing E2-E10 ESR1::CCDC170 showed increased sensitivity to combinations of tamoxifen or fulvestrant with lapatinib or dasatinib compared to endocrine therapy alone.
