In this 2018 study, the authors aimed to identify driver events in 'double negative' clear cell sarcoma of the kidney (CCSK) where neither BCOR ITDs nor the YWHAE::NUTM2 gene fusion are detected. Eleven CCSK cases were included in the study, from pediatric patients aged 2 - 8 years. Using RT-PCR, BCOR exon 15 ITDs were detected in 10/11 cases, with only 1 case, an 8-year-old male, found to be a double negative. The case was identified to have a BCOR::CCNB3 fusion by a NanoString-based sarcoma fusion assay, with exon 15 of BCOR fused to exon 5 of CCNB3, confirmed by RT-PCR and Sanger sequencing. CCNB3 immunoreactivity was identified in the BCOR::CCNB3 case and not in the BCOR ITD CCSK cases tested. The authors conclude this is the first report of a BCOR::CCNB3 fusion detected in a CCSK of a young child, with the same fusion typically seen in primary bone and soft tissue sarcomas of male adolescents, and that other cases of double negative CCSK require characterization.

In this 2020 study, the authors report two patients with BCOR::CCNB3 fusion-positive clear cell sarcoma of the kidney (CCSK). Cases were males aged 10 and 14 years who presented with advanced disease. With initial testing, both cases were negative for a BCOR ITD. However, RT-PCR and Sanger sequencing were able to detect a BCOR::CCNB3 gene fusion. The authors concluded that all reports of CCSK with a BCOR::CCNB3 fusion have been detected in males older than the typical age (<4 years of age) of presentation for CCSK, and recommend testing for the BCOR::CCNB3 fusion in CCSK patients lacking a BCOR ITD or YWHAE::NUTM2 gene fusion.

In this 2017 study, the authors describe two primary renal sarcomas harboring BCOR::CCNB3 gene fusions and compare the morphological and immunochemical features to typical clear cell sarcoma of the kidney (CCSK). The two tumors were diagnosed in males aged 11 and 12 years and were unclassified at diagnosis with overlapping features of CCSK and renal synovial sarcoma. The BCOR::CCNB3 gene fusion was detected by FISH in the two cases. Although these tumors were originally unclassified, with the molecular findings the cases were considered compatible with a CCSK diagnosis. The authors conclude there may be a “BCOR-alteration family” of renal and extra-renal neoplasms with overlapping clinicopathologic features.

Among pediatric fibroblastic and myofibroblastic proliferating superficial lesions, lipofibromatosis (LPF), composed of an admixture of adipose tissue and fibroblastic elements, has been variously classified as infantile fibromatosis or fibrous hamartoma of infancy. A group of superficial soft tissue tumors occurring in children and young adults, with a notably infiltrative growth pattern reminiscent of LPF, variable cytologic atypia, and a distinct immunoprofile of S100 protein and CD34 reactivity, suggestive of neural differentiation, was described. To better characterize this group of LPF-like neural tumors (LPF-NT), genomic characterization (RNA sequencing) was performed, and revealed NTRK1 fusions (TPR::NTRK1 and TPM3::NTRK1) in two index cases and in 10/14 additional cases (using FISH). Of these 10, 4 had LMNA::NTRK1. No NTRK1-rearrangements were found in 25 classic LPF. NTRK1 immunostaining was found to be positive only in NTRK1 rearranged and S100 positive LPF-NT but negative in classic LPF.

In this paper, the collateral vulnerabilities that arise as a consequence of the inactivation or loss of function of certain tumour suppressor genes, specifically in malignant pleural mesothelioma (MPM), was studied. It was reported that BAP1 loss leads to enhanced EZH2 expression, which leads to enhanced cell proliferation and tumourigenesis.

The effect of CDK4/6 inhibitors (abemaciclib or palbociclib) was tested in patient-derived malignant pleural mesothelioma (MLM) cell lines. Of the three patient-derived cell lines, two of the cell lines harbored mutated BAP1 (ICO_MPM1 and ICO_MPM2). All of the MPM cell lines treated with increasing CDK4/6 inhibitor concentrations exhibited decrease in cell number. At 100 nM, a mean 54.5% reduction was seen in the cell lines treated with abemaciclib, while a mean 53.4% reduction was seen in cell lines treated with palbociclib. At 500 nM, a mean 64.3% reduction was noted in cell lines treated with abemaciclib, and a mean 64.1% reduction was noted in cell lines treated with palbociclib. Overall, it was reported that treatment of MPM cell lines with CDK4/6 inhibitors resulted in decreased cell proliferation.

RNA sequencing identified NUTM1 fusions in six patients with primary undifferentiated soft tissue and visceral tumors. Fusions included BRD4::NUTM1 (three cases), BRD3::NUTM1, MXD1::NUTM1, and BCORL1::NUTM1, however only the BRD4::NUTM1 and BRD3::NUTM1 cases were positive for NUTM1 IHC. Independent testing by fluorescence in situ hybridization confirmed the presence of the NUTM1 and partner gene rearrangement. The breakpoints were located at NUTM1 exon 3 or 5 (NM_001284292.1) and BRD4 exon 11 (NM_058243.2) or BRD3 exon 9 (NM_007371.3). Despite some overlap with NUT midline carcinoma, the authors note that the tumors observed also differed in several ways, tentatively labeled these malignant neoplasms as "NUT-associated tumors", and speculate that they might represent an overarching category that also includes NUT midline carcinoma.

The combination effect of APR-246 and cisplatin was studied in cisplatin-resistant ovarian cancer cell lines. A decrease in IC50 value from 52±11 to 3.2±0.8 μM (p <0.05) for cisplatin was recorded in cisplatin-resistant cell lines (cell line A2780 with V172F mutation) when treated with APR-246. Thus a complete restoration of sensitivity to cisplatin was reported. APR-246 was also tested in patient-derived cells with hotspot p53 mutation (R248Q) where the patient was clinically resistant to cisplatin and doxorubicin. APR-246 resensitized these cells to cisplatin. In addition to resensitizing the cells, APR-246 appeared to increase cisplatin efficacy in these cells.

This study examined the combined effects of APR-246 and doxorubicin in doxorubicin-resistant ovarian cancer cell lines. It revealed a decrease in IC50 value for doxorubicin from 0.95±0.11 μM to 0.12±0.01 μM in doxorubicin-resistant cell lines, upon treatment with APR-246. Thus a complete restoration of sensitivity to doxorubicin was reported. Furthermore, APR-246 resensitized patient-derived cells carrying the hotspot tp53 mutation (R248Q), which had shown clinical resistance to both cisplatin and doxorubicin. Notably, APR-246 not only restored sensitivity to doxorubicin in these cells but also enhanced its efficacy.

In this global phase 3 trial, 257 patients with ALK-positive Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer were treated with either alectinib (n = 130) or chemotherapy (n = 127). 93.8 % of the patients who had received alectinib versus 63% who were in the chemotherapy group were alive and disease-free at 2 years. A hazard ratio of 0.24 (95% CI; 0.13 - 0.43, p < 0.001) was reported for disease recurrence or death, which implies a 76% lower risk with adjuvant alectinib than chemotherapy. 98.4% of the patients in the alectinib group, and 93.3% of the patients in the chemotherapy group reported at least one adverse event. Serious adverse events were reported in 13.3% of the patients in the alectinib group compared to 8.3% of the patients in the chemotherapy group. Overall, the study found improved disease-free survival in the alectinib group compared to the chemotherapy group.

In this phase 2 clinical trial, 267 patients with HER2 expressing solid tumours received Trastuzumab Deruxtecan. The cohort included patients with locally advanced, unresectable, or metastatic solid cancers, excluding breast, colorectal, gastric, and non-small-cell lung cancers. The median DOR across all groups was 11.3 months (95% CI; 9.6-17.8), with patients with IHC 3+ having the longest median DOR of 22.1 months (95% CI; 9.6 - not reached). The pancreatic cohort had the lowest median DOR of 5.7 months. The median PFS was 6.9 months (95% CI; 5.6 - 8.0), with the longest median PFS being 11.9 months (95% CI; 8.2 - 13.0) in patients with IHC3+. The median OS across all the cohorts was 13.4 months (95% CI; 11.9 - 15.5), with the longest median OS of 21.1 months (95% CI; 15.3 - 29.6) in the IHC3+ group. Overall, trastuzumab deruxtecan exhibited clinically meaningful PFS and OS in pretreated patients.

In this phase 3 trial, 308 patients with NSCLC harbouring EGFR exon 20 insertions were treated with a combination of amivantamab and chemotherapy (carboplatin-pemetrexed) [n = 153] or chemotherapy alone [n = 155]. The median PFS in the aminvantamab-chemotherapy group was 11.4 months which was significantly higher than the chemotherapy group (median PFS of 6.7 months). The hazard ratio reported for disease progression was 0.40 (95% CI, 0.30 - 0.53, p <0.001), while the hazard ratio reported for death for amivantamab-chemotherapy compared to chemotherapy was 0.67 (95% CI; 0.42 - 1.09, p =0.11). The median objective response in the amivantamab-chemotherapy group was 9.7 months (95% CI; 8.2-13.5) compared to 4.4 months (95% CI; 4.1-5.6) in the chemotherapy group. The majority of patients in the cohort reported at least one adverse event. Overall, the study reported significantly better clinical results in the patients treated with amivantamab-chemotherapy combination therapy compared to patients treated with chemotherapy alone as a first-line treatment.

molecular_profile: EGFR L858R OR EGFR Exon 19 Deletion
evidence_statement: In this phase 3 clinical trial, 557 patients with NSCLC harbouring EGFR mutations (exon 19 deletion or L858R mutation) were randomly assigned to two groups and treated with either osimertinib with chemotherapy or osimertinib monotherapy. Significantly higher PFS was noted in the group treated with osimertinib and chemotherapy compared to osimertinib monotherapy, with a hazard ratio of 0.62 (95% CI; 0.49 - 0.79, p < 0.0001). After 24 months, 57% (95% CI; 50-63) and 41% (95% CI; 35-47) of the patients in the osimertinib and chemotherapy versus osimertinib monotherapy groups respectively, were alive and progression-free. An objective response was reported in 83% of the patients in the osimertinib-chemotherapy group, while an objective response was observed in 76% of the patients in the osimertinib monotherapy group. Grade ≥ 3 AEs were observed more frequently in the combination therapy group compared to the monotherapy group.

In this ongoing phase 2 trial (FIREFLY-1), 76 patients, aged 6 months to 25 years, with pediatric low-grade glioma harbouring BRAF alterations (BRAF fusions or BRAF V600E mutations) were treated with tovorafenib (DAY-101). The overall response rate according to the RAPNO-LGG criteria was 51% (95% CI; 40-63) and the median PFS and DOR were 13.8 months (95% CI; 8.3-16.9) and 13.8 months (95% CI; 11.3 - NR) respectively. All patients experienced at least one adverse event which may be treatment-emergent, and 63% of the patients experienced Grade ≥3 adverse events.

In this 2011 study, the authors identified the genes involved in a reciprocal t(1;3)(p36;q25) translocation that had been detected in epithelioid haemangioendothelioma (EHE) by karyotype. RNA isolated from an EHE with the known t(1;3)(p36;q25) translocation underwent whole-transcriptome sequencing and they detected a fusion that contained exon 2 of WWTR1 fused to exon 9 of CAMTA1. Using RT-PCR they confirmed the presence of the WWTR1::CAMTA1 fusion in another 4 cases of t(1;3)(p36;q25) positive EHE. The fusion involved either exon 2 (type 1 fusion transcript) or exon 3 (type 2 fusion transcript) of WWTR1 in-frame to exon 9 of CAMTA1. To determine the incidence of WWTR1::CAMTA1 they performed FISH with break-apart probes that flanked the WWTR1 or CAMTA1 gene regions on 47 EHE samples. The analysis detected CAMTA1 rearrangement in 39 of 45 EHE tumors (87%) and 42 of 47 (89%) harbored a rearrangement of the WWTR1 gene region, while all other vascular tumors were negative. The authors conclude that the gene fusion is exclusively present in almost all EHEs, demonstrating it to be a disease-defining genetic alteration.

In this 2014 study, the authors included a cohort of 39 cases of epithelioid hemangioendothelioma (EHE) from different anatomical sites to investigate gene fusions by FISH and RT-PCR. The patients' ages ranged from 9 to 85 years. For the 35 samples they were able to test successfully, 33 were positive for WWTR1::CAMTA1 (94%) and 2 were positive for YAP1::TFE3 (6%). There were 8 cases with a detected fusion gene via RT-PCR that were negative with FISH testing, and 3 cases negative with RT-PCR that had a positive FISH result. Exon 4 of WWTR1 was fused to CAMTA1 exon 8 in 13 cases and exon 9 in 7 cases, and exon 3 of WWTR1 was fused to CAMTA1 exon 9 in 3 cases. The authors conclude that identification of the fusion in EHEs can provide important diagnostic information, especially in cases with aberrant morphology or limited biopsy material.

molecular_profile: PIK3CA Mutation OR PTEN Mutation OR AKT1 Mutation
evidence_statement: In a phase 3 trial (NCT04305496) of 708 patients with advanced HR+ HER2- breast cancer, the combination of the AKT inhibitor capivasertib and the estrogen receptor degrader fulvestrant resulted in significantly longer progression-free survival compared to fulvestrant alone. Among the 289 patients (40.8%) with alterations (including PIK3CA, AKT1, or PTEN alterations), the median progression-free survival was 7.3 months in the capivasertib–fulvestrant group compared to 3.1 months in the placebo–fulvestrant group with a hazard ratio of 0.50 (95% CI, 0.38 to 0.65). In the capivasertib–fulvestrant group, 110 patients had PIK3CA mutations, 18 had AKT mutations, 21 had PTEN alterations, 2 had PI3KCA and AKT1 double mutations, and 4 had both PIK3CA and PTEN alterations. A breakdown of response by individual mutation was not provided.

In a phase 1-2 trial (NCT03093116), the ROS1/ALK/NTRK inhibitor repotrectinib demonstrated efficacy in NSCLC with ROS1 fusions. Among the 71 ROS1-inhibitor-naive patients, 56 (79%; 95% CI, 68 to 88) had a response, with a median duration of response of 34.1 months and a median progression-free survival of 35.7 months. In the 56 patients who had previously received one ROS1 tyrosine kinase inhibitor and no chemotherapy, 21 (38%; 95% CI, 25 to 52) had a response, with a median duration of response of 14.8 months and median progression-free survival of 9.0 months.

In a phase 1-2 trial (NCT03093116), the ROS1/ALK/NTRK inhibitor repotrectinib demonstrated efficacy in NSCLC with ROS1 fusions. In the 56 patients who had previously received one ROS1 tyrosine kinase inhibitor and no chemotherapy, 21 (38%; 95% CI, 25 to 52) had a response, with a median duration of response of 14.8 months and median progression-free survival of 9.0 months. Of note, 10 out of 17 patients (59%; 95% CI, 33 to 82) with the resistance mutation ROS1 G2032R responded to repotrectinib treatment.

molecular_profile: APC Mutation OR CTNNB1 Activating Mutation
evidence_statement: In a phase 3 trial (NCT03785964) involving 142 adults with progressing desmoid tumors, the gamma-secretase inhibitor nirogacestat demonstrated a significant progression-free survival benefit compared to placebo (hazard ratio = 0.29; 95% CI, 0.15 to 0.55). The objective response rate was significantly higher with nirogacestat than placebo (41% vs. 8%). Nirogacestat also provided significant improvements in secondary patient-reported outcomes, including pain, symptom burden, physical functioning, and health-related quality of life. Desmoid tumors have activation of the WT pathway (with ~90% having CTNNB1 mutations and 10% harboring APC mutations) which is associated with activation of the NOTCH pathway. According to the subgroup analysis, patients with either APC mutations or CTNNB1 mutations showed improved progression-free survival with nirogacestat compared to placebo. However, there are no desmoid tumor patients without CTNNB1 or APC mutations making it impossible to conclude that these mutations are the specific reason desmoid tumors respond to nirogacestat.

molecular_profile: FGFR1 Amplification OR FGFR2 Amplification OR FGFR3 Amplification OR FGFR4 Amplification
evidence_statement: In this phase II trial, 35 patients harbouring tumours with FGFR1-4 amplifications were treated with FGFR1-4 inhibitor, erdafitinib. 33 of the 35 patients were eligible and treated, while biopsies were never received for two patients. Of the 33, 13 did not have their mutational status confirmed because of low FGFR copy number, while 18 had their mutational status confirmed by the NCI central laboratory. The most common subtypes were breast cancers (9/18; 50%) and GI cancers (4/18; 22%). FGFR1 was the most common amplification noted (12/18; 67%). The most common co-alterations were TP53, MYST3, ZNF70, and CCND1. All 18 patients discontinued treatment due to primary efficacy analysis. There were 5 cases with stable disease, but none with partial response or better. For the 33 patients cohort, the ORR was 0% and nine cases of stable disease. The median PFS and OS were 1.7 months (90% CI; 1.1-1.8) and 4.2 months (90% CI; 2.3 - 9.3) respectively. Overall the study reported no clinically relevant benefits of erdafitinib in patients harbouring FGFR1-4 amplified tumours, due to its inability to meet its primary end point of efficacy.

In this phase 2 clinical trial, 35 patients harbouring tumours with HER2 amplifications (copy number (CN) ≥7) were treated with a combination of trastuzumab and pertuzumab. Patients with breast/gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma or patients who had previously received HER2-directed therapy were excluded from the trial. 25 of the 35 patients were included in the primary efficacy analysis. The ORR reported was 12% (2/25; 90% CI; 3.4-28.2). The median PFS and OS was 3.3 months (90% CI; 2.0-4.1) and 9.4 months (90% CI; 5.0-18.9) respectively. Overall, the study did not meet its predefined benchmark, and hence, a combination of trastuzumab and pertuzumab was reported to have no clinically relevant benefits in patients with HER2 amplified tumours.

molecular_profile: ERBB2 Activating Mutation OR ERBB2 T790M
evidence_statement: In this phase 2 clinical trial, 19 patients with tumours harbouring EGFR mutations (T790M or activation mutations) were treated with osimertinib, an EGFR TKI. Of the 19 patients, 13 were evaluable for efficacy. The ORR and 6-month PFS was 15.4% (90% CI; 2.8 - 41.0) and 16.7% (90% CI; 0-34.4) respectively. Overall, the study did not meet its prespecified end-point and therefore found no clinically relevant benefit of osimertinib treatment within their cohort.

In this phase 2 clinical trial, 50 patients were treated with trametinib, a MEK1/2 inhibitor. Among them, 46 had tumours harbouring NF1 mutations (S1 protocol), while 4 had non-uveal melanomas harbouring the GNA11 Q209L mutation (S2 protocol). The 6 month PFS in S1 and S2 subprotocols was 21% (90% CI; 12-34) and 50% (90% CI; 22-100) respectively. The median OS was 10.4 months in the S1 (90% CI; 7.4-13.3) and 19.2 months (90% CI; 18.1 - NA) in the S2 subprotocol. In the S1 subprotocol, 2 patients had a partial response (4.3% ORR; 90% CI; 0.8-13.1), while in the S2 subprotocol, 1 patient experienced a partial response (25% ORR; 90% CI; 1.3-75.1). These results show that inactivating NF1 or GNA11 mutations alone are not good indicators of response to trametinib in heavily pretreated patients with solid tumours. While this study did not meet its pre-specified endpoints, partial responses were noted in some of the patients treated with trametinib.

In this phase 2 clinical trial, the efficacy of RAF inhibitor tovorafenib (DAY-101) was investigated in patients between the ages of 6 months and 25 years, with pediatric low-grade gliomas harbouring BRAF alterations (fusions, rearrangements, or V600 mutations). The trial had two arms, arm 1 (n = 77) tested the efficacy of tovorafenib, while arm 2 (n=60) was an extension cohort, which provided treatment access for patients with RAF altered pLGG after arm 1 closure. The RANO-HGG criteria was used to assess efficacy in patients in arm 1. The overall response rate was 67% (95% CI; 54-78). Specifically, 12 (17%) patients had a complete response, 34 (49%) patients experienced a partial response, and 18 (26%) patients had stable disease as the best response. The ORR in patients with BRAF fusions and BRAF V600E mutations was 69% (95% CI; 56-81) and 50% (95% CI; 19-81) respectively. A relatively higher ORR was noted in patients who had received prior MAPK therapy compared to patients who hadn't received prior MAPK therapy. Specifically, the ORR was 71% (95%CI; 54-84) in patients who had received prior MAPK therapy, and 61% (95% CI; 41-78) in patients who hadn't received prior MAPK therapy. The median PFS reported was 19.4 months (95% CI; 16.9 - NR).

In this phase 1/2 clinical trial, 55 patients (40 MDS, 11 AML, 4 MDS/myeloproliferative neoplasms) with myelodysplastic syndromes harbouring TP53 mutations were treated with a combination of eprenetapopt and azacitidine. The ORR was 71% , with 44% achieving complete response. The study reported that patients harbouring only TP53 mutations, and no other somatic mutations by NGS, had higher rates of complete response (69% v 25%; p = 0.006). Overall, the combination therapy of eprenetapopt and azacitidine demonstrated clinically relevant benefits in patients with MDS and AML carrying TP53 mutations.

In this study, using genome sequencing the authors identified a t(4;9)(q13;q31) in six acinic cell carcinoma cases (AciCCs). The 4q13 breakpoints were at the secretory Ca-binding phosphoprotein (SCPP) gene cluster and the 9q31 breakpoints were located upstream of Nuclear Receptor Subfamily 4 Group A Member 3 (NR4A3). They then developed a hybrid capture based NGS approach and identified nine additional AciCCs with t(4;9)(q13;q31). They went on to utilize a break apart FISH probe and detect split signals indicating a NR4A3 gene locus rearrangement in 24 of 28 evaluable AciCCs. The t(4;9)(q13;q31) did not result in coding fusion transcripts but rather caused upregulation of NR4A3 through enhancer hijacking. Twenty-eight of 29 acinic cell carcinomas (97%) showed nuclear immunostaining for NR4A3, while normal salivary gland tissue was negative. Overexpression of NR4A3 in mouse salivary gland cells increased expression of known NR4A3 target genes and stimulated cell proliferation. The authors conclude that enhancer hijacking resulting in NR4A3 upregulation is the key oncogenic driver event in the majority of salivary gland acinic cell carcinomas.

This study examined the role of KMT2A/C mutations as a potential biomarker for predicting the effectiveness of immunotherapy. In the primary ICI-treated cohort (n = 546), the researchers observed that individuals with KMT2A/C mutations had a significantly improved prognosis in terms of PFS compared to individuals with wildtype KMT2A/C (Hazard Ratio = 0.66, p = 0.002). Moreover, the group with KMT2A/C mutations exhibited a higher durable clinical benefit (DCB: 48.3% vs 29.8%) compared with the wildtype group, as well as a higher ORR (40.9% vs 20.3% ; P<0.001) in the wildtype group. In an expanded cohort (n = 1395), those with KMT2A/C mutations showed better OS compared to wildtype patients (Hazard Ratio = 0.68, p=0.003). Overall, the study findings suggest that KMT2A/C mutations can serve as a predictive biomarker of the effectiveness of ICI treatment.

The study investigated the sensitivity of RB1-mutant osteosarcoma cell lines to PARPi. It found that cell viability, measured by AUC values after 5 days, was significantly lower in RB1-defective cell lines compared to RB1-normal lines when treated with three different PARPi: olaparib, niraparib, and talazoparib. Further, the study confirmed this selective sensitivity using clonogenic assays for all three PARPi in RB1-defective osteosarcoma cells. Overall, the study establishes an association between PARPi sensitivity and RB1-defective status in otherwise PARPi insensitive osteosarcoma.

In this phase 1b study, the combination treatment of eprenetapopt (APR-246) and pembrolizumab was investigated for its efficacy in patients with advanced or metastatic solid tumors. Out of the 37 patients who had received this therapy, 33 had TP53 mutations. Among the 29 patients in the efficacy-assessable cohort, the clinical benefit rate (CBR) was found to be 13.8%, with 4 patients experiencing clinical benefit. Specifically, 5 patients achieved SD for at least 5 weeks. Two out of these 5 patients had wildtype TP53, while the remaining 3 had mutant TP53.

In this phase 3 double-blind trial, the efficacy of capivasertib and fulvestrant combination therapy was tested in 708 patients with HR+/HER2- breast cancer. Among these 708 patients, 40.8% (n = 289) harboured AKT pathway alterations. The control group received a placebo plus fulvestrant. The median PFS in the population with AKT pathway alterations for the capivasertib-fulvestrant group was 7.3 months compared to 3.1 months in the placebo-fulvestrant group (HR - 0.50; 95% CI [0.38-0.65], p<0.001). In the capivasertib–fulvestrant group, 110 patients had PIK3CA mutations, 18 had AKT mutations, 21 had PTEN alterations, 2 had PI3KCA and AKT1 double mutations, and 4 had both PIK3CA and PTEN alterations. A breakdown of response by individual mutation was not provided.

A 67-year-old male with a diagnosis of Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM), IDH-wildtype, WHO grade 4 underwent a craniotomy with gross total resection. A BCR::NTRK2 fusion (ex1::ex17) was detected by comprehensive targeted tissue genomic profiling by NGS. NTRK2 protein kinase domain was retained (exons 17-21) in this fusion. Patient completed eight weeks of radiation therapy. However, there was evidence of recurrence. Entrectinib, an NTRK/ROS1/ALK tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy was initiated. After 33 weeks of therapy MRI showed decreased size of the recurrent lesion, and by the end of 15 months of therapy the patient remained asymptomatic. Later surveillance by MRI detected multiple sites of tumor enhancement. Authors suggest this case is the first case of adult GBM which showed successful but transitory use of entrectinib therapy.

Tumors from a cohort of melanoma patients were analyzed with whole exome sequencing. Median nonsynonymous exonic mutational load was 197 mutations per sample (range: 7 to 5854). The cohort was stratified by patients who achieved clinical benefit (n=27, defined as complete or partial response to the monoclonal antibody against CTLA-4 ipilimumab, or stable disease with overall survival over 1 year). No clinical benefit (n=73) was defined as progressive disease or as stable disease with overall survival less than 1 year. A smaller separate group (n=10) had early progression but overall survival over 2 years. Mutational load was significantly correlated to to clinical benefit from ipilimumab by Mann-Whitney test (P=0.0076). Average number of exonic mutations in the group that derived benefit was ~ 500, and ~ 100 mutations per sample in those that did not show benefit. Neoantigen load was strongly correlated with exonic mutational load.

In whole genome analysis of tumor and normal tissue from 97 breast cancers from TCGA, 132 kataegis loci were identified, and were enriched in chromosomes 8, 17, and 22, and depleted on chromosomes 2, 9, and 16. A classifier was built to predict presence or absence of kataegis from RNAseq data and the model was applied to 998 TCGA tumors with only RNA-seq data. This analysis classified 180 breast tumors with kataegis and 232 without kataegis with a 95% confidence level. In these 412 patients, kataegis was associated with ER and PR negativity, and HER2 positivity, as well as TP53 mutation and older age of onset. The authors then defined good prognosis as living patients or patients dying after age 55, and poor prognosis as dying before age 55. Kataegis was found as the only variable that significantly contributed to prognosis (p = 0.020, t test) by this approach and also by a cox proportional hazard model approach. The authors also reported that expression in kataegis tumors were more epithelial like and suggest they have lower migration potential.

In a retrospective study of 5,290 chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) patients where chromosome-banding analysis (CBA) data was available, karyotype complexity was assessed for clinical impact. Karyotypes were classified using 2016 International System for Human Cytogenetic Nomenclature. CK was defined as having 3 or more clonal aberrations in the CBA. CK cases were subdivided into 3 subgroups based on whether they were carrying 3 (n = 355 [45%]), 4 (n= 168 [21%]), or >= 5 (n = 271 [34%]) abnormalities. These subgroups were defined as low, intermediate, and high, respectively. The High-CK group had significantly shorter overall survival (median OS, 3.1 years; P < .001) compared with either low-CK or intermediate-CK cases (median OS for low-CK was 12.3 and intermediate-CK was 7.25 years).

This study looked specifically at the prognostic significance of Microsatellite Instability High (MSI-H) in sporadic Australian Clinico Pathological Stage C colorectal cancer in patients from a single center treated by surgery alone. It consisted of 255 patients, 197 M and 58 F, and 25 had urgent surgery. Seven micro satellite markers were utilized, patient was MSI-H if more than 40 percent markers showed instability. 9 percent of cases showed MSI-H, with 40 to 100 of markers unstable (mean 67 percent). Microsattelite stable and MSI-L were pooled. MSI-H was found significantly more likely on right colon than left or rectum (P<0.00001), or on larger tumors (p=0.002). OS was significantly greater for MSI-H than for the MSS and MSI-L combined HR 0.44 (0.23-0.85) p=0.015 Of the 7 markers used for detecting NSI-H, C-myb and BAT27 demonstrated greatest sensitivity. Authors speculate that increased level of tumor-infiltraring lymphocytes and the expansive rather than infiltrative growth pattern counteract the more aggressive features which had been noted associated to MSI-H cancers.

Samples from 395 patients with de novo or secondary AMP were processed by SNP arrays and chromothripsis was assessed using CTLP-Scanner. Patients were classified as either positive or negative for chromothripsis. 26 patients (6.6%) had chromothripsis involving different chromosomes. Chromothripsis patients had significantly older median age (67 vs 60 years, p = 0.002) and had lower white blood cell count. Chromothripsis positive patients had increased rate of complex karyotype and classified as high risk (HR) by European Leukemia Network (ELN) standards. Chromothripsis patients had worse overall survival (median OS 120 vs 258 days, p = 0.011). This trend in overall survival continued to hold when patients with haematopoietic stem cell transplantation were censored, and also in the HR subgroups of chromothripsis positive versus negative.

Chromothripsis defined a group of patients with poor prognosis. Samples from 395 patients with de novo or secondary AMP were processed by SNP arrays and chromothripsis was assessed using CTLP-Scanner. Patients were classified as either positive or negative for chromothripsis. 26 patients (6.6%) had chromothripsis involving different chromosomes. In patients receiving induction chemotherapy, there was a difference in overall survival (OS) between patients with and without chromothripsis (median OS of 120 and 295 days, respectively, p=0.040). This trend in overall survival continued to hold when patients with haematopoietic stem cell transplantation were censored (median OS of 120 vs 242 days, p=0.055).

In this randomized phase II trial, 180 patients with microsatellite stable (MSS) colorectal cancer were treated with either a combination of durvalumab and tremelimumab (D+T; n=119) or best supportive care (BSC; n=61). The study found that a tissue tumor mutational burden (TMB) of ≥ 10 mutations per megabase (mut/mb) was not predictive of benefit from D+T treatment compared to BSC (HR 0.71; 95% CI [0.28-1.80]; p=0.47). However, a plasma TMB (pTMB) of ≥ 28 mut/mb was predictive of a benefit from D+T treatment (HR 0.34; 95% CI [0.13-0.85]; p=0.022). Additionally, a clonal pTMB of ≥ 10.6 mut/mb (HR 0.10; 95% CI [0.014-0.79]; p=0.029) and a subclonal pTMB of ≥ 25.9 mut/mb (HR 0.20; 95% CI [0.061-0.69]; p=0.010) were also predictive of benefit from D+T therapy.

The study began with a total of 443 patients with advanced NSCLC that were randomly assigned to either regimen A (paclitaxel and cisplatin with gemcitabine) or regimen B (cisplatin and vinorelbine). RRM1 expression was measured by IHC. There was no statistically significant difference in response for patients in arm A with either positive or negative RRM1 status.

molecular_profile: PIK3CA Mutation OR RB1 Mutation OR ESR1 Mutation
evidence_statement: In this phase III trial (PALOMA-3), patients with ER+, HER2- advanced breast cancer were treated with CDK4/6 inhibitors. Patients were randomized to receive palbociclib plus fulvestrant (P+F) or placebo plus fulvestrant (F). A paired ctDNA exome sequencing was conducted to analyze clonal composition. RB1 mutations were identified in 6/127 patients (p=0.041), part of the P + F arm, while no RB1 mutations were identified in the patients treated with fulvestrant alone, at EOT (end of treatment). ESR1 mutations were noted in 25.1% at day 1, and 31.3% of the patients at EOT. An increased proportion of PIK3CA mutations were noted at EOT compared to day 1 (19% v/s 26.7%; p = 0.00069). Additionally, the proportions of patients with new PIK3CA mutations did not differ between the two treatment groups, which suggests that these mutations may play a role in fulvestrant resistance. Strong evidence was reported for positive selection for ESR1 Y537S through the treatment in both treatment groups (p=0.0037), suggesting this mutation may promote resistance to fulvestrant. The data also indicates that resistance to fulvestrant may be a major genetic driver of resistance to the combination treatment.

phenotypes: Middle age onset,Late young adult onset,Late onset
evidence_statement: In this 2007 study, the authors identified 38 cases of t(9;22)(q34;q11), also known as Philadelphia positive (Ph+), acute leukemia of myeloid origin. However, 18 cases were excluded as they displayed mixed lineage features, and a further four were excluded as they were considered secondary acute myeloid leukemia. In total, they included 16 cases of Ph+ AML confirmed to be de novo, with an overall incidence of 0.35% among all cases of AML considered in the study. The patients were aged from 30 to 82 years. Using RT-PCR the 12 cases with sufficient material were confirmed to have the BCR::ABL1 fusion transcript. The p210 fusion transcript was detected in 10 cases, while the p190 fusion transcript was detected in the remaining 2 cases. The authors concluded that Ph+ AML has an aggressive clinical course. The authors confirmed the presence of BCR::ABL1 in de novo AML and distinct from cases of chronic myelogenous leukemia in myeloid blast crisis.

phenotypes: Late young adult onset,Late onset,Middle age onset
evidence_statement: In this 1996 study, the authors identified 11 cases of t(9;22)(q34;q11), also known as Philadelphia chromosome [BCR::ABL1], positive acute myeloid leukaemia (AML) from approximately 700 cases that had undergone cytogenetic analysis. The patients were aged from 27 to 71 years. The cases were observed to have a shorter survival, and immunophenotyping revealed positivity for CD33/CD13 and CD34. Lymphoid-associated markers were found in 7 of 9 cases tested. The authors confirmed a subset of de novo AML carries the t(9;22)(q34;q11) translocation.

phenotypes: Middle age onset,Intermediate young adult onset,Late young adult onset
evidence_statement: In this 2010 study, the authors included 5876 acute myeloid leukaemia (AML) cases with successful karyotype analysis. The cytogenetic aberration t(9;22)(q34;q11) [known to result in a BCR::ABL1 fusion] was detected in 47 cases (0.8%). These patients were aged from 22 to 58 years. The authors found that t(9;22) was associated with significantly poorer overall survival. A subset of AML cases was confirmed to carry the t(9;22)(q34;q11) translocation.

phenotypes: Middle age onset,Juvenile onset,Young adult onset
evidence_statement: In this 2017 study, the authors sought to characterize NUT carcinomas. They included a cohort of 12 aggressive malignant tumors with rearrangement of the NUTM1 gene, assessed by RT-PCR, FISH, positive nuclear NUTM1 immunohistochemistry, and/or t(15; 19) detection by cytogenetics. The median age at onset was 18 years (with a range of 12 –50 years). RT-PCR or FISH confirmed the fusion partner as BRD4 in 9 of 12 cases, and a finding of t(15;19) (q13;p13) by cytogenetics confirmed BRD4 as the partner in 1 case. All cases tested had positive anti-NUTM1 antibody immunostaining. The primary tumor was found to be lateralized in two-thirds of the cases, rather than localized to the midline, supporting the change in name from "NUT midline carcinoma" to "NUT carcinoma". The authors state that 50% of cases initially had an alternative diagnosis and recommend NUTM1-specific antibody immunostaining in cases of undifferentiated or poorly differentiated carcinoma to properly diagnose NUT carcinoma at an earlier stage.

In this 2020 study, the authors included a total of 141 NUT carcinomas defined by rearrangement of NUTM1 detected by IHC, cytogenetics, FISH or sequencing. The median age at diagnosis was 24 years (range of 18 days to 80 years). Fusion partners were confirmed by either cytogenetics, FISH or sequencing. The majority (78%) of tumors harbored a BRD4::NUTM1 fusion, 15% harbored a BRD3::NUTM1 fusion, 6% harbored a NSD3::NUTM1 fusion, 1 of 141 harbored a ZNF532::NUTM1 fusion and 1 of 141 harbored a ZNF592::NUTM1 fusion. For the remaining 14 cases the fusion partner gene to NUTM1 was not identified. The majority of tumors arose from the thorax or head and neck, but tumors were also seen in bone, soft tissue, and kidney. Outcomes in patients were overall poor, however, the authors conclude that they have identified three clinically and molecularly defined prognostic risk groups: group A is nonthoracic, BRD3::NUTM1, or NSD3::NUTM1 with a significantly improved prognosis (OS of 36.5 months); group B is nonthoracic, BRD4::NUTM1 with a poor prognosis (OS of 10 months); and group C is thoracic with a very poor prognosis (OS of 3.5 to 5.6 months) regardless of the NUTM1 fusion partner.

In this 2004 study, the authors sought to identify carcinomas with translocation t(15;19)(q13, p13.1), which results in the novel oncogenic fusion BRD4::NUTM1 (described as NUT). The authors screened malignant tumors with epithelial differentiation, in patients less than 40 years of age, with poorly differentiated histomorphology, rapid clinical progression, and/or cytogenetic evidence of chromosome 15q or 19p rearrangement. In total, using FISH with dual-color assays evaluating chromosome 19p13.1 BRD4 and 15q13 NUTM1 breakpoints, they detected 11 tumors to have a NUTM1 rearrangement, with 7 of the cases detected in 98 previously unscreened samples and the others in known positive cases. Patients with a NUTM1 rearrangement ranged from 3 to 35 years of age. The NUTM1 rearrangement was consistent with BRD4::NUTM1 in 8/11 cases and 3/11 were found to have a rearrangement of NUTM1 but not BRD4, suggesting the existence of other rearrangements involving NUTM1 which the authors designate NUT-variant carcinomas. The authors conclude that NUTM1 rearranged carcinomas can arise from various midline epithelial surfaces and are associated with poor outcome.

The ctDNA of 46 patients with hepatocellular carcinoma was analyzed to investigate whether EGFR alterations could lead to lenvatinib resistance. Among these patients, 16 had been treated with lenvatinib, and 30 had received immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). At the time of disease progression, EGFR amplification was observed in one patient who had normal baseline EGFR levels, and in another patient, EGFR amplification increased from 4.8 to 7 copies. To retrospectively assess whether lenvatinib treatment suggested early treatment failure, three patient cohorts were established: those with EGFR/ERBB2 alterations before lenvatinib treatment (cohort 1; n = 6), those without EGFR/ERBB2 alterations prior to treatment (cohort 2; n = 32), and those with EGFR/ERBB2 alterations before ICI treatment (cohort 3; n = 17). The median PFS in cohort 1 was lower (2.2 months; 95% CI: 1.6-2.8) than in cohort 2 (5.9 months; 95% CI: 2.0-9.8) and cohort 3 (7.1 months; 95% CI: 1.0-13.2). Similarly, the median OS was also shorter in cohort 1 (3.9 months; 95% CI: 0.5-7.3) compared to cohort 2 (9.2 months; 95% CI: 7.3-11.1) and cohort 3 (16.9 months; 95% CI: 6.2-27.6). These findings suggest that EGFR alterations may be a key mechanism driving lenvatinib resistance.

In the STARTRK-NG (NCT02650401) phase 1/2 trial, a 10 year old patient with prior chemotherapy treatment who had Ganglioglioma in the Spine, with a tumor category of low grade glioma, and WHO histology grade of I, was given enterectinib. Patient had the BCR::NTRK2 fusion. Treatment duration at data cutoff was 2.5 months. The patient showed stable disease as response.

Sensitivity to durvalumab was tested in patients with triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) harbouring CD274 gain/amplification. CD274 amplifications were noted in 42% (n=23) of the TNBC samples. Patients with this biomarker were reported to be highly sensitive to durvalumab (HR = 0.17, 95% CI; 0.05-0.55; p = 0.0009). Additionally, the HR in patients with CD274 gain/amplification (HR=0.18; 95% CI: 0.05-0.71; p =0.0059; n =23) was lower than that in patients without CD274 gain/amplification (HR=1.12; 95% CI: 0.42-2.99; p=0.8139; n=32). Overall, CD274 was reported as a potential biomarker for sensitivity to durvalumab.

NUT carcinoma is known to be driven by BET fusion proteins, including BRD4::NUTM1 and BRD3::NUTM1, raising the possibility of response to BET inhibitors. Of 19 patients with NUT carcinoma treated with the BET inhibitor molibresib (GSK525762) in a phase 1/2 trial, 4 had a PR (3 with BRD3::NUTM1 and 1 with unknown partner), 8 had SD, and 4 were progression-free for more than 6 months.

As part of this trial, 27 pediatric patients (aged 2-20), harbouring, RET-mutant medullary thyroid cancer (MTC, n = 14), RET fusion-positive papillary thyroid cancer (RTC, n=10), or other tumour types (n=3), were treated with selpercatinib. The ORR was 83.3% (10/12) in patients with RECIST measurable disease at baseline. The ORR of patients with PTC was 100% (5/5), and the ORR was 83.3% in patients with MTC (5/6). One patient with MTC had stable disease and no patients with MTC/PTC had PD.

In this 2014 study, the authors compared 10 primary sclerosing epithelioid fibrosarcomas (SEF), 4 cases of low-grade fibromyxoid sarcoma (LGFMS), and one primary hybrid SEF/LGFMS. Patients with SEF ranged from 28 to 91 years of age. Using RT-PCR, they detected in-frame fusions in 3/4 cases with suitable samples, joining either exon 7, 8, or 11 of EWSR1 to exon 6 of CREB3L1. Split signals at EWSR1 and CREB3L1 were detected by FISH in an additional case. All cases of LGFMS and the hybrid case were found to have a FUS::CREB3L2 fusion by RT-PCR. None of the 10 pure SEFs showed evidence of FUS rearrangement. The authors conclude EWSR1 and CREB3L1 rearrangements are predominant over FUS and CREB3L2 rearrangements in pure SEF, and that SEF and LGFMS are different tumor types.

In this 2017 study, the authors utilized SNP arrays, expression profiling, transcriptome, and whole-exome sequencing to further characterize sclerosing epithelioid fibrosarcoma (SEF) and low-grade fibromyxoid sarcoma (LGFMS)/SEF hybrid tumors. The study included 13 tumors classified as pure SEF and six tumors from 4 cases of hybrid SEF/LGFMS. The patients' ages ranged from 18 to 74 years. RNA-seq detected the EWSR1::CREB3L1 gene fusion in 8/13 pure SEF cases, with 2/13 positive for EWSR1::CREB3L2, and one each for FUS::CREM, FUS::CREB3L2, and PAX5::CREB3L1, while all hybrid tumors were found to have a FUS::CREB3L2 fusion. SNP array showed both the pure SEF and hybrid tumors had multiple imbalances and structural rearrangements, and the authors suggest this could account for the poor outcome of SEF patients compared to LGFMS, which were found to be much less complex.

In this 2015 study, the authors aimed to further characterize the molecular characteristics of pure sclerosing epithelioid fibrosarcoma (SEF) and hybrid SEF/low-grade fibromyxoid sarcoma (LGFMS) lesions using FISH and/or RNA-Seq. A total of 18 cases included 10 cases of pure SEF and 8 cases of hybrid SEF/LGFMS. The overall mean age at diagnosis was 44 years (range 18–78). The pure SEF cases were found to have the well-known EWSR1::CREB3L1 fusion in 6/10 cases, a previously unidentified EWSR1::CREB3L2 fusion in 2/10 cases, a FUS rearrangement with an unknown partner in 1/10, and an EWSR1 rearrangement with an unknown partner in 1/10 case. On the other hand, the hybrid SEF/LGFMS tumors all showed the presence of a FUS::CREB3L2 fusion. The authors conclude identification of different fusions by gene-specific FISH probes can confirm differences underlying the histologically different pure SEF (mostly EWSR1 rearranged) from LGFMS variants (mainly FUS rearranged).

phenotypes: Middle age onset,Late young adult onset,Intermediate young adult onset
evidence_statement: In this 2014 study, the authors compared 10 primary sclerosing epithelioid fibrosarcomas (SEF), 4 cases of low-grade fibromyxoid sarcoma (LGFMS), and one primary hybrid SEF/LGFMS. Patients with LGFMS ranged from 22 to 53 years of age. All cases of LGFMS and the hybrid case were found to have a FUS::CREB3L2 fusion by RT-PCR. None of the 10 pure SEFs showed evidence of FUS rearrangement. EWSR1::CREB3L1 was detected in SEF. The authors conclude EWSR1 and CREB3L1 rearrangements are predominant over FUS and CREB3L2 rearrangements in pure SEF while FUS::CREB3L2 is common in LGFMS, and that SEF and LGFMS are different tumor types.

RT-PCR analysis of 59 low-grade fibromyxoid sarcomas (LGFMS) and 52 non-LGFMS tumors selected for their resemblance to LGFMS (LGFMS-like tumors), identified a FUS::CREB3L2 fusion in 45 cases, a FUS::CREB3L1 in 3 cases, and no fusion in 11 cases of LGFMS. FUS exon 6 and CREB3L2 exon 5 were most frequently rearranged. Median age at LGFMS diagnosis was 35 years (range 11 to 75 years). 7 of 52 non-LGMFS neoplasms contained a FUS-CREB3L2 fusion with 4 of these diagnosed as sclerosing epithelioid fibrosarcoma, a sarcoma known to have molecular and morphological overlap with LGMFS. The presence of these FUS fusions and the histology may be helpful in diagnosis.

phenotypes: Juvenile onset,Middle age onset,Young adult onset
evidence_statement: In this study, an RT-PCR assay detected a FUS::CREB3L2 transcript in 14 of 16 (88%) low-grade fibromyxoid sarcoma (LGFMS) cases, whereas the fusion was not detected in any of the 123 other soft-tissue tumors (including desmoid-type fibromatoses, myxofibrosarcomas, soft-tissue perineuriomas, and congenital or adult fibrosarcomas). Patients ages ranged from 13 to 58 years. The fusion product involved exon 6 of FUS and exon 5 of CREB3L2 in the majority of cases. This supports FUS::CREB3L2 detection as a reliable approach to accurately diagnose LGFMS.

The efficacy of adagrasib + cetuximab combination therapy was tested in 94 patients harbouring colorectal cancers with KRAS G12C mutations. ORR was used as the primary end-point for the study. The ORR and disease control rate were 34.0% and 85.1% respectively. The median duration of response and progression free survival were 5.8 months (95% CI; 4.2-7.6). and 6.9 months (95% CI; 5.7-7.4) respectively. The overall survival was 15.9 months (95% CI; 11.8-18.8).

disease: Glandular Pattern Ovarian Yolk Sac Tumor
evidence_statement: RNA-seq data was generated for 12 Yolk Sac Tumour (YST) samples, including 3 sensitive primary tumours and 9 relapsed tumours. Analysis revealed that OVOL2 expression was significantly higher in relapsed tumours compared to cisplatin-sensitive tumours. Furthermore, OVOL2 expression was elevated across various cancer cell lines (Wilcoxon rank-sum test, p = 4.8 × 10⁻⁹), particularly in ovarian cancer cell lines (Wilcoxon rank-sum test, p = 6.7 x 10⁻³). To further investigate the role of OVOL2 in cisplatin resistance, in-vitro tests were conducted. OVOL2 was silenced in an ovarian YST cell line (NOY1), which exhibits higher OVOL2 expression than the normal human ovarian surface epithelial cell line (HOSEpiC), using two independent small interfering RNAs (siRNAs). Silencing OVOL2 sensitized NOY1 cells to apoptosis upon cisplatin treatment. These results suggest that OVOL2 overexpression may contribute to cisplatin resistance in YST cell lines.

The germline variant rs143348853 (5bp deletion), creates MEF2 transcription factor binding site, which induces activity in the locus around AXIN2 gene and associates with elevated AXIN2 expression. Individuals carrying this genetic variant have better 10 year survival prognosis in case of CLL.

A 57-year old male with no significant smoking history presented with lung squamous cell carcinoma in the right lung. Oncomine Dx Target Test was done and revealed EGFR exon 19 deletion and de novo EGFR T790M mutation. Patient was treated with chemotadiotherapy and one course of durvalumab until a brain metastasis appeared. Stereotactic radiotherapy was then performed, but 4 months after the termination of durvalumab, the tumor increased in size. Treatment was then switched to osimertinib and partial response was achieved two months later. The authors also summarized 16 other cases of lung squamous cell carcinoma patients that were treated with osimertinib, 12 of which responded in partial responses.

This pediatric patients harboured a chordoma with high TBXT expression when compared with TCGA and POG570 data, and a high CD8+ infiltration score. The patient was treated with nivolumab, and experienced improvement in symptoms including decreased pain and improved mobility. Additionally after 3 cycles of nivolumab, the patient exhibited partial response according to RANO criteria (58% reduction in target lesion). Target lesion remained smaller compared to baseline tumour after 7 and 11 cycles, however, slow progression was observed over time compared to best response documented. After 14 cycles, the patient continued to experience clinical benefit.

Colorectal cancer cell line HT29 was invected with KRAS lentivirus constructs for wildtype, A146V, A146T, A146P, and empty. Cells were treated with the anti-EGFR monoclonal antibody cetuximab, and MEK inhibitor PD98059 for 24 hours. Cells infected with A146V and A146T constructs maintained high (aproximately 100%) cell viability at concentrations of zero to 300 ug/ml cetuximab and zero to 20 uM PD98059, using MTT assay. Wildtype, empty vector, and A146P cells showed reduced viability down to 50% at most concentrations measured for each drug. The authors concluded that A146V and A146T were resistant to both drugs, while cells transfected with A146P were sensitive to the drugs.

phenotypes: Pediatric onset,Early young adult onset,Intermediate young adult onset
evidence_statement: In the STARTRK-NG (NCT02650401) phase 1/2 trial, 43 pediatric and young adult patients (age <22 years) with recurrent or refractory solid tumors, including primary CNS tumors, were evaluated for response to entrectinib. The study enrolled patients with or without *NTRK1/2/3*, ROS1, or ALK fusions. Among the 15 patients with *NTRK1/2/3* fusions (4 NTRK1, 4 NTRK2, 7 NTRK3), the confirmed objective response rate (ORR) by blinded independent review was 60.0% (9/15; 95% CI 32.3-83.7). Responses in this group were observed in 5 of 11 patients with primary CNS tumors and all 4 patients with extracranial solid tumors. In contrast, the non-fusion population (n = 17) had an investigator-assessed ORR of 5.9% (1/17; 95% CI 0.15-28.7), which was a single complete response in a neuroblastoma patient with an ALK F1174L point mutation. The authors conclude that entrectinib resulted in rapid and durable responses in pediatric patients with solid tumors harboring *NTRK1/2/3* fusions.

5577 colon carcinoma tumors were evaluated for BRAF, KRAS, and mismatch repair status. From those successfully evaluated, 201 had microsatellite instability (MSI or MSI-H) and BRAF V600E, 72 had MSI and KRAS exon 2 mutation, and 204 had MSI and no KRAS or BRAF mutation. In addition, 279 were microsatellite stable (MSS or MSI-L) and BRAF V600E, 1450 had MSI and KRAS exon 2 mutation, and 2205 had MSI and no KRAS or BRAF mutation. MSS patients with BRAF V600E were associated with shorter time to recurrence (HR = 1.54, 95% CI = 1.23 to 1.92, P < .001). Overall survival in MSS with BRAF V600E was poorer than wild-type (HR = 2.01, 95% CI = 1.56 to 2.57, P < .001). This prognostic effect was not seen in BRAF or KRAS mutant patients that had MSI tumors.

molecular_profile: KRAS Exon 2 Mutation AND MSI Low
evidence_statement: 5577 colon carcinoma tumors were evaluated for BRAF, KRAS, and mismatch repair status. From those successfully evaluated, 201 had microsatellite instability (MSI or MSI-H) and BRAF V600E, 72 had MSI and KRAS exon 2 mutation, and 204 had MSI and no KRAS or BRAF mutation. In addition, 279 were microsatellite stable (MSS or MSI-L) and BRAF V600E, 1450 had MSI and KRAS exon 2 mutation, and 2205 had MSI and no KRAS or BRAF mutation. MSS patients with KRAS exon 2 mutations were associated with shorter time to recurrence (HR = 1.60, 95% CI = 1.40 to 1.83, P < .001). Overall survival in MSS with KRAS exon 2 mutations was poorer than wild-type (HR = 1.62, 95% CI = 1.38 to 1.91, P < .001). This prognostic effect was not seen in BRAF or KRAS mutant patients that had MSI tumors.

In this trial, 139 patients with lung adenocarcinomas harbouring EGFR activating mutations were randomly assigned to two groups to receive either EGFR-TKIs alone (n = 70) or a combination of TGFR-TKIs plus metformin (n = 69). The median PFS for both the groups was 10.9 months (95% CI; 9.8-16.3). However, univariate analysis revealed that the combination therapy of metformin plus EGFR-TKIs was associated with better PFS when compared with EGFR-TKIs treatment alone (13.1 months [95% CI; 9,8-16.3] vs 9.9 months [95%; 7.5-12.2], p=0.01). Additionally patients who received the combination therapy had 40% less risk of progression compared the group that received monotherapy (HR, 2.71; 95% CI, 1.20-6.30, p = 0.02). The median OS was also longer in patients in the metform + EGFR-TKIs group (31.7 months; 95% CI, 20.5-42.8 vs 17.5 months; 95% CI, 11.4-23.7; P = .02). Overall, the study reported that the combination therapy performed better in patients with lung adenocarcinomas with EGFR mutations when compared with the EGFR-TKI monotherapy.

molecular_profile: MTOR Mutation OR PIK3CA Mutation OR PTEN Mutation OR AKT1 Mutation OR AKT2 Mutation
evidence_statement: In this study, 30 patients with advanced solid malignancies harboring mTOR/AKT/PI3K pathway alterations were treated with Sapanisertib. The tumor types included sarcomas, breast, ovarian, head and neck, colorectal, lung, renal, endometrial, gastroesophageal junction, prostate, stomach, urachus, and cervical cancer. Four patients achieved partial response, with three of them having PTEN mutations and one having AKT and mTOR mutations. Fifteen patients had stable disease as their best response. The median overall survival was 18 months (95% CI: 7.2 - NE), and the median progression-free survival was 6 months (95% CI: 2.8 - 14.6). Of the 24 evaluable patients, 19 (79%) had disease control (SD or PR).

The authors reviewed histologically diagnosed astroblastomas at the National Institute of Mental Health and Neurosciences (Bangalore, India) between 2011 and 2018. Eight cases were identified and were tested with an MN1 break-apart FISH assay. Five of the eight cases demonstrated evidence of a 'break-apart' pattern, from which an MN1 alteration was inferred. Two of the five cases with MN1 alteration by FISH exhibited low-grade histology. The remaining three cases showed features of high-grade histological features, of which two recurred.

10 of 27 cases of histologically defined astroblastomas studied demonstrated an inferred MN1 rearrangement by break-apart FISH testing. Of these, all eight cases with material available for methylation profiling were classified as 'high-grade neuroepithelial tumor with MN1 alteration' (HGNET-MN1). Chromosome copy number profiles were analyzed using the methylation array data and notable losses included chromosomes 22q (in 1 of 8 cases), 14 (in 3 of 8 cases), and broad regions of X (in 2 of 8 cases). All cases harbored an unmethylated MGMT promoter region. A mixture of low- and high-grade histology was observed, with characteristic histological features including increased vascular and general hyalinization/sclerosis, with an absence of eosinophilic granular bodies. OLIG2 immunostaining was positive in a majority of cases (8 of 10), with a striking female preponderance (9 of 10) noted.

In an analysis of 27 histologically defined astroblastomas, 10 had MN1 rearrangements, 7 had BRAF p.V600E mutations, 2 had RELA rearrangements, and 8 had none of these drivers identified. Astroblastoma, MN1-altered showed significantly increased overall survival compared to those histologically defined astroblastomas with BRAF p.V600E mutations (p=0.013). When compared to histologically defined astroblastomas without driver mutations, overall survival in astroblastoma, MN1-altered was increased but did not reach statistical significance due to the low number of patients. The mean overall survival of astroblastoma MN1-altered was 138 months (68 to 221 months, n=7) compared to 2 to 141 months (mean, 61 months; n = 7) for patients with BRAF V600E. Given the favorable prognosis, the authors suggest a more conservative approach in this tumor type.

phenotypes: Juvenile onset,Young adult onset,Middle age onset
evidence_statement: This study identified a recurrent MALAT1::GLI1 fusion in 4 of 4 (100%) gastroblastomas from patients ranging in age from 9 to 56 years old. Initially, the fusion was identified using transcriptome sequencing in 2 cases and then validated in all 4 cases by RT-PCR and/or FISH. The fusion joins exon 1 of MALAT1 to either intron 5 or exon 6 of GLI1 with a novel transcription start site generated in exon 6 in both cases. The fusion retains the DNA-binding zinc finger domains (exons 7-10) and transactivation domain (exon 12) of GLI1. Functionally, the fusion leads to overexpression of GLI1 and activation of the Sonic hedgehog pathway. This MALAT1::GLI1 fusion appears specific to gastroblastoma, as it was not detected in other controls tested, including synovial sarcoma, leiomyoma, leiomyosarcoma, desmoid-type fibromatosis, Ewing sarcoma, Wilms’ tumor, gastrointestinal stromal tumor, gastric carcinomas, plexiform fibromyxoma, sonic hedgehog-type medulloblastomas, normal gastric mucosa, or muscularis propria. The authors suggest this fusion could serve as a useful diagnostic biomarker for gastroblastoma.

In two MAP2K4-amplified PDX models of uterine leiomyosarcoma, LEY-11 and LEY-16, novel MAP2K4 inhibitor PLX8725 inhibits tumor growth (PDX LEY-11 n=10, p<0.001) (PDX LEY-16 n=8 p=0.0062, n=9 p=0.001), and extends overall survival (PDX LEY-11 n=10, p=0.0047) (PDX LEY-16 n=8 p=0.0058, n=9 p=0.039).

In this non-randomized phase 2 KEYNOTE-158 trial 1066 patients with solid tumours and tumour mutation burden (TMB) >=10 mutations/Mb were treated with anti-PD1 antibody pembrolizumab. Of 790 patients evaluable for TMB status and included in the efficacy analysis, 30/102 (29%; 95% CI 21-39) patients in the TMB-high group had objective response, while 43/688 (6%; CI 5-8) patients in the non-TMB-high group had objective response. The authors conclude that TMB-high status is associated with robust response to pembrolizumab as a monotherapy.

Exomes were sequenced from two cohorts of non small cell lung cancer patients who were treated with pembrolizumab. In a discovery cohort of 16 patients, durable clinical benefit (DCB - partial or stable response lasting >6 months) was measured. In patients with DCB, median number of nonsynonymous mutations was 302. Median number of mutations was 148 in patients with no DCB with pembrolizumab (p=0.02). Median number of mutations in the cohort was 209. 73% of patients with mutations above 209 showed DCB, while 13% of those with mutations below the median showed DCB (p=0.04). Median progression free survival was 14.5 versus 3.7 months between the two groups. In a validation group of 18 NSCLC samples, the median mutation burden was 244 in patients with DCB, and 125 in patients with no DCB. In patients with mutation burden above the median (200), there was 83% DCB with pembrolizumab, and 22% DCB in patients below the median mutation burden of 200. In all patients tested, C-to-A transversions were more frequent in patients with DCB, and C-to-T transitions were less frequent in DCB patients.

Fresh tumor tissue 291 cervical cancer patients was fresh frozen at -70 degrees. DNA from samples was purified and analyzed via PCR for HPV 16, 18, and 6. HPV was found in 247 (85%) of tumors. HPV-16 was found in 52%, and HPV-18 in 20%, and other HPV types in found in 13% of tumors. no HPV DNA was detected in 15%. Clinical data were obtained from records. Presence of HPV DNA was associated in patients 45 years old or younger, with cigarette smoking history. HPV type was not associated with prognostic factors in this patient group. In a homogeneously treated subgroup of 171 patients who had type II radical hysterectomy and pelvic lymphadenectomy, HPV-18 was found as an independent prognostic factor. Estimated 5-year survival was 84% (80%- 88%) with HPV-16 tumors, 59% (48%-70%) for HPV-18 tumors, and 77% (64%-90%) for tumors with no detected HPV. Authors conclude it may be clinically useful to assess HPV type in early stage cervical cancers.

Human newborn forskins were prepared into 10x10 mm squares, and grafted into acid mice due to their lack of immunological functions. Foreskins were grafted onto backs of mice, usually within 4 hours of circumcision. After 3 weeks grafts appeared as normal human skin, and expressed human involucrin. HPV-16 DNA was obtained from W12 human cervical keratinocyte cell line, attached to gold particles, and introuduced into grafts via a system that uses electric spark discharge to accelerate the gold carrier particles to the target cells for transfection. 7 of 8 grafts on 4 mice survived the transfection, and of these two displayed signs of HPV infection including warty appearance and lesions. HPV-16 DNA was confirmed via PCR in the larger lesion.

A retrospective analysis from three cancer centres in China examined the use of pembrolizumab, as monotherapy or combined with chemotherapy, in 116 patients with MSI-high or TMB-high advanced solid tumours. Among 77 TMB-high (>=10 mutations/Mb) patients there were 31 partial responses and 5 complete responses, with an overall response rate of 46.7%. The median PFS was 8.5 months (95% CI 5.3-11.7 months) and the median duration of response among the 36 responders was 17.2 months (95% CI 4.8-29.6 months). At data cut-off 30 patients with TMB-high tumours remained on pembrolizumab. Only six patients had grade three adverse events (AEs) and no patient required therapy discontinuation due to AEs.

phenotypes: Pediatric onset,Intermediate young adult onset,Early young adult onset
evidence_statement: In this 1986 study the authors included 329 newly diagnosed patients with B-lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL), including 157 children and 172 adults. Cytogenetic analysis detected a t(9;22)(q34;q11) abnormality, also known as Philadelphia chromosome (Ph+) and known to result in a BCR::ABL1 fusion, in 9 children (5.7%) and 29 adult (16.9%) patients. Patients with the BCR::ABL1 fusion had a poor survival regardless of age. The authors conclude by emphasising the key role of the t(9;22)(q34;q11) and other studied cytogenetic abnormalities in determining tha nature and clinical course of disease, and stress the importance of performing cytogenetic analysis for ALL cases.

phenotypes: Pediatric onset,Early young adult onset,Intermediate young adult onset
evidence_statement: In this 1999 study the authors included 1322 B-lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) cases in patients under the age of 21 years. Cytogenetic data showed that 30 cases (2.3%) had the t(9;22)(q34;q11) known to result in a BCR::ABL1 fusion. The event free survival was significantly worse for patients with the BCR::ABL1 fusion in spite of intensified chemotherapy used in the pre-tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) era. The authors conclude that BCR::ABL1 positive ALL is a high-risk genetic type of disease.

phenotypes: Early young adult onset,Pediatric onset,Intermediate young adult onset
evidence_statement: In this 1991 study the authors included 363 children diagnosed with B-lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL). Cytogenetic analysis idenitified a t(9;22) (q34;q11) also known as BCR::ABL1 in 15 cases (4.1%). The t(9;22) identified B-ALL cases that were in the pre-tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) era associated with extremely low event-free and overall survival rates, despite an intensive therapeutic approach.

phenotypes: Intermediate young adult onset,Pediatric onset,Early young adult onset
evidence_statement: In this large 2022 landscape study the authors include 2,754 children, adolescents and young adults (AYA) with newly diagnosed B-ALL (n=2,288 cases) or T-ALL (n=466). Median age at diagnosis was 6.4 years (range 0 to 30). Somatic structural variants, including gene fusions, were detected with whole genome sequencing and RNA sequencing. BCR::ABL1 fusion (described as Ph+) was detected in 65/1270 (5%) B-ALL cases. Co-occurence of alterations in PAX5 and IKZF1 were frequent in Ph+ B-ALL. The authors found that ETV6::RUNX1 fusion and hyperdiploid ALL are the most common B-ALL subtypes in pediatric patients, while the BCR::ABL1 subtype with the prevalence of 5% was less common than in adults.

disease: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With MNX1::ETV6 Fusion
evidence_statement: In this 2001 study, the authors identified AML patients with 7q and 12p (ETV6) cytogenetic abnormalities from a cohort of 130 patients aged 0 to 17 years. Of the 125 cases with suitable karyotypes, 5 were confirmed by re-examination of the karyograms or FISH analysis to have the t(7;12)(q36;p13) also known as MNX1::ETV6 (previously known as HLXB9::ETV6). The authors noted that the 5 cases were aged between 0 and 18 months of age, and represented 5/23 cases in this age group without Down syndrome. The authors also included a further 5 cases with (7;12)(q36;p13) after re-examination of other archived karyotype databases. The authors conclude that the t(7;12) is associated with hematologic malignancies in children who are 18 months of age or younger.

disease: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With MNX1::ETV6 Fusion
evidence_statement: In this 2006 study, the authors examined cytogenetics for the presence of a 7q31-36 and 12p11-13 chromosomal abnormality in 320 infants and pediatric ALL and AML patients younger than 36 months of age. Of the 59 AML cases 6 patients (aged 2 to 18 months) were found to harbor the t(7;12)(q36;p12) also known as MNX1::ETV6 (previously known as HLXB9::ETV6), and represented 5/18 patients with infant AML (0 to 12 months of age). One infant ALL case also harbored the t(7;12)(q36;p13). All t(7;12)-positive AML samples had an additional copy of chromosome 19. Four t(7;12)-positive cases were confirmed by RT-PCR to have a fusion of HLXB9 (MNX1) exon 1 to ETV6 exon 3. The authors conclude that the t(7;12)(q36;p13) is almost exclusively present in infant AML and is often associated with a gain of chromosome 19.

disease: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With MNX1::ETV6 Fusion
evidence_statement: In this 2018 study, the authors included 651 pediatric patients diagnosed with AML. Seven patients were found to have a t(7;12)(q36;p13) also known as MNX1::ETV6 (previously known as HLXB9::ETV6), with the median age at diagnosis being 6 months (range 2 to 8 months), and representing 8.6% of AML patients below one year of age. All seven children were also found to have a gain of chromosome 19. The authors conclude that t(7;12)(q36;p13) should be considered as a specific AML subgroup in the WHO classification.

Neratinib-resistant cell lines were established by stepwise escalation method and high concentration method in breast cancer cell line BT-474 and lung cancer cell line H2170 with HER2 amplification. Expression levels of YES1 and phosphorylation levels of SRC family proteins were found to be upregulated in the cell lines. YES1 knockdown was performed using siRNA, which allowed for the restoration of anti-tumour effect of neratinib in the resistant cell lines. Treatment with dasatinib, an SRC inhibitor, in combination with neratinib also helped overcome the resistance to neratinib. These results suggest that YES1 plays an important role in resistance to HER2-targeted drugs
