evidence_statement: In this 2022 study the authors included 4 cases of sinonasal acinic cell carcinoma and 10 acinic cell carcinoma cases of the parotid gland. All four sinonasal patients were male, aged from 27 to 70 years. Using immunohistochemistry they detected positive NR4A3 nuclear staining in all 14 cases, while negative nuclear staining was observed in 39 other sinonasal tumors. In 3 of the 4 sinonasal Acinic cell carcinoma evaluated by NR4A3 break apart FISH, they tested positive to a rearrangement. Using RT-PCR the authors detected a significant increase in NR4A3 mRNA levels in all salivary gland and sinonasal acinic cell carcinoma patients compared with normal parotid gland tissue. The authors conclude that this is the first study to show that NR4A3 could serve as a reliable marker to distinguish sinonasal acinic cell carcinoma from other sinonasal tumors.

In this 2023 study the authors included 4 cases of acinic cell carcinoma of the salivary gland. The age of the patients ranged from 13 to 16 years, and included 2 males and 2 females. Immunohistochemistry showed the tumour cells from all four patients had strong, diffuse nuclear positive staining to NR4A3, while the adjacent benign salivary tissue was negative. In this study the authors considered NR4A3 immunohistochemical staining as a surrogate marker for t(4;9)(q13;q31) and a highly sensitive and specific marker for acinic cell carcinoma.

A retrospective analysis of 871 non-squamous NSCLC patients treated with chemotherapy (platinum compound plus pemetrexed) combined with immunotherapy (pembrolizumab) found that those with STK11 mutations had significantly shorter PFS and OS compared to those with wild-type STK11. The median PFS was 4.8 months in the STK11 mutation group compared to 7.0 months in the wild-type group (PFS hazard ratio (HR) = 1.60, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.24–2.07, P = 0.002 by log-rank test), while median OS was 11.1 months in the mutant group and 16.7 months in the wild-type group (OS HR 1.55, 95% CI: 1.18–2.05, P = 0.014).

A retrospective analysis of 871 non-squamous NSCLC patients treated with chemotherapy (platinum compound plus pemetrexed) combined with immunotherapy (pembrolizumab) found that those with KEAP1 mutations had significantly shorter PFS and OS compared to those with wild-type KEAP1. The median PFS was 2.7 months in the KEAP1 mutation group compared to 5.7 months in the wild-type group (HR 2.07, 95% CI: 1.35–3.17, P < 0.0001 by log-rank test), while median OS was 7.6 months in the mutant group and 16.6 months in the wild-type group (HR 2.24, 95% CI: 1.42–3.54, P < 0.001). KEAP1 mutation was also associated with lower objective response rate (14.3% versus 43.0%, P < 0.0001). Worse outcome on chemoimmunotherapy in the KEAP1 mutation group was independent of KRAS mutational status, TMB and PD-L1 expression.

A retrospective analysis of 871 non-squamous NSCLC patients treated with chemotherapy (platinum compound plus pemetrexed) combined with immunotherapy (pembrolizumab) found that those with STK11 or KEAP1 mutations had significantly shorter PFS and OS compared to those that were wild-type for these genes. Patients with co-mutation of STK11 and KEAP1 fared even worse that those with a single mutation, with a response rate of 7.1% compared to 29.6% (STK11 mutation) or 28.6% (KEAP1 mutation). Similarly, PFS and OS were 2.7 months and 7.8 months for co-mutated patients compared to 5.0 months and 11.1 months for STK11-mut/KEAP1-wt, 1.5 months and 6.9 months for STK11-wt/KEAP1-mut, and 8.4 months and 19.7 months for STK11-wt/KEAP1-wt.

A phase 3 randomized trial assessed dostarlimab or placebo (combined with carboplatin-paclitaxel) in 494 patients with recurrent or primary advanced (stage III/IV) endometrial cancer (RUBY trial). Endometrioid carcinoma, serous carcinoma, and carcinosarcoma were diagnosed in 54.7%, 20.6%, and 8.9% of patients, respectively. MMR/MSI status was assessed using IHC, NGS, and/or PCR, identifying 118 patients (23.9%) with dMMR–MSI-H tumors. In this first interim report, for dMMR–MSI-H subgroup, the 24-month PFS for dostarlimab arm (n=53) was 61.4% (95% CI, 46.3−73.4) vs. placebo arm (n=65) was 15.7% (95% CI, 7.2−27.0) in the subgroup (HR, 0.28; 95% CI, 0.16−0.50; P<0.001). The 24-month OS for dostarlimab arm was 83.3% (95% CI, 66.8−92.0) vs. placebo arm was 58.7% (95% CI, 43.4−71.2) in the dMMR–MSI-H subgroup (HR, 0.30; 95% CI, 0.13−0.70). For pMMR-MSS subgroup, the 24-month PFS for dostarlimab arm (n=192) was 28.4% (95% CI, 21.2−36.0) vs. placebo arm (n=184) was 18.8% (95% CI, 12.8−25.7) in the subgroup (HR, 0.76; 95% CI, 0.59−0.98). The 24-month OS for dostarlimab arm was 67.7% (95% CI, 59.8−74.4) vs. placebo arm was 55.1% (95% CI, 46.8−62.5) in the pMMR-MSS population (HR, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.52−1.02). Dostarlimab plus carboplatin–paclitaxel significantly improved PFS in patients with primary advanced (stage III/IV) or recurrent endometrial cancer, especially in dMMR–MSI-H patients.

A 14.6-year-old male [ID: 6] with a family history of neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) affecting both parents and a sibling. The patient was asymptomatic at diagnosis, and a biopsy of the left frontal glioma (diffuse astrocytoma) was performed. Tumour sequencing revealed a germline (presumed) NF1 variant (c.4930G>C, p.D1644H, VAF=51%) and a somatic stop-gain mutation (p.Q1189*, c.3565C>T, VAF=14%). CNV analysis revealed gains in chromosomes 5 (4n), 8, 15q, and 19. No focal gene amplifications or deletions were reported. His treatment included LITT and Selumetinib. No tumor progression or recurrence has been observed over 7.7 months of follow-up.

In the overall population, the HR for PFS2 was 0.66 (95% CI, 0.52−0.84), with the dMMR/MSI-H subgroup showing a greater benefit (HR, 0.33; 95% CI, 0.18−0.63) than the pMMR/MSS subgroup (HR, 0.74, 95% CI, 0.57−0.97).

The tumor progressed at 33.0 months. Sequencing analysis of the recurrent tumor was same as previous tumour. However, copy number analysis revealed gains in 9q, 12, 14q, and interstitial 17q, and losses in 10p, distal 11p, distal 11q, interstitial 13q, distal 13q, distal 17q, and 20p. CDKN2A/B (9p21.3) remained homozygously deleted. DNA methylation profiling classified the initial tumor to molecularly high-grade group, HGAP (high-grade astrocytoma with piloid features). Adjuvant therapies included radiotherapy and temozolomide. The patient remains alive at 44.8 months of follow-up.

This study reported 47 neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) patients with biallelic inactivation of NF1 genes were detected in all glial tumors. Targeted capture-based next-generation sequencing (479 cancer-related genes for detection of sequence variants, also for structural variants and copy number analysis), and DNA methylation profiling were performed. DNA methylation analysis identified a molecular low-grade group classified as "pilocytic astrocytoma arising in the setting of neurofibromatosis type 1" (PA-NF1), and a molecular high-grade group. A 34.2-year-old male (ID: 38) with no known family history of NF1. The patient presented with gait disturbance. A cerebellar tumor subtotal resection was diagnosed as pilocytic astrocytoma. Tumor sequencing revealed germline (presumed) NF1 missense mutation (c.4526G>A, p.R1509H, VAF=87%). Additional somatic mutations detected were ATRX (c.927_934del, p.E310fs*9, VAF=45%) and CDKN2A (c.193+1G>C, VAF=46%). Copy number analysis detected chromosomal gains in proximal 9p, distal 9p, 12q, and 17q, with losses in chromosome 1, interstitial 9p, 11q, and 13q. CN-LOH was detected in 17q (containing NF1). The patient experienced tumor progression at <1 month postoperatively and died of glioma at 4.4 months.

A 48 year old male with lung adenocarcinoma who was a smoker presented with diminished vision and tinnitus, and multiple intracranial brain metastasis were identified by CT. Metastatic site was submitted for molecular profiling. Histopathological analysis confirmed diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma, and immunophenotyping confirmed this. ALK protein expression was negative. NGS identified EGFR::RAD51 fusion at the metastatic site, and reduction in copy number of CDKN2A. Breakpoints were intron 24 for EGFR (NM_005228 chr7:55,268,165) and intron 3 of RAD51 (NM_002875 chr15:40,994,701) using hg19. Erlotinib 150 mg/qd was administered and decrease in tumor size was seen after one month via CT scan, and this was classified as partial response, with stable disease after 5 months treatment. The authors conclude that this case report supports erlotinib treatment of EGFR::RAD51 fusion NSCLC patients.

This article identified in-frame EGFR-SHC1 fusions in a 61-year-old male smoker with stage IIIA NSCLC, retaining functional kinase domains. RNA-based NGS fusion assays was used for detecting actionable fusions in driver-negative cases.

In the transplantable MC38 colon carcinoma cell line, expression of PIK3CA:p.H1047R (or constructs with similar function) confers survival advantage under PD-1 blockade compared with wildtype, which can be reversed by PI3K inhibition. This effect is mediated by tumour microenvironment modulation.

In this article, the authors develop a method to detect gene fusion events using RNA-seq data and apply it to nearly 7,000 samples from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA). Through this approach, they identify several novel and recurrent kinase gene fusions.

A phase 3 randomized trial evaluated pembrolizumab (+ adjuvant chemotherapy) vs. placebo (+ adjuvant chemotherapy) in 1,095 newly diagnosed high-risk (non-endometrioid histology with FIGO stage I/II; endometrioid histology with p53/TP53 abnormality; or any histology with FIGO stage III/IVA) endometrial cancer patients (pembrolizumab, n = 545; placebo, n = 550). Tumour MMR status was assessed using immunohistochemistry (VENTANA MMR RxDx Panel). dMMR cases were 141 (26%) in the pembrolizumab arm and 140 (25%) in the placebo arm. Interim analysis revealed 119 (22%) DFS events (recurrence or death) in the pembrolizumab arm and 121 (22%) in the placebo arm. DFS events in dMMR subgroup (n = 281) favored pembrolizumab (HR 0.31, 95% CI 0.14–0.69; pembrolizumab = 6% events, placebo = 18% events). In pMMR subgroup (n = 814), DFS events was comparable between treatment arms (HR 1.20, 95% CI 0.91–1.57; pembrolizumab = 27% events, placebo = 23% events). Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy arm had lesser DFS events in dMMR but not in pMMR tumours.

A 65-year-old female with lung adenocarcinoma underwent NGS testing, revealing an EGFR-MACF1 fusion at the RNA level (mutation abundance: 17%) and EGFR amplification (copy number: 24.15). The fusion involved EGFR exons 1–23 and MACF1 exons 59–93. Per RECIST guidelines, she showed a partial response to almonertinib, with progression-free survival exceeding 9 months.

A 58-year-old male with stage IVB lung adenocarcinoma presented with respiratory symptoms and widespread metastases. NGS revealed EGFR-GNAT3 fusion (EGFR exons 1–24 to GNAT3 exon 8; 76.3% abundance) and EGFR amplification (copy number: 8.1). Initial chemoembolization led to tumor shrinkage, but treatment interruption and limited response to almonertinib followed. The patient died of lung infection and multi-organ failure; OS was <7 months.

This case study reports the first case of a KIF5B-EGFR fusion (KIF5B exon 15–EGFR exon 18) in primary lung adenocarcinoma. The patient showed a significant partial response to afatinib and bevacizumab after 2 months of treatment. KIF5B, located on chromosome 10, encodes a kinesin motor protein involved in organelle transport along microtubules.

47 patients with locally advanced rectal cancer were treated with dostarlimab. 41 completed treatment and achieved a clinical complete response. No patients experienced local or distant disease recurrence. Further, twenty patients achieved a sustained clinical complete response with a median follow-up of 28.9 months (95% CI 22.9 -37.1) from first treatment. Results were reported initially in 2022 PMID: 35660797 (16 patients), and at ASCO in 2024 (inclusive of PMID:35660797, abstract reporting on 47 patients). A larger multi-center study (AZUR-1) is in progress (PMID: 40107952, NCT05723562). PMID: 35660797 cites dostarlimab administered at 500 mg every 3 weeks for 6 months (nine cycles), to be followed by standard radiation therapy (total dose of 5040 cGy given in 28 fractions).

A 62 year-old female never smoker diagnosed of lung adenocarcinoma that was negative for EGFR and ALK alterations (EGFR hotspot tissue NGS) was treated with carboplatin/ pemetrexed/ bevacizumab (x 6 cycles) followed by maintenance (x4 cycles) prior to PD. She then went on nivolumab (x6 cycles) until Progressive Disease (PD) with pleural effusion and brain metastasis. An EGFR::RAD51 fusion was detected in the pleural fluid by Foundation Medicine. The DNA fusion consists of EGFR exons 1-24 (breakpoint in EGFR intron 24) coupled to RAD51 exons 4-10 (breakpoint in RAD51 intron 3). Patient was treated with afatinib (at 40 mg/d, then 30 mg/d) following detection of the EGFR::RAD51 fusion and showed stable disease after 6 months. The authors note that EGFR::RAD51 was not seen in earlier assays of the tumor, and state that this might be due to the appearance of the fusion during tumor evolution, or due to it being missed by earlier assays. They note that other detections of the fusion came from Foundation Medicine assays, and most other assays are not designed to cover EGFR exons 24 and 25.

This is a case report of 29-year-old diagnosed with metastatic adenocarcinoma of the left lung. The patient was treated with chemotherapy (cisplatin 75 mg/m2 and pemetrexed 500 mg/m2 every 3 weeks) and immunotherapy (pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks) for 4 cycles then maintenance with pembrolizumab and pemetrexed for 4 cycles before PD on lungs, brain and lymph nodes. FoundationOne DX1 on a new mediastinal lymph node biopsy detected an EGFR::RAD51 fusion. Patient was then treated with erlotinib (150mg/d) and achieved PR on all tumour sites three weeks following treatment initiation. The patient was switched to Osimertinib (80 mg/d) after being on erlotinib for two months due to renal toxicity. Further tumour response was observed at subsequent restating imaging and the patient is still on treatment 10 months since EGFR-TKI initiation.

A 37-year-old never smoker was diagnosed of pulmonary adenocarcinoma with mucinous pattern. FoundationOne DX1 panel detected an EGFR::RAD51 fusion and the patient was treated with first-line gefitinib. The patient achieved CR three months after treatment initiation and developed PD after one year.

This is a case report of a 45-year-old male never smoker that was diagnosed with metastatic lung adenocarcinoma. The patient responded poorly to the initial chemoimmunotherapy (carboplatin, pemetrexed, nivolumab, and ipilimumab) and progressively deteriorated. Following the detection of an EGFR::RAD51 gene fusion by repeat NGS using FoundationOne Liquid CDx, the patient was treated with Osimertinib (80mg/d) and experienced dramatic symptom improvement within one month of treatment initiation. Despite asymptomatic intracranial metastases with stable systemic disease at 9 months, the patient remained on therapy and continued to show PR 12 months after initiation of Osimertinib.

This is a case report of a 58-year-old never-smoker diagnosed with metastatic lung adenocarcinoma. The patient was treated with multiple lines of chemotherapy ((1) carboplatin/pemetrexed, (2)docetaxel 75 mg/m2 once every 3 weeks/ramucirumab, (3) paclitaxel/ramucirumab, and (4)gemcitabine) prior to developing peritoneal progression. An EGFR::ERBB4 fusions was then identified using Foundation Medicine. The DNA-based testing demonstrated fusion between EGFR exons 1-27 and EGFR exons 18-28, while subsequent RNA-based fusion testing demonstrated an in-frame transcript coupling EGFR exon 25 to ERBB4 exon 18. Following identification of the EGFR::ERBB4 fusion, the patient was enrolled in a trial of tarloxotinib, a pan-ERBB/HER kinase inhibitor, which was discontinued after <4 months following further peritoneal progression and ovarian metastases. The patient was then enrolled in a trial of fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan-nxki (T-DXd), where she remained on therapy with stable disease for approximately 20 months until peritoneal and ovarian progression. The patient then received mobocertinib (160mg/d), achieving CR of all peritoneal lesion and PR of ovarian metastases on the initial scan. Dozens of intraparenchymal foci were detected approximately 6 months following mobocertinib initiation, patient was switched to Osimertinib (80mg/d) which led to continuous PR in the ovaries, resolution of brain metastases, and reduction of the lesion in the right front lobe. The patient remains on Osimertinib eight months after.

evidence_statement: In this study, the authors characterized the TEL (currently ETV6)::AML1 (currently RUNX1) gene fusion in B-lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) with the t(12;21)(p12;q22) using cytogenetic and molecular methods, including FISH, PCR, Southern blot hybridization, and sequencing. Analysis of nine patient specimens (two AML, seven B-ALL) and two cell lines revealed that the TEL (ETV6) gene breakpoint in t(12;21)(p12;q22) differs from the one in t(5;12)(q33;p13) seen in Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemia (CMML). The TEL (ETV6) gene remained active on both derivative chromosomes, with der(21) expressing a 5’ ETV6::3'RUNX1 fusion transcript lacking the ETS DNA-binding domain, while der(12) expressed the ETS domain under an unknown promoter (G4). Additionally, ETV6 was deleted from the normal chromosome 12. The breakpoint in the RUNX1 gene was at its 5’ end, upstream of breakpoints in other myeloid malignancies [t(8;21), t(3;21)]. The ETV6::RUNX1 fusion protein retained helix-loop-helix (HLH) domain from the ETV6-encoded protein which interacts with transcriptional regulators, and nearly entire RUNX1-encoded protein. The chimeric protein was predicted to cause dysregulated transcription of lymphoid lineage-specific genes. These findings provide insight into the molecular mechanisms of ETV6::RUNX1-driven leukemogenesis in B-ALL.

In this study, the authors investigated the t(12;21)(p13;q22) in pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). The t(12;21) is typically not visible by karyotype analysis and is rarely detected by conventional cytogenetics (<0.05% of cases). However, using molecular techniques, the authors identified the resulting TEL::AML1 (known currently as ETV6::RUNX1) fusion transcript in 22% of pediatric ALL patients, making it the most frequent genetic alteration in this disease. The TEL::AML1 (ETV6::RUNX1) fusion results from the rearrangement of TEL (ETV6), a helix-loop-helix ETS-like transcription factor, and AML1 (RUNX1), the DNA-binding subunit of the core-binding factor (CBF) transcription complex. Patients harboring the TEL::AML1 (ETV6::RUNX1) fusion exhibited distinct clinical features, including an age range of 1 to 10 years, B-lineage immunophenotype, non-hyperdiploid DNA content, and an excellent prognosis. These findings underscore the role of ETV6::RUNX1 fusion in defining a common and clinically relevant subtype of pediatric B-ALL.

Analysis was performed on 224 advanced prostate cancer (PCA) patient samples which had clinical outcome information. Elevated PSA levels in patients after radical prostatectomy are associated with metastases and poor outcome, and in this study clinical failure was defined as a PSA greater than 0.2 ng/ml after radical prostatectomy and successive increasing PSA values. In the patient samples, elevated AR-V7 staining was associated with greater risk for PSA recurrence after radical prostatectomy (log-rank test, p < 0.0001). AR-V7 was a significant predictor of PCA recurrence after adjusting for other variables such as Gleason sum score, preoperative PSA, size of largest individual nodule of invasive cancer, and surgical margin status via multivariable Cox Regression Analysis. AR-V7 was the strongest predictor with a hazard ratio of 2.5 (95% CI: 1.3–4.6, p=0.004).

disease: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With NUP98 Rearrangement
evidence_statement: In this 2016 study the authors included 153 pediatric non-Down syndrome patients diagnosed with acute megakaryoblastic leukemia (AMKL) which is a rare subtype of acute myeloid leukemia. All patients were screened for NUP98::KDM5A, CBFA2T3::GLIS2, RBM15::MKL1 and KMT2A rearrangements with polymerase chain reaction (PCR). The PCR primers for NUP98::KDM5A were designed to detect a NUP98 exon 12 fusion to exon 27 of KDM5A. The NUP98::KDM5A gene fusion was detected in 14 patients (9%) with a median age of 1.9 years (range 0.8-8.5); it was mutually exclusive with other tested fusions and its' presence was associated with an unfavorable outcome. The NUP98::KDM5A fusion is the primary abnormality in a subtype of pediatric AML commonly presenting with magakaryoblastic differentiation and associated with a poor clinical outcome.

disease: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With NUP98 Rearrangement
evidence_statement: In this 2011 study the authors included pediatric and adult cohorts of patients diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Initially, using RT-PCR, they detected the cytogenetically cryptic NUP98::NSD1 in-frame gene fusion of NUP98 exon 12 to exon 6 of NSD1 in 2/45 pediatric cytogenetically normal AML (CN-AML) patients and in 1/47 adult CN-AML cases. A further 1101 AML cases were then screened using RT-PCR and the identical NUP98::NSD1 in-frame fusion was detected in 23 (2.1%) cases. The NUP98::NSD1 fusion was detected more frequently in pediatric patients with a median age of onset at 17 years (range 2 to 63), and was particularly frequent in children when considering only the CN-AML cases. Three additional cases with cytogenetically visible 11p15-aberrations were also confirmed to have NUP98 gene fusions, however with alternate partners including JARID1A, TOP1 and DDX10. NUP98::NSD1 was frequently associated with FLT3 ITD (91% of cases) and WT1 mutations (45% of cases). The authors conclude that the cryptic NUP98::NSD1 fusion defines a previously unrecognized group of young AML patients associated with an unfavorable outcome and routine screening for NUP98::NSD1 at diagnosis is essential.

evidence_statement: In this 2014 study the authors investigated the presence of NUP98::NSD1 fusion in pediatric and adult acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patients. Utilizing reverse transcriptase-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) the NUP98::NSD1 fusion was identified in 39/920 (4%) patients. Since 36 of the 39 NUP98::NSD1 patients were either FLT3 ITD positive or cytogenetically normal (CN-AML) a further 620 patients who harbored FLT3 ITD and/or CN-AML were included for screening, with the NUP98::NSD1 identified in 63 (10%) patients. All patients harbored the identical in-frame fusion of NUP98 exon 12 and NSD1 exon 6. Age of patients with NUP98::NSD1 varied from <1 to 50 years of age (median, 10 years), indicating that NUP98::NSD1 is more frequent in younger age. NUP98::NSD1 cases frequently (82%) harbored a FLT3 ITD, and 26% harbored simultaneously FLT3 ITD and WT1 mutations. The authors conclude that the NUP98::NSD1 fusion, frequently co-occurring with FLT3 ITD, defines a subgroup of AML patients at very high risk for induction failure; the study supports upfront screening of CN-AML for the cytogenetically cryptic NUP98::NSD1 fusion.

disease: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With NUP98 Rearrangement
evidence_statement: In this 2023 study the authors included 2,235 children and young adults diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). NUP98 fusions were detected in these patients either by karyotype of RNA sequencing. Overall 160 patients (7.2%) were identified to have a NUP98 rearrangement. The most common NUP98 translocations were NUP98::NSD1 (108/160) and NUP98::KDM5A (32/160), however 20 patients were detected with 13 different NUP98 translocation partners, including HOXA9 (n=4), HOXD13 (n=3), PHF15 (n=2), PHF23 (n=2) and single cases of BPTF, BRWD3, DDX10, HMGB3, HOXA13, KAT7, PRRX1, SET, and TOP1. NUP98 fusions were enriched in children aged 3-10 years old. NUP98 fusion breakpoints by RNA sequencing revealed a high diversity of NUP98 exon junctions, although 85% of NUP98 fusions had a breakpoint junction in exon 12 or 13, the remaining cases had breakpoints occurring in various positions from exon 11 to exon 29. The NUP98::KDM5A immunophenotype corresponded to megakaryocytic maturation. For NUP98:NSD1 cases, enrichment of FLT3 ITD (74%) and WT1 mutations (42%) was detected. The authors conclude that NUP98 fusions constitute a highly refractory class of AML, regardless of fusion partner.

evidence_statement: In this 2018 study, the authors analyzed tumor samples from 13 patients diagnosed with IG-MYC–positive neoplasms exhibiting a precursor B-cell phenotype. This entity is molecularly distinct from classical Burkitt lymphoma (BL), which arises from mature germinal center B cells, whereas these cases originate from the same immature B-cell precursors like precursor B-cell leukemias/lymphomas (pB-ALL/LBL currently known as B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (B-ALL/LL)]. The cohort included 11 leukemic presentations and 2 nodal cases, with six patients displaying L3/Burkitt-like morphology. The median age at diagnosis was 21 years (range 3–75), with a predominance in males (11 out of 13 patients). Relapse samples from three patients were also included. IG-MYC translocations involved IGH in 10 cases, IGK in 1, and IGL in 2. Notably, four cases (including the cell line 380) harbored a concurrent t(14;18)/IGH-BCL2 translocation, with a median age of 18 years (range 13–43), making transformation from an undetected follicular lymphoma unlikely. Supporting this, cell line 380 lacked mutations typically observed in follicular lymphoma. The IG-MYC rearrangements in pB-ALL/LBL were found to result from aberrant V(D)J recombination, a mechanism characteristic of early B-cell development. Most cases lacked functional B-cell receptor (BCR) expression due to biallelic IGH alterations and harbored NRAS or KRAS mutations, while mutations commonly found in BL were absent. DNA methylation profiling demonstrated that the cases clustered with precursor B cells and pB-ALL/LBL rather than with BL. These findings support the conclusion that recurrent IG-MYC translocations define a subset of pB-ALL/LBL characterized by distinct molecular features.

In this 2018 study, the authors described three rare adult cases of B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (B-ALL/LBL) exhibiting Burkitt lymphoma-like morphology driven by isolated IGH/MYC translocations—a genetic abnormality typically associated with mature B-cell neoplasms. All three cases occurred in male patients presenting initially with diffuse lymphadenopathy. Cases 1 and 2 were diagnosed as B-ALL with markedly elevated lymphoblast counts in the peripheral blood and bone marrow, while Case 3, a patient with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection, was diagnosed with B-LBL based on a retroperitoneal lymph node biopsy, without bone marrow or peripheral blood involvement. Despite the Burkitt-like morphology, all cases retained an immature B-cell immunophenotype, justifying their classification as MYC-positive B-ALL/LBL. These cases are exceptionally rare, particularly in the absence of concurrent BCL2 rearrangements. The study utilized clinical assessments, flow cytometry, immunohistochemistry, fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), and cytogenetic analyses to characterize the immunophenotype and detect MYC rearrangements. All three patients presented with aggressive clinical features, demonstrated variable responses to therapy, and ultimately had poor prognoses. The findings highlight that MYC rearrangements characterize a subtype of B-ALL/LBL with unique clinical and molecular features and unfavorable outcome.

In this 2022 study, the authors reported a rare case of atypical Burkitt leukemia/lymphoma (BL) in a 10-month-old infant, exhibiting overlapping features of both classical BL and its precursor form, preBLL. PreBLL is generally characterized by an immature B-cell immunophenotype, IGH::MYC translocations arising from aberrant V(D)J recombination, and frequent NRAS/KRAS mutations. In contrast, classical BL is associated with mature B-cell markers and recurrent mutations in MYC, ID3, and CCND3. The patient in this case demonstrated immunophenotypic immaturity, including the absence of CD20 and surface immunoglobulins, alongside BL-like morphology and an IGH::MYC rearrangement generated through V(D)J recombination. Whole-exome sequencing identified somatic mutations in FBXO11, commonly seen in classical BL, as well as TNIK and a mosaic KRAS mutation, the latter being more typical of preBLL and developmental disorders. These findings indicate a maturation stage intermediate between classical BL and preBLL. Despite the atypical molecular and phenotypic presentation, the patient achieved sustained remission following high-risk chemotherapy and remained disease-free after 38 months. This case illustrates association of IGH::MYC rearrangement with a unique type of preBLL distinct from BL.

A 56 year old woman presents with poorly differentiated stage IIIC lung adenocarcinoma. Chemoradiotherapy and 12-month durvalumab was administered with significant response. 11 months after durvalumab treatment, the patient experienced disease progression and biopsy revealed an adenocarcinoma. Next-generation sequencing (NGS) revealed a KIF5B-MET fusion variant (e24::e15), PDGFRA mutation, and RICTOR amplification. Patient was enrolled in telisotuzmab vedotin phase 2 clinical trial, to which there was partial regression of axillary lymph node. 8 months later, the patient experienced another disease progression, with NGS reporting KIF5B-MET fusion without any other oncogenic mutations. The patient was then administered capatinib, with dramatic response after 3 months of therapy. At the time of the paper, the patient had been on capmatinib for nine months with no significant adverse side effects. The authors suggest that capatinib can be used as salvage therapy for patients with acquired resistance to telisotuzumab vedotin.

Functional activity and treatment response were evaluated for several fusions identified in patients with gene expression profiles showing BCR::ABL1-like B-ALL. Phosphoflow on leukemic samples from 2 patients harboring NUP214::ABL1 fusions showed downstream activation of ABL1 by showing endogenous increased phosphorylation of the ABL1 target CRKL, which could be inhibited by treatment with either imatinib or dasatinib. Five non-BCR::ABL1-like primary B-ALLs specimens tested did not show increased phosphorylation of CRKL or response to either TKI. Additionally, bone marrow harvested from xenograft mice established from a patient harboring the fusion were injected into the tail vein of NSG mice. Following engraftment, mice were randomized to dasatinib or vehicle treatment resulting in a significant reduction in leukemic burden (blast count) in mice receiving dasatinib relative to vehicle control with a durable response maintained up to 8 weeks (N=5/group).

In murine 32D cells expressing either FLT3 internal tandem duplication (ITD) or FLT3-ITD-N676K, FLT3-ITD kinase activity was inhibited by tyrosine kinase inhibitor PKC412 at a 20nM dose. However, the FLT3-ITD-N676K mutant showed high levels of phosphorylated tyrosine up to a concentration of 50nM. In a proliferation assay, a 10-fold higher concentration of PKC412 was necessary to inhibit cellular proliferation in FLT3-ITD-N676K cells compared to FLT3-ITD cells. In addition, FLT3-ITD-N676K cells were resistant to apoptosis. Overall, this study reported FLT3 N676K as the cause of clinical resistance to PKC412 in one patient with AML.

FLT3 F691L was observed in 2 patient samples collected after at least 28 days of treatment with crenolanib. Prior to treatment with crenolanib, both patients were treated with quizartinib. Ba/F3 cells transduced with retroviral vector expressing F691L did not show cell transformation in an interleukin-3 withdrawal assay. Ba/F3 cells expressing double-mutant FLT3 F691L/D835Y resulted in cell transformation and crenolanib resistance.

In this study, the authors employed next-generation sequencing (NGS) to compare the genetic profiles of lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) patients with and without adrenal metastases. An EGFR-SUMF2 fusion was identified in one of the 90 primary LUAD tumor samples from a patient with adrenal metastases

disease: Embryonal Tumor With Multilayered Rosettes, C19MC-altered
evidence_statement: This landmark study contributed to the recognition of embryonal tumor with multilayered rosettes (ETMRs) as a distinct entity in the 2016 WHO classification. Previously, ETMRs were included within the heterogeneous central nervous system-primitive neuroectodermal tumors (CNS-PNETs). ETMRs were reclassified following the identification of focal amplification at chromosome 19q13.4 encompassing a miRNA cluster (C19MC). Using DNA copy number profiling and fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), the authors detected this amplification in 11 of 45 (~25%) primary CNS-PNETs, but in only 1 of 263 cases of non-CNS-PNETs, highlighting its specificity. In conclusion, this study provided the first molecular diagnostic marker for ETMR, a rare and aggressive pediatric brain tumor.

This study aimed to identify the mechanism underlying overexpression of a miRNA cluster on chromosome 19q13.4 (C19MC) and its oncogenicity in embryonal tumors with multilayered rosettes (ETMRs). Through analyses of 12 ETMR samples (including 2 recurrences), C19MC fusions downstream of the TTYH1 promoter were found in all cases. C19MC is the largest miRNA cluster in primates, containing 46 miRNA genes. This study found that miR-519a and miR-512-3p, encoded by the cluster, change the genome-wide methylation signature through the aberrant activation of DNMT3B, a DNA methyltransferase, to reawaken a fetal neural development program. This effect occurs through these two miRNAs targeting DNMT3B’s negative regulator RBL2. In summary, overexpression of C19MC driven by the TTYH1 promoter is the primary tumor-specific event that drives ETMR formation through its encoded oncogenic miRNAs.

This cohort study examined the molecular landscape of embryonal tumors with multilayered rosettes (ETMRs) at diagnosis and relapse. ETMRs have previously been shown to frequently (~90%) exhibit amplification or fusion of the chromosome 19 miRNA cluster (C19MC). Here, a larger cohort was analyzed, comprising 193 primary ETMR cases along with 23 matched relapse specimens. Based on the copy-number profiles inferred from methylation arrays, 90% of cases exhibited C19MC amplification. Furthermore, structural rearrangements involving C19MC were identified, with fusion partners including MYO9B on chromosome 19, MIRLET7BHG, or the previously known TTYH1. Collectively, this study presented a relatively large cohort for this rare disease; it confirmed the presence of C19MC genomic alterations in nearly all the cases, and identified several structural aberrations in C19MC through comprehensive molecular profiling.

A case of metastatic renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is reported with a novel translocation t(X;9)(p11.23;p13.3) and RNA-seq identification of a putative corresponding fusion: VCP::TFE3. TFE3 fusion positive RCC was confirmed by TFE3 break-apart FISH. Previous studies have suggested a possible relationship between TFE3 fusions and prognosis in renal cell carcinoma. The patient exhibited long survival for this disease. The patient died after 7 years, with a long period of apparent control of metastatic disease by cabozantinib.

In this 2024 case report the authors describe a case of BCR::ABL1-like B-ALL with unusual granular morphology in a female patient, 12 year old, with the following symptoms: paroxysmal headache, vomiting, but no jaundice or bleeding. CBC revealed moderate leukocytosis, 90% lymphoblast-like cells, severe anemia and normal paltelet count. Examination of peripheral blood smear revealed 87% blasts with high nucleocytoplasmic ratio, fine chromatin, and one to several nucleoli, but without Auer rods. Strickingly, most of the blasts had azurophilic granules in cytoplasm. Same blast morphology was noted during bone marrow examination with concern for granular lymphoblastic leukemia. Flow data on blood: CD45-, CD10+, CD19+ (dim), CD22+, cCD79a+, HLA-DR+, CD25+ (partial), CD34+, CD38+ (partial), MPO-, cCD3-, CD7-, CD33-, CD11c-, CD4-, CD8-, CD5-, CD7-. Karyotype was normal. FISH was negative for CRLF2, ABL1, ABL2, CSF1R rearrangements. 46-gene fusion screening by RT-PCR was negative. Copy number test (not specified) was consistent with deletions involving EBF1 (ex1-10), IKZF1 (ex1-7), PAX5 (ex2, ex5-8). Whole transcriptome sequencing detected an IGH::EPOR fusion. Based on the presence of this fusion the authors made a diagnosis of BCR::ABL1-like B-ALL. Patient received chemotherapy with VDLP (prednisone/ vincristine/ daunorubicin/ darubicin) and CAP (cyclophosphamide/ cytarabine/6 mercaptourine) with no achieving CR; switched to dexamethasone induction with improvement of WBC, then received VP (vincristine/ dexamethasone).

This is a case report from MD Anderson Cancer Center. A 40yo Caucasian male patient was diagnosed with B-ALL with IGH::EPOR fusion. The patient received 4 cycles of R-hyper-CVAD and archived CR with MRD at 0.01% by flow, followed by MUD HSCT. He relapsed 2 months s/p HSCT. Flow at RL detected 83% blasts: CD10+, CD19+, CD22+, CD34+, CD38+, CD45(dim), CD66c+, cytoplasmic CD79a+, CD123+, HLA-DR+, TdT+, CD2-, CD3-, CD4-, CD5-, CD7-, CD13-, CD14-, CD15-, CD20-, CD25-, CD33-, CD36-, CD41-, CD56-, CD64-, cytoplasmic IgM-, CRLF2-, MPO-. Chromosome analysis detected complex karyotype 45,X,-Y,add(13) (p11.2),add(17)(p11.2),-20,+21[2]/44~46,idem[cp2]/46,XY[16]. NGS revealed JAK2, KRAS, FLT3, RUNX1, and TP53 mutations. Archer FusionPlex was positive for IGH::EPOR, but FISH was negative for EPOR or IGH rearrangements or BCR::ABL1 or KMT2Ar. A diagnosis of BCR::ABL1 like B-ALL was made based on established association of EPOR rearrangements with IGH locus with this disease subtype. THe patient was treated with chemotherapy in combination with blinatumomab and achieved CR with negative MRD.

phenotypes: Late onset,Middle age onset,Intermediate young adult onset,Late young adult onset
evidence_statement: This MD Anderson Cancer Center study describes six adult patients (3 males and 3 females, median age 39 yo) with t(14;19)(q32;p13) resulting in IGH::EPOR. 3 patients did not receive any prior chemotherapy, whereas 3 presented with refractory/relapsed disease post-induction. Major symptoms at presentation: fatique, lower extremity swelling, bone pain; 3 patients had splenomegaly. No CNS involvement or extramedullary disease. The median Hb 8.8 g/dl, median PLT count 31 k/ul. All patients had circulating blasts, increased serum lactate dehydrogenase levels and serum beta-2-microglobulin level. Blast morphology: variably condensed chromatin, prominent nucleoli, agranular cytoplasm. Marrow was hypercellular for all patients, with median blast count at 90%. Flow consistent with precursor B-cell immunophenotype: CD10+, CD19+, CD20+, CD22+, CD34+, CD38+, HLA-DR+, TdT+, CD1a-, CD2-, CD3 (surface and cytoplasmic), CD4-, CD5-, CD7-, CD8-, CD14-, CD15-, CD25-, CD41-, CD56-, CD117-, MPO-. Chromosome analysis revealed t(14;19)(q32;p13) in all 6 patients, 2 patients had complex karyotype. FISH with IGH and EPOR probes showed 1F on der(14). All patients received combination chemo, but all relapsed, 5/6 died after 12 months. The manuscript describes clinical, morphologic, immunophenotypic and genetic characteristics of B-ALL caused by EPOR rearrangments with the IGH locus, which are rare primary drivers in B-ALL with BCR::ABL1 like features.

This 2021 study reports 3 adolescent/young adult patients with IGH::EPOR-positive B-ALL treated with post-induction chemotherapy combined with JAKi ruxolitinib or TKI ponatinib. Patient 1 was hispanic female (18yo) with t(14;19), negative FISH and IGH::EPOR detected by Archer FusionPlex (RNA) and DNA NGS. NGS detected partial deletion of IKZF1 and PAX5. This patient received post-induction therapy with ruxolitinib (COG AALL1521 phase II clinical trial), had complicated treatment course and persistent disease, received auto CD19 CART and archieved MRD-negative remission with HSCT from matched sibling with MRD-negative remission >3 years s/p HSCT. Patient 2 was 13 yo female with hyperdiploid karyotype (+X,+2,+5,+6,+8,+9,+10,+19,+21,+22). Archer FusionPlex detected IGH::EPOR and KRAS mutation. Her post-induction chemo was also combined with ruxolitinib with MRD<0.01%, in remission since. Patient 3 was 17yo Caucasian female with normal karyotype and IGH::EPOR by RT-PCR at diagnosis. Her consolidation therapy included cyclophoshamide, cytarabine, 6-mercaptopurine and ponatinib with complicated course. She received blinatumomab with continued ponatinib and achieved MRD negativity followed by allo HSCT.This case series summarizes clinical, morphologic, immunophenotypic and genetic characteristics of B-ALL caused by EPOR rearrangments with the IGH locus, which are rare primary drivers in B-ALL with BCR::ABL1 like features.

This 2017 study is result of collaboration of multiple institutions and was led by St. Jude Children's Research Hospital team. The total cohort of 3115 B-ALL patients (all ages) was studied, with 212 with expression profile of BCR::ABL1-like B-ALL (based on gemone and/or transcriptome sequencing). 19 out of 212 cases (8.9%) revealed 4 types of EPOR rearrangements: insertion of EPOR distal to the IGH enhancer (73.7%), insertion of EPOR into IGK at 2p11.2 (10.5%), cytogenetically visible t(14;19)(q32;p13) (10.5%), and insertion of EPOR upstream of LAIR1 (leukocyte-associated immunoglobulin-like receptor 1) at 19q13 (5.3%). The authors demonstrated that all these EPOR rearrangements resulted in truncation of the cytoplasmic tail of EPOR with preservation of Y368 tyrosine residue essential for receptor activation and loss of distal regulatory tyrosine residues (Y426, Y454, Y456, Y504) and resulted in JAK/STAT signaling activation (potential for treatment). All EPORr cases showed no expression distal to the rearrangement by ex8 specific assay (potential for screening). Interestingly, the authors used 3 EPORr cases to isolate leukemic, stem cell, progenitor, mature cell populations to test for EPORr, which was identified not only in blasts, but also in CD33+ myeloid cells (all 3 cases), myeloid progenitors (1 case), and even in normal B-cell obtained at the time of remission in 1 case. The study described genomic structure of EPOR rearrangements in B-ALL and confirmed their association with B-ALL with BCR::ABL1-like features.

Preclinical experiments using patient-derived GBM cell lines were performed to examine efficacy of CDK4/6 inhibitor palbociclib. The cell line CCF-STTG1 that harbours CDK6 amplification was sensitive to palbociclib, as denoted by >95% reduction in BrdU incorporation.

disease: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With MECOM Rearrangement
evidence_statement: In this study, 17 patients with a variant pericentric inv(3) were identified from an institutional cytogenetics database, out of283 myeloid neoplasms with a MECOM rearrangement (MECOM-R) confirmed by FISH,. Patients are 13 males and 4 females, with an age range 42-85 yrs, median age 67 yrs, and diagnosed with AML (n=15), MDS (n=1) and CMML (n=1). Using metaphase FISH with commercially available MECOM dual color breakapart DNA probes, chromosomal breakpoints were identified at 3p23 (n=11), 3p25 (n=3), 3p21 (n=2) and 3p13 (n=1), in addition to the 3q26.2 breakpoint leading to MECOM-R. These pericentric inversions (inv(3)) detected by metaphase FISH were missed by initial karyotyping in 16 of the 17 cases. Somatic mutations were detected with NGS-based analysis on an 81-gene panel. Similar to classic/ paracentric inv(3)/GATA2::MECOM-R, pericentric inv(3) patients in this showed cytopenia, morphological dysplasia of megakaryocytes, -7/del(7q) and dismal outcomes (mean OS of 14 months). Unique features such as thrombocytopenia (15/17; 88%), increased monocytes in peripheral blood (15/17; 88%), and decreased megakaryocytes (11/17; 65%) were also observed. An average of 3 mutation events per case were identified in the study cohort which is higher than the average of 2 mutation events per case in classic inv(3)/t(3;3). The highest frequency of mutations was detected in gene NRAS (35%), followed by RUNX1, FLT3, ASXL1, PTPN11, SF3B1 and TP53. These 7 genes accounted for 53% of the mutation events. Mutations in SF3B1 are reported more commonly in the classic inv(3)/t(3;3) cases and were found in only 3 cases of pericentric inv(3)/MECOM-R cohort. As pericentric inv(3)s are subtle/ cryptic, reflex MECOM-R BAP FISH is recommended in myeloid neoplasms showing -7/del(7q), an aberration found at a high frequency of 75% in this study. Detection of pericentric inv(3) with MECOM-R may change the classification of the neoplasm from intermediate-risk to high-risk and the diagnosis from MDS to AML in some cases. In summary, the study shows that atypical 3q26/MECOM–R with loci in the p arm of chromosome 3 result in leukemia with the same clinical and pathology characteristics as the classical inv(3)/t(3;3)(q21q26), and may be classified together as a single entity of MECOM-rearranged AML.

disease: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With MECOM Rearrangement
evidence_statement: This study evaluates the frequency of MECOM rearrangements by fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) in 76 AML and 21 MDS patients with various 3q chromosomal aberrations. Patients were referred to four institutions in Italy (in Bologna, Ferrara, Padova, Rovigo) between 1995-2014. MECOM rearrangements were found in 51 of the 97 patients (54.8%) most of which showed 3q26 involvement by chromosome banding analysis (CBA). Of the 51 patients: 26 patients showed inv(3)/t(3;3) and 15 patients showed other balanced 3q26 translocations (t(3q26)). Of the remaining 10 patients with various 3q abnormalities (10.3%), 5 showed balanced translocations involving 3q21 or 3q25 and leading to RPN1/MECOM rearrangement, 2 showed intrachromosomal gene amplification leading to MECOM overexpression, and 3 patients were missed for 3q26 involvement by CBA due to suboptimal quality of chromosome morphology during sample preparation. All cases showed MECOM overexpression by real-time quantitative PCR. Detection of such cryptic MECOM rearrangements by FISH in this study suggests that the frequency of MECOM involvement in myeloid malignancies is underestimated. The study showed that AML with variant MECOM rearrangements has same characteristics as AML with classic inv(3)(q21q26). As MECOM rearrangements are associated with very short overall survival (OS) and poor prognosis, patients with any 3q abnormalities should be screened for MECOM rearrangement.

disease: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With MECOM Rearrangement
phenotypes: Childhood onset,Middle age onset,Young adult onset,Juvenile onset
evidence_statement: In this study, samples from 33 patients presenting with AML or MDS were collected from either the Erasmus Hematology Department biobank (The Netherlands) or from the Munich Leukemia Laboratory (Germany). Multiple assays were used for sample characterization including metaphase karyotyping, MECOM interphase FISH,quantitative real-time PCR on mRNA, SNP array analysis, sequencing of the targeted chromosomal region 3q21.1-3q26.2 (3q-capture), RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), exome sequencing and whole genome sequencing.. 33 patients with atypical 3q26 rearrangements were identified and 25 of those showed MECOM involvement. Among these 25, losses or gains on 3q26 or on partner loci were seen in 7 cases, and no copy number losses or gains were seen in 12, indicative of balanced translocations. 4 of the 33 cases showed amplification of 3q26/MECOM by both FISH and SNP array. Overexpression of EVI1 in 30 of the 33 atypical 3q26 cases was seen, while in 29 cases MDS-EVI1 expression level was either absent or very low. The breakpoint region in 23 of the 33 cases was identified to occur either upstream (74%) or downstream (26%) of the EVI1 gene. The translocated gene partner of MECOM/3q26 was identified in 20 of the 33 cases and involved previously reported genes (THADA, CDK6, MYC and ARID1B) as well as novel and unique partner loci such as TGFBR2, HSPA8, TCF4 among others. These genes are known to be active in myeloid cells and are involved in superenhancer hijacking by the MECOM locus. These translocated enhancers contact and coactivate the promoter of EVI1 but not the promoter of MDS-EVI1. In more than 50% of the 33 cases, GATA2 expression was found to be monoallelic or skewed due to cryptic GATA2/MECOM translocation. The study concludes that both atypical 3q26/MECOM and the classical inv(3)/t(3;3)(q21q26) may be classified together as a single entity of 3q26-rearranged AMLs.

Analysing 101 samples of metastatic prostate cancer biopsy, a high friequency of structural variants in the AR gene were identified (23/101), comprising a heterogeneous mix of deletion, inversion, trandem duplication and translocation events. Of those cases with AR gene rearrangements, a higher frequency of structural variants were observed genome-wide. AR gene rearrangmeents were observed with slightly higher frequency in those treated with one or both second-generation AR signaling inhibitors (abiraterone or enzalutamide) compared with treatment-naive patients, or those treated with first-generation agents. Five patients who had corresponding primary tumours available for analysis did not demonstrate specific AR gene rearrangements. On introduction of AR gene rearrangments identified in 3 study patients to prostate cancer cell lines via CRISPR/Cas9 system, a relative growth advantage of cells harbouring those specific AR rearrangments was observed, under conditions modeling AR-targeted therapy. In those tumours which harboured an AR gene rearrangement, but no other identifiable AR gene alteration (SNV / amplification), diverse expression of AR splice variants were observed, distinct from AR-V7. AR-V7 (and AR-V9) were also expressed, however, at lower levels than these novel transcripts. In tumours harboring AR gene rearrangments together with AR gene amplication, expression of AR-V7 (as well AR-V4 and AR-V9) was frequent. AR-V7 also contributed a higher fraction to overall AR mRNA expression, as compared to the novel AR splice variants.
One case with presumably EGFR::USP42 fusion was mentioned in OrigiMed database of Chinese patients with lung adenocarcinoma. EGFR breakpoint in intron 27.
In a retrospective cohort study of 39 pediatric AML patients carrying PICALM::MLLT10 fusions, both the 5-year event-free survival rate (22%) and 5-year overall survival rate (26%) were poor.

molecular_profile: FUS::TFCP2 Fusion AND ALK Exon 2-18 Deletion
evidence_statement: A 31 year old male initially thought to have a mandibular osteosarcoma that was resected and treated with adjuvant radiation and cisplatin-doxorubicin. He had a mandibular recurrence with multiple pulmonary nodules 12 months after diagnosis, at which point he underwent whole genome and whole transcriptome sequencing of their lesion. In both RNA and DNA, an in-frame deletion of exons 2-18 of ALK which retains the kinase domain and leads to activation as well as a FUS::TFCP2 fusion resulting from a rearrangements between FUS intron 6 (exons 1-6) and TFCP2 intron 1 (exons 2-15) were identified. The combination of these variants led to a change in diagnosis to an intraosseous rhabdomyosarcoma (tentatively a subtype of spindle cell rhabdomyosarcoma by WHO 2020).

molecular_profile: FUS::TFCP2 Fusion AND ALK Exon 2-18 Deletion
evidence_statement: A 31 year old male initially thought to have a mandibular osteosarcoma that was resected and treated with adjuvant radiation and cisplatin-doxorubicin. He had a mandibular recurrence with multiple pulmonary nodules 12 months after diagnosis, at which point he underwent whole genome and whole transcriptome sequencing of their lesion. In both RNA and DNA, an in-frame deletion of exons 2-18 of ALK which retains the kinase domain and leads to activation as well as a FUS::TFCP2 fusion resulting from a rearrangements between FUS intron 6 (exons 1-6) and TFCP2 intron 1 (exons 2-15) were identified. His cancer progressed following ifosfamide-etoposide chemotherapy and then after radiation with regorafenib, leading to hypoxic respiratory failure and mechanical ventilation. Compassionate use of alectinib was then given, resulting in dramatic clinical improvement within 48 hours, allowing him to stop ventilation. By 2 weeks there was radiological evidence of response. After 3 weeks there was new evidence of subcutaneous metastasis and pericardial involvement. The patient died of his disease 4 weeks after starting alectinib. The authors posit that this is still evidence of response but this was short lived due to the aggressiveness of the tumor and it's advanced stage at the time of treatment.

This study provides preclinical evidence that EZH2 Y641N and Y641F mutations function as oncogenic drivers in B-cell lymphomas. In BCL1 lymphoma cells, expression of either mutant led to increased H3K27me3 levels and conferred a significant growth advantage over wild-type EZH2 or control. Both mutations enhanced clonogenicity, producing over 10-fold more colonies than wild-type EZH2. Also, both mutations impaired IL2/IL5-induced differentiation and proliferation arrest in BCL1 cells. This resistance to cytokine-induced maturation was accompanied by significantly reduced expression of Prdm1. These findings support the conclusion that Y641N and Y641F promote epigenetic repression of differentiation-associated genes and support sustained proliferation, establishing a cellular phenotype favorable to lymphomagenesis.

The study demonstrates that EZH2 A677G is a gain-of-function mutation in B-cell lymphoma. In enzymatic assays, A677G uniquely utilized unmethylated, monomethylated, and dimethylated substrates with nearly equal efficiency. Structural modeling indicated that the A677G mutation enlarges the lysine tunnel to accommodate dimethylated substrates, while retaining the crucial Y641 residue for orienting unmethylated and monomethylated substrates. To evaluate its biological effect, the authors transiently expressed A677G in wild-type EZH2 MCF-7 cells, which resulted in marked global increases in H3K27me3 levels and a reduction in H3K27me2, relative to wild-type EZH2. These findings support the role of A677G as an activating mutation capable of altering the epigenetic landscape.

In a retrospective study on TCGA data, the presence of non-synonymous mutations in TET1 is enriched in patients responding to immune checkpoint inhibitor treatment (n=519, P = 0.003). In an ICI-treated cohort (n = 1395), TET1 mutation status is associated with better OS (R = 0.47 [95% CI, 0.25 to 0.88], adjusted P = 0.019) independent of TMB, MSI status and cancer type.

The authors studied the role of KIT D816V in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) using engineered TF-1 cells to express either wild-type KIT or KIT D816V. They discovered that KIT D816V led to constitutive activation of autophagy (increases autophagic flux in AML cells), measured by increased LC3-II levels, Cyto-ID staining, and GFP-LC3 puncta. This autophagic response was dependent on STAT3 activation. To assess the functional relevance, they used shRNA-mediated knockdown of autophagy genes ATG12 and VPS34, which resulted in significantly reduced proliferation, decreased clonogenicity in methylcellulose assays, and increased apoptosis in KIT D816V-expressing cells. Finally, in NSG mouse xenografts, knockdown of ATG12 in KIT D816V cells led to reduced tumor burden and significantly prolonged survival, directly demonstrating that KIT D816V–induced autophagy supports tumor progression in vivo. These results demonstrate that KIT D816V promotes AML progression by engaging STAT3-driven autophagy, which supports tumor cell survival and growth

The authors studied the role of the KIT D816V variant in promoting inflammation in systemic mastocytosis. They used patients’ bone marrow-derived mast cells, as well as mouse mast cell line (MCBS1, engineered to express wild-type or D816V-KIT), and the human mast cell line HMC-1.2, which expresses KIT D816V. Results demonstrated that KIT D816V but not wild-type KIT, induced significantly elevated IL-6 mRNA and protein expression under unstimulated conditions, reflecting ligand-independent activation. To dissect the signaling mechanism, they used Ruxolitinib (JAK1/2 inhibitor), LY294002 (PI3K inhibitor), and U0126 (MEK inhibitor), along with siRNA-mediated knockdown of STAT5. Inhibition of STAT5, PI3K, JAK2, or MEK/ERK all significantly reduced IL-6 production in D816V-expressing cells, while STAT3 and STAT4 knockdowns had no effect. These results were further supported by observations in primary patient-derived bone marrow cultures, where IL-6 levels and STAT5 activity correlated with KIT D816V allelic burden and mast cell content. These findings demonstrate that KIT D816V drives autonomous IL-6 secretion through activation of JAK2/STAT5, PI3K, and MEK/ERK pathways.
HeLa cell lines and A549 xenografts expression shRNA targeting PPP2R2A are sensitive to PARP inhibition by ABT-888 when PPP2R2A is knocked down.

disease: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With MLL Rearrangement
evidence_statement: In this 2018 study the authors include 1,023 young people diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). The age at presentation for the participants ranged from 0 to 29 years (median of 10 years). The presence of KMT2A rearrangements was determined from manual review of available cytogenetic results, combined with genome sequencing and RNA-sequencing findings from the study. A cytogenetic KMT2A abnormality was detected in 38% of infants (less than 3 year of age), 13% of children (aged 3 to 14 years), and 11% of adolescent and young adults (aged 15 to 29 years). Multiple KMT2A fusion partners were detected, with MLLT3 occurring most frequently. The study illustrates that KMT2A rearrangements define a subtype of AML common in children and young adults.

disease: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With MLL Rearrangement
evidence_statement: In this 2024 study the authors included patient data from 1256 children (aged less than 19 years) across 15 different countries diagnosed with KMT2A rearranged acute myeloid leukemia (AML). KMT2A rearrangements were detected by cytogenetics, with some confirmed by fluorescence in situ hybridization, or reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction, within the local centers. Multiple KMT2A fusion partners were detected, with KMT2A::MLLT3 (n = 544, 43.3%), KMT2A::MLLT10 (n = 218, 17.4%), KMT2A::AFDN (n = 92, 7.3%), and KMT2A::ELL (n = 75, 6.0%) most frequent, together accounting for around 75% of cases. The authors found that different fusion partners, morphology and/or additional cytogenetic abnormalities may impact outcomes.

disease: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With MLL Rearrangement
evidence_statement: In this 2023 publication the authors include 3401 KMT2A rearranged leukemia samples obtained from different diagnostic centers worldwide, and subject them to DNA sequence analyses. Of these patients, 1116 were diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML), including 197 patients aged less than 12 months, 465 patients aged 1 to 18 years and 441 patients older than 18 years (for 13 patients age was unknown). AML patients displayed a diverse number of partner genes with MLLT3 (n = 339; 30.4%) and MLLT10 (n = 209; 18.7%) the most common. KMT2A rearrangements typically involve in-frame fusions with KMT2A as the 5' partner and KMT2A breakpoints in AML patients almost always occur somewhere between intron 7 and exon 13 (NM_001412597.1). KMT2A-partial tandem in-frame duplications that involve the N-terminus can also occur, mostly frequently in AML in adult patients.

The is a cytogenetic case study of a 10-year-old female with pure pigmented dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans (DFSP), also called Bednar tumor, on her right shoulder. Karyotype of tumor cells was 47,XX with 2 copies of der(22)t(17;22)(q22;q13). BAC clones mapping to 22q13.1 at the PDGFB locus, and 17q21.33 at the COL1A1I locus and used as FISH probes detected COL1A1-PDGFB gene fusion on the derivative der(22) chromosomes. RT-PCR and Sanger sequencing narrowed down the fusion to exon 41 of COL1A1 and exon 2 of PDGFB. Adult Bednar and DFSP tumors typically show ring chromosomes composed of der(22) material, while pediatric DFSP tumors show a linear structural abnormality of an unbalanced translocation t(17;22)(q22;q13). This is the first reported pediatric case of a pure Bednar tumor with a linear chromosomal structural abnormality involving chromosomes 22 and 17, in addition to having a normal chromosome 22 and two normal chromosomes 17. The COL1A1 breakpoint at exon 41 in the COL1A1-PDGFB fusion gene is newly reported in this case study and reaffirms the known variability in COL1A1 breakpoints spanning exons 6-49.

The authors studied 27 archival formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) samples of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans (DFSP) cases obtained from Texas Children's Hospital and University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center. The cases included 16 females and 11 males with an age range of 1-73 years and diagnosed with DFSP and diffuse expression of CD34 by immunohistochemistry. Using a highly sensitive multiplex RT-PCR-direct sequencing assay developed for FFPE tissue, the authors detected COL1A1-PDGFB fusion transcripts with 18 different COL1A1 forward primers spanning the α-helical domain (exons 5-49) and a single PDGFB reverse primer. Break-apart FISH was performed using BAC DNA clones mapping centromeric and telomeric of the PGDFB locus. Sequencing analysis confirmed in-frame fusion of exon 2 of PDGFB to different breakpoints in COL1A1 (exons 7, 10, 29, 40, 46, and 49 and introns between exons 13:14, 26:27, 30:31, 33:34, 43:44, 45:46, 46:47). Of these, COL1A1 breakpoints in exon 49 and in introns between exons 13:14 and 30:31, are novel. Using both RT-PCR and FISH techniques, the authors report a higher prevalence of COL1A1-PDGFB rearrangements (96%) in DFSP cases than reported in earlier studies, and attribute this to the high sensitivity of their multiplex RT-PCR direct sequencing assay. Testing FFPE specimen with both FISH and RT-PCR would prove helpful for the differential diagnosis of atypical, fibrosarcomatous and metastatic DFSP.

In this study, paraffin-embedded tissue microarray (TMA) evaluation of translocation t(17;22)(q22;q13) was performed on 40 tissue samples from 24 female and 16 male DFSP patients (37 primary tumors, 3 local recurrences) obtained from 3 hospitals in Barcelona, Spain. The median age of these DFSP patients was 43 y and the age range was 15-87 y. A second tissue microarray included 20 samples from dermatofibroma (DF) patients. Samples from 6 postsurgical scars were used as negative controls. FISH was performed using dual-color dual-fusion BAC clones to detect the cytogenetic COL1A1-PDGFB translocation. From the evaluable 29 DFSP cases, 86% (n=25) showed the COL1A1-PDGFB FISH signal pattern, which was absent in all DF control cases and in the 6 scars. Of these 25 COL1A1-PDGFB positive DFSP cases, 19 showed multiple (more than 3) copies of the translocation. Tumor size correlated positively with a higher proportion of DFSP tumor cells showing the fusion signal, and DFSPs with fibrosarcomatous areas (DFSP-FS) also showed cells with 6 or more COL1A1-PDGFB gene fusions signals.

The POSEIDON (NCT03164616) open-label, randomized phase 3 trial included 1,013 patients with metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC), of whom 637 had nonsquamous histology and 612 were evaluable for genomic alterations. Patients were randomized to receive either platinum-based chemotherapy alone, chemotherapy plus the PD-L1 inhibitor durvalumab, or chemotherapy combined with both durvalumab and the CTLA4 inhibitor tremelimumab. Among patients with STK11 and/or KEAP1 mutations, the median overall survival was 15.8 months in the dual checkpoint blockade group (durvalumab + tremelimumab + chemotherapy) compared to 7.3 months in the chemotherapy-only group (hazard ratio for death, 0.50; 95% confidence interval, 0.29 to 0.87). Median progression-free survival was 6.2 months in the dual checkpoint group versus 2.8 months in the chemotherapy group (hazard ratio, 0.52; 95% CI, 0.28 to 0.95). The objective response rate was 42.9% in the dual checkpoint group and 28.0% in the chemotherapy group. In patients without STK11 or KEAP1 mutations, the addition of CTLA4 blockade did not significantly improve outcomes. Dual immune checkpoint blockade was associated with increased immune-related adverse events, though no new safety concerns were identified.

In an in vitro study, MCF-7 cells expressing the EGFR N771delinsGY (N771GY) mutation demonstrated sensitivity to dacomitinib (PF00299804), with YFP-EGFR-ICD relocation observed at 50 nM. In comparison, cells expressing the EGFR L858R sensitizing mutation responded at 1 nM, whereas cells expressing the EGFR T790M resistance mutation showed no response at concentrations up to 1 uM. Sensitivity was assessed by YFP-EGFR-ICD relocation following treatment.

In an in vitro study, MCF-7 cells expressing the EGFR A767_V769dup mutation demonstrated sensitivity to dacomitinib (PF00299804), with YFP-EGFR-ICD relocation observed at 10 nM. In comparison, cells expressing the EGFR L858R sensitizing mutation responded at 1 nM, whereas cells expressing the EGFR T790M resistance mutation showed no response at concentrations up to 1 uM. Sensitivity was assessed by YFP-EGFR-ICD relocation following treatment.

In a multinational cohort study of metastatic colorectal cancer (CRC), a novel LANCL2::EGFR fusion was detected by comprehensive NGS assay in one EGFR amplified (250 copies), RAS/BRAF wildtype CRC sample. In-frame LANCL2(e1)-EGFR(e15) fusion transcript was identified by RNA sequencing and further confirmed by RNAScope® ISH with probes designed against the sequence 20bp on both upstream and downstream of the fusion breakpoint (Supplementary Figure 4). The patient was treated with FOLFIRI-panitumumab and achieved PR with progression-free survival of 8.1 months and overall survival of 16.6 months (Supplementary Table 2). The tumour also carries mutations in APC, TP53, RICTOR, and amplification of RB1. An EGFR p.Ser464Leu variant was detected by liquid biopsy following resistance to EGFR targeting therapy was developed.

OSI-906, an IGF1R/INSR inhibitor, sensitizes cell lines to cabazitaxel, resulting in better overall survival in mouse xenografts of patient derived chemotherapy resistant castration-resistant prostate cancer cell (CPRC) lines. These results were also demonstrated using three CPRC cell line cultures in-vitro (DU145, 22Rv1, and ARCaPM).

This study reports the effect of FLT3-ITD mutations on the rate of progression of MDS to AML and on a patient's overall survival. The study cohort consisted of 82 MDS patients, with paired samples analyzed at the time of diagnosis of MDS and AML available for 70 patients. FLT3-ITD was detected in 5 cases only at the time of MDS diagnosis and in 7 during progression to AML only. The authors conclude that the incidence of FLT3-ITD during progression of MDS to AML is significantly higher compared to MDS cases not undergoing AML transformation (3/70 vs 10/70, p<0.001) and the median time of progression is shorter for patients with FLT3-ITD (2.5+/-0.5 vs 11.9+/-1.5 months, p=0.114). In addition, survival of patients with FLT3-ITD is significantly shorter compared to patients with FLT3-wt (5.6+/-1.3 vs 18.0+/-1.7 months, p=0.0008).

This study provided in vivo evidence showing the adipocyte-specific oncogenicity of the FUS::CHOP fusion transcript in liposarcoma, using a transgenic mouse model with ubiquitous FUS::CHOP expression driven by the elongation factor 1a (EF1a) promoter. These mice uniformly developed liposarcoma without sex bias and exhibited characteristic symptoms similar to those in human liposarcoma. No tumors were detected in other tissues. Mechanistically, FUS::CHOP expression in vivo blocked adipocyte differentiation by inducing the expression of the nuclear receptor peroxisome proliferative-activated receptor gamma (PPARg). The study provides evidence that the FUS::DDIT3 fusion acts as the primary oncogenic driver in myxoid liposarcoma (MLS) and is thus a suitable diagnostic marker for this tumor type.

This preclinical study examined the effect of the FUS::DDIT3 fusion protein on the oncogenic role of IGF-1R/PI3K/Akt signaling in myxoid liposarcoma (MLS) and explored the therapeutic potential of IGF-1R inhibitors, including NVP-AEW541 in this disease. Immunohistochemistry (IHC) revealed elevated expression and activating phosphorylation of various components in the IGF-1R signaling pathway in MLS clinical specimens (n=60). Overexpression of FUS::DDIT3 in HT1080 fibrosarcoma cells induced IGF2-IGF-1R/PI3K/Akt activation. Topical administration of NVP-AEW541 onto MLS xenograft tumors on the chick chorioallantoic membrane (CAM) was found to significantly suppress tumor growth in vivo (p<0.05). The study shows that the FUS::DDIT3 fusion drives oncogenic program in MLS; it is a defining abnormality and a suitable diagnostic marker for this tumor type.

Ningetinib inhibited Ba/F3 cells with FLT3 ITD-F691L in cell proliferation assays. FLT3-ITD-F691L cells treated with ningetinib for 6 hours demonstrated inhibition of FLT3 phosphorylation and also phosphorylation of downstream proteins STAT5, AKT and ERK. BALB/c mice injected with GFP-positive Ba/F3-FLT3-ITD-F691L cells had a lower leukemic burden after treatment with ningetinib compared with gilteritinib or quizartinib. In a MOLM13-FLT3-ITD-F691L mouse model, treatment with ningetinib resulted in a greater decrease of human CD45 positive cells in bone marrow and spleen compared to mice administered giltertinib or quizartinib.

This study describes two novel PLAG1 fusions, TRPS1–PLAG1 and NDRG1–PLAG1, identified in histologically confirmed cases of chondroid syringoma. Both fusions involve promoter swapping, placing PLAG1 expression under the control of the 5′ fusion partner. This activation mechanism parallels that seen in pleomorphic adenomas and other benign myoepithelial tumors. These findings expand the molecular spectrum of PLAG1-driven neoplasia and support the role of PLAG1 fusions in the pathogenesis of cutaneous mixed tumors.

Whole-genome sequencing of single-cell-derived hematopoietic clones from chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) patients revealed that the BCR::ABL1 fusion is acquired 3 to 14 years prior to clinical diagnosis, initiating a prolonged subclinical phase of clonal expansion. These findings establish BCR::ABL1 as an early, driving event in CML pathogenesis and highlight its prognostic relevance in defining the molecular timing and trajectory of disease evolution.

Loss-of-function of NF1, a tumor suppressor and negative regulator of RAS signaling, is recurrent in melanoma and contributes to MAPK pathway activation. This study demonstrates that NF1 loss in melanoma cells leads to increased EGFR activation, and that pharmacologic inhibition of EGFR impairs downstream signaling and suppresses tumor growth in both in vitro and in vivo models. These findings suggest that NF1 loss may serve as a predictive biomarker for sensitivity to EGFR-targeted therapies in NF1-mutant melanoma, offering a potential therapeutic strategy for patients lacking conventional actionable mutations.

The KOMET-001 Phase 1 trial evaluated the menin inhibitor ziftomenib (KO-539) in patients with relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML) harboring either NPM1 mutations or KMT2A rearrangements. Among 61 patients treated at the recommended phase 2 dose of 600 mg daily, ziftomenib achieved a composite complete remission rate of 25% in the NPM1-mutant cohort, with 75% of responders reaching MRD negativity. Responses were durable, and treatment was generally well tolerated, with most adverse events being manageable and reversible. These results position ziftomenib as a promising targeted therapy for genetically defined AML subgroups, particularly for patients lacking effective treatment options following relapse or resistance to standard therapies.

evidence_statement: In this retrospective multicenter study, 218 patients diagnosed with B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (B-ALL) harboring ZNF384 rearrangements were analyzed between 1992 and 2018 across 16 international consortia. ZNF384 rearrangements were found in about 5% of pediatric and 10% of adult B-ALL cases and were mutually exclusive with other well-defined genetic subtypes. FISH), RT-PCR, and NGS identified ZNF384 fusion transcripts with partners such as EP300, TCF3, TAF15, and CREBBP. Detection of ZNF384 fusions was critical for classifying B-ALL cases lacking other recurrent cytogenetic abnormalities. EP300::ZNF384 fusions showed a distinct clinical profile, including older age at diagnosis and favorable outcomes, while other ZNF384 rearrangements exhibited unique immunophenotypic features like aberrant myeloid marker expression (CD13, CD33). These findings highlight the diagnostic importance of ZNF384 rearrangements in B-ALL and support their recognition as a distinct molecular entity.

evidence_statement: In this study, the authors investigated a targeted diagnostic approach to identify ZNF384 rearrangements in B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (B-ALL) based on immunophenotypic features. Since ZNF384 fusions are often cryptic and linked to dim CD10 expression and aberrant CD13/CD33 expression, 109 B-ALL patients with <80% CD10 expression and negative BCR-ABL1 status were screened. ZNF384 rearrangements were found in 14 cases, with EP300::ZNF384 as the most common fusion. Flow cytometry screening, FISH followed by RT-PCR and Sanger sequencing identified further fusion partners including EP300, TAF15, and TCF3. Recognizing ZNF384 fusions is particularly valuable for diagnosing B-ALL cases that do not harbor other defining cytogenetic or molecular alterations.
