evidence_statement: In a preclinical genomic and functional study of pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia (n = 81 paired diagnosis–relapse samples), recurrent RAS-pathway mutations involving NRAS (exons 2-3), KRAS (exons 2-3), FLT3 (ITD, TKD), PTPN11 (exons 3 and 13) were identified in 44% (95% CI 33–55%) of relapse cases, with most mutations (83%) acquired after treatment (p < 0.01). Functional assays in KOPN-8, NALM-6, and REH cell lines demonstrated that RAS-mutant leukemic cells were sensitive to the MEK inhibitor selumetinib (AZD6244), resulting in reduced pERK signaling and cell viability in vitro. These findings establish RAS-pathway mutations as mediators of relapse and suggest potential therapeutic sensitivity to MEK inhibition in relapsed ALL.

In a preclinical study using 5 CD80-overexpressing Burkitt B-cell lymphoma cell lines (Raji, Daudi, Ramos, DHL4, 2F7), treatment with the anti-CD80 monoclonal antibody galiximab (25–100 µg/mL) inhibited NF-κB, AKT, YY1, Snail, and Bcl-XL signaling, leading to reduced proliferation and enhanced sensitivity to cisplatin-induced apoptosis (p < 0.01). Galiximab combined with CDDP induced synergistic apoptosis (confirmed by isobologram analysis) and increased active caspase-3 and Annexin-V positivity, whereas single-agent galiximab showed minimal apoptosis. Knockdown of YY1 or Snail or inhibition of Bcl-XL by 2MAM-A3 replicated the galiximab sensitization effect.

In a preclinical study using STK11/LKB1-deficient pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) cell lines (TB 32047, PANC-1, SUIT2, SU86.86, KPC792) and C57BL/6 orthotopic mouse models (n = 5 per group), the PDE4 inhibitor roflumilast (50 μM in vitro; 5 mg/kg/day in vivo) significantly reduced migration (p < 0.05 - 0.001) and tumor weight in STK11 knockout PDAC models compared with vehicle, without affecting cell viability. Loss of STK11 increased expression of PDE4D, PDE4B, and PDE10A, and roflumilast reversed pro-migratory/angiogenic gene signatures. Treatment was well tolerated with no observed toxicity.

In preclinical small cell lung carcinoma (SCLC) models with YES1 amplification or high expression, treatment with the YES1 inhibitor CH6953755 (30 mg/kg, q2d) or dasatinib (45 mg/kg daily) produced marked antitumor effects. In high-YES1 xenografts, CH6953755 reduced tumor growth by 55% in DMS53 and 85% in H209 models, while dasatinib achieved 39% and 65% reductions, respectively. Complete tumor regression occurred in one DMS53 xenograft, and partial regressions were observed in approximately two-thirds of H209 xenografts following CH6953755. Low-YES1 (H69) tumors showed minimal sensitivity, and no treatment-related toxicity was detected in histologic analysis of kidney or liver tissues.

In a cell line screen using MCF-7, exogenous expression of FGFR1 confers resistance to fulvestrant and fulvestrant plus ribociclib. In a study using breast cancer cell lines MCF-7 and T47D, overexpression of FGFR1 was found to confer resistance to fulvestrant plus ribociclib. Conversely, inhibition of FGFR signaling in three estrogen-receptor positive breast cancer cell lines with FGFR1 amplification restores sensitivity to fulvestrant/palbociclib combination. Growth of patient derived xenograft models harbouring FGFR1 amplification can be suppressed by the combination of FGFR inhibitor, fulvestrant and palbociclib. These observations are consistent with those of the MONALEESA cohort, where amplification or mRNA overexpression of FGFR1 is associated with shorter PFS when treated with CDK4/6 inhibitor, suggesting that FGFR1 amplification or overexpression is a mechanism of resistance to the combination treatment of fulvestrant and CDK4/6 inhibitor.

molecular_profile: NFE2L2 Mutation OR KEAP1 Mutation OR CUL3 Mutation
evidence_statement: In a retrospective study of stage IV NSCLC patients treated with first-line platinum doublet chemotherapy (n = 103; 51 KEAP1/NFE2L2/CUL3-mutant, 52 WT), mutations in NFE2L2, KEAP1, or CUL3 were associated with significantly shorter time to treatment failure (2.8 vs 8.3 months; HR 2.19, 95% CI 1.42–3.38; p = 0.00036) and overall survival (11.2 vs 36.8 months; HR 2.17, 95% CI 1.34–3.52; p = 0.0016) compared with matched controls. In KRAS wild-type cases, OS (11.2 vs 38.1 months; p = 0.0039) and time on treatment (2.6 vs 8.5 months, p = 0.0001) remained shorter when compared to WT patients. Preclinical Keap1-deleted Trp53-based LUAD and LSCC mouse models lacking Kras mutations demonstrated increased clonogenic survival after exposure to cisplatin, carboplatin, paclitaxel, and etoposide, confirming that Keap1 loss drives intrinsic chemoresistance through NRF2 pathway activation.

In a mutational analysis of 1,145 primary cancers, NFE2L2 (NRF2) mutations occurred predominantly in squamous cell carcinomas (SCCs) of the esophagus (11.4%), skin (6.3%), lung (15.8%), and larynx (13.0%), but not in other tumor types. Most mutations (95.5%) occurred at SCC and clustered within or near the DLG (residues 24-30) or ETGE (residues 77-82) motifs in exon 2, disrupting KEAP1-NRF2 binding. None of the esophageal or skin SCCs contained KEAP1 mutations. All NFE2L2-mutant SCCs showed nuclear NRF2 accumulation with increased GCLC and NQO1 expression, consistent with constitutive pathway activation.

In preclinical pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) models with high NQ01 expression, which indicates the NFE2L2 (NRF2) pathway activation, the small molecule NSC84167 (NSLC01, 50 mg/kg) selectively inhibited tumor growth (p < 0.01, n = 7-8) and induced apoptosis in NRF2-high but not in NRF2-low PDXs. Across conventional and patient-derived PDAC cell lines, NSLC01 sensitivity correlated with NQO1 expression (r = −0.5563, p = 0.021), and NRF2 knockdown reversed drug sensitivity.

In the phase III randomized open-label CheckMate 8HW trial (NCT04008030; n = 303, 255 centrally confirmed MSI-H/dMMR metastatic colorectal cancer), nivolumab plus ipilimumab significantly improved progression-free survival versus investigator’s choice of chemotherapy (mFOLFOX6 or FOLFIRI with or without bevacizumab or cetuximab) as first-line treatment (24-month PFS 72%, 95% CI 64–79 vs 14%, 95% CI 6–25; p < 0.001). The restricted mean survival time at 24 months was 10.6 months longer (95% CI 8.4–12.9) with nivolumab plus ipilimumab, and grade 3–4 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 23% vs 48% of patients, respectively.

In the phase III randomized open-label CheckMate 8HW trial (NCT04008030; n = 707 randomized; centrally confirmed MSI-H/dMMR: n = 296 nivolumab+ipilimumab vs 286 nivolumab) showed nivolumab plus ipilimumab significantly improved progression-free survival versus nivolumab monotherapy across all treatment lines (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.48–0.81; p = 0.0003). Median PFS was not reached (95% CI 53.8-NE) with nivolumab plus ipilimumab and 39.3 months (22.1-NE) with nivolumab. Objective response rate was 71% (95% CI 65–76) vs 58% (95% CI 52–64; p = 0.0011), with complete responses in 30% and 28%, respectively. Grade ≥3 AEs occurred in 22% vs 14%, including diarrhea/colitis (3%), hypophysitis (3%), and adrenal insufficiency (3%), with three treatment-related deaths reported (2 myocarditis/pneumonitis in combination arm, 1 pneumonitis in monotherapy arm).

A 10‐year‐old female patient presented with pancytopenia and normal eosinophils and had the diagnosis of B‐lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma. FISH identified a CHIC2 deletion, suggestive of FIP1L1::PDGFRA fusion, which was subsequently confirmed on RNA sequencing. Cytogenetics were negative for BCR::ABL1, ETV6::CBFA2, MLL, and TCF::PBX1. The patient had high‐risk induction treatment per COG AALL1732. End of induction flow cytometry and FISH demonstrated no minimal residual disease. The patient commenced targeted therapy with imatinib (260 mg/m2/day), whilst continuing standard chemotherapy. The patient completed all subsequent treatment per COG AALL1732, with the addition of imatinib. At the time of writing, the patient remains in remission 6 months post completion of all therapy.

A previously healthy 2-year-old girl presented with right supraorbital swelling, hepatosplenomegaly, anemia (Hb 8.2 g/dl) and leukocytosis (WBC 19.5 × 109/L) with eosinophilia of 32% and an absolute eosinophilic count of 6.3 × 109/L.. An incisional biopsy of the supraorbital mass revealed B-cell lymphoblastic lymphoma (B-LBL) and FISH test for FIP1L1::PDGFRA gene fusion was positive in 70% of the cells studied. The final diagnosis was B-cell lymphoblastic lymphoma arising in the setting of myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with eosinophilia and PDGFRA rearrangement. The patient was started on imatinib 340 mg/m2/day with concomitant therapy for B-LBL per the Children Oncology Group standard therapy for localized B-LBL. Five months following treatment, the patient's supraorbital swelling had completely resolved, with near-complete resolution of the right orbital mass. Bone marrow analysis showed morphologic remission and was negative for PDGFRA rearrangement by FISH. After 2.5 years of treatment, the multiagent chemotherapy for B-LBL was completed and the patient is now on imatinib monotherapy with close follow-up.

Loss-of-function mutations in CDK12 disrupt transcription of DNA damage response genes (BRCA1, ATR, FANCI, FANCD2), reducing homologous recombination and sensitizing tumor cells to DNA cross-linking agents and poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitors, while CDK12 amplification with ERBB2 in breast cancer promotes expression of DNA repair genes and cell invasion. Preclinical models further showed that CDK12 inhibition induces synthetic lethality with MYC overexpression, EWS/FLI rearrangement, and PARP or CHK1 inhibition, confirming its dual functional roles in oncogenesis and therapeutic vulnerability.

In this 2017 study reviewing 753 sarcoma cases, 11 tumors with the BCOR::CCNB3 fusion were identified using immunohistochemistry and RT-PCR. These tumors were found exclusively in males, with a mean age of 12.9 years, and were predominantly located in the axial skeleton. Morphologically, the tumors showed spindled or round cells, vesicular nuclei, fine chromatin, inconspicuous nucleoli, and a characteristic arciform vascular pattern. Over 50% stained positive for SATB2 and Pax8, suggesting potential diagnostic value for these markers in identifying BCOR::CCNB3 positive sarcomas.

therapies: Trastuzumab Emtansine Regimen,Trastuzumab Deruxtecan Regimen,Disitamab Vedotin
evidence_statement: In a real-world cohort of metastatic breast cancer (n = 63; 30 HER2-positive, 33 HER2-low), patients received HER2-targeted antibody-drug conjugates (trastuzumab deruxtecan (68.25%), disitamab vedotin (14.29%), or trastuzumab emtansine (17.46%)). Those with ERBB2/CDK12 co-amplification showed significantly longer progression-free survival (PFS 19.33 months vs 5.43 months; HR 0.13; 95% CI 0.04–0.45; p < 0.001), including in the HER2-positive subgroup (PFS 19.33 months vs 6.87 months; HR 0.18; 95% CI 0.05–0.72; p = 0.007). Conversely, cell cycle–related gene amplifications were associated with inferior PFS (2.07 months vs 8.40 months; HR 5.24; 95% CI 2.11–13.01; p < 0.001), particularly in HER2-low tumors (2.07 months vs 8.27 months; HR 4.23; 95% CI 1.50–11.91; p = 0.004). Multivariate analysis confirmed these associations (ERBB2/CDK12 HR 0.16; 95% CI 0.04-0.65; p = 0.010; cell cycle HR 4.46; 95% CI 1.08–18.40; p = 0.039).

In BRAF-mutated melanoma cell lines (A375, WM983A/B, WM164, Colo829), the selective CDK12/13 inhibitor SR-4835 inhibited proliferation (IC₅₀ = 80.7–160.5 nM) and at 30/100nM, reduced RNA polymerase II (RPB1) Ser2 phosphorylation, leading to decreased expression of DNA damage response genes (BRCA1, RAD51, ATM, FANCI, FANCD2) and accumulation of γH2AX. SR-4835 acted as a molecular glue degrader, recruiting the CDK12–cyclin K complex to the CUL4–RBX1–DDB1 ubiquitin ligase complex, promoting degradation (cyclin K half-life = 47.8 min vs > 120 min in control). This degradation required DDB1 and was blocked by MLN7243, MLN4924, or MG132. Structure-activity analysis showed that the benzimidazole side-chain of SR-4835 is essential for this activity.

In micropapillary breast carcinoma and a subset of HER2-amplified breast cancers, genomic disruptions of CDK12 (out-of-frame rearrangements and breakpoints within the HER2 amplicon) were associated with reduced CDK12 mRNA (p = 0.0360, t-test) and protein expression (p = 0.0438, t-test) in tumor samples. The CDK12-null MDA-MB-453 cell line displayed sensitivity to the PARP inhibitors (BMN673 and olaparib). siRNA-mediated CDK12 silencing in ER-positive cell lines (MCF7, T47D) increased BMN673 sensitivity and reduced RAD51 foci formation, whereas re-expression of full-length CDK12 in MDA-MB-453 restored PARP resistance. SUM149 (BRCA1-mutant) served as a positive control for homologous recombination deficiency and PARP inhibitor sensitivity. Group-level SF50 values did not differ significantly between HER2-amplified cell lines with and without CDK12 disruption (p = 0.207, BMN673 and p = 0.375, olaparib, t-test).

In prostate cancer models, CDK12 loss impaired homologous recombination deficiency and sensitized cells to PARP inhibitors (olaparib, rucaparib, talazoparib, veliparib) in a gene dosage-dependent manner, with complete loss showing greater sensitivity than partial loss. CDK12 KO xenografts treated with rucaparib (150 mg/kg daily) exhibited significantly reduced tumor growth and increased γH2AX staining (p < 0.01). In the TRITON2 phase II trial (NCT02952534), 7 of 11 (63.6%) patients with biallelic CDK12-mutated mCRPC had PSA reductions, and 4 of 6 (66.6%) achieved radiographic disease control, whereas monoallelic or rearranged cases showed no response.

In the phase II trial (NCT02992743) of letetresgene autoleucel (lete-cel) in human leukocyte antigen ((HLA)-A*02:01–, HLA-A*02:05–, and/or HLA-A*02:06–positive), NY-ESO-1 (CTAG1B)-expressing advanced or metastatic myxoid/round cell liposarcoma (n = 20 treated), ORR was 20% (95% CI 2.5-55.6) with reduced-dose lymphodepletion and 40% (95% CI 12.2-73.8) with standard-dose lymphodepletion; median PFS was 5.4 months (95% CI 2.0-11.5) and 8.7 months (95% CI 0.9-NE), respectively. Grade ≥3 cytokine release syndrome occurred in 10% and 30% of patients, and all events resolved. These results support the activity of lete-cel for HLA-/NY-ESO-1-positive MRCLS.

Microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) colorectal cancers (CRC) respond to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICPIs), but response rates vary, often < 50%, highlighting the need for better stratification. This retrospective study evaluated tumor mutational burden (TMB) as a predictive biomarker in 22 MSI-H mCRC patients treated with PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors, including 19 on pembrolizumab. Among these patients, ORR was 68% (15/22), with 7 complete and 8 partial responses. TMB was strongly associated with ORR and PFS in both univariate (P < 0.001) and multivariate (P < 0.01) analyses. Log-rank analysis identified the optimal TMB cut-point between 37 and 41 mutations/Mb. All patients with TMB ≥37 responded; most (6 of 9 ) with lower TMB progressed. Median PFS was not reached in the TMB-high group (median follow-up >18 months), while it was 2 months in the TMB-low group. Validation in a larger cohort of 18,140 CRC cases (821/4.5% MSI-H) confirmed the cut-point (37.4 mutations/Mb), corresponding to the 35th percentile. Patients below this threshold were less likely to benefit from PD-1/PD-L1 monotherapy. TMB was measured from formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue using a hybrid capture-based NGS assay (Foundation Medicine), targeting 315–324 cancer-related genes across a 0.8–1.2 Mb genomic region. The assay used somatic-only sequencing with computational germline filtering. TMB calculations included both synonymous and non-synonymous variants and were validated against whole exome sequencing (WES), ensuring methodological accuracy. These findings support integrating TMB into clinical workflows and highlight the need for prospective validation in larger cohorts.

In non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) models, KEAP1-mutant cell lines (H838, H460) exhibited strong sensitivity to NSC84167 (NSLC01) in MTT cell viability assays, with IC₅₀ values well below 1 µM, which is considerably lower than the 3 µM cutoff for sensitivity. In contrast, KEAP1-wild-type cells (HCC193, H1299) were resistant. This pattern suggests that loss of KEAP1 and subsequent NRF2 pathway activation predict a response to NSLC01.

In a preclinical study of uterine cancer cell lines resistant to EphA2 inhibitors (HEC-1A, Ishikawa, RL-95), EphA2-positive cells treated with the MEK inhibitor trametinib restored sensitivity to dasatinib and ALWII (EphA2 inhibitors) in MTT cell viability assays, demonstrating a synergistic interaction (combination index < 1, p < 0.01). The combination of trametinib + dasatinib increased apoptosis (p < 0.01), decreased pMAPK, Jagged1, and c-MYC, and upregulated BIM and EphrinA1, consistent with MEK-pathway suppression restoring EphrinA1 feedback. In an orthotopic HEC-1A mouse model (n = 40; 10 per group: vehicle, dasatinib 15 mg/kg daily, trametinib 1 mg/kg daily, or dasatinib + trametinib combination), the combination reduced tumor weight and nodule count more than either monotherapy (p < 0.001) without added toxicity, indicating that MEK inhibition overcomes resistance to EphA2 inhibitors through crosstalk between the EphA2, MEK, and NOTCH pathways.

In uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma (TCGA, n = 382), EPHA2 overexpression correlated with JAG1, MYC, NOTCH1, NOTCH3, and HES1 expression (Spearman r = 0.25-0.43; p < 0.01). Elevated MAP3K15, DLL3, or HEYL mRNA levels were associated with shorter OS (MAP3K15 p < 0.001; DLL3 p = 0.019; HEYL p = 0.007), and high MAP3K15 expression (HR = 6.68; 95% CI 2.75–16.2; p < 0.001). These findings show that EPHA2 and MAP3K15 overexpression with NOTCH activation are linked to poor outcomes and suggest resistance to EphA2-targeted monotherapy, supporting dual EphA2–MEK inhibition approaches.

This retrospective study examined the association between TMB and clinical response to immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) across multiple cancer types. 1,662 advanced cancer patients treated with at least one dose of ICI, including avelumab, durvalumab, ipilimumab, nivolumab, pembrolizumab or tremelimumab as monotherapy or in combination (146 received anti-CTLA-4, 1,256 received anti-PD-1 or PD-L1, and 260 received the combination), were included in the study. Tumour-derived and matched normal germline DNA were sequenced using the MSK-IMPACT targeted 468-cancer gene panel. TMB was calculated as the number of somatic nonsynonymous per megabase sequences. Using top 20% within each cancer type as the cutoff, a significant association of improved overall survival with higher TMB was observed in patients with bladder (n=214, p=0.040), colorectal (n=110, p= 0.031), head and neck (n=138, p=7.42 × 10e-3), and non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) (n=350, p= 2.30× 10e-4), and across the whole cohort (n=1,662, p= 1.59 × 10e-6). A similar trend was also observed in breast cancer (n=45), esophagogastric cancer (n=126), melanoma (n=321), renal cell carcinoma (n=151), and cancer of unknown primary (n=90), despite not reaching statistical significance. This association was also observed using different cut points ranging between top10-50% to define high TMB. Similarly, improved clinical benefit/ progression free survival were also associated higher TMB among patients with NSCLC, melanoma, esophagogastric, head and neck, and renal cell carcinoma. Notably, distinct from these cancer types, no association between higher TMB and improved patient survival was observed in glioma (n=117). A cohort of 5,371 advanced cancer patients who did not receive ICI were also included in this study. A lack of prognostic benefit of TMB status was observed both across the cancer types and within each histology, demonstrating the observed survival difference among patients with TMB high tumours was attributed to ICI treatment. The authors also noted that stratifying by TMB decile within histology was chosen in this study to demonstrate the relationship between TMB and patient prognosis, although this method may not be ideal for clinical use. Overall, this study demonstrated the clinical value of higher TMB in predicting superior overall survival in patients across multiple cancer types. However, the authors also noted that stratifying by TMB decile within histology was chosen in this study to demonstrate the relationship between TMB and patient prognosis, although this method may not be ideal for clinical use.

In ER⁺/RB1-deficient breast cancer models resistant to CDK4/6 inhibitors, PRMT5 inhibition with pemrametostat (IC₅₀ = 49.8-268.5 nM) or JNJ-64619178 reduced proliferation and induced G₁ arrest in MCF-7, T47D, and KPL1 cells. In MCF-7_RBKO xenografts (n = 40; 10 per group: vehicle, pemrametostat 200 mg/kg daily, fulvestrant 5 mg/kg weekly, or combination), suppressed tumor growth and achieved 6/9 partial and 1/9 complete remissions, while in RB1-deleted ER⁺ PDXs (n = 8), 4/8 partial remissions occurred. These findings show that PRMT5 inhibition with or without fulvestrant overcomes CDK4/6-inhibitor resistance in ER⁺/RB1-deficient breast cancer.

In preclinical RCC models (n ≈ 5/group), Setd2 loss enhanced sensitivity to the ATR inhibitor VE822 (60 mg/kg orally, 5 days/week) and anti–PD-1 antibody (100 µg intraperitoneally, every 3 days) reduced tumor volume (p < 0.05-0.01) and produced complete responses in two mice, with increased CD4, CD8, and CD11 infiltration and upregulation of Ccl5, Cxcl10, Cd274, and Pdcd1. Across human RCC cohorts (TCGA-KIRC WT n = 400, mut n = 51; Braun nivolumab WT n unknown, mut subset included; Samstein ICB WT n = 195, mut n = 72; IMmotion150 atezolizumab ± bevacizumab WT n = 138, mut n = 55), SETD2 mutations were associated with prolonged OS in ICB-treated patients and higher ORR (25/69 vs 39/172). These data support SETD2 mutation as a predictive biomarker for enhanced immunotherapy response in renal cell carcinoma, potentially potentiated by ATR inhibition.

In clear cell RCC, SETD2 loss predicts sensitivity to PI3Kβ pathway inhibition: SETD2-deficient 786-0 and SETD2-mutant A498 cells treated with PI3Kβ inhibitors TGX221 or AZD8186 showed reduced viability, proliferation, spheroid formation, and migration vs SETD2-proficient 786-0 (AZD8186 IC50 0.29 μM [786-0 KO], 0.01 μM [A498] vs 21 μM [786-0 WT]; multiple assays p ≤ 0.05), while PI3Kα inhibition had no effect and PI3Kδ was modest; the AKT inhibitor MK2206 reproduced these effects. In vivo, AZD8186 (30 mg/kg/day by orogastric gavage) significantly suppressed the growth of SETD2-mutant A498 xenografts and reduced final tumor weight (p < 0.05; tumor-volume p < 0.0001).

A 39-year-old Chinese man was hospitalized in May 2021 with concerns of thirst and weight loss. Immature B lymphocytes were detected in blood (83.8%) and bone marrow (87%) and FISH showed the absence of BCR::ABL1 fusion, but additional BCR signals suggested a rearrangement of BCR. FISH using a 4q12 tricolor rearrangement probe indicated a rearrangement of PDGFRA. G-banded chromosome analysis was 46, XY, t(4;22)(q12;q11.2) [1]/45,idem,−7 [19]. RNA sequencing identified the profile of BCR::ABL1-like B-ALL with BCR::PDGFRA transcripts with BCR exons 1–16 fused with PDGFRA exons 12–23, forming an in-frame BCR::PDGFRA. The patient received a vincristine-idarubicin-cyclophosphamide-pegaspargase- methylprednisolone regimen; however, he relapsed with central nervous system infiltration in July 2021. Dasatinib (100 mg/day) was administered in August, but ineffective. In September 2021, 39.46% and 10.56% leukemia cells were detected in the bone marrow and CSF, respectively, and new gene mutations in EZH2 (p.Pro698Arg and p.Asn546Ile) were detected. Dasatinib was replaced with imatinib (600 mg/day) in October 2021. In December, flow cytometry (FCM) of the CSF was negative for leukemia cells. Furthermore, the bone marrow smear showed complete remission, and FCM showed 0.23% MRD. In January 2022, a bone marrow smear continued to show complete remission. FCM showed that the MRD declined to 0.02% and 0.008% in January and February, respectively. Meanwhile, RT-qPCR detected a 3.35 log reduction in the BCR::PDGFRA transcript from the baseline in February. The patient continued treatment with a combination of imatinib and chemotherapy. However, MRD increased to 0.2% in March 2022. Because of the COVID-19 pandemic, continuous treatment could not be received and the patient died in July 2022 due to the disease progression.

In a retrospective TCGA cohort of microsatellite-instable colorectal adenocarcinoma (n = 43; KMT2D LOF = 16, WT = 27), KMT2D loss of function was associated with higher TMB (p < 0.001), higher neoantigen scores (p < 0.05), higher cytolytic activity (p < 0.05), and higher IFNγ signaling scores (p < 0.05), with a trend toward higher PredictIO ICI-response scores (p = 0.057) and no significant OS difference (log-rank p = 0.10). Across small ICI-treated POG and MSK-IMPACT cohorts, KMT2D-LOF similarly associated with higher TMB (p < 0.05).

In microsatellite-instable (MSI) colorectal carcinoma cell-line assays, KMT2D loss of function (LOF) stratified sensitivity to WRN perturbation. In DepMap viability data, WRN knockout was lethal in MSI KMT2D-LOF lines compared with KMT2D-WT MSI or KMT2D-WT MSS lines (ANOVA Tukey HSD p < 0.001). Using WRN inhibitors HRO761 and VVD-133214 (RO7589831), all 10 KMT2D-LOF MSI COAD/READ lines were drug-sensitive, whereas 0 of 3 KMT2D-WT or missense lines were resistant (Fisher’s exact p = 0.022; OR = ∞). Among 14 WRN-essential cell lines, KMT2D-LOF and MMR-gene LOF co-occurred in 64 % (9/14) and 85 % (12/14) of cases, respectively, both enriched relative to non-essential lines (p = 0.0007 and 0.0009; OR = 20 and 21, respectively). KMT2D-LOF MSI lines (e.g., LOVO, SW48, LS180, MFE319) showed the largest [AT]ₙ microsatellite-repeat expansions.

In a sub-analysis of a randomized phase II trial in extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma (EWSR1-NR4A3 and TAF15-NR4A3 fusions) and mesenchymal chondrosarcoma (HEY1-NCOA2 fusion)(trabectedin n = 5; BSC n = 3), the three MCS patients treated with trabectedin 1.2 mg/m² q3w achieved PFS 22.2, 7.5, and 12.5 mo with a 6-month progression-free rate of 100% and best responses of 1 partial response (PR) of -58% and 2 stable disease (SD) of 1% and -1% (no progressive disease (PD)). Whereas, three MCS patients in the BSC arm all had PD (median PFS 1.0 mo, 95 % CI 0.3-1.0). No ≥ G4 or fatal AEs occurred.

High Tumor Mutation Burden (TMB >19 mutations/Mb) represents a robust and platform-validated genomic biomarker predictive of clinical benefit from PD-1/PD-L1 immune checkpoint blockade in non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). This threshold was derived through regression tree modeling across multiple sequencing platforms (MSK-IMPACT, DFCI-OncoPanel, and whole-exome sequencing) and validated in three large, independent cohorts totaling 1,552 patients. Patients with high TMB demonstrated significantly improved objective response rate (49.1% vs 21.5%, p<0.001), progression-free survival (11.4 vs 2.8 months, p<0.001), and overall survival (36.1 vs 12.4 months, p<0.001) compared with those with low TMB, independent of PD-L1 expression levels. Molecular and immune profiling revealed that high-TMB NSCLCs exhibit enhanced CD8⁺ and PD-1⁺ T-cell infiltration, increased PD-L1 expression, and activation of antigen presentation pathways. The authors suggested that TMB >19 mut/Mb is a clinically actionable biomarker for identifying NSCLC patients most likely to respond to PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors.

This retrospective study evaluated the clinical utility of blood tumour mutational burden (bTMB) as a predictive biomarker for atezolizumab efficacy in advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) who had progressed from first-line therapy using samples collected prospectively from 2 randomized trials. The cfDNA assay used in this study utilised the same 1.1 Mb tissue FoundationOne hybridization capture panel (394 genes). The bTMB score was calculated by identifying all base substitutions present at an allele frequency of ≥0.5%, with predicted germline variants filtered out. Pre-treatment plasma bTMB demonstrated a positive correlation with the patient-paired tissue TMB (tTMB) (Spearman rank correlation = 0.64, n=259). Based on this correlation, an optimal cut-off point of ≥ 16 mutations per megabase (with a minimum somatic allele frequency ≥ 1%) was selected for subsequent clinical evaluation. Applying the cut off of bTMB ≥ 16 mutations per megabase to the POPLAR study (NCT01903993) (n=211) demonstrated improved progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) benefit with atezolizumab versus docetaxel. At this cut-off, the PFS hazard ratio (HR) was 0.57. The median PFS was 4.2 months in the atezolizumab arm and 2.9 months in the docetaxel arm; the median OS values were 13.0 and 7.4 months, respectively. The biomarker-treatment interaction for PFS at bTMB ≥ 16 trended towards significance (interaction P = 0.055). The predictive value was independently validated in the larger OAK study (NCT02008227) (n=583). Patients bTMB ≥16 muts/Mb showed significant PFS benefit from atezolizumab (HR: 0.65, P=0.013), with the biomarker-treatment interaction for PFS being statistically significant (P=0.036). Although the OS benefit in this subgroup was substantial (median 13.5 versus 6.8 months, HR: 0.64), the treatment interaction for overall survival was not significant. The findings support bTMB ≥16 mutations per megabase as a non-invasive biomarker for predicting enhanced PFS benefit from atezolizumab in advanced NSCLC patients who have progressed on first-line therapy.

This retrospective analysis assessed the association between tumor mutational burden (TMB) and the efficacy of nivolumab plus low-dose ipilimumab as first-line treatment for advanced/metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in the CheckMate 568 trial (NCT02477826). The TMB was calculated using the FoundationOne CDx assay, which covers 324 genes. TMB was defined as the number of somatic, coding, base substitutions, and short indels per Mb of genome examined, with predicted germline variants excluded from the calculation. Of the 139 patients enrolled, 98 had successful TMB results, where 49% of patients had high-TMB (defined as ≥ 10 mut/Mb). The overall response rate (ORR) was 44% in the high-TMB group versus 12% in the low-TMB group. The association of efficacy with TMB was independent of tumor PD-L1 expression status. TMB was shown to be an informative classifier for ORR (AUC= 0.73; 95% CI, 0.62-0.84). Median progression-free survival (PFS) was also longer in patients with high-TMB compared to those with low-TMB (7.1 months [95% CI, 3.6 to 11.3 months] and 2.6 months [95% CI, 1.4 to 5.4 months], respectively). At 6 months, 55% of the high-TMB subgroup remained progression-free vs 31% in the low-TMB subgroup. The cut-off of 10 mut/Mb was selected for this retrospective analysis as the ORR exceeded 40% which was higher than historical chemotherapy responses, and a higher TMB cutoff did not result in additional improvement. Further prospective validation in a larger randomized study is required to validate this selected cut-off and its predicative effect for nivolumab plus low-dose ipilimumab in NSCLC.

In this 2009 study, the authors included 336 chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) patients at diagnosis, of which 25 patients (7.44%) exhibited variant Philadelphia (Ph) chromosome translocations. A control group of patients with the standard t(9;22) translocation was used for comparison. Conventional cytogenetics and fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) were utilized to characterize the variant translocations and investigate deletions on the derivative chromosome 9 [der(9)]. Variant Ph translocations, involving chromosomes 9, 22, and one or more additional chromosomes, were identified in all 25 cases. The BCR::ABL1 fusion gene was detected in all patients, confirming the diagnosis of CML despite the complex karyotypes. Deletions adjacent to the ABL1 gene on der(9) were observed in 15 of the 25 cases (60%), a significantly greater proportion than that found in typical Ph translocations (12–15%). The genesis of these variants was attributed to both one-step (36%) and two-step (56%) mechanisms, with the latter being more prevalent. The cohort was composed of patients where any chromosome could be involved, with breakpoints preferentially located in the CG-richest regions of the genome. The authors concluded that the BCR::ABL1 fusion is the fundamental diagnostic event in CML, even in cases with complex variant translocations. They identified that these variant translocations are associated with a markedly higher incidence of deletions on der(9). Proper assessment of the prognostic significance of these variants requires categorization based on their mechanism of genesis and 9q34 deletion status.

disease: Round Cell Sarcoma With EWSR1-non-ETS Fusion
evidence_statement: A small case series examined molecular features along with clinicopathologic and immunohistochemical characteristics of sarcomas with EWSR1::NFATC2 gene fusions. The study included 6 cases (5 males and 1 female; age range 24-67 years), comprising 3 male cases of primary bone tumors of the radius and the remaining 3 cases involving primary soft tissue tumors. A dual-color, EWSR1 break-apart probe set (chr22q12 proximal and distal probes) detected EWSR1 rearrangement and concurrent amplification of its 5'-region in all cases. The EWSR1::NFATC2 gene fusion was confirmed using the corresponding FISH probes. RT-PCR followed by Sanger sequencing identified the fusion joining the 5'-end of EWSR1 (exon 7) and 3'-end of NFATC2 (exon 3). Together, the recurrent EWSR1::NFATC2 fusion identified a novel entity of small round cell sarcoma.

disease: Round Cell Sarcoma With EWSR1-non-ETS Fusion
evidence_statement: This landmark study represents the first description of the EWSR1::NFATC2 fusion in Ewing-like sarcomas, leading to the establishment of 'round cell sarcoma with EWSR1-non-ETS fusions' as a new disease entity in the 2020 WHO Classification of Soft Tissue and Bone Tumors. Four male cases (aged 16-39 years) of primary bone tumors were included; all expressed an in-frame EWSR1::NFATC2 fusion transcript. Array-CGH (n=3 cases) and interphase FISH (n=1 case) revealed amplification of chromosomes 22q12 and 20q13. RT-PCR followed by Sanger sequencing revealed fusion between exon 8 of EWSR1 and exon 3 of NFATC2. Using the fiber-FISH technique, the genomic breakpoints were mapped to intron 8 of EWSR1 (22q12) and intron 2 of NFATC2 (20q13). Mechanistically, this fusion results in loss of the N-terminal regulatory region and replacement of a weak nuclear localization signal (NLS) of NFATC2 with a strong NLS of EWSR1, leading to an uncontrolled nuclear localization and activation of the chimera protein.

molecular_profile: KMT2C Mutation OR KMT2D mutation OR KMT2A Mutation OR KMT2B Mutation
evidence_statement: In a retrospective pan-cancer analysis of four immune checkpoint therapy (ICT)–treated cohorts (melanoma n = 287; NSCLC n = 131; total n = 418), KMT2 family mutations were associated with improved ICT response (durable clinical benefit 44.6 % vs 25.4 %; OR 2.60, 95 % CI 1.66 - 4.07; p = 1.67e-04). In subgroup analyses, benefit was observed in melanoma (OR 2.21, 95 % CI 1.29 - 3.78) and NSCLC (OR 3.82, 95 % CI 1.65 - 8.85). Mutations in KMT2C specifically correlated with greater response (OR 3.48, 95 % CI 1.98–6.12; p = 5.46e-05). These results, consistent with findings in a pan-cancer cohort of 9,981 tumors linking KMT2 mutations to high TMB and immune activation, support KMT2 family mutations as a likely predictive biomarker for favorable ICT response across solid tumors.

This study analyzed over 300 patient with advanced solid tumors and melanoma across 22 tumor types from four KEYNOTE clinical trials to define genomic and immune predictors of response to pembrolizumab (anti–PD-1 immunotherapy). Using whole-exome sequencing and NanoString gene profiling, they evaluated tumor mutational burden (TMB) and the T cell–inflamed gene expression profile (GEP) in formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded pretreatment samples. TMB cut-off values for the pan-tumor and single-indication clinical cohorts were the Youden Index values derived in AUROC analysis (102.5 for pan-cancer, 86 for HNSCC, and 191.5 for melanoma group). TMB and GEP profiles were also analyzed within The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) database of 6384 tumors and the WES cut-off >100 mutations per exome was chosen for high TMB to match the Youden TBM pan-cancer cut-offs. TMB and GEP were independently predictive of clinical response and progression-free survival in KEYNOTE cohorts, and together they stratified patients into four biologically distinct subgroups: those with high TMB/high GEP had the highest objective response rates (37–57%), and the longest progression-free survival, whereas those with low TMB/high GEP or high TMB/low GEP showed moderate response rate (12-35% and 11-42%, respectively), and patients with low TMB/low GEP tumors rarely responded (0–9%). The two markers were only weakly correlated (Spearman correlation coefficient at r ~ 0.2), indicating that TMB and GEP are independent predictive markers, with TMB capturing neoantigen load, while GEP reflecting T-cell activation within the tumor microenvironment. Integrative analyses of TCGA data confirmed these findings and revealed resistance-associated alterations such as mutation in STK11, KEAP1, and APC in high TMB and low GEP lung and colorectal cancers, but not in the pan-cancer analysis. In addition, TMB highly correlated with neoantigen load in pan-cancer cohort (r=0.87), HNSCC (r=0.83), and melanoma cohort (r=0.9). Overall, the study established TMB and GEP as complementary, tumor-agnostic predictors of benefit from PD-1 blockade and provided a framework for precision immunotherapy and biomarker-guided combination strategies.

In a set of 116 NSCLC tissues, 72 were tested for alterations in exons 7, 10, and 15 by sequencing. Sequencing of normal control tissue was not described. FGFR3 expression was also tested by IHC. From the 72 samples, 2 heterozygous FGFR3 mutations were found, and both were T450M in exon 10. 1 patient was a 54 year old F and had undergone a radical lobectomy with stage cT2a N1M0 lung adenocarcinoma. FGFR3 expression was positive and EGFR exon 19 deletion was present. The second patient was a 78 year old M with squamous cell carcinoma and had undergone radical lobectomy, and had stage T2a N1M0. This patient had negative FGFR3 stain and EGFR wildtype.

An Asian germline dataset (jMorp-14KJPN) was analyzed and five significantly enriched non-synonymous single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) on the FGFR3 gene locus were found (Q29H, G65R, L164V, T450M, and A720S). These are specific to the Asian population. In a set of 389 Japanese bladder cancer patients (124 non-muscle invasive and 265 muscle-invasive), these SNPs were not enriched. FGFR3 levels were not increased in patients with these SNPs, and the authors state there seemed to be no survival difference based on the FGFR3 status, which indicated no clinical implication of these Asian-specific FGFR3 SNPs. The T450M C>T mutation had T allele frequeny of 3.02 in jMorp-14KJPN.

In the TIMER dataset, levels of MMP1 is increased in cancers compared with normal tissue, where its levels in sacituzumab govitecan (SG)-resistant tumours are higher than SG-sensitive tumours by IHC. In the TCGA database, high levels of MMP1 is associated with poor prognosis in patients with hormone-positive breast cancer. Breast cancer cell lines (MCF-7 and T47D) slowly exposed to, and eventually becoming resistant to sacituzumab govitecan exhibit mesenchymal-like morphology and increased mRNA expression of MMP1. MMP1 overexpression in SG-resistant breast cancer cell lines is associated with increased colony formation and migration. Mechanistically, MMP1 induces EMT rhough NF-kB pathway activation, while inhibition of MMP1 overcomes SG resistance in pre-clinical models. Together, these evidence shows that MMP1 overexpression is associated with SG resistance.

The Phase 3 trial for the selective and brain-penetrant RET kinase inhibitor selpercatinib in Medullary Thyroid Cancer (MTC) LIBRETTO-531 (NCT04211337) consisted of 291 total patients. The patients had pathologically confirmed unresectable locally advanced or metastatic MTC, and had no history of treatment with kinase inhibitors. Patients had a prospectively identified pathogenic RET alteration, either somatic or germline, and 182 patients had RET M918T (~63%). From the patients with M918T, 121 were treated with selpercatinib, and 61 were treated with control (physician’s choice of vandetanib or cabozantinib). In the M918T subgroup analysis, control patients had median progression-free survival (PFS) of 17.5 months, while in the selpercatinib-treated patients the median PFS was not met. Hazard Ratio (95% CI) was 0.40 (0.21–0.77) between M918T control and selpercatinib treated patients.

In the concurrently randomized cohort of the same phase 3 trial in ER-positive, HER2-negative breast carcinoma (NCT04975308; n = 426, 213 per arm), imlunestrant plus abemaciclib improved investigator-assessed PFS vs imlunestrant alone regardless of ESR1-mutation status (median 9.4 mo (95% CI, 7.5 -11.9) vs 5.5 mo (95% CI, 3.8 - 5.6); HR 0.57, 95% CI 0.44 - 0.73; P < 0.001); interim OS was immature (15% of the patients died) and not significant (HR 1.34, 95% CI 0.81 - 2.21; P = 0.25), and grade ≥3 AEs occurred in 48.6% with the combination with key events including neutropenia 19.7%, diarrhea 8.2%, anemia 7.7%.

In a randomized, open-label phase 3 trial in ER-positive, HER2-negative breast carcinoma (EMBER-3, NCT04975308; n = 874; ESR1-mut subgroup n = 256), imlunestrant monotherapy (n=331) improved investigator-assessed PFS vs standard endocrine therapy (n = 330) in ESR1-mutated disease (median 5.5 vs 3.8 mo; restricted mean survival time diff 2.6 mo, 95% CI 1.2 - 3.9; p < 0.001), while the overall-population PFS comparison was not significant (HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.72 - 1.04; P = 0.12); interim OS HR in ESR1-mut was 0.55 (95% CI 0.35 - 0.86; p = 0.008) but did not meet multiplicity threshold, and grade ≥3 AEs occurred in 17.1% vs 20.7%.

molecular_profile: PIK3CA Exon 21 Mutation AND PIK3CA Exon 10 Mutation

The authors report a case of a 6-year-old child with leukemia and the clinical and morphologic characteristics of acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL), but without evidence of the expected t(15;17) or a PML-RARA cryptic fusion. RNA-seq revealed a chimeric torque teno minivirus (TTMV)-RARA fusion. The virus was found to be integrated into RARA intron 2 and the overall fusion transcript was predicted to remain in-frame with RARA exon 3 (as would be expected in more classical PML::RARA fusions). The TTMV portion of the fusion appeared to contain the conserved domain of TTMV ORF2. Further analysis of cohorts at the author's institution identified one additional example of TTMV::RARA in a 3-year-old child affected by an AML lacking any cytogenetic abnormality or pathogenic somatic mutation.

This part of the open-label multipart phase 3 trial, CheckMate 277 (Trial ID: 29658845), examined the performance of nivolumab plus ipilimumab compared to chemotherapy among non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients with a high tumour mutational burden (TMB) (>= 10 mutations/ megabase). Stage IV/ recurrent NSCLC patients that were chemotherapy treatment naïve were recruited. Patients with tumour programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression of at least 1% were randomly assigned to receive nivolumab plus ipilimumab, nivolumab monotherapy, or chemotherapy; while those with tumour PD-L1 expression of < 1% were randomly assigned to be treated with nivolumab plus ipilimumab, nivolumab plus chemotherapy, or chemotherapy. Tissue TMB was determined by the FoundationOne CDx assay. Patients with high TMB achieved significantly longer progression-free survival (PFS) with nivolumab plus ipilimumab (n = 139) (1-year PFS of 42%, median PFS of 7.2 months with 95% confidence interval [CI], 5.5 to 13.2), compared to chemotherapy alone (n = 160) (1-year PFS of 13.2%, median PFS of 5.5 months with 95% CI, 4.4 to 5.8) (hazard ratio [HR] 0.58; 97.5% CI, 0.41 to 0.81; P<0.001). 45.3% of patients achieved objective response with nivolumab plus ipilimumab, compared to 26.9% with chemotherapy. The benefit of nivolumab plus ipilimumab over chemotherapy was consistent across histologic subtypes and despite whether the tumour PD-L1 expression was at least 1% or lower than 1%. On the contrary, among the patients with low TMB, the clinical benefit was not significantly different between patients treated with nivolumab plus ipilimumab (n= 191) (median PFS of 3.2 months with 95% CI, 2.7 to 4.3) and those treated with chemotherapy (n=189) (median PFS of 5.5 months with 95% CI, 4.3 to 5.6) (HR 1.07; 95% CI, 0.84 to 1.35). In conclusion, this study demonstrated significant clinical benefit of first-line nivolumab plus ipilimumab over chemotherapy among NSCLC patients with a high TMB, irrespective of the expression level of tumour PD-L1.

A pediatric patient had a hematopathologic diagnosis of B-ALL determined through bone marrow aspirate analysis. The patient had a hemoglobin level of 3 g/dL, severe neutropenia, and a normal platelet count. The karyotype was 46,XX,t(9;10)(q34.1;q22)[2]/47,idem,þder(10)t(9;10)[12]/46,XX[6]. cDNA libraries were generated from bone marrow, and a fusion of ZMIZ1 (exon 18), and ABL1 (exon 2) was found and confirmed with RT-PCR and sequencing. The patient took part in arm B the Children's Oncology Group study AALL1631 (NCT03007147), which compares the addition of imatinib to 2 different chemotherapy backbones for patients with Philadelphia chromosome–positive or ABL-fusion–positive B-ALL. The patient was treated successfully with multimodal chemotherapy and imatinib. After the first 2 cycles, bone marrow showed no evidence of leukemia, which is consistent with a complete remission. The patient remains in continuous first remission, and continues to receive maintenance chemotherapy plus imatinib.

therapies: Selective Estrogen Receptor Covalent Antagonist H3B-6545
evidence_statement: In a multicenter open label phase 1 to 2 trial in locally advanced or metastatic ER positive, HER2 negative breast carcinoma (NCT03250676; n = 151; RP2D cohort 450 mg once daily n = 115, response evaluable n = 94), H3B-6545 produced median PFS 4.6 months (95% CI 3.5 - 6.7) and median OS 21.5 months (95% CI 16.6 - 25.5) with an ORR of 20.2% (95% CI 12.6 - 29.8; one sided p ≤ 0.0001 vs null ORR 5%), DCR 61.7% (95% CI 51.1, 71.5 51.1 - 71.5), CBR 41.5% (95%CI 31.4 - 52.1) and median DOR 9.23 months (95% CI 5.88 - 20.24). In the clonal ESR1 Y537S subgroup at 450 mg (n = 28), the drug achieved ORR 32.1% (95% CI 15.9 - 52.4), CBR 57.1% (95%CI 37.2 - 75.5), median PFS 7.3 months (95% CI 3.1 -11.1) and median OS 18.6 months (95% CI 10.9 - NR). Grade 3 or 4 TEAEs occurred in 52% of patients at 450 mg, with notable AESI including sinus bradycardia in 45.2% (no grade 3 or higher), rash in 15.2% and QT prolongation in 9.9% with grade 3 or higher events in 3.3%. Primary endpoints were RP2D determination and ORR, which met the prespecified efficacy threshold at 450 mg.

Cos7 cells transfected with mutant FLT3 D835Y cDNA demonstrated FLT3 ligand-independent tyrosine phosphorylation. 32D cells stably expressing mutant FLT3 D835Y proliferated without either IL-3 or recombinant human FLT3 ligand at the same level as FLT3 ITD-mutant expressing 32D cells.

MLN518 inhibited the proliferation of Ba/F3 cells transduced with FLT3 activation loop mutation D835Y (IC50 > 10 micromolar). In addition, MLN518 inhibited phosphorylation of FLT3, STAT5 and ERK. Treatment of Ba/F3 cells with 10 micromolar of MLN518 for 30 minutes (and subsequently adding IL-3 for 5 minutes) restored STAT5 and ERK phosphorylation.

In a phase Ib/II trial of bazedoxifene 40 mg daily plus palbociclib 125 mg (NCT02448771; HR positive, HER2 negative breast carcinoma; n = 36), the regimen produced a 24 week clinical benefit rate of 33.3%, median PFS 3.6 months (95% CI 2.0 - 7.2) and median OS 26.5 months (95 % CI 20.7 - NR), with grade 3-4 neutropenia in 47.2%. In patients with baseline ctDNA sequencing (n = 28), activating PIK3CA mutations (n = 6) were associated with significantly shorter PFS than wild type (n = 22) (HR 4.4, 95 percent CI 1.5 - 13, p = 0.0026), indicating reduced benefit from this combination.

Variant Allele Frequency was 40.42 percent. The patient was treated with 200 mg/day of gilteritinib and had complete remission with incomplete hematological recovery as their best response.

In a phase 3 trial comparing gilteritinib (120 mg/day) to salvage chemotherapy (SC) in adults with relapsed or refractory FLT3- mutated AML, patients were required to have FLT3 ITD or TKD (tyrosine kinase domain D835 or I836 mutations). 328 patients had ITD only, 31 had TKD only, and 7 had combination ITD and TKD. 215 ITD patients received gilteritinib with median overall survival (OS) of 9.3 months, and 113 received SC with OS of 5.6 months for salvage chemotherapy. Hazard ratio (95% CI) was 0.62 (0.47–0.82), favoring Gilteritinib. Median overall survival was similar in patients between FLT3 ITD mutations alone (9.3 months), and FLT3 TKD mutations alone (8.0 months). 44 ITD patients (20.5%) had complete remission with gilteretinib, and 11 (9.7%) with SC treatment.

In a multinational open label phase II dose randomized study of sunvozertinib in platinum pretreated advanced NSCLC with EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations (WU-KONG1B, NCT03974022; efficacy n = 85 for 200 mg-random, n = 89 for 300 mg-random, and n = 107 for 300 mg-all), sunvozertinib produced IRC confirmed ORRs of 45.9% (97.5% CI, 33.6 - 58.5), 47.2% (97.5% CI, 35.1 - 59.5), and 45.8% (97.5% CI, 34.8 - 57.0) at 200 mg-random, 300 mg-random, and 300 mg-all, respectively (P < 0.0001 vs null ORR 17%), with median PFS 8.4, 7.7, and 6.9 months and 12-month OS rates 62.1, 73.7, and 69.4%. Across the 200 mg-random and 300 mg-random cohorts, the 770_SVD subtype represented 24.7% and 18.0% of patients, with cORRs of 47.6% and 56.3%, respectively. Meanwhile, the 769_ASV subtype accounted for 21.2% and 23.6%, with cORRs of 33.3% and 57.1%, respectively. Across treated patients (200 mg-random n = 91; 300 mg-all n = 111), grade ≥3 treatment related AEs occurred in 40.7% and 58.6%, most commonly diarrhea (2.2% vs 18.0%), blood CPK increase (6.6% vs 12.6%), and anemia (4.4% vs 6.3%), with no treatment related deaths; both dose levels met the prespecified primary endpoint of IRC confirmed ORR.

In a single-arm phase 1/2 trial in microsatellite stable BRAF V600E metastatic colorectal cancer (NCT04017650; n = 26), combination encorafenib + cetuximab + nivolumab achieved an ORR of 50 % among evaluable patients (12/24; 95 % CI 29 - 71; confirmed ORR 42 %, 95 % CI 22–64; intention-to-treat ORR 46 %, 95 % CI 27 - 67) and DCR 96 % (95 % CI 79 - 100), with median duration of response 7.7 months (95 % CI 4.5 - NR), median PFS 7.4 months (95 % CI 5.6 - 9.6) and median OS 22.0 months (95 % CI 11.2 - 25.8), thereby meeting the co-primary endpoint of best radiographic response and supporting clinical benefit of this triple combination in this biomarker-defined population. Co-primary safety objectives were also met, with grade 3-4 treatment-related AEs reported in 23% of patients (including asymptomatic elevated lipase 12% and amylase 8%, colitis 4%, maculopapular rash 4%, leukocytosis 4%, and grade 4 nivolumab-related myositis/myocarditis 4%).

A patient (29/M) had 2 weeks with oral cavity ulcer and nasal bleeding and was diagnosed with AML with marrow including 91.5 % blasts with morphologic features of AML-M5. Karyotype was abnormal (47, XY, +8). Peripheral blood had a white blood cell count of 5.33 × 10^9/L, a platelet count of 30 × 10^9/L, and hemoglobin level of 69 g/L. recurrent AML-related mutations of CEBPA, c-KIT, DNMT3A, FLT3-ITD, FLT3-TKD, and NPM1 were tested for and not found, but only FLT3-TKD (D835Y G > T) was found. He was started on sorafenib 200 mg twice daily, however it was withdrawn since he developed erythema multiforme, which disappeared within 4 days after discontinuation of sorafenib. Sorafenib was restarted, and erythema multiforme appeared, causing discontinuation a second time. He then received a matched related donor hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, and remained in complete morphologic remission and undetectable MRD level by MFC, but with chronic graft vs host disease.

In a retrospective cohort analysis of colon adenocarcinoma treated with PD-1/PD-L1 immune checkpoint inhibitors from the MSKCC ICIs-treated COAD dataset (n = 76; NCOA3-mutant n = 7, NCOA3-wild-type n = 69), NCOA3 mutation was associated with improved OS vs wild type (P = 0.038), consistent with enhanced benefit from checkpoint blockade in the mutant group. In contrast, in the TCGA COAD cohort without uniform immunotherapy exposure (OS n = 378; DFS n = 241), NCOA3 mutation did not significantly affect OS (P = 0.359) or DFS (P = 0.124).

The authors report a TTMV-RARA (viral fusion) in a 39-year-old patient with leukemia and blasts that were APL-like with increased promyelocytes. The fusion was identified by targeted long read sequencing and confirmed by PCR amplification and Sanger sequencing. Given the established role of RARA in APL tumors, the authors assert that this highly unusual TTMV-RARA fusion is a distinctive driver of APL-like leukemia.

A study of 204 children with B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia from three Dutch trials (DCOG ALL-8, 9, 10) and two German trials (COALL 06-97, 07-03) included 73 cases of BCR-ABL1-like B-ALL that were tested to detect fusions involving ABL1, PDGFRB, JAK2 and CSF1R. 12 cases with tyrosine kinase-activating fusion were found (16%) including one ZMIZ1-ABL1 case that was confirmed with RT-PCR.

A 60-year-old presented with bloating and shortness of breath. Records showed leukocytosis (white blood cell count of 12 × 109/L) with enlarged spleen. A comprehensive molecular profiling (whole exome and whole transcriptome sequencing) determined that CTNNB1 I35T and FBXW11 F517S missense mutations were mutually exclusive and collectively account for 94% (25/32 and 5/32 patients respectively) of salivary gland basal cell adenoma (BCA) and nearly absent (1/11 for each mutation) in basal cell adenocarcinoma (BCAC). evidence_statement: In a multicentre retrospective cohort study of 122 paediatric patients (aged 1-18 years) with newly diagnosed ABL-class fusion (ABL1 fusion-positive, ABL2 fusion-positive, CSF1R fusion-positive, and PDGFRB fusion-positive) B-cell acute lymphocytic leukaemia, who had not received tyrosine-kinase inhibitors as a first-line treatment, 40 had an in frame ABL1 Fusion, and of these 16 were a ZMIZ1::ABL1 fusions. Patients with ZMIZ1::ABL1 had a median MRD between 10^-4 and 10^-3 at the end of induction therapy, but between different ABL1 fusions MRD did not differ significantly.

therapies: Selective Estrogen Receptor Covalent Antagonist H3B-6545
evidence_statement: In ERα-positive breast cancer xenograft and PDX models expressing ERαWT or ERαY537S (ST986, ST1799, ST941, ST2177, ST2056), oral H3B-6545 produced dose-dependent antitumor activity, including TGI of 61%, 85%, 81%, and 85% at 3, 10, 30, and 100 mg/kg in the ST941 ERαY537S/WT PDX model, TGI of 48% with fulvestrant vs 75% with H3B-6545 at 3 mg/kg in the MCF7 ERαWT model, and TGI of 74% with fulvestrant vs 87%, 94%, and 98% at 3, 10, and 30 mg/kg in the ST2177 ERαY537S PDX model, with tumor regressions observed at 10–30 mg/kg. H3B-6545 also retained cellular potency in MCF7 lines carrying ESR1 H524L, with GI50 values of 0.6 nmol/L (ERαWT) and 5.3 nmol/L (ERαY537S), whereas fulvestrant and raloxifene showed >30-fold loss of activity in the ERαY537S/H524 setting.

In the first in human open label phase 1 trial of PF-07799933 for BRAF-mutant advanced solid tumors (NCT05355701; n = 30; BRAFV600E n = 22, BRAF class II/III n = 8), 20 patients with BRAFV600-mutant cancers treated with PF-07799933 alone or with binimetinib or cetuximab achieved 5 confirmed responses (0/3 at 50 mg QD, 1/7 at 150 mg QD, 4/7 at 225 mg BID including one complete response, plus one post cutoff PR at 225 mg BID + binimetinib). Responses included PRs in melanoma, colorectal cancer, thyroid cancer, and NSCLC, and a confirmed CR in a BRAFV600E primary brain tumor, with one thyroid cancer achieving approximately 80% tumor reduction after addition of binimetinib and one Class III ACC patient achieving a molecular ctDNA CR despite radiographic PD. Median duration of response was not reached, and no dose-limiting toxicities occurred.

molecular_profile: NRAS Mutation OR KRAS Mutation OR BRAF Mutation
evidence_statement: In a first in human open label phase 1 dose escalation and expansion study of lifirafenib in advanced solid tumors (NCT02610361; n = 131; BRAF-mutated n = 53, KRAS/NRAS-mutated n = 66; biomarker BRAF or RAS mutation; primary endpoint investigator assessed ORR in expansion), BRAF-mutated patients had an ORR of 17.0% (9/53; 1 CR, 8 PR) and DCR 67.9% (36/53), including confirmed PRs in BRAF V600 melanoma (5/23), BRAF V600E thyroid cancer (2 patients), and BRAF V600E LGSOC (1 patient), with median DoR 31.7 months (95% CI 6.8 – 31.7) during dose escalation and 11.1 months (95% CI 1.9 – not reached) during dose expansion. KRAS/NRAS-mutated patients had an ORR of 3.0% (2/66) and DCR 53.0% (35/66), with median duration of SD 4.1 months (95% CI 3.5 – 4.9) and common grade ≥3 treatment-related AEs in expansion including hypertension (8.3%) and fatigue (7.3%)

Concurrent inactivating mutations in ARID1A and ARID1B were identified in 12 of 24 BRG1/INI1-intact dedifferentiated endometrial or ovarian carcinomas, with all co-mutated tumours showing complete loss of ARID1B and loss of ARID1A in the undifferentiated component, consistent with SWI/SNF-A complex disruption and arrested cellular differentiation. These ARID1A/ARID1B co-inactivated tumours displayed aggressive clinical behaviour comparable to BRG1- or INI1-inactivated dedifferentiated carcinomas, with more than 50% of patients in both groups dying within 2 years (P = 0.15).

In TCGA endometrial carcinoma (n = 509), ARHGAP35 was somatically mutated in 108 tumors with 152 mutations at 126 positions (20.2%), and pan cancer analysis showed ARHGAP35 mutations in >2% of all tumors, ranking it among the top 30 most significantly mutated cancer genes. In functional assays, 124 tumor-derived ARHGAP35 variants expressed in HEK-293T and endometrial cancer cell lines frequently impaired p190A RhoGAP activity and its suppression of Gα13 signaling, with 55/124 mutations (23 nonsense, 15 frame-shift, 15 missense, 2 in-frame deletions) losing RhoGAP-mediated inhibition of Rho activation and 57/124 mutations (24 missense, 19 nonsense, 12 frame-shift, 2 in-frame deletions) failing to suppress AP-1 transcription and Gα13QL-induced foci formation, consistent with loss-of-function enhancement of the Gα13–Rho–AP-1 axis in endometrial cancer.

phenotypes: Juvenile onset,Early young adult onset,Childhood onset
evidence_statement: In a group of 73 of Dutch and German children with Ph-Like B Cell Precursor ALL, 12 tyrosine kinase-activating fusion genes were found. 4 of the Fusions were EBF1::PDGFRB. Leukemic cells taken from three EBF1::PDGFRB patients tested for imatinib sensitivity in ex vivo cultures, and were found to be sensitive to 15 and 30 μM imatinib. In comparison, there was no cytotoxic response in four EBF1::PDGFRB negative samples, and two of the control samples showed growth under imatinib. 100 μg/ml prednisolone augmented growth inhibition in 2/3 of the EBF1::PDGFRB cultures.

molecular_profile: ERCC2 Mutation OR ERCC3 Mutation OR ERCC4 Mutation OR ERCC5 Mutation
evidence_statement: In two independent retrospective pan-cancer cohorts without ICI treatment (TCGA cohort 1 n = 3292; MSK-MET cohort 2 n = 25,659), tumors harboring ERCC2/ERCC3/ERCC4/ERCC5 mutations showed improved OS vs ERCC-WT cases with HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.62-0.91; p = 0.009) in cohort 1 and HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.69-0.83; p < 0.001) in cohort 2. In cohort 1, ERCC-mutated tumors also demonstrated longer PFS (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.68-0.98; p = 0.045).

evidence_statement: In a retrospective pan-cancer ICI-treated cohort from MSKCC (cohort 3, n = 1661), ERCC2/ERCC3/ERCC4/ERCC5-mutated tumors demonstrated improved OS vs ERCC-WT tumors (HR 0.54, 95% CI 0.42-0.70; p < 0.001), and ERCC-MT melanoma and NSCLC patients had better OS (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.42-0.90; p = 0.035). In an independent validation cohort of ICI-treated melanoma and NSCLC (cohort 4, n = 459), ERCC-MT cases showed improved OS (HR 0.56, 95% CI 0.37-0.84; p = 0.03) and a higher response rate (51.9% vs 26.8%; Fisher exact p = 0.005). In both of these cohorts, there was a higher TMB in the ERCC-MT subgroup than ERCC-WT.

In MiaPaCa2 xenografts (n = 5 per arm), C-DIM12 30 mg/kg daily, combined with gemcitabine 100 mg/kg twice weekly, produced greater tumor-volume reduction and prolonged median survival from 20 to 97 days compared with gemcitabine alone.

In the AOM–DSS mouse colon tumor model (n = 8/group), aspirin (28 mg/kg/day) reduced tumor number and decreased epithelial proliferation (Ki67 and BrdU staining) and lowered circulating pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-10, IL-17, IL-13, TNF-α, TNFSF8, GM-CSF, G-CSF, MCP-5, MIG, and TARC). It also reduced arachidonic acid tumorigenic metabolites (PGE2, PGF2α, LTA4, 5-HETE, and 13-HODE), supporting chemopreventive activity. In CRC cell lines (HCA-7, DLD1, HT-29), aspirin (5 mM) decreased TOP reporter activity and WNT6 protein, while WNT6 knockdown reduced proliferation, identifying WNT6 as an aspirin-sensitive effector of Wnt-driven growth. TCGA colon adenocarcinoma data showed that low WNT6 expression correlated with approximately 30% higher 8-year survival, indicating elevated WNT6 as a potential biomarker of aspirin-targetable Wnt signaling in CRC.

Bumetanide directly inhibits NKCC1 (SLC12A2) with an IC50 of 0.16–0.28 μM in hNKCC1-transfected HEK293 cells, which is substantially more potent than the NKCC1 inhibitor ARN23746 (IC50 ~20 μM) and STS66 (IC50 ~40 μM). In NKCC1-expressing HEK293 cells, bumetanide inhibited Cl– influx more potently than the novel derivatives ARN23746 and ARN24092, reducing influx by 58.8% and 71.7% at 10 and 100 μM, respectively, compared with 45.7% and 92.8% for ARN23746 and 13.9% and 51.9% for ARN24092 (IC50 values not reported), supporting NKCC1 as a bumetanide-sensitive chloride importer.

In prostate cancer cell lines with loss of the Y-linked histone demethylase KDM5D (knockdown in LNCaP and VCaP, or deletion in LNCaP-104R2 and E006AA), ATR signaling was activated, and the selective ATR inhibitor VE822 (VX-970/Berzosertib) produced greater inhibition of cell proliferation and increased DNA damage/apoptosis than in KDM5D-expressing controls (cell viability and immunoblot assays, 72 h VE822, independent experiments, p < 0.05). In xenograft mouse models using KDM5D-deficient (LNCaP-104R2 and E006AA) versus KDM5D-positive (LNCaP and 22RV1 cells) (n = 6 mice per arm), oral VE822 (60 mg/kg 4 times weekly for 4 weeks) significantly suppressed tumor growth only in KDM5D-deficient tumors (ANOVA p < 0.05), supporting KDM5D loss as a predictive biomarker of ATR inhibitor sensitivity in prostate carcinoma.
