In a clinicopathologic and molecular series of astroblastoma (n = 8; biomarker MN1 rearrangement; primary endpoint diagnostic detection), MN1 break-apart FISH identified rearrangements in all informative tumors (5 of 5; 2 of 7 non-informative). Array CGH in 4 of 8 tumors showed focal alterations at the MN1 locus on 22q12.1 with associated chromothripsis-like X-chromosome deletions. The article notes recurrent MN1 fusion partners described in HGNET–MN1 tumors, including MN1–BEND2 (three tumors) and MN1–CXXC5 (one tumor), supporting MN1 rearrangement and its known fusion variants as defining diagnostic features of astroblastoma.

therapies: Antisecretory Factor-enriched Egg Yolk Powder Supplement,Temozolomide
evidence_statement: Antisecretory factor (AF) induction by the SPC diet or Salovum in GBM xenografts (GBM43, GBM6) reduced NKCC1-mediated chloride influx, chloride permeability, and blocked regulatory volume increase in tumors characterized by NKCC1 overexpression. It also showed decreasing interstitial pressure and increasing ADC and drug uptake, including a 7-fold rise in doxorubicin. These effects significantly improved survival across both models compared with controls (GBM43 SPC n = 12 vs control n = 7, p < 0.01; Salovum n = 5 vs control n = 7, p < 0.05; GBM6 SPC n = 13 vs control n = 8, p < 0.05; Salovum n = 10 vs control n = 8, p < 0.05). AF reduced proliferation (Ki67, p < 0.05), increased apoptosis (cleaved caspase-3, p < 0.05), and decreased NKCC1 phosphorylation, effects reproduced by bumetanide (NKCC1 inhibitor blocking chloride influx and cell-volume recovery), confirming NKCC1 as the druggable mechanism. Combined AF induction and low-dose temozolomide (TMZ 5 mg/kg × 2 days) prevented tumor regrowth and achieved 100% survival at 120 days compared with TMZ alone (TMZ n = 9 vs SPC+TMZ n = 7, p < 0.01), supporting NKCC1-driven chloride transport inhibition as a chemosensitizing strategy in GBM.

In this study the authors examined six gynecologic tract perivascular epithelioid cell tumors (PEComas) that were previously diagnosed as PEComa but demonstrated unusual morphology suggestive of TFE3 involvement. A comparison group of eleven conventional PEComas was also included. TFE3 break-apart FISH and immunohistochemistry were utilized to evaluate for TFE3 gene abnormalities. TFE3 rearrangements were identified in all six test cases, whereas none of the conventional PEComas showed TFE3 rearrangement. The TFE3-rearranged tumors showed a distinctive immunophenotype characterized by strong nuclear TFE3 expression, absent or minimal melanocytic marker expression, and lack of smooth muscle marker positivity, in contrast to the conventional PEComa profile. Morphologically, TFE3-rearranged PEComas demonstrated predominantly pure epithelioid clear-cell morphology with an alveolar or nested growth pattern, differing from the mixed epithelioid–spindled architecture typical of conventional lesions. The cohort included five females and one male, aged 17–52 years. The authors concluded that they have identified a distinct subset of PEComas with characteristic morphology and immunophenotype, defined by v::TFE3 gene fusions, which separate them diagnostically from conventional PEComa and support their classification within the family of TFE3-associated neoplasms.

In this 2025 study, the authors included 14 confirmed TFE3-rearranged perivascular epithelioid cell tumors (PEComas), previously classified as benign (9 tumors) or malignant (5 tumors), and compared them to the molecular features of TSC2/1-inactivated PEComas. DNA sequencing and FISH were utilized to investigate genetic correlates of malignancy. Complex chromosomal copy number alterations (CNAs) were detected in three of four (75%) assessable malignant tumors and were absent in all benign tumors. Inactivating alterations in TP53, RB1, or ATRX were rare among the malignant tumors, observed in only 1 of 5 cases, contrasting with patterns seen in malignant TSC2/1-inactivated PEComas. The cohort comprised 11 females and 3 males, with a wide age range at diagnosis, from 9 to 64 years (median 31.5 years). Tumors occurred in diverse anatomical sites, including the uterus, extremities, colon, nasal cavity, neck, retroperitoneum, bladder, and ovary. The authors concluded that complex CNAs are a frequent genetic correlate of malignancy in TFE3-rearranged PEComas and may serve as a diagnostic marker, and that these tumors lack the highly recurrent TP53, RB1, or ATRX alterations characteristic of TSC2/1-inactivated PEComas.

disease: Round Cell Sarcoma With EWSR1-non-ETS Fusion
evidence_statement: This case series presented 7 NFATC2-rearranged sarcomas, including 4 EWSR1::NFATC2 and 3 FUS::NFATC2 cases, and developed an ACAN-encoding aggrecan immunohistochemistry as a diagnostic tool for these tumors. All cases were primary bone tumors with 6 located in the long bones (4 femur, 2 tibia) and 1 in the ilium. Using RNA-seq, the FUS::NFATC2 fusion was found to join exon 6 of FUS with exon 3 of NFATC2 in all three cases. FISH analysis using the FUS break-apart probe (BAP) was applied to one case and identified an unbalanced pattern with gains of the 5’ FISH probe (data not shown). Array-CGH further showed more complex genomic profiles in all FUS::NFATC2 cases compared with one tested EWSR1::NFATC2 sample. This study expanded the evidence for the recurrent FUS::NFATC2 fusion in the rare round cell sarcoma.

disease: Round Cell Sarcoma With EWSR1-non-ETS Fusion
evidence_statement: This is the first study to identify the FUS::NFATC2 gene fusion. Using multi-omics approach and targeted sequencing, the authors comprehensively characterized the molecular landscape of a large cohort of Ewing sarcoma (-like) tumors (101 samples, including 65 tumors and 36 cell lines). Seven of 62 (11.3%) tumors analyzed by RNA-seq were found to lack a typical Ewing sarcoma EWSR1 gene fusion. One case was found to harbor a novel, in-frame FUS::NFATC2 fusion joining the TET family member FUS (exon 6) and the non-ETS family transcription factor NFATC2 (exon 9). This observation was further verified by RT-PCR followed by Sanger sequencing. This work provided the first evidence of FUS::NFATC2 gene fusion, which leads to the establishment of the new disease entity “round cell sarcoma with EWSR1-non-ETS fusions”.

In a single-center retrospective review of recurrent malignant gliomas with EGFR alterations (n = 6, 2 GBM), osimertinib showed a manageable safety profile with thrombocytopenia in 2 patients (grade 2 and grade 3 on concurrent bevacizumab) and no rash or QTc prolongation. Among 4 patients evaluable for radiographic response, 1 achieved PR and 2 achieved SD with times on osimertinib of 77–294 days, including 2 EGFR vIII altered GBMs that remained on treatment for 236 and at least 294 days. These findings suggest that EGFR vIII rearrangements with amplification may be associated with extended clinical benefit on osimertinib in heavily pretreated (≥2 prior regimens) current malignant glioma.

In a pooled analysis of five phase I–II trials and an expanded access program of ONC201 (dordaviprone) for recurrent H3 K27M–mutant diffuse midline glioma (NCT02525692, NCT03295396, NCT03416530, NCT03134131, NCT05392374; n = 50), the RANO-HGG ORR was 20.0% (1 CR, 9 PR; 95% CI 10.0–33.7) with DCR 40.0% (95% CI 26.4–54.8; SD n = 10), median DOR 11.2 months (95% CI 3.8–NR), TTR 8.3 months (range 1.9–15.9), 6-month PFS 35.1% (95% CI 21.2–49.3), and median OS 13.7 months (95% CI 8.0–20.3), with 12- and 24-month OS of 57.3% (95% CI 41.4–70.3) and 34.7% (95% CI 20.7–49.2). Using RANO-LGG criteria, the ORR was 26.0% (95% CI 14.6–40.3; 6 PR, 7 MR) and DCR 42.0% (95% CI, 28.2 to 56.8; SD, n = 8), and when combining the best responses across either RANO system, the ORR was 30.0% (95% CI 17.9–44.6) and DCR 44.0% (95% CI, 30.0–58.7; SD, n = 7); corticosteroid reduction ≥50% occurred in 46.7% of evaluable patients (7/15; 95% CI, 21.3–73.4), median TTR 3.7 months (range 1.9–5.6) and KPS/LPS improvement in 20.6% (7/34, 95% CI, 8.7 to 37.9) median TTR 3.5 months (range 1.9–22.4).

MYC p.S146L, a recurrent substitution in the N-terminal transactivation domain near Myc Box 2, increased MYC–TRRAP binding in quantitative interaction assays and co-immunoprecipitation, with significantly higher proximity ligation signal than wild-type MYC (p < 0.05–0.0001). In MCF10A cells, MYC S146L enhanced MYC-target gene activation, reduced migration (p < 0.05–0.001), and increased survival in low-attachment conditions (p < 0.0001), consistent with an oncogenic gain-of-function. In colon organoids and p53-wildtype HCT116 cells, MYC S146L caused negative selection and increased apoptosis, which was attenuated by TP53 loss, indicating a context-dependent phenotype.

In biliary tract cancer (BTC) models with PBRM1 loss-of-function (EGI1 and CCC5), sensitivity to PARP inhibitors increased significantly, with lower IC50 values for niraparib (2.25 µM vs 6.62 µM, p = 0.0001) and olaparib (59.32 µM vs 70.75 µM, p = 0.01) compared with PBRM1-proficient cells, and ATR inhibition with berzosertib showed enhanced sensitivity as well (0.172 µM vs 0.415 µM, p < 0.0001). Combined berzoseritb + niraparib produced further synergy (IC50 0.05 µM vs 0.08 µM, p < 0.0001). Clinically, a patient with PBRM1-mutated BTC treated with niraparib achieved radiographic stable disease at 4 and 8 weeks with improved symptoms and no treatment-related toxicity, supporting PBRM1 loss as a predictive biomarker of response to PARP with or without ATR inhibition in BTC

Across a multicenter cohort of CNS embryonal tumors (n = 9), recurrent BRD4::LEUTX fusions were identified by RNA sequencing, with all cases retaining LEUTX exon 2 and variable BRD4 breakpoints (exons 11, 13, or 14), and all tumors matched a distinct DNA-methylation cluster (Heidelberg v12 score 0.79–1.0) defining this entity. These tumors occurred in very young children (≤4 years), showed highly cellular embryonal histology with diffuse synaptophysin (5/5) and OLIG2 expression (4/5), and lacked recurrent genomic alterations beyond the fusion. These findings support BRD4::LEUTX as a diagnostic biomarker for a distinct CNS embryonal tumor subtype.

In this 2025 retrospective study, 14 spindle cell rhabdomyosarcoma (SCRMS) cases previously identified as possessing ZFP64::NCOA2 or ZFP64::NCOA3 fusions were pulled from clinical archives to assess clinicopathologic, immunohistochemical, and molecular genetic features. Key observations include a strong male prevalence, middle-age occurrence (median 41 years; range 22-81 years), wide anatomic distribution, and NCOA3 fusions are more common than NCOA2 fusions. Arising primarily from soft tissue, these tumors displayed both fascicular and spindle cell morphologies within a hyalinized collagenous background and various degrees of skeletal muscle marker expression, although occasional focal or diffuse round cell morphologies were also observed. All cases were analyzed by targeted RNA sequencing platforms from various laboratories, with specific fusions noted between ZFP64 exon 5::NCOA2 exon 14 fusion in 6 cases (43%) and ZFP64 exon 5::NCOA3 exon 14/15 fusion in 8 cases (57%). Ten of these cases were also characterized by DNA methylation profiling, revealing ZFP64 SCRMS as an epigenetic sarcoma subtype distinct from other RMS. SCRMS with ZFP64::NCOA2/3 fusions are associated with frequent distant metastases, local recurrences, and death, and therefore these fusions may provide benefit as prognostic markers.

molecular_profile: KRAS G12C OR KRAS G12D OR KRAS G13D OR RET M918T OR KRAS G12A OR KRAS G12V OR KRAS G12R OR KRAS Amplification OR KRAS G12S OR KRAS G13R OR KRAS G12P
evidence_statement: In the randomized discontinuation Phase II MOST-Plus trial of advanced/metastatic solid tumors with sorafenib-targeted somatic alterations (NCT02029001; n = 35 randomized; KRAS G12A/C/D/P/R/S/V n = 29, KRAS G13D/R n = 2, KRAS amplification n = 2, RET M918T n =1), patients with stable disease at 12-week induction who continued sorafenib had superior PFR-16w compared with interruption (65% [95% CrI 43.4–83.7] vs 25% [95% CrI 7.8–48.1]). Maintenance sorafenib also improved median PFS (5.6 mo [95% CI 1.97–6.77] vs 2.0 mo [95% CI 1.61–3.91], p = 0.0231) and showed a trend toward improved OS (14.3 mo [95% CI 8.9–23.8] vs 8.0 mo [95% CI 3.5–15.2], p = 0.0857). These findings support that tumors harboring KRAS G12 or G13 alterations, KRAS amplification, or RET M918T derive greater progression-free benefit from continued sorafenib after SD.

molecular_profile: ESR1::NCOA3 Fusion OR ESR1::NCOA2 Fusion OR GREB1::NCOA2 Fusion
evidence_statement: In uterine tumors resembling ovarian sex cord tumor (UTROSCT; n = 4), RNA sequencing identified recurrent ESR1::NCOA3 (n = 2), ESR1::NCOA2 (n = 1), and GREB1::NCOA2 (n = 1) fusions, involving NCOA2/3 exon 14–15 joined to ESR1 exon 3 or GREB1 exon 2, all confirmed by FISH. These fusion-positive tumors demonstrated marked ESR1 mRNA overexpression and a shared transcriptional profile with up-regulation of WT1, AR, HOXA10, HOXA11, and PBX1, forming a distinct cluster separate from other sarcomas. These findings support ESR1::NCOA2 and related NCOA2/3 rearrangements as defining diagnostic markers for UTROSCT.

In NIH3T3 colony formation assays, cells expressing N540K displayed a transformed phenotype and showed approximately 20 fold increased colony formation over wildtype cells. In comparison, activating variant FGFR3 K650E showed approximately 70 fold increase. In addition, there was approximately 2 fold increased ratio of phospho-ERK/ERK signaling over wildtype in western blots when cells were expressing N540K.

molecular_profile: PIK3CA E545K AND FGFR3 S249C AND FGFR3 N540K
evidence_statement: In this study of 21 patients with FGFR-driven urothelial carcinoma treated with selective FGFR inhibitors (including erdafitinib), post-progression molecular analyses (tissue and/or ctDNA sequencing) identified secondary FGFR3 kinase domain mutations as a mechanism of acquired resistance. In one patient (MR86) who initially harbored FGFR3 S249C and PIK3CA E545K and was treated with erdafitinib (best response −25%; progression-free survival 2.7 months), an FGFR3 N540K mutation was detected in post-progression tumor tissue but was absent at baseline, indicating emergence during therapy. Functional studies using Ba/F3 models demonstrated that the FGFR3 N540K mutation reduces sensitivity to FGFR inhibitors, including erdafitinib, supporting its role as a resistance-associated alteration.

A urothelial cancer patient (ID CTC1845) with activating mutation FGFR3 Y373C was treated with a sequence of erdafitinib and futibatinib which also had intervening immunotherapy. At progression on futibatinib, a ctDNA sample was collected and FGFR3 N540K was seen at VAF 4%. Other FGFR tyrosine kinase domain mutations were noted: V55L at VAF 3% and L608V at VAF 2%.

Western blots were performed on Ba/F3 cells expressing driver fusion FGFR3::TACC3 and FGFR3::TACC3 plus FGFR3 N540K. In the FGFR3::TACC3 plus FGFR3 N540K cells, levels of phosphoylated FGFR (p-FGFR), along with p-ERK and p-S6 were markedly increased in comparison to FGFR3::TACC3 alone.

Ba/F3 cells expressing the FGFR3::TACC3 fusion with or without the N540K mutation were treated with multiple FGFR inhibitors, including erdafitinib and futibatinib. In parental Ba/F3 cells, the IC50 values were 1352.2 nM for erdafitinib and 8588.7 nM for futibatinib, whereas in cells expressing FGFR3::TACC3 alone, IC50 values were 0.02 nM and 0.03 nM, respectively. In Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR3::TACC3 with the N540K mutation, IC50 values increased to 25.9 nM for erdafitinib and 19.5 nM for futibatinib. Across the inhibitor panel, IC50 values exceeded 100 nmol/L for all agents except erdafitinib and futibatinib.

molecular_profile: ESR1::NCOA3 Fusion OR GREB1::NCOA2 Fusion OR ESR1::CITED2 Fusion OR ESR1::v Fusion OR GREB1::v Fusion
evidence_statement: In a retrospective UTROSCT cohort (n = 17, follow-up n = 13), 3 patients (23.1%) carrying GREB1::NCOA2, ESR1::NCOA3 or ESR1::CITED2 fusions developed pelvic, abdominal or pulmonary recurrence, with recurrence rates of 33.3% in GREB1 fusion cases (1/3) and 25.0% in ESR1 fusion cases (2/8). The authors also integrated data from 73 previously reported UTROSCT cases and observed that recurrence was more frequent in tumors with GREB1 rearrangements than in those with ESR1 rearrangements, supporting a pattern of higher recurrence risk in GREB1-rearranged disease.

In the phase 1/2 trial LIBRETTO-121 (NCT03899792), for patients 0.5-21 yrs old with advanced RET-altered solid tumors, dosing started at 92 mg/m2 twice a day of Selpercatinib. Patients had RET-mutant medullary thyroid cancer (MTC, n = 14), RET fusion-positive papillary thyroid cancer (PTC, n = 10), or other tumors (n = 3). M918T was the most common mutation in MTC (10/14) and NCOA4-RET fusion most common in PTC (5/10). Treatment ranged from 0.4 to 40.8 months, and 22 pts remained on treatment at time of this report. Overall response rate was 10/12 in patients with measurable disease at baseline, with 1 having stable disease and 1 with progressive disease. No PTC or MTC patients had progressive disease. At median follow up of 18 months, the median progression free survival had not yet been reached.

Two novel somatic interstitial in-frame deletions in RET, with unknown transformation potential, were identified in medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) tumor samples. One of these (RET E632_L633del) was compared to already established variants (as positive controls) including RET M918T, which authors describe as typical of MEN2B phenotype familial MTC and as a frequent somatic mutation in sporadic MTC. In-vitro transforming activity was tested using focus formation assays on NIH3T3 cells. Vectors for control, M918T, and E632_L633del with neomycin resistance were made and expressed in NIH3T3, and selection with G418 performed. 1.4 x 10^4 M918T and 9.6 x 10^3 control colonies (colonies/ug DNA used in transfection) survived G418 selection. 1.8 x 10^2 transformed loci formed for M918T cells, but <1 x 10^–2 formed for wildtype control. This ratio was 0.013 transformed loci per M918T colony.

In a study of 56 Medullary Thyroid Cancer patients (50 somatic and 6 hereditary) two patients had somatic p.E632_L633del. One of them had p.E632_L633del and p.D898_E901del found in lymph node metastasis. Primary tumor was not available for testing. One of them had heterozygous p.E632_L633del in the primary tumor, and a mix of heterozygous and homozygous E632_L633del in lymph node metastasis and in distant metastasis.

A total of 56 metastatic medullary thyroid cancer cases (50 sporadic, 6 familial) were analyzed for RET mutations. A total of 7 cases were found to have a RET germline mutations however one case had a mutation previously shown to have low transforming potential and was considered sporadic. 34/50 sporadic cases had M918T mutations and 3/6 familial cases carried a RET M918T germline mutation. All three showed local recurrences/metastases, and one had instances of pheochromocytoma.

Ba/F3 cells transformed with E632_L633del showed IL-3 independent growth. Selpercatinib inhibited growth of the cells at approximately 16 nM. This was 4-5 fold higher than the IC50 for RET M918T cells, but comparable to results for fusion KIF5B::RET. Selpercatinib totally abolished proliferation at > 33nM. The authors note that at clinical doses of 160mg, selpercatinib concentration is estimated to reach >100 nM, suggesting the potential for strong in vivo inhibition of E632_L633del driven proliferation.
Exogenous expression of RET E632_L633del transformed Ba/F3 cells, causing interleukin-3 independent proliferation. This proliferation was abolished with various RET inhibitors.

A 35 yr old man presented with a 9 month history of worsening right side flank pain and no significant family history. Calcitonin was elevated. After imaging, total thyroidectomy with modified radical right neck dissection and right seventh rib resection was done on the patient. Histology confirmed medullary thyroid cancer with no nodal involvement but tumor necrosis and Ki67 proliferative index of 8%, suggesting high grade disease. Somatic mutation RET Glu632_Leu633del was found by next generation sequencing, with variant allele frequency of 30%. Copy number variation of exon 11 was not seen. After surgery, imaging found lesions in T12 vertebral body and in liver. 18 months after diagnosis patient was given 160 mg selpercatinib twice daily as part of LIBRETTO-001 trial (NCT03157128). A partial response was seen at cycle 9 (4 week cycles). At cycle 13 progressive disease and increased size of liver lesions was seen. Radiation was used to treat a new left ilium lesion after cycle 28. After 12 months further progression was seen No new mutations were found in tests, but the panel was unable to detect fusions. Selpercatinib treatment was ended, and the patient died before new treatment was able to start. Authors conclude that patient had an initial partial response but this was followed by significant progression which reflected a poor overall response to selpercatinib, and that therefore patients with 632_633del are at risk of poor response to this treatment, and additionally patients that progress on selpercatinib could potentially benefit from an early change in treatment.

Wildtype or 632_633del RET was expressed in HEK293 cells, and MAPK reporter response assays were performed on these cells in triplicate, at various concentrations of inhibitors including selpercatinib and pralsetinib. The IC50 for reducing MAPK activity with selpercatinib was 43.62 for wildtype RET and 149.1 for RET 632_633del. The IC50 for reducing MAPK activity with pralsetinib was 51.53 for wildtype RET and 168.5 for RET 632_633del. The authors conclude that these experiments confirm a significant reduction in efficacy of selpercatinib and pralsetinib on cells with the 632_633del mutation.

A patient with advanced progressive medullary thyroid cancer and distant metastatic disease harbored the somatic RET E632_L633del indel and was treated under the LIBRETTO-201 (NCT03906331) trial. Selpercatinib treatment was started at dosage of 160 mg twice per day and the patient had a partial response with approximately -30% change to baseline in target lesions, and approximately -20% change to baseline in non target lesions. Dose was reduced from 160 to 120 mg twice per day. At end of data collection in November 2021, the patient continued selpercatinib after 17 months of treatment.

In follow up analyses of the AUGMENT-101 trial of revumenib in patients with acute leukemia, the authors identify MEN1 variants in bone marrow specimens obtained after treatment. These variants were not detectable in pre-treatment samples by ddPCR. NGS detected at least one MEN1 variant in four patients. An apparent variant hotspot was observed in the region of amino acid residue 327-349. A broader survey of 31 revumenib treated patients using ddPCR for five specific variants in this region identified 12 patients (38.7%) with one or more MEN1 variants. Longitudinal analysis in two patients demonstrated increasing variant frequency over several weeks on therapy. Patient derived xenograft experiments involving three distinct tumor models and exposure to the Menin-inhibitor VTP-50469 demonstrated acquisition of the same MEN1 variants. After long term exposure to Menin inhibition, 22 xenografted mice relapsed, and MEN1 variants were identified in 15 of these (68%). A high-throughput base editor drug resistance screening assay identified the same amino acid positions. Based on these results the authors propose that putative MEN1 resistance variants correspond to the MLL1 (KMT2A) binding pocket of MEN1. Additional in vitro experiments for specific MEN1 variants (M327I, G331R, T349M) using MOLM13 and OCI-AML3 lines confirmed that these variants confer resistance to Menin inhibition.

In a multinational open label phase II dose randomized study of sunvozertinib in platinum pretreated advanced NSCLC with EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations (WU-KONG1B, NCT03974022; efficacy n = 85 for 200 mg-random, n = 89 for 300 mg-random, and n = 107 for 300 mg-all), sunvozertinib produced IRC confirmed ORRs of 45.9% (97.5% CI, 33.6 - 58.5), 47.2% (97.5% CI, 35.1 - 59.5), and 45.8% (97.5% CI, 34.8 - 57.0) at 200 mg-random, 300 mg-random, and 300 mg-all, respectively (P < 0.0001 vs null ORR 17%), with median PFS 8.4, 7.7, and 6.9 months and 12-month OS rates 62.1, 73.7, and 69.4%. Across treated patients (200 mg-random n = 91; 300 mg-all n = 111), grade ≥3 treatment related AEs occurred in 40.7% and 58.6%, most commonly diarrhea (2.2% vs 18.0%), blood CPK increase (6.6% vs 12.6%), and anemia (4.4% vs 6.3%), with no treatment related deaths; both dose levels met the prespecified primary endpoint of IRC confirmed ORR.

In an open-label phase II Pediatric MATCH subprotocol of vemurafenib for relapsed or refractory solid tumors with BRAF V600 mutations (NCT03220035; n = 4 evaluable), all four treated patients carried BRAF V600E mutations and included one case each of high-grade glioma, histiocytic disorder, ameloblastoma and Ewing sarcoma. One patient with high-grade glioma achieved a confirmed PR (25%) with a PFS of 12.9 months (95% CI 0.82–NA), while 1 patient progressed and 2 discontinued. Grade 3–4 AEs included acute kidney injury, hyperglycemia, and maculopapular rash, with no treatment-related deaths.

In thyroid cancer cell lines, MK2206 selectively inhibited the proliferation of cells harboring PI3K/Akt pathway activating mutations (PIK3CA, PTEN, RAS or RET/PTC) with IC50 values mostly below or around 0.5 µM, whereas mutation-negative cells showed minimal response with IC50 values up to >1000 µM. The average inhibition efficacy at 1 µM and 3 µM MK2206 was significantly higher in mutation-positive vs mutation-negative cells (59.2 ± 11.3% vs 36.4 ± 8.8%, P < 0.005; 64.4 ± 11.5% vs 38.5 ± 18.9%, P < 0.02). Transfection of PIK3CA H1047R or E545K into resistant SW1736 cells increased p-Akt and enhanced MK2206 sensitivity (IC50 1.76 and 2 µM vs 33 µM in vector control), supporting mutation-dependent drug sensitivity.

molecular_profile: ATM Mutation OR TP53 Mutation OR PIK3R1 Mutation OR PIK3CB Mutation OR NTRK1 Mutation OR CSF2RB Mutation
evidence_statement: In primary soft tissue sarcoma cultures (UPS n = 25, SS n = 12), tumors with at least one mutation in apoptosis pathway genes (TP53, ATM, PIK3CB, PIK3R1, NTRK1 or CSF2RB; Mut+ n = 10, Mut− n = 27) were more often resistant to doxorubicin by CSRA (SI > 250), with resistance in 9/10 Mut+ vs 14/27 Mut− and sensitivity in 1/10 vs 13/27 (p = 0.036). Excluding one TP53 L344R specimen strengthened this association (p = 0.006). Across the cohort, overall resistance rates were 71% for doxorubicin, 64% for ifosfamide, 43% for doxorubicin + ifosfamide, 68 % for docetaxel, 61% for gemcitabine and 45% for docetaxel + gemcitabine, and no significant association between mutation status and resistance was observed for Ifosfamide (p = 0.56), Dox+Ifo (p = 0.24), Docetaxel (p = 0.36), Gemcitabine (p = 0.14) or Doc+Gem (p = 0.21).

In a single-arm phase II trial of pemetrexed in previously treated metastatic urothelial carcinoma selected for MTAP deficiency by IHC (NCT02693717; n = 7), 3 patients (42%) achieved ORR, with median PFS 5.3 months and median OS 7.7 months after a median follow-up of 7.1 months. In a combined clinical dataset including a retrospective cohort (total n = 21), objective responses to pemetrexed were seen in 4/4 MTAP-deficient vs 1/10 MTAP-proficient urothelial carcinomas in the historical cohort (ORR 100% vs 10%). While in the phase II trial, no grade 4–5 treatment-related AEs occurred, and anemia was the most common AE, including grade 3 anemia in 3/7 (43%) patients.

In a retrospective cohort of metastatic lung adenocarcinoma from the BATTLE-2 trial (n = 72), patients with CDKN2A and MTAP co-underexpression tumors (n = 26; representative for 9p21 loss) demonstrated a significantly higher ORR to pemetrexed–platinum chemotherapy (54%) than the other three RNA-defined groups (CDKN2A-hi/MTAP-hi, CDKN2A-lo/MTAP-hi, CDKN2A-hi/MTAP-lo) combined (24%; p = 0.018). In a multivariable model of the 10 most frequently altered lung cancer genes, only MTAP-low expression remained independently associated with increased likelihood of response, whereas other genes showed no significant association. Imaging showed partial responses in CDKN2Alo/MTAPlo tumors compared with progression in CDKN2Ahi/MTAPhi tumors.

The use of circulating tumor DNA in blood for TMB assessment was tested. The cancer gene panel NCC-GP150, which covers the whole exon regions of 150 genes, was created and tested for correlation against established methods for TMB assessment. Testing compared whole exome sequencing (WES) results from tissue samples of 48 Chinese advanced NSCLC patients with NCC-GP150 from matched blood samples from those patients. A Spearman correlation of 0.62 (P<0.001) was reported between these results, when the cutoff between high and low blood TMB (H-bTMB) was greater or equal to 6. In a test with 33 different cancer types, NCC-GP150 correlated strongly with established WES results in 25/33 of the tumor types. 50 advanced NSCLC patients were treated with PD-1 or PDL-1 inhibition. When the H-bTMB cutoff was set to 6, then a minimum hazard ratio favoring H-bTMB patients was seen of HR=0.39 (0.18-0.84) P=.02. For the subset of patients with anti-PD1/PD-L1 therapy as first- or second-Line treatment, results were stronger with HR=0.08 (0.02-0.36) P=.001 at a cutoff of H-bTMB of 6. In this subgroup overall response rate was significantly different (P=0.003), 61.1% in H-b-TMB and 6.7% in L-bTMB. Additionally, in responders bTMB was significantly higher (median 10) than in non responders (median 5, P=0.008). The authors conclude that ctDNA-based bTMB measured using the NCC-GP150 panel is a potential biomarker for anti–PD-1 and anti–PD-L1 treatment in NSCLC.

In a retrospective study, 29 gastrointestinal stromal tumors with morphologic diagnosis by H&E staining and immunoreactivity to KIT (CD117) were evaluated for gain of function KIT or PDGFRA variants. Snap frozen cells with >=95% tumor cells were subjected to RT-PCR to identify variants and gene expression microarrays. Patient 29 had a spindle cell type histology that was positive for CD117 staining on IHC and an exon 11 Kit inframe deletion p.Q556_I563del. In 14/15 tumors with KIT mutations had high KIT expression by microarray analysis. Unsupervised hierarchical clustering also differentiated all but 1 tumor with KIT variants from those with PDGFRA variants, demonstrating similar expression profiles by a variety of KIT mutations.

In a large retrospective study evaluating SMARCA4 variants from 131,668 solid tumor patients, 9434 patients were identified to have one or more SMARCA4 variants. The G1162 residue was noted to be a recurrent hotspot within the DNA binding domain. Using FRET nucleosome remodeling assays in 293T cells and ATAC-seq of transduced NCI-H1944 cells demonstrated the G1162C variant showed deficient chromatin remodeling and downstream gene expression. This variant was also unable to rescue NCI-H1944 cells with SMARCA2 knockdown, while wildtype SMARCA4 and some other SMARCA4 variant overexpression could, demonstrating this variant to be a loss of function variant.

In this 2022 study, the authors included 40 patients aged ≤12 months diagnosed with spindle cell rhabdomyosarcoma (SCRMS) enrolled in international trials and registries, of whom 39 presented with localized disease. FISH or RT-PCR was utilized to investigate VGLL2 and NCOA2 gene fusions. Among 26 tumors with available molecular evaluation, VGLL2 and/or NCOA2 gene rearrangements were detected in 13 (50%) cases. These included NCOA2-VGLL2 fusions in 2 tumours, NCOA2-related fusions (TEAD1-NCOA2) in 5, and VGLL2-related fusions (VGLL2-CITED2) in 6. No gene fusion was identified in 12 cases, and the remaining 14 cases were not tested or had insufficient tissue. The cohort was composed of 18 females and 21 males, with a median age at diagnosis of 2.5 months. The authors concluded that they have identified a subset of spindle cell rhabdomyosarcoma occurring in infants, in which recurrent VGLL2 and NCOA2 gene fusions are present in half of the cases with available molecular data, supporting their role in the biology of infantile SCRMS.

Tumor DNA sequencing identified the MEN1 M322V (aka M327V) variant in two patients (#1 & 3) with KMT2A rearranged AML on the AUGMENT-101 phase 1 trial of Revumenib. An additional ddPCR assay targeting five variants identified a total of 5 patients from AUGMENT-101 with M332V who had exposure to Revumenib. The variant was not detected in pre-treatment samples. The M322V variant was also detected in two mice with patient derived xenografts of MLL::AF6 driven AML after long term treatment with the MENIN inhibitor VTP-50469. A MEN1-focused CRISPR–Cas9 base-editor screen for resistance variants did not identify this amino acid position but the authors conclude that the M322/M327 residue was not amenable to base editing by this approach.

In a TCGA study of 295 primary gastric adenocarcinomas, fresh frozen tumors underwent several molecular techniques copy number arrays, exome sequencing, RNA sequencing, and in a subset whole genome sequencing. Whole genome sequencing identified in frame gene fusions in 74 cases with mRNA sequencing confirming 2 cases with CLDN18::ARHGAP26 fusions. Evaluation of cases without WGS, RNA sequencing identified an additional 9 cases with the CLDN18::ARHGAP26 fusion, totaling 11 tumors. Fusions linked exon 5 of CLDN18 to ARHGAP26 at exon 10 (N=1) or exon 12 (N=10). RNA data confirmed the fusion activated a cryptic splice site in exon 5 of CLDN18 that retained the C-terminal GAP domain of ARHGAP26. These fusions were enriched in genomically stable tumors and mutually exclusive with RHOA mutations.

Tumor DNA sequencing identified the MEN1 M322I (aka M327I) variant in two patients (#5 & 6) on the AUGMENT-101 phase 1 trial of Revumenib. An additional ddPCR assay targeting five variants identified a total of 5 patients from AUGMENT-101 with M332I who had exposure to Revumenib. The variant was not detected in pre-treatment samples. In two patients, the frequency of M322I was observed to increase over cycles 2,4,6 of treatment. The M322I variant was also detected in one mouse with patient derived xenograft of MLL::AF6 driven AML after long term treatment with the MENIN inhibitor VTP-50469. A MEN1-focused CRISPR–Cas9 base-editor screen for resistance variants did not identify this amino acid position but the authors conclude that the M322/M327 residue was not amenable to base editing by this approach. In vitro expression and editing assays to introduce M322I also confirmed a robust decrease in revumenib sensitivity associated with this variant.

In this 2013 study, the authors included 21 spindle cell and sclerosing rhabdomyosarcomas (RMS), and a control group of 4 embryonal RMS and 3 ectomesenchymomas. RNA sequencing and FISH were utilized to investigate NCOA2 gene abnormalities. NCOA2 gene rearrangements were detected in 3 of the 10 pediatric spindle cell RMS (in a 4-week-old, 3-month-old, and 7-month-old) and not detected in any of the tumors from older children, adults, sclerosing RMS, or the control group. SRF::NCOA2 fusions were present in one tumor, and TEAD1::NCOA2 fusions were identified in another, with RT-PCR confirming fusion of SRF exon 6 with NCOA2 exon 12 in the first case. The cohort was composed of 2 females and 1 male, all under one year of age, with tumors arising in the chest wall or posterior neck. The authors concluded that they have identified a subset of spindle cell rhabdomyosarcoma occurring almost exclusively in infants, characterized by recurrent NCOA2 gene rearrangements, which distinguishes it from morphologically similar tumors in older patients.

molecular_profile: TP53 R273C OR TP53 G245S OR TP53 R213*
evidence_statement: In the phase I study of pazopanib and vorinostat in 36 patients with advanced solid tumors, detection of hotspot TP53 mutation was associated with a higher rate of SD ≥6 months/PR, longer median PFS (months), and longer median OS (months) compared to patients without a hotspot TP53 mutation. In colorectal cancer cases, detected TP53 hotspot mutations included TP53 R213*, TP53 G245S, and TP53 R273C. In the subgroup of patients with metastatic colorectal cancer and sarcoma treated with pazopanib and vorinostat, those with detected hotspot TP53 mutations (n = 6) had a significantly longer median PFS of 6.5 months (95% CI 3.0–9.0; p = 0.023) compared to 2.0 months (95% CI 1.8–2.2; p = 0.023) in TP53-undetected cases (n = 10), and a significantly longer median OS of 19.8 months (95% CI 8.2–31.4; p = 0.021) versus 7.2 months (95% CI 0.6–13.8; p = 0.021), respectively.

Tumor DNA sequencing identified the MEN1 T344M (aka T349M) variant in one patient (#4) on the AUGMENT-101 phase 1 trial of Revumenib. An additional ddPCR assay targeting five variants identified a total of 10 patients from AUGMENT-101 with T344M who had exposure to Revumenib. The variant was not detected in pre-treatment samples. In two patients, the frequency of T344M was observed to increase over cycles 2-6 of treatment. The T344M variant was also detected in 12 mice with patient derived xenografts of several models of AML after long term treatment with the MENIN inhibitor VTP-50469. Among these, 9 instances of T344M were observed in MLL::AF10 pediatric AML grafts, and the other 3 instances in single engrafted tumors of: MLL::AF6, NPM1c, and MLL::AF9 driven models respectively. A MEN1-focused CRISPR–Cas9 base-editor screen for resistance variants identified position T344/T349 as a driver of resistance. In vitro expression and CRISPR–Cas9 editing assays to introduce T344M also confirmed a robust decrease in revumenib sensitivity associated with this variant. A combination of MOLM13 (MLL::AF9), MV4;11 (MLL::AF4) and OCI-AML3 (NPM1-mutant) lines were used for these variant over-expression and CRISPR–Cas9 engineered variant assays.

Tumor DNA sequencing identified the MEN1 G326R (aka G331R) variant in one patient (#2, who also had a MEN1 M322I) on the AUGMENT-101 phase 1 trial of Revumenib. An additional ddPCR assay targeting five variants identified a total of 3 patients from AUGMENT-101 with G326R who had exposure to Revumenib. The variant was not detected in pre-treatment samples. In one patient, the frequency of G326R was observed to increase over cycles 2-6 of treatment. The G326R variant was NOT detected in any of 22 patient derived xenograft of several AML models after long term treatment with the MENIN inhibitor VTP-50469. A MEN1-focused CRISPR–Cas9 base-editor screen for resistance variants identified position G326/G331 as a driver of resistance. In vitro lentiviral expression assays to introduce G326R into MOLM13 (MLL::AF9) and OCI-AML3 (NPM1-mutant) cells also confirmed a robust decrease in revumenib sensitivity associated with this variant.

disease: Round Cell Sarcoma With EWSR1-non-ETS Fusion
evidence_statement: This case series study reported 11 neoplasms harboring the EWSR1::PATZ1 gene fusion with 7 in the soft tissue and 4 in the brain. Paired-end sequencing identified a somatic intra-chromosomal paracentric inversion on chromosome 22 involving EWSR1 and PATZ1, located ~2 Mb apart, in all cases. This rearrangement permits transcription of both genes in the same orientation. Two soft tissue cases,1 myoepithelial carcinoma and 1 undifferentiated low-grade sarcoma, were further characterized by RT-PCR with Sanger sequencing. In the former case, EWSR1 exon 8 was fused to PATZ1 exon 1 with a 28-nucleotide insertion derived from EWSR1 intron 8 encoding 10 amino acids. In the latter case, EWSR1 exon 8 was also fused to PATZ1 exon 1, with concurrent presence of an in-frame deletion within exon 1 sequence. Further comprehensive molecular profiling revealed loss/deletion of CDKN2A/CDKN2B in 5 of 7 soft tissue cases (71.4%), with 1 showing concurrent MDM2 amplification. This study expanded the evidence for the recurrent EWSR1::PATZ1 fusion in small round cell sarcoma.

DNA was extracted from the paraffin-embedded tissues of 86 NSCLC tissues. 72 of the samples were tested for FGFR3 alterations in exons 7, 10, and 15 by sequencing, and two showed point mutations causing T450M. FGFR3 was found to be expressed in By IHC, FGFR3 was immunoreactive in 26 of the 86 NSCLC cases. FGFR3 expression was seen in 84.6% of the lung adenocarcinoma cases and 15.4% of lung small cell carcinoma cases. From the 70 NSCLC cases with wild-type FGFR3, 20 (28.6%) cases were FGFR3 positive. High FGFR3 expression correlated with better overall survival (P=0.016) and disease free survival (P=0.040). In addition, multivariate analysis indicated that FGFR3 was an independent prognostic factor HR=0.294 (0.102–0.850) P=0.024, for overall survival in NSCLC patients. Other characteristics of high FGFR3 group were more females, more non-smokers, earlier T stage, fewer lymph node metastases, earlier clinical stage, and higher EGFR mutation rate. The authors conclude that the findings indicate FGFR3 is associated with a favorable prognosis and is a novel independent prognostic biomarker for OS of NSCLC patients, but also note that they only included patients with surgically resectable NSCLC in stages I–IIIA, and that a favorable prognostic role of FGFR3 may only occurr within early-stage NSCLC.

Tumor DNA sequencing identified MEN1 mutations at several residues in the AUGMENT-101 phase 1 trial of Revumenib. An additional ddPCR assay targeting five variants identified a total of 4 patients from AUGMENT-101 with G326D (aka G331R) who had exposure to Revumenib. The G326D variant was detected in a single patient derived xenograft of an AML models (of 22 grafts total) after long term treatment with the MENIN inhibitor VTP-50469. This graft had the G326D variant as well as MEN1 T344M. A MEN1-focused CRISPR–Cas9 base-editor screen for resistance variants identified position G326/G331 as a driver of resistance.

disease: Round Cell Sarcoma With EWSR1-non-ETS Fusion
evidence_statement: This case series study presented clinical, histopathological, and molecular findings of 9 EWSR1::PATZ1-rearranged sarcomas, including one previously reported case. The cohort included 4 males and 5 females ranging in age from 10 to 81 years. These tumors most occurred in the thoracoabdominal soft tissues (5 in abdominal wall soft tissues, 3 in the thorax, 1 in the posterior neck). Molecularly, the EWSR1 (exon8)::PATZ1(exon 1) gene fusion, with or without the inclusion of part of EWSR1 intron 8, was identified in all cases by NGS. Select cases were subjected to FISH analyses. All 4 tested cases (8/100 nuclei in 3 cases; 9/100 nuclei in 1 case) showed EWSR1 break-apart signals, yet none reached the diagnostic cutoff (10% positive nuclei). Combined FISH and NGS analyses further revealed CDKN2A homozygous or heterozygous deletion in 3 of 6 cases. Chart review and pathological examination showed diverse clinical courses and a broad morphologic spectrum. Collectively, EWSR1::PATZ1 sarcomas are clinically and morphologically heterogeneous diseases, and FISH is an suboptimal for the detection of the EWSR1 rearrangement in this disease.

disease: Round Cell Sarcoma With EWSR1-non-ETS Fusion
evidence_statement: This study presented molecular and clinicopathologic findings of a cohort of 17 EWSR1::PATZ1 soft tissue sarcomas. These tumors occurred in 12 males and 5 females with 15-71 years of age (median age, 50 years) and involved the thoracoabdominal soft tissues (14 cases; 82%), lower extremities (2 cases; 12%), and tongue (1 case; 6%). Targeted RNA sequencing identified EWSR1::PATZ1 gene fusions in all cases, with variable breakpoints located within exon 7-9 of EWSR1, with exon 8 being the predominant breakpoint (14/17, 82%), fused to exon 1 of PATZ1. Genomic breakpoints were obtained from 12 cases showing multiple junction configurations of the EWSR1::PATZ1 gene fusion at the genomic level. The study also showed broad morphological features with more favorable outcome than previously described for EWSR1::PATZ1 positive sarcomas. Notably, this study had two times more male than female patients, although no male predominance had been described previously for the EWSR1::PATZ1 fusion sarcomas.

Tumor DNA sequencing identified the MEN1 S155T (aka S160T) variant in one patient (#3, who also had a MEN1 M322V) on the AUGMENT-101 phase 1 trial of Revumenib. The S155T variant was NOT detected in any of 22 patient derived xenograft of several AML models after long term treatment with the MENIN inhibitor VTP-50469. A MEN1-focused CRISPR–Cas9 base-editor screen for resistance variants identified position S155/S160 as a driver of resistance.

The S155C (S160C) variant was detected in one of 22 patient derived xenograft of several AML models after long term treatment with the MENIN inhibitor VTP-50469. In this graft, it co-occured with a MEN1 T344M variant. A MEN1-focused CRISPR–Cas9 base-editor screen for resistance variants identified position S155/S160 as a driver of resistance.

Results from phase II of the AUGMENT-101 trial are reported for patients with NPM1 mutant relapsed/refractory AML (≥3 previous lines of therapy) treated with revumenib. Patients received revumenib with or without a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 64 adult patients were evaluated. Complete remission (CR) or CR with partial hematologic recovery (CRh). The CR + CRh rate was 23.4% (1-sided P = .0014) and the overall response rate (ORR) was 46.9%. The median duration of response was 4.7 months. NPM1 mutations were centrally confirmed for all included patients (using Focus Myeloid panel, Flagship Biosciences, Inc; or NPM1 Mutation assay, Invivoscribe, Inc). The precise nature of the NPM1 variants in individual patients was not provided in the publication.

molecular_profile: NPM1 MUTATION AND ( IDH2 Mutation OR IDH1 Mutation )
evidence_statement: Results from phase II of the AUGMENT-101 trial are reported for patients with NPM1 mutant relapsed/refractory AML (≥3 previous lines of therapy) treated with revumenib. Patients received revumenib with or without a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 64 adult patients were evaluated. Complete remission (CR) or CR with partial hematologic recovery (CRh) was evaluated. Patients with NPM1 mutation and either IDH1 or IDH2 mutations achieved higher CR + CRh rates than the overall population (75.0% [6/8] and 50.0% [4/8], respectively). Refer to civic.eid:1274 for details on overall response for all NPM1 mutant +ve patients.

In an open-label adaptively randomized phase II trial of dual immune checkpoint blockade in platinum-resistant ovarian clear cell carcinoma (NCT03026062 plus 1 patient from NCT01928394; n = 34, PPP2R1A-mutant n = 11 vs PPP2R1A-wild-type n = 23), tremelimumab plus durvalumab (combination or sequential) or ipilimumab plus nivolumab was associated with greater sensitivity to ICB, with longer OS (median 66.9 vs 9.2 months; HR 0.40; 95% CI 0.15 - 1.08; one-sided log-rank p = 0.031) and longer PFS (median 3.0 vs 1.8 months; one-sided log-rank p = 0.034) in PPP2R1A-mutant vs PPP2R1A-wild-type tumours. In PPP2R1A-wild-type cases, ARID1A mutation status was not associated with a statistically significant OS difference (n = 23; median OS 9.2 vs 5.1 months; one-sided log-rank p = 0.055), and grade ≥3 immune-related adverse events occurred more frequently in PPP2R1A-mutant vs PPP2R1A-wild-type patients (45.5% vs 13.0%; p = 0.079).

In functional preclinical models, CDH1 loss was associated with activation of ECM–DDR2–AKT signaling and increased sensitivity to kinase inhibition. Reactome analysis of AKT3-associated genes in CDH1-low gastric tumours showed significant enrichment of extracellular matrix organisation pathways including DDR2 (adjusted p = 1.4 × 10⁻⁶). CDH1−/− cells and organoids were more sensitive to dasatinib than WT (cells EC50 0.01 vs 0.1 µM, p = 0.00005; organoids EC50 0.4 vs 2.6 µM) with greater apoptosis (20.0% vs 6.8% at 0.2 µM) and preferential suppression of AKT phosphorylation (63% vs 25%).

In functional preclinical models, loss of CDH1 (E-cadherin deficiency) created a synthetic lethal vulnerability to allosteric AKT inhibition. CDH1−/− mammary epithelial cells showed greater sensitivity to allosteric AKT inhibitors (ARQ-092, MK2206, perifosine, SC66), with >60% reduced viability compared to WT and increased apoptotic priming (20–40% higher mitochondrial depolarisation). In isogenic gastric cancer cells, CDH1−/− cells were selectively sensitive to ARQ-092 and MK2206, despite higher basal AKT activation. In mouse-derived gastric organoids, Cdh1-deleted organoids exhibited significantly reduced growth following AKT inhibition (MK2206: 52% vs 185% area increase in WT; p = 0.0005). TCGA STAD analysis further showed AKT3 expression was negatively correlated with CDH1 expression (r = −0.439; p < 2.2 × 10⁻¹⁶), supporting a functional link between CDH1 loss, AKT3 dysregulation, and AKT inhibitor sensitivity.

In functional preclinical analyses of colorectal cancer, loss of FHIT expression resulted in impaired apoptotic signaling and increased tumour cell survival. FHIT-deficient tumour cells showed reduced apoptosis and altered regulation of cell-cycle and death pathways compared with FHIT-expressing controls, supporting loss-of-function effects of FHIT in tumour suppressive biology. Quantitative measures of apoptotic rate or fold-change were not explicitly reported.

phenotypes: Late onset,Middle age onset,Juvenile onset,Young adult onset,Childhood onset
evidence_statement: In this 2015 study, formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue samples were retrieved from the diagnostic pathology archives of the Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital (RNOH) and the Basel Bone Tumour Reference Centre (BBTRC). All cases were reviewed by specialist bone tumour pathologists and classified according to World Health Organization (WHO) criteria. To investigate the oncogenic driver of Giant Cell Tumour of Bone (GCT), whole-genome sequencing was performed on five cases and whole-exome sequencing on one case. In addition, targeted hotspot sequencing using a 14-gene panel, including H3F3A and H3F3B, was conducted to assess the specificity of the p.G34W alteration. This analysis included 91 GCTs and 321 other osteoclast-rich bone lesions. No driver mutations other than the H3F3A p.G34W mutation were identified in the sequenced genomes and exome. Targeted sequencing detected this mutation in 83 GCT cases, with single cases of H3F3A p.G34R and p.G34M; no mutations were found in H3F3B. Both GCTs that metastasized to the lung harbored the H3F3A p.G34W mutation. Overall, H3F3A p.G34 alterations were present in 96% (85/89) of GCTs and absent in other bone tumours in this cohort, supporting their role as highly sensitive and specific molecular markers for GCT.

In this 2015 study, formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tumor samples diagnosed between 1996 and 2014 as giant cell tumor of bone (GCTB), chondroblastoma, chondromyxoid fibroma, aneurysmal bone cyst, or telangiectatic osteosarcoma were retrieved from the Leiden University Medical Centre. A total of 75 GCTB samples were analyzed, including 15 recurrences from 12 patients. H3F3A hotspot mutations were assessed using Sanger sequencing, and immunohistochemistry for H3K36 trimethylation and ATRX expression was performed to evaluate correlation with mutation status. H3F3A G34W/V mutations were identified in 41 of 59 GCTBs (69%) (39 G34W, 2 G34V). Rare variants included a G34 stop codon and a TCT insertion at position 35. H3K36 trimethylation was present in 59 of 60 cases and was more frequent in mutated tumors, whereas ATRX loss showed no correlation with mutation status. Only G34W/V variants were considered mutation-positive for correlation analysis due to the uncertain significance of other variants. In conclusion, H3F3A mutation analysis (particularly G34W/V) by Sanger sequencing represents a highly specific, though less sensitive, diagnostic tool for distinguishing GCTB from other giant cell–containing bone tumors.

In a neoadjuvant letrozole study of ER+/HER2− breast cancer (n = 72), FGFR1 amplification was enriched in endocrine-resistant tumors (9/21, 43%) versus sensitive (3/40, 7%) and intermediate (1/11, 10%) tumors (p = 0.0011), defined by post-treatment Ki67. FGFR1 co-amplification with 11q12–14 (FGF3/FGF4/FGF19) occurred in 90% (8/9) FGFR1-amplified tumors and was strongly associated with letrozole resistance (p = 0.0001). In ER+/FGFR1-amplified PDX models (n = 8 per arm), fulvestrant + lucitanib produced superior tumor regression versus monotherapy (≥50% volume reduction in all treated mice) with reduced p-FGFR1 (Y653/4) and ERα by IHC, supporting FGFR1 amplification as a predictive biomarker of endocrine resistance and FGFR inhibition as a sensitizing strategy.

In this study, the authors investigated a case of pseudomyogenic hemangioendothelioma in a 33-year-old woman presenting with multifocal lytic bone lesions. Previous studies had demonstrated recurrent SERPINE1::FOSB and ACTB::FOSB fusions in pseudomyogenic hemangioendothelioma; however, this tumor lacked those known rearrangements. Using RNA sequencing, RT-PCR, and Sanger sequencing, the authors identified a novel in-frame WWTR1::FOSB fusion, joining exon 4 of WWTR1 (3q25) to exon 2 of FOSB (19q13). The fusion transcript places FOSB under the control of the WWTR1 promoter and is predicted to encode a 553-amino-acid chimeric WWTR1::FOSB transcription factor. Immunohistochemistry demonstrated strong nuclear FOSB expression in the tumor cells, supporting fusion-driven overexpression. Cytogenetic analysis showed a normal karyotype, highlighting the utility of RNA-based methods in detecting cryptic rearrangements. The authors conclude that, in addition to SERPINE1::FOSB and ACTB::FOSB, WWTR1::FOSB represents another recurrent FOSB-related fusion in pseudomyogenic hemangioendothelioma. Detection of FOSB rearrangements and associated nuclear FOSB overexpression may serve as a valuable diagnostic marker to distinguish pseudomyogenic hemangioendothelioma from its histologic mimics.

phenotypes: Middle age onset,Juvenile onset,Late young adult onset
evidence_statement: In this 2017 study the authors included four cases of gastroblastoma with control cases of histologic mimics. Gastroblastoma patients were aged 9, 27, 28 and 56 years. RNASeq identified a MALAT1::GLI1 fusion in two gastroblastomas, with MALAT1 exon 1 fusing to GLI1 exons 5 or 6, and RT-PCR confirming the presence of the fusion. FISH was positive for rearrangement and fusion of the MALAT1 and GLI1 loci in all four cases. Of the contols, one plexiform fibromyxoma was positive for MALAT1 rearrangement but negative for GLI1 rearrangement, with all other controls negative for MALAT1::GLI1. Pathway analysis on differentially expressed genes identified upregulation of the Sonic hedgehog pathway. The authors conclude that gastroblastoma should exist as a distinct entity characterized by the presence of a somatic, recurrent, oncogenic MALAT1::GLI1 fusion gene.

In this 2023 case study the authors investigate a tumour with biphasic morphology composed of epithelial and spindle cell components, diagnosed in a 29-year-old woman. RT-PCR analysis revealed that the tumor harbored the MALAT1::GLI1 fusion gene. The authors also summarised the 16 cases of gastroblastoma that have been reported in the literature, with the MALAT::GLI1 fusion gene identified in 5 of these cases, with testing not performed in 9 cases and the 2 remaining cases showing EWSR1::CTBP1 and PTCH1::GLI2 fusions. They conclude that they have identified another case for this rare entity and postulate the potential role of targeted therapeutics, as nuclear expression of PD-L1 and HDAC2 was observed.

In this 2019 case study the authors investigate a gastric antral tumor with morphological, immunophenotypic and genotypic features consistent with gastroblastoma in a 79-year-old male. Molecular analysis identified a MALAT1::GLI1 fusion gene that retained exon 6 of GLI1. A previous "paraganglioma" detected in the patient was also found to harbor the MALAT1::GLI1 gene fusion, hence the present tumor was assumed to represent the relapse of a disease that ﬁrst presented at 74 years. The authors conclude that they have another example of a gastroblastoma, which is exceedingly rare, and have extended the known age range that this tumor can occur.

In mice, the authors expressed two ATM missense variants (D2880A and N2885K) and a hematopoietic stem cell specific Cre recombinase that inactivates the conditional ATM allele (which behaves similarly to the WT allele). This inactivation expresses kinase-dead ATM protein in all the mice’s blood cells and lymphocytes. The authors also incorporated ATM null mice controls originating from the same litter. Results showed that the median survival of thymic lymphoma for kinase-dead mutated mice (ATM-KD) was 35 days shorter than ATM null mice (p < 0.03). Furthermore, among the ATM-KD mice that developed thymic lymphoma (75%), all of them developed Pten deletions, yet not in the ATM null mice. ATM-KD mice also had higher rates of chromatid breaks compared to ATM null mice.

In mice, the authors expressed two ATM missense variants (D2880A and N2885K) and a hematopoietic stem cell specific Cre recombinase that inactivates the conditional ATM allele (which behaves similarly to the WT allele). This inactivation expresses kinase-dead ATM protein in all the mice’s blood cells and lymphocytes. The authors also incorporated ATM null mice controls originating from the same litter. Results showed that the median survival of thymic lymphoma for kinase-dead mutated mice (ATM-KD) was 35 days shorter than ATM null mice (p < 0.03).

In murine embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs), the authors expressed two ATM missense variants (D2880A and N2885K) and a hematopoietic stem cell specific Cre recombinase that inactivates the conditional ATM allele (ATM KD/-). This inactivation expresses kinase-dead ATM protein in all the mice’s blood cells and lymphocytes. The authors also incorporated ATM null MEFs (ATM -/-) and ATM MEFs with only one inactivated conditional ATM allele (ATM +/-). The ATM KD/- MEFs showed significantly higher sensitivity to camptothecin compared to ATM -/- and ATM +/- MEFs. Furthermore, shRNA knockdown of mutated ATM, containing R3282C, in Granta519 (a human lymphoma cell line) significantly restored the hypersensitivity camptothecin response to a moderate degree (p < 7.26x10e-6).

In a mouse model, expression of kinase-dead ATM missense variants (D2880A and N2885K) combined with Cre-mediated inactivation of a conditional wild-type ATM allele generated Atm KD/− hematopoietic cells expressing only kinase-dead ATM. Irinotecan treatment eradicated activated NOTCH1-driven Atm KD/− T-cell leukemia in vivo, as evidenced by absence of leukemia cells in the spleen, reduced spleen size and weight, and increased apoptosis. In contrast, irinotecan did not eradicate isogenic Atm KD/C leukemias retaining a wild-type ATM allele, supporting loss of wild-type ATM in the context of kinase-dead ATM as a predictive biomarker of sensitivity to Topo1 inhibition.

This exploratory analysis of the Phase 3 MYSTIC trial (NCT02453282) evaluated blood tumour mutational burden (bTMB) as a predictive biomarker for first-line durvalumab with or without tremelimumab vs chemotherapy in patients with advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The cfDNA assay used was GuardantOMNI (500 genes, 2.145 Mb) and the bTMB was calculated by identifying somatic synonymous and non-synonymous single nucleotide variants (SNVs) and short insertions/deletions (indels) at all variant allele frequencies. Pre-treatment plasma bTMB demonstrated a positive correlation with the patient-paired tissue TMB (tTMB) (Spearman rank correlation = 0.6, n=352). In the population evaluable for bTMB (n= 809), patients with bTMB ≥20 mut/Mb showed improved overall survival (OS) for durvalumab plus tremelimumab vs chemotherapy (median, 21.9 months vs 10.0 months; unadjusted HR, 0.49). The improved OS for durvalumab plus tremelimumab vs chemotherapy was not observed in patients with bTMB < 20 mut/Mb. Similarly, bTMB ≥20 mut/Mb, but not <20 mut/Mb, was also associated with improved PFS and ORR for durvalumab plus tremelimumab vs chemotherapy. These findings support a bTMB threshold of 20 mut/Mb as predictive of optimal clinical benefit in OS, PFS, and ORR for durvalumab with tremelimumab.

In ovarian carcinoma (OVCA) preclinical models, CCNE1 amplification predicted synergistic sensitivity to lunresertib (RP-6306) + camonsertib (RP-3500). CCNE1 copy number correlates with synergy by MTT assay (R² = 0.87, p = 0.0064) and ~80% growth inhibition at low-dose combination (RP-6306 31 nM + RP-3500 7.8 nM) in CCNE1-overexpressing cells. The sensitive CCNE1-amplified OVCA cell lines were OVCAR3, FUOV1, COV318 (CN>5) and CCNE1 copy gain were OVCAR8, OVSAHO (CN 2-5). In CCNE1-amplified OVCA PDX models (WO-19, WO-77), combination treatment (RP-6306 5–10 mg/kg + RP-3500 5 mg/kg) significantly increased tumor suppression and improved survival. This method of treatment also reduced metastases vs monotherapy (WO-19 metastases p = 0.0401 and p = 0.0122), with tumor progression (tumor volume > 1000 mm³) as the primary endpoint.

In endometrial carcinoma (EMCA) preclinical models, CCNE1 amplification predicted synergistic sensitivity to lunresertib (RP-6306) + camonsertib (RP-3500), with ~80% growth inhibition at low-dose combination (RP-6306 31 nM + RP-3500 7.8 nM) in CCNE1-overexpressing cells and minimal effect in CCNE1-low parental models. Sensitive CCNE1-amplified EMCA cell models included KLE, as well as CCNE1-induced WO-20 and SNU685 models. In the CCNE1-amplified EMCA PDX model WU-115, RP-6306 (5–10 mg/kg) plus RP-3500 (5 mg/kg) induced tumor regressions and improved survival versus monotherapy (p = 0.0240–0.002 vs RP-6306; p = 0.0032–0.002 vs RP-3500), with tumor progression (tumor volume > 1000 mm³) as the primary endpoint.

In the breast carcinoma cohort of the phase II TAPUR trial (NCT02693535), patients with BRCA1/2 alterations treated with olaparib (26 evaluable) had 1 CR (BRCA2 loss), 11 PR (BRCA1 n=5, BRCA2 n=4, BRCA1/2 n=2), 6 SD16+ (BRCA1 n=1, BRCA2 n=4, BRCA1/2 n=1) yielding ORR 46% (95% CI, 27-67) and DCR 69% (90% CI 55-100; p < 0.001 vs null 15%). Median PFS was 26 weeks (95% CI 15–33) and median OS 55 weeks (95% CI 33–100) in this cohort. Across all TAPUR cohorts combined (NCT02693535; n = 116 evaluable; BC n = 26, BTC n = 18, LC n = 25, UC n = 15, HP n = 32), patients with advanced solid tumors harboring BRCA1/2 alterations treated with olaparib achieved 13 CR, 15 PR, 20 SD≥16 weeks, and 68 PD, corresponding to an ORR of 24% (95% CI 17–33). An 8-year-old girl presented with secondary BRAF V600-mutant histiocytic sarcoma following T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia. After the poor response to initial salvage chemotherapy, the patient responded well to dabrafenib and trametinib combination therapy and remained in partial remission with no disease progression for 3 years.

In a bladder cancer cohort with matched tumor–normal samples (n = 104), KMT2C expression was significantly reduced in tumors compared to normal tissue (71/104 pairs; p < 0.001). shRNA-mediated KMT2C loss in bladder cancer cell lines (HTB9, T24) impaired homologous recombination, demonstrated by reduced RAD51 foci formation, defective replication fork recovery, and increased chromosomal aberrations after irradiation (chromosome fusions and radial chromosomes; n = 3; p < 0.01 to p < 0.001). These findings support KMT2C loss as a driver of DNA repair deficiency.

In preclinical xenograft models derived from KMT2C-deficient tumors (HTB9 BC, H1437 NSCLC, T84 COAD, Cal-33 HNSCC), PARP1/2 inhibition with olaparib significantly reduced tumor growth compared to KMT2C-proficient controls (e.g., HTB9 KD1 tumor weight 0.072 ± 0.023 g vs 0.862 ± 0.156 g vehicle; p < 0.05). Mechanistically, KMT2C knockdown caused homologous recombination deficiency in HTB9 and T24 bladder cancer cells. This was demonstrated by reduced RAD51 foci formation, impaired replication fork recovery, and increased chromosomal aberrations after irradiation, resulting in reliance on PARP-mediated DNA repair. Together, these data support KMT2C loss of function as a functional driver of HR deficiency and a predictive biomarker of PARP inhibitor sensitivity.

In preclinical gastric carcinoma models, NPTXR overexpression conferred sensitivity to NPTXR-targeted therapy. In xenograft mouse models of gastric cancer (MKN1; n = 3–4 mice per group), treatment with anti-NPTXR polyclonal or monoclonal antibodies markedly suppressed peritoneal metastatic tumor burden compared with control IgG, measured by reduced luciferase signal intensity and significantly smaller total nodule volume. In vitro, anti-NPTXR mAb-1 enhanced the antiproliferative effects of 5-fluorouracil and cisplatin, while NPTXR knockdown or knockout in gastric cancer cell lines (MKN1, N87, NUGC3, MKN45) reduced proliferation, migration, invasion, adhesion, and ALDH-positive stem-like populations, and induced mitochondrial membrane depolarization and caspase-3 and -9 activation.

In preclinical urothelial carcinoma (UC) models, combined loss of KMT2C/KMT2D increased sensitivity to EGFR inhibitors, with Kmt2c/d-deficient cells showing significantly reduced IC50 values for afatinib and gefitinib compared to WT controls across three independent in vitro experiments (both P < 0.0001). Enhanced growth suppression following EGF withdrawal (p = 0.0005), gefitinib (100 nM) (p = 0.0133), and afatinib (100 nM) (p = 0.0004). In sgKmt2c + sgKmt2d + Pten KO syngeneic UC allografts, afatinib treatment produced significantly smaller tumors than vehicle controls (n = 10 tumors/group/replicate; two independent replicates; P = 0.0007) and was associated with lower EGFR Y845 phosphorylation (n = 3 tumors/group; P = 0.0312) and reduced Ki-67 positivity (n = 5 tumors/group; P = 0.0007) by IHC.

In preclinical lung squamous cell carcinoma models, KMT2D loss increased sensitivity to SHP2 inhibition (SHP099) and pan-ERBB inhibition (afatinib). Enhanced growth suppression was observed in Kmt2d-deficient murine LUSC cell lines and in human LUSC models (LK2, HARA-sgKMT2D) compared with KMT2D-wild-type controls in cell viability and colony formation assays across multiple independent experiments. In vivo, Trp53−/−;Kmt2d−/− orthotopic mouse tumors treated with SHP099 plus afatinib showed reduced tumor growth in all mice (9/9). Tumor volume was reduced by >50% in 6/9 mice, and 7/9 mice continued to show tumor shrinkage at 6 weeks. Median survival was 84 days, compared with 41 days for vehicle and 64 days for SHP099 monotherapy. KMT2D-wild-type PDX-2 and PDX-4 showed limited or no response.

evidence_statement: In a case report of metastatic cholangiocarcinoma harboring an FGFR2 W290_P307>C (16.25% Variant allele frequency) alteration together with CDH1 Q677fs*7 (23.1% VAF) and CDKN2A/B frameshift mutations (p16INK4a S56fs*51 and p14ARF Q70fs*78; 18.9% VAF), pazopanib monotherapy (800 mg daily) produced a radiologic response across liver and bone lesions. The patient remained on treatment for 7.5 months before disease progression, which was accompanied by worsening symptoms. At progression, a combination regimen of pazopanib 200 mg daily, crizotinib 250 mg daily, and palbociclib 75 mg every other day resulted in a 53% reduction in SUL peak by PERCIST (from 2.86 to 1.33), metabolic regression of hepatic and skeletal lesions, and no grade 3–4 toxicities, representing the first clinical evidence supporting preclinical synthetic lethality between CDH1 alteration and ROS1 inhibition.

In preclinical lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) models, loss-of-function KMT2D (truncating/inactivating) was associated with greater sensitivity to glycolysis inhibition, most consistently 2-deoxy-D-glucose (2-DG). In vitro, KMT2D-truncating LUAD cell lines (H1568 [E758], DV-90 [P2118fs], CORL-105 [R2188fs]) showed stronger growth inhibition than KMT2D-WT lines (A549, H1792, H1437, H23, H358) when treated with 2-DG (p(AUC)=0.018; Wilcoxon rank-sum; n=3) and POMHEX (p(AUC)=0.036; n=3). Selectivity was weaker for koningic acid (p(AUC)=0.071; n=3) and vorinostat/SAHA (p(AUC)=0.071; n=3). In vivo, 2-DG (500 mg/kg every other day) preferentially reduced tumor growth in xenografts from KMT2D-mutant cells, with H1568 tumors showing smaller volumes vs vehicle (n=12/group; p<0.05) while KMT2D-WT H358 tumors did not show a significant effect (n=6/group; ns). Similarly, DV-90 xenografts were inhibited (n=6/group; p<0.05) while KMT2D-WT H1792 xenografts were not (n=6/group).

In this 2019 study, targeted RNA sequencing using the Archer FusionPlex technology was validated and implemented to detect oncogenic fusion transcripts in 62 genes recurrently rearranged in solid tumors, including sarcomas, without prior knowledge of fusion partners. A total of 192 formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) bone and soft tissue tumor samples from January 2016 to January 2018 were submitted to Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center for analysis. In-frame gene fusions were identified in 79 of 184 cases (43%), including 6 cases (3%) with novel fusion partners. In two cases of pseudomyogenic hemangioendothelioma present in this study cohort the testing revealed FOSB fusions with a novel partner gene ACTB. In both ACTB::FOSB fusion positive pseudomyogenic hemangioendothelioma cases the ACTB exon 3 was joined with the FOSB exon 2. The FOSB breakpoint in the ACTB::FOSB fusion matched previously reported breakpoints. This study further confirms specific association between FOSB fusions and pseudomyogenic hemangioendothelioma.
